This manual not only comprehensively and systematically introduces the common standards, formulas and data for hydraulic cylinder design, but also, based on the summary of relevant standards and the author's practical experience, provides technical requirements for hydraulic cylinders and their components, taboos for the design and manufacture of hydraulic cylinders, test methods for hydraulic cylinders, and a large number of product drawings of hydraulic cylinders that have been tested on actual machines (or empirical tests). Furthermore, through research and engineering tests (including some verification and re-inspection), it screens out new technologies for the design and (re)manufacturing of hydraulic cylinders with practical value or engineering application prospects.

This manual has the characteristics of novel content, large amount of information, wide range of sources, complete specifications, strong practicability, reliable data, and convenient use.

This manual can be used by personnel engaged in the selection, design, process, processing, assembly, testing, acceptance, on-site maintenance and upkeep, remanufacturing, and product marketing of hydraulic cylinders, hydraulic machinery, equipment, or devices, and can also be used as a reference by teachers and students of related majors in colleges and universities.

Foreword
In hydraulic transmission systems, power is transmitted and controlled through pressurized fluid circulating in a closed circuit. The hydraulic cylinder is one of the components in such systems, serving as a device that converts hydraulic power into linear mechanical force and motion. The hydraulic cylinder consists of several moving parts and assemblies, including a piston rod running within the cylinder barrel, or a piston rod and piston integrated coaxially and in parallel.

Among hydraulic transmission systems and components, aside from tanks and piping, the technical design that engineering technicians are most likely to encounter is the hydraulic cylinder. Although the design and manufacturing of hydraulic cylinders are relatively simple and easy compared to other hydraulic components or devices, it is actually quite difficult to truly design and manufacture a good hydraulic cylinder. This is because its working conditions are more difficult to determine than those of hydraulic valves or pumps, and it may also be affected by unexpected factors. Moreover, hydraulic cylinders are often produced as single units or in small batches, making it difficult to achieve perfection in materials, heat treatment processes, process equipment, assembly, and inspection. Any small mistake can lead to major accidents. Taking hydraulic press cylinders as an example, if the sealing system design is unreasonable, or if the dimensions, geometric tolerances, or surface roughness of designed and manufactured parts are not properly handled, internal and external leakage will occur, and merely replacing seals can cause significant waste of manpower and materials. There have been incidents where cracks occurred at the flanged end of a piston rod due to heat treatment problems, leading to early fatigue fracture and causing hydraulic press slide blocks to fall off, resulting in personal injury. These firsthand experiences remind every designer that when designing hydraulic cylinders, one must consider all aspects carefully, be cautious, follow standards, and use calculation methods that have been proven and recognized through engineering practice.

Nowadays, manufacturing hydraulic cylinders is somewhat easier than in the past, as there are now commercial cylinder tubes that comply with JB/T11718-2013 "Technical Conditions for Hydraulic Cylinder Tubes," precision seamless steel tubes with inner diameter that comply with GB/T32957-2016 "Cold Drawn or Cold Rolled Precision Seamless Steel Tubes for Hydraulic and Pneumatic System Equipment," and seamless steel tubes that comply with YB/T46732018 "Cold Drawn Seamless Steel Tubes for Hydraulic Cylinder Tubes." However, this brings about the problem of connecting and sealing the front and rear end caps. If not handled properly, it may result in batch scrap. Therefore, the manufacturing process of hydraulic cylinders is particularly important. It is necessary to correctly guide production and ensure product quality by designing and summarizing processing techniques and process equipment based on actual hydraulic cylinder production.

Large internal leakage and/or external leakage may be the primary and most intuitive manifestation of poor or deteriorating quality in a hydraulic cylinder. The actual service life of a hydraulic cylinder is often determined by the amount of leakage. At the same time, most of the content in current hydraulic cylinder standards is about sealing requirements or related to sealing, making the design of the hydraulic cylinder sealing device or sealing system particularly important.

The assembly of hydraulic cylinders requires specialized skills. Due to production batch sizes, hydraulic cylinder assembly generally cannot use complete interchangeability assembly method, and often requires grouping method, adjustment method, or repair assembly method. Therefore, operators need to be proficient not only in the drawings and assembly process of hydraulic cylinders, but also in measurement technology, assembly dimension chain calculation, and fitter technology. In this sense, a good hydraulic cylinder is not only designed but also assembled.

Whether it is the finalization (appraisal) of a hydraulic cylinder or its factory (acceptance) inspection, testing is required. Therefore, the comprehensiveness, correctness, and feasibility of hydraulic cylinder testing methods are particularly important. Moreover, the reliability, durability, and environmental adaptability of hydraulic cylinders are determined through testing, which is especially important for hydraulic cylinders used in ships, aerospace, and even military fields. To this end, this manual provides a relatively comprehensive introduction to laboratory environmental testing methods for military equipment.

Hydraulic cylinders are usually just one component in a hydraulic system, or one part in a hydraulic press (machinery), and must meet the technical conditions of the hydraulic press (machinery). Nowadays, the design and manufacturing of hydraulic cylinders often neglect research and understanding of the entire hydraulic press (machinery), resulting in hydraulic cylinders that cannot well meet the technical requirements of the whole machine, making hydraulic cylinders one of the components with the shortest service life in the entire machine. This manual
5:
This handbook provides an overview of hydraulic cylinder design and selection from the perspective of the entire hydraulic machine, based on relevant standards for hydraulic presses (machines) and the author's experience in designing and manufacturing hydraulic presses (machines). It also presents the author's views on content related to hydraulic cylinders in technical conditions for hydraulic presses, for reference and use by readers when designing and selecting hydraulic cylinders for hydraulic presses (machines).

Like other hydraulic components, hydraulic cylinders can only operate safely and reliably under certain conditions (such as specified operating conditions) to ensure a certain service life. Therefore, hydraulic cylinders need to be used correctly and maintained and serviced properly. Among these, the selection, use, and maintenance of hydraulic working media are particularly important. However, online testing (monitoring) of hydraulic working media not only requires necessary equipment but also requires relevant personnel to have certain practical experience.

In recent years, new standards, new materials, new structures, new processes, new products, new technologies, new design theories, and methods have emerged in the field of hydraulic cylinder design and manufacturing. This handbook timely incorporates and summarizes the phased technical achievements, including aspects of green manufacturing and remanufacturing.

Worth promoting is a new design concept and method, which is to integrate the concept of remanufacturing into the design of new hydraulic cylinders, making new hydraulic cylinders remanufacturable. The specific approach is: during the design of new hydraulic cylinders, evaluate the remanufacturability of the hydraulic cylinder and its parts to meet the standards, and correct any problems found.

This handbook follows the new development concept and upholds the spirit of keeping pace with the times and innovation, striving to achieve the best combination of scientificity, advancement, practicality, and reliability, in order to maximize the rapid improvement of the ability of design personnel for hydraulic cylinders and hydraulic machinery, equipment, or devices with hydraulic cylinders as actuators to independently innovate, to meet the needs of building an innovative country.

This handbook has the following characteristics:

1. Comprehensive, new, and accurate standards
This handbook not only comprehensively and systematically cites and excerpts standards related to hydraulic cylinder design and manufacturing published and implemented before December 31, 2018, such as G B / T 3 5 0 2 3—2 0 1 8 "Reliability Evaluation Method for Hydraulic Components", G B / T3 6 5 2 0 . 1—2 0 1 8 "Hydraulic Transmission Polyurethane Seal Size Series Part 1: Dimensions and Tolerances of Piston Reciprocating Motion Seals", G B / T 3 6 5 2 0 . 2—2 0 1 8 "Hydraulic Transmission Polyurethane Seal Size Series Part 2: Dimensions and Tolerances of Piston Rod Reciprocating Motion Seals", G B / T 2 3 4 8—2 0 1 8 "Fluid Transmission Systems and Components Cylinder Diameter and Piston Rod Diameter", G B / T3 7 1 6 2 . 1—2 0 1 8 "Hydraulic Transmission Monitoring of Contamination by Fluid Particles Part 1: General Provisions", and even includes G B / T 3 7 4 0 0 . 1 0—2 0 1 9 "General Technical Conditions for Heavy Machinery Part 10: Assembly" and G B / T 3 7 4 0 0 . 1 6—2 0 1 9 "General Technical Conditions for Heavy Machinery Part 16: Hydraulic Systems" published on August 30, 2019, and implemented on March 1, 2020, and based on the author's summary of application experience, explains matters that should be noted when citing these standards.

2. Practical and reliable content
This handbook includes standards, commonly used formulas and materials for hydraulic cylinder design and manufacturing, technical requirements for hydraulic cylinders and their parts, etc., providing comprehensive, accurate, and practical reference standards, documents, and materials for engineering and technical personnel to design hydraulic cylinders, such as listing a large number of hydraulic cylinder drawings that have been tested on engineering prototypes (or empirical tests) in Section 4.9 and compiling Section 3.9 based on practical experience, providing truly useful references for engineering and technical personnel to design and manufacture hydraulic cylinders.

3. Adhering to innovation and pursuing advancement
Innovation is the primary driving force for leading development. Some content in this handbook is given by the author for the first time, such as the failure modes of the hydraulic cylinder sealing system given according to G B / T 3 5 0 2 3—2 0 1 8. Taking Chapter 5 of this handbook as an example, not only are the test methods specified in G B / T1 5 6 2 2—2 0 0 5 "Hydraulic Cylinder Test Method" and J B / T 1 0 2 0 5—2 0 1 0 "Hydraulic Cylinder" innovated (including errata), but also the author's views on the test methods specified in D B 4 4 / T 1 1 6 9 . 2—2 0 1 3 "Servo Hydraulic Cylinder Part 2: Test Method" and G B / T 3 2 2 1 6—2 0 1 5 "Hydraulic Transmission Test Method for Proportional/Servo Control Hydraulic Cylinders" are presented and explanations are given.

Chapter 1 Basic Design and Manufacturing of Hydraulic Cylinders
1.1 Commonly Used Standard Catalogs for Hydraulic Cylinder Design and Manufacturing
A standard is a normative document, based on the comprehensive achievements of science, technology, and experience, formulated according to the principle of consensus and approved by a recognized institution, with the characteristics of common use and repeatability, in order to achieve the best order within a certain range.
A document that clarifies requirements is called a specification. Normative documents are general terms for documents such as standards, technical specifications, procedures, and regulations.
The design and (re)manufacturing of hydraulic cylinders involve many current standards. According to these related standards, hydraulic cylinders can be designed and manufactured in a standardized manner, thereby obtaining unified, simplified, coordinated, and optimized hydraulic cylinders.
The design and (re)manufacturing of hydraulic cylinders, including the re-manufacturing of hydraulic cylinders and their parts, involves relevant international, national, industry, and local standard catalogs, as shown in the following tables.

1.2.2 Excerpts of Scope and Normative References of Hydraulic Cylinder Product Standards
Product standards are standards that specify the requirements to be met by products to ensure their applicability.
In the following excerpts of standards, the current standard date is added to the normative references that do not specify a date; for replaced standards, new standards are cited, and necessary corrections are made.
When conducting quality assessment and accident arbitration based on the following standards, the original standard provisions shall still be followed, i.e., for all dated references, all subsequent amendments (excluding corrections) or revised versions are not applicable to the standard, but the parties who have reached an agreement based on the standard are encouraged to study whether to use the latest versions of these documents. For undated references, the current version of the referenced documents is applicable to this standard.

1.3 Common Standards for Hydraulic Cylinder Design and Manufacturing - Terms and Definitions and Their Explanations
1.3.1 Terms and Definitions Defined in Common Standards
Terms are the most basic subject of standardization. For terms and definitions, if there are no recognized standards, the formulation of other technical standards in a technical field will become a difficult and time-consuming task, which will ultimately lead to low work efficiency and a high probability of misunderstandings.
Terms are the linguistic (word) references to general concepts in specific professional fields. Terms should have the property of univocity, at least within a related discipline or a professional field, otherwise ambiguity, polysemy, and synonymy phenomena will occur.
Within a standard or a series of standards (or different parts of a standard), the same term should be used for the same concept. Synonyms should be avoided for defined concepts. Each selected term should have only one meaning as much as possible.
Before establishing terms and definitions for a concept in a certain standard, it should be checked whether terms and definitions for that concept have already been established in other standards. If they have been established, the standard that defines the concept should be cited, and there is no need to redefine it.
If it is necessary to repeat a term that has already been standardized, the standard from which the definition comes should be indicated. If an already standardized definition must be rewritten, a note should be added.
Terms should not contain requirements, nor should they be written in the form of requirements. The expression of a definition should be able to replace its term in context.
In the field of fluid power and control technology, terms have specific meanings. When formulating, modifying standards, writing journals, reports, and related technical documents, the terms specified in each standard should be used.

3.1
Proportional/Servo-Controlled Hydraulic Cylinder
A hydraulic cylinder used for proportional/servo control with dynamic performance requirements.

The process (characteristic) of a proportional/servo-controlled hydraulic cylinder's input signal (corresponding to the actual displacement of the piston rod or cylinder barrel) tracking the input step signal (corresponding to the desired step displacement).

The time taken for the output signal of the step response curve to start from reaching 10% of the steady-state amplitude (or target value) to initially reaching 90% of the steady-state amplitude (or target value).

Under rated pressure, when the input constant amplitude sinusoidal current varies within a certain frequency range, the complex ratio of the output displacement signal to the input current, including amplitude-frequency characteristics and phase-frequency characteristics.

The ratio of the amplitude of the output displacement signal to the amplitude of the input current.
Note: The frequency at which the amplitude ratio is -3 dB is the amplitude-frequency bandwidth.
3.3.2 Phase-Frequency Characteristic
The phase angle difference between the output displacement signal and the input current.
Note: The frequency at which the phase lag is 90° is the phase-frequency bandwidth.
3.4 Dynamic Friction Force
The dynamic resistance force experienced by the piston and piston rod of a proportional/servo-controlled hydraulic cylinder under loaded motion conditions.
3.5 Working Stroke
The maximum distance traveled by the moving part of a hydraulic cylinder from one working position to another under steady-state operating conditions.

3.1 Component
An independent unit composed of one or more parts, excluding piping, that functions as a component in a hydraulic transmission system.
Note: Refers to hydraulic components such as cylinders, pumps, motors, valves, and filters.
Author's Note: This definition differs from that in GB/T 17446-2012 and has issues.

The ability of a product to perform the required functions under specified conditions and within a specified time interval.
[GB/T 29300.13-2008, Definition 191-0206]
Note: When this ability is expressed in terms of probability, it is called reliability.
Author's Note: GB/T 29300.13-2008 has been partially replaced by GB/T 29300.99-2016, where the definition of (product) reliability is: the ability to perform the required functions without failure under specified conditions and within a specified time interval.

The interruption of a component's ability to perform the required functions.
[GB/T 29300.13-2008, Definition 191-0401]
Author's Note: GB/T 29300.13-2008 has been partially replaced by GB/T 29300.99-2016, where the definition of (product) failure is: the loss of the ability to perform the required functions.
3.4 B10 Life
The average life when the reliability of a component is 90% after it has been put into use without any repair; or the average life when 10% is expected to fail.
3.5 Mean Time To Failure (MTTF)
The mathematical expectation of the time before failure.
[GB/T 29300.13-2008, Definition 191-1207]
Note: That is, the average working time from the time the component is put into operation until it fails, without any repair.
Author's Note: GB/T 29300.13-2008 has been partially replaced by GB/T 29300.99-2016, where "Mean Time To Failure" is replaced by "Mean Operating Time To Failure," and the definition is: the expected value of the operating time before failure.
3.6 Mean Cycles To Failure (MCTF)
The mathematical expectation of the number of cycles before failure.
3.7 Threshold
A value used to compare with test data of a component's performance parameters (such as leakage, flow rate, and working pressure).
Note: This value is used as a key parameter for performance comparison, typically defined by experts as a certain value, but it does not necessarily indicate the termination of the component's operation.

1.3.2 Explanation on Some Terms and Definitions
Terms (concepts) and definitions are the starting point of the life (service life) cycle of a product, and their importance is self-evident.
1. Proportional/servo controlled hydraulic cylinder
In the current standards and some mechanical (hydraulic) design manuals and hydraulic technology monographs, terms such as cylinder, oil cylinder, hydraulic cylinder, servo cylinder, servo hydraulic cylinder, hydraulic booster, hydraulic actuator, hydraulic actuator, hydraulic servo actuator, and proportional/servo controlled hydraulic cylinder have been used. Some of them have been defined in relevant standards. For example, "cylinder" and "servo cylinder" are defined in GB/T17446-2012, but the term "servo cylinder" is limited to only being related to pneumatic technology; in GB/T32216-2015, the term "proportional/servo controlled hydraulic cylinder" is defined, which is a hydraulic cylinder used for proportional/servo control with dynamic performance requirements; in HB083-2005, there are names such as "hydraulic booster" and "hydraulic actuator", although there are no definitions, but there are explanations; "hydraulic servo actuator" is seen in reference [83], but its source is unclear; in QJ1495-1988, terms such as "actuator", "servo actuator", "electro-hydraulic servo actuator", and "servo hydraulic cylinder" are defined, which are applicable to aerospace product technical documents, and various papers, monographs, and civilian product technical documents can also refer to them; in DB44/T11691.1-2013 (already abolished, for reference only), the term "servo hydraulic cylinder" is defined, which is a hydraulic cylinder with static and dynamic index requirements. By cooperating with built-in or external sensors, servo valves or proportional valves, controllers, etc., it can form a hydraulic control system with high control accuracy and fast response speed. Static indexes include trial operation, pressure resistance, internal leakage, external leakage, minimum starting pressure, load starting friction force, eccentricity, leakage under low pressure, stroke detection, load efficiency, high temperature test, durability, etc.; dynamic indexes include step response, frequency response, etc.
According to the current standards, this manual uses "proportional/servo controlled hydraulic cylinder", "servo controlled hydraulic cylinder", "servo hydraulic cylinder", or "hydraulic cylinder".
According to or referring to some current standards, such as GB/T8129-2015, "servo hydraulic cylinder" is tentatively defined as a hydraulic cylinder whose cylinder advance, cylinder return movement and/or stop are operated according to instructions. The instruction may indicate the required next position value, or it may indicate the feed speed required to move to that position, or it may indicate the time, amplitude and/or frequency for which it remains at the predetermined position (nearby).
It should be noted here:
1) Do not call the hydraulic cylinder and servo valve integrated together a "servo hydraulic cylinder". If so, the definition of "servo hydraulic cylinder" in QJ1495-1988 cannot continue to be used.
2) In some fields, hydraulic vibration generators (or vibration generators, exciters, etc.) may also refer to servo controlled hydraulic cylinders. Please refer to standards such as GB/T22982-2010.
It needs to be emphasized that at least the term "hydraulic cylinder" should be used in the field of hydraulic technology, because it needs to be distinguished from "air cylinder"; it is not advisable to use "servo cylinder" because it has been defined as a term only related to pneumatic technology.
2. Cylinder stroke
Terms such as "stroke", "cylinder stroke", "working stroke", and "full stroke" have been defined or used in relevant standards. For example, in GB/T17446-2012, "cylinder stroke" is defined as: the distance moved by its movable part from one limit position to another limit position; it also includes some expressions related to "cylinder stroke", such as "adjustable stroke cylinder (or adjustable stroke hydraulic cylinder)" is defined as: the stroke stop position of which can be adjusted.
53:
A cylinder whose position can be changed to allow variation in stroke length. Additionally, the term "full stroke" has been used in standards such as C B/T3812—2013, J B/T10205—2010, Q C/T460—2010, and D B 44/T11691.1—2013; while "maximum cylinder stroke" has been defined in reference [108].

If "stroke" is the distance between two extreme positions, then the stroke cannot be changed; if the extreme positions can be changed, then they are not extreme positions. Therefore, one of the definitions of extreme position and stroke must be negated (or ignored, or its meaning changed). If "stroke" can be varied, i.e., adjustable, then there would be no parameter in hydraulic cylinders that can be calibrated (represented) for basic parameters, thus there is a need to define the term "maximum cylinder stroke" and its definition.

In reference [108], "maximum cylinder stroke" is defined as the distance moved by its movable part from the cylinder's return (forward) dead center to the cylinder's forward (return) dead center.

Since "maximum cylinder stroke" can be defined, "minimum cylinder stroke" can also be defined, thus "cylinder stroke" can be understood as having a certain range, or expressed as "cylinder stroke range".

Further, "cylinder working stroke range" can be defined, and "maximum cylinder stroke" and "minimum cylinder stroke" should be included in the "cylinder stroke range".

For servo hydraulic cylinders, defining "maximum cylinder stroke", "minimum cylinder stroke", "cylinder stroke range", and "cylinder working stroke range" is of great significance.

Because "cylinder forward dead center" is defined as the cylinder's forward limit position restricted by the cylinder structure, "maximum cylinder stroke" is determined by the cylinder structure, and is one of the characteristics that distinguishes this cylinder from other cylinders. This characteristic should be unique and have a definite meaning, i.e., the cylinder's forward dead center. The cylinder's forward dead center has only one (point) in a specific servo hydraulic cylinder, and it is also unique.

Under "cylinder working stroke range", "maximum working stroke" and "minimum working stroke" can be derived. Since "cylinder working stroke range" is included in "cylinder stroke range", "maximum working stroke" and "minimum working stroke" are also included in "maximum cylinder stroke" and "minimum cylinder stroke". Therefore, servo hydraulic cylinders can set "soft limits" through the control system they are in to avoid the moving parts colliding with other cylinder parts.

In G B/T36484—2018 "Terminology for Forging Machinery", there are multiple terms related to stroke, all defined as: "... the maximum distance of movement."

3. Load-bearing Dynamic Friction Force and Dynamic Friction Force

"Load-bearing dynamic friction force" and "dynamic friction force" are related to servo hydraulic cylinders or proportional/servo controlled hydraulic cylinders. Whether they are synonyms or which one is more accurate is a problem that servo hydraulic cylinder designers need to consider.

In D B 44/T11691.1—2013, the term "load-bearing dynamic friction force" is defined as the motion resistance generated by the cylinder barrel, end cap, and sealing device to the piston rod under the condition of the servo hydraulic cylinder piston rod moving with load. In G B/T32216—2015, the term "dynamic friction force" is defined as the motion resistance experienced by the piston and piston rod under the condition of the proportional/servo controlled hydraulic cylinder moving with load.

Whether it is "load-bearing dynamic friction force" or "dynamic friction force", there are certain problems with their terms and definitions, which are briefly explained as follows:

1) Although "load-bearing dynamic friction force" is slightly better than "dynamic friction force", both repeat the term "dynamic friction force" in tribology. Even if rewriting the already standardized definition, it should be explained.

2) In the definition of "load-bearing dynamic friction force", the statement "the motion resistance generated by the cylinder barrel, end cap, and sealing device to the piston rod" is questionable.

3) In the definition of "dynamic friction force", plunger hydraulic cylinders should not have a piston, so the definition "the motion resistance experienced by the piston and piston rod" is not rigorous enough.

4) Under unclear load conditions (not specified or limited in the term), whether it is possible to detect (test) or repeatedly detect (test) the "dynamic friction force" within a certain detection (test) accuracy range is debatable. What kind of influence do various loads have on the dynamic friction force and the static/dynamic characteristics of hydraulic cylinders, as well as the non-linear characteristics of dynamic friction essence, modeling uncertainty, etc. are all topics that hydraulic workers are currently researching.

For hydraulic cylinders specified in J B/T10205—2010, dynamic friction force is part of the load efficiency test.

Based on the above brief analysis, the author believes that using the set of terms "running friction force", "no-load running friction force", and "loaded running friction force" to distinguish other hydraulic cylinders (specific) is more appropriate.

4. Leakage

In various standards, literature, and materials, it is very common to use "leakage" to describe the condition (phenomenon) of welds, parts, assemblies (devices). For example, in G B/T24I—2007, the term "leakage" is defined as the phenomenon of pressure transmission medium appearing on the outer surface of the metal tube base or weld under test pressure; at the same time, "destructive test" is also defined using "leakage", which is a test that continuously increases test pressure until the metal tube shows leakage or rupture. In G B25974.1—2010, "external leakage" is defined as the leakage of hydraulic components, with more than one drop of working fluid leaking out within an average of 5 minutes; in G B/T30206.2—2013, "leakage/seal leakage" is defined as a very small amount of fluid leakage on the surface of accessories, usually caused by the sealing parts undergoing periodic pressure loads resulting in compression expansion. For liquids, a thin oil film will form on the outer surface of the accessories, but no liquid droplets should form within the specified time. In J B/T13141—2017, "leakage" is defined as...
54:
This passage discusses various aspects of sealing in hydraulic cylinders. Key points include:

1. The definition of "leakage" as the phenomenon of hydraulic fluid escaping from inside a cylinder to the atmosphere under certain pressure and viscosity conditions.

2. Different classifications of leakage, such as distinguishing between "oil leakage" (more than one drop in 10 minutes) and "oil seepage" (less than one drop in 10 minutes).

3. The assertion that the main type of leakage in hydraulic cylinder seals is "blow-by" or "leakage through," rather than seepage, which is characterized by molecular leakage through capillaries.

4. The importance of not using the amount of leakage to distinguish between leakage and seepage, and that any leakage not caused by porosity in the sealing material should be described as leakage.

5. The application of the definition of "leakage" from GB/T 2247-2007 to metal tubes, welds, etc.

6. The lack of a clear definition for "coaxial seal" in relevant standards, and the suggestion to use "sliding ring type combined seal" instead.

7. The definition of "elastic material" and its inconsistency with other standards.

8. The importance of establishing the concept of "hydraulic seal system" to promote design thinking and improve sealing technology.

9. The characteristics of a hydraulic cylinder seal system, including satisfying sealing requirements, generally consisting of piston seal system and piston rod seal system, and emphasizing coordinated configuration of seal components.

10. The distinction between seal systems and single seals or simple seal configurations that don't have a synergistic effect.
55:
Coordination and unified configuration of all sealing components.
The term "hydraulic cylinder sealing system" is defined as follows: A set of sealing components arranged in series according to hydraulic cylinder sealing requirements, designed to create sealing, control leakage, and/or prevent contamination.

It should be noted that the sealing components referred to here specifically include sealing rings, retaining rings, guide rings, and dust seals used on hydraulic cylinders. A sealing assembly consists of one or more sealing components and matching parts (such as retaining rings, springs, metal shells), combined with guide rings, support rings, and backing rings.

Definitions of terms such as "minimum starting pressure," "load efficiency," and "combined hydraulic cylinder" can be found in Section 5.1.1. For issues related to the naming of digital hydraulic cylinders, see Section 5.5.

1.6.3 Resistance Calculation Formulas

Actual fluids will cause energy loss due to viscous friction force (motion resistance) during flow. Generally, this energy loss due to motion resistance is divided into friction (pressure) loss along the path and local resistance (pressure) loss.

The energy loss of fluid on the calculated length of a pipe section is the sum of friction (pressure) loss along the path and local resistance (pressure) loss.

1. Calculation of Friction Loss Along the Path

Friction loss along the path is related to the flow state of the fluid. Under given conditions, the quantitative standard (index) used to indicate whether the flow is laminar or turbulent is the critical Reynolds number.

Calculation formulas for friction loss along the path in circular pipes are shown in Table 1-40.

1.6.4 Flow from Orifice and Pipe Nozzle, Flow through Gap, Hydraulic Shock Calculation Formulas
1. Flow Calculation for Orifice and Pipe Nozzle
The flow calculation formulas for orifice and pipe nozzle are shown in Table 1-49.
2. Flow Calculation for Fluid Flow through Annular Gap
For hydraulic cylinders, the flow calculation formula for fluid flow through annular gap is usually used to calculate (estimate) the leakage at static and dynamic seals of hydraulic cylinders. Therefore, the volume flow symbol in Table 1-50 is qV, and it complies with the provisions of JB/T10205-2010 "Hydraulic Cylinders" for quantities and symbols.
The flow calculation formula for fluid flow through annular gap is shown in Table 1-50.
3. Hydraulic Shock Calculation
In hydraulic system components, accessories and pipelines, the pressure rise caused by a sudden decrease in flow may cause hydraulic (pressure) shock.
When the movement speed of the hydraulic cylinder changes drastically (such as starting, stopping or reversing), the hydraulic (pressure) shock caused by the inertial force due to the rate of change of momentum of the liquid in the cavity and moving parts is calculated using the formula in Table 1-51.

Since the stress at points r = r1 and r = r2 (on the inner and outer cylindrical surfaces of the thick-walled cylinder under internal pressure) differs greatly, most of the material in the outer layer of the cylinder cannot be fully utilized. 5. Calculation formula for rod stability
Hydraulic cylinder has at least one end that can move back and forth. Hydraulic cylinder can be simplified as a rod with uniform or non-uniform cross-section. For a rod (deformable body) in a deformed state, the balance between external load and elastic internal force it causes can be stable or unstable. The stability of the equilibrium state of a deformable body depends on the value of the compressive load applied on it. The extreme value of this load is called "critical load" Fkp.
For a rod (hydraulic cylinder) simplified as having uniform diameter d, when installation distance and stroke have a ratio greater than 10, i.e. l/d>10, rod stability generally needs to be calculated or checked (or verified). See Table 1-67 for calculation formula.

1.7.3 Allowable Stress and Static Calculation of Hydraulic Cylinder
1. Allowable Stress
1) Allowable stress when the hydraulic cylinder is subjected to centric rated force. The normal stress of individual parts of the hydraulic cylinder shall not exceed 70% of the yield limit or the 0.2% residual deformation limit of the material (this also applies to the tangential stress caused by liquid pressure); the tangential stress shall not exceed 65% of the yield limit of the material.
The normal stress at the high-pressure end of the hydraulic cylinder shall not exceed 80% of the yield limit of the material.
2) Allowable stress when the column and the supporting jack are subjected to twice the centric rated force. When the column and the supporting jack are in the fully retracted state and subjected to twice the centric rated force, the stress shall not exceed the yield limit of the material.
Note: This requirement only includes mechanical loads and excludes liquid pressure.
3) Allowable stress when the column and the supporting jack are subjected to eccentric rated force. When subjected to eccentric rated force, the normal stress (boundary stress) of the bent parts of the column and the supporting jack shall not exceed the yield limit of the material.
When the eccentric rated force is also subjected to lateral loads (e.g., used for stabilizing the support frame), the normal stress of the bent parts of the column and the supporting jack shall not exceed the yield limit of the material.
4) Allowable stress of welds. Under the load conditions of 1) to 3), the stress of the welds shall not exceed the percentage values of the allowable stress of the parent material listed in Table 1-68.

3. General Thread Tolerances
The thread engagement length is divided into three groups: short group (S), medium group (N), and long group (L). The length ranges for each group should conform to the provisions of Table 1-74.
To reduce the number of cutting tools, thread tolerance classes should be selected according to Tables 1-75 and 1-76.

If the actual engagement length of the thread is unknown (such as for standard bolts), it is recommended to determine the thread tolerance class according to the medium group (N).
According to the usage conditions, thread tolerance accuracy is divided into the following three levels:
- Precision: Used for precision threads.
- Medium: Used for general-purpose threads.
- Rough: Used for situations where thread manufacturing is difficult, such as on hot-rolled bars and deep blind holes.

Thread Marking A complete thread marking consists of a thread characteristic symbol, dimension symbol, tolerance zone symbol, and other necessary individual information for further explanation. The characteristic symbol for ordinary threads is "M". The dimension symbol for single-line threads is "Nominal Diameter × Pitch", with the numerical units of nominal diameter and pitch being millimeters. Example 1: M 8×1 indicates a single-line fine thread with a nominal diameter of 8 mm and a pitch of 1 mm. For coarse threads, the pitch item can be omitted. Example 2: M 8 indicates a single-line coarse thread with a nominal diameter of 8 mm and a pitch of 1.25 mm. The tolerance zone symbol consists of the pitch diameter tolerance zone symbol and the major diameter (for internal threads) or minor diameter (for external threads) tolerance zone symbol. The pitch diameter tolerance zone symbol is placed first, followed by the major/minor diameter tolerance zone symbol. Each diameter's tolerance zone symbol is composed of a numerical value indicating the tolerance grade and a letter (uppercase for internal threads, lowercase for external threads) indicating the tolerance zone position. If the pitch diameter tolerance zone symbol is the same as the major/minor diameter tolerance zone symbol, only one tolerance zone symbol is marked. The thread dimension symbol and tolerance zone are separated by a hyphen "-". Example 3: External thread: M 10×1-5g6g indicates an external thread with a pitch diameter tolerance zone of 5g and a major diameter tolerance zone of 6g. M 10-6g indicates a coarse external thread with both pitch diameter and major diameter tolerance zones of 6g. Internal thread: M 10×1-5H6H indicates an internal thread with a pitch diameter tolerance zone of 5H and a minor diameter tolerance zone of 6H. M 10-6H indicates a coarse internal thread with both pitch diameter and minor diameter tolerance zones of 6H. When indicating thread fits, the internal thread tolerance zone symbol is placed first, followed by the external thread tolerance zone symbol, separated by a slash "/". Example 4: M 6-6H/6g indicates a fit composed of an internal thread with a tolerance zone of 6H and an external thread with a tolerance zone of 6g. M 20×2-6H/5g6g indicates a fit composed of an internal thread with a tolerance zone of 6H and an external thread with a tolerance zone of 5g6g. In the following cases, the tolerance zone symbols for medium tolerance accuracy threads can be omitted: a) Internal thread: - - - 5H for nominal diameters less than or equal to 1.4 mm; - - - 6H for nominal diameters greater than or equal to 1.6 mm. Note: For threads with a pitch of 0.2 mm, the tolerance grade is 4. b) External thread: - - - 6h for nominal diameters less than or equal to 1.4 mm; - - - 6g for nominal diameters greater than or equal to 1.6 mm. Example 5: M 10 indicates a coarse external thread with pitch diameter and major diameter tolerance zones of 6g and medium tolerance accuracy, or a coarse internal thread with pitch diameter and minor diameter tolerance zones of 6H and medium tolerance accuracy. Other necessary information in the marking includes the thread engagement length group and direction of rotation. For threads with short and long engagement lengths, it is recommended to mark "S" and "L" symbols after the tolerance zone symbol, separated by a hyphen "-". For threads with medium engagement length, the engagement length group symbol (N) is not marked. Example 6: M 20×2-5H-S indicates an internal thread with short engagement length. M 6-7H/7g6g-L indicates internal and external threads with long engagement length. 27 Hydraulic Cylinder Manual

1.7.5 Processability and Structural Elements of Cylinder Component Design
1. Review of Product Structure Processability
All newly designed products or improved design products should undergo a review of product structure processability during the design process. For incoming product drawings, a review of product structure processability must be conducted before trial production.
The purpose of reviewing product structure processability is to ensure that the product meets processability requirements under the premise of satisfying quality and user requirements, and can be manufactured using relatively economical and reasonable methods under existing production conditions. It also aims to reduce the negative impact on the environment during the manufacturing process, improve resource utilization, improve working conditions, reduce harm to operators, and facilitate use, maintenance, or recycling.
Processability is divided into production processability and usage processability; the evaluation form is also divided into qualitative evaluation and quantitative evaluation. The evaluation of product structure processability mainly considers the following factors:
1) The type and complexity of the product.
2) The production volume or production type of the product.
3) Production efficiency and economy.
4) Existing production, usage, maintenance, and recycling conditions.
(1) Basic Requirements for Processability of Casting, Forging, Stamping, Welding, Heat Treatment, Machining, and Assembly of Component Structures
1) Processability of Casting Component Structures:
a. The wall thickness of castings should be appropriate and uniform. Under the premise of meeting component requirements, large wall thickness differences should be avoided as much as possible to reduce manufacturing difficulty.
b. The casting fillets should be reasonable and no sharp corners should be present.
c. The structure of the casting should be simplified as much as possible and have a reasonable draft angle for easy demolding.
d. The thickness and distribution of ribs should be reasonable to avoid deformation or cracking of the casting during cooling.
e. The material selection for castings should be reasonable.
f. The internal cavity structure of the casting should minimize the number of cores and facilitate core fixing and venting.
2) Processability of Forging Component Structures:
a. The structure should be as simple and symmetrical as possible.
b. Die forgings should have a reasonable forging draft angle and fillet radius.
c. The material and structure should have forgeability.
3) Processability of Stamping Component Structures:
a. The structure should be as simple and symmetrical as possible.
b. Sharp corners should be avoided in the outer shape and inner holes as much as possible.
c. The size of the fillet radius should be conducive to forming.
d. The material selection should meet process requirements.
4) Processability of Welding Component Structures:
a. The materials used for welded components should have weldability.
b. The arrangement of welds should be conducive to reducing welding stress and deformation, and minimizing energy and welding material consumption.
c. The form, position, and size of the weld joint should meet the requirements for welding quality.
d. The technical requirements for welded components should be reasonable.
e. The component structure should be conducive to welding operation.
f. Requirements for operational safety and reduction of environmental pollution should be met.
5) Processability of Heat Treatment Component Structures:
a. The technical requirements for heat treatment should be reasonable.
b. Heat-treated components should avoid sharp corners, sharp edges, and blind holes as much as possible.
c. The cross-section should be as uniform and symmetrical as possible.
87:
d. The material of parts should be compatible with the required physical and mechanical properties.
e. The heat treatment process of part materials should cause minimal environmental pollution.
6) Cutting processability of part structure:
a. Requirements for dimensional tolerances, geometric tolerances, and surface structure should be economical and reasonable.
b. Geometric shapes of machined surfaces should be as simple as possible.
c. Surfaces with mutual positional requirements should be machined in as few setups as possible.
d. Parts should have reasonable process datum and try to be consistent with design datum.
e. Structural elements of parts should be unified as much as possible, and try to use common equipment and standard tools for machining.
f. The structure of parts should facilitate simultaneous processing of multiple pieces.
g. The structure of parts should facilitate clamping, machining, and inspection.
h. The structure of parts should facilitate using less cutting fluid during machining.
7) Assembly processability:
a. Complex process equipment should be avoided as much as possible during assembly.
b. In the structure of assembly units or their components weighing more than 20 (or 15) kg, structural elements for lifting should be provided.
c. Intermediate disassembly and reassembly of related components should be avoided during assembly.
d. The connection methods of various components should ensure quick assembly and disassembly using the least tools as much as possible.
e. Various connection structural forms should facilitate mechanization and automation of assembly work.
(2) Main index items for reviewing product structural processability (see Table 1-81)
Table 1-81 Main index items for reviewing product structural processability (excerpted from GB/T 24737.3-2009)
Serial Number Index Item Index Calculation Formula
1 Product manufacturing labor
2 Unit product material consumption
3 Material utilization coefficient Km = Net weight of product / Material consumption quota for the product
4 Product structural assembly coefficient Ka = Sum of number of parts in independent components of the product / Total number of parts of the product
5 Product process cost
6 Product maintenance labor
7 Machining accuracy coefficient Kac = Number of dimensions with tolerance requirements marked on product or part drawing / Total number of surfaces of the product or part
8 Surface roughness coefficient Kr = Number of surfaces with roughness requirements marked on product or part drawing / Total number of surfaces of the product or part

10 Structural standardization coefficient Kst = Number of standard parts of the product / Total number of parts of the product
11 Structural element unification coefficient Ke = Number of same structural elements used in various parts of the product / Number of size specifications of that structural element
(3) Contents of processability review
To ensure good processability of the designed product, process review should be conducted at all stages of product design.
1) Review in preliminary design stage:
a. Analyze the rationality of structural schemes from a manufacturing perspective.
b. Analyze structural inheritance.
c. Analyze the degree of standardization, modularization, generalization, and serialization of the structure.
d. Analyze whether the various components of the product are conducive to assembly, adjustment, and maintenance.
e. Analyze whether the various components of the product are conducive to recycling and reuse after scrapping.
f. Analyze whether the selection of main materials is reasonable.
g. Possibility of processing main components in-house or outsourcing.
2) Review in technical design stage:
a. Analyze the feasibility of parallel assembly and inspection of various components of the product.
b. Analyze the feasibility of final assembly.
c. Analyze the feasibility of avoiding or reducing cutting machining during assembly.
d. Analyze the feasibility of manufacturing high-precision complex parts in-house.
e. Analyze the checkability of main parameters and the reasonableness of main assembly accuracy.
f. Analyze the feasibility of outsourcing special parts for processing.
3) Review in working drawing design stage:
a. Whether each component has assembly datum and is conducive to assembly.
b. The feasibility of splitting large components into smaller components for parallel assembly.
c. The feasibility of recycling and reusing components after scrapping.
d. Review the processability of casting, forging, stamping, welding, heat treatment, cutting machining, special machining, and assembly of parts.
e. Review the possible harmful environmental impacts or safety hazards during the manufacturing process of parts, and whether these impacts or hazards can be avoided or reduced.

1 4. Welding and related process method code
Each process method can be identified by a code. Welding and related process methods generally use a three-digit code representation. Among them, a single-digit code represents the major category of the process method, a two-digit code represents the classification of the process method, and a three-digit code represents a specific process method.
The codes for welding and related process methods are shown in Table 1-118.
1 5. Size, proportion and simplified representation of weld symbols (excerpted from GB/T 1 2212-2012)
In technical drawings, weld symbols are generally used to represent welds according to the provisions of GB/T3 2 4-2008 "Weld Symbol Representation Method". When drawing welds, they can be represented by views, section views or section drawings, or they can be represented schematically by axonometric drawings.

1.6 Classification and Codes for Metal Heat Treatment Processes
Metal heat treatment processes are classified into two main levels: basic classification and additional classification, with further subdivisions possible within each main level.
(1) Basic Classification
Based on the general name, type, and specific name of the process (classified according to the resulting microstructure or infiltrated elements), heat treatment processes are classified into three levels, as shown in Table 1-121.
(2) Additional Classification
Additional classification is a more detailed classification of certain process conditions within the basic classification. It includes the heating method and code for implementing the process, as shown in Table 1-122; annealing process and code, as shown in Table 1-123; and quenching cooling medium and cooling method and code, as shown in Table 1-124.

2. Technical Requirements for Electroplating of Hydraulic Cylinder Parts (Excerpt from GB/T 2574.2-2010)
(1) Basic Requirements
Before electroplating, the material, dimensional accuracy, and surface defects of the parts to be plated should be inspected. Parts that do not meet the requirements should not enter the electroplating process.
(2) Types of Plating Layers
1) Piston Rod: The piston rod should adopt one of the following composite plating layers:
a) Copper-tin alloy and hard chromium.
b) Copper-tin alloy and white chromium.
c) White chromium and hard chromium.
2) Other Parts: Other parts are generally electroplated with zinc, and other plating types that effectively protect the surface of the parts are allowed.
(3) Thickness of Plating Layers
1) Composite Plating Layers: The thickness of composite plating layers:
a) Copper-tin alloy: 20-35μm; hard chromium: 30-45μm.
b) Copper-tin alloy: 20-35μm; white chromium: 30-55μm.
c) White chromium: 20-35μm; hard chromium: 30-45μm.
2) Zinc Plating or Other Plating Layers: The thickness of zinc plating or other plating layers:
a) 7-15μm.
b) 15-25μm.
3) Special Plating Layers: The thickness of plating layers with special requirements shall be executed according to the provisions of the drawing documents.
(4) Hardness of Plating Layers
a) Copper-tin alloy and white chromium ≥500 HV.
b) White chromium and hard chromium ≥800 HV.
c) Copper-tin alloy and hard chromium ≥800 HV.
(5) Appearance Quality of Plating Layers
1) Inspection Environment: The appearance quality inspection should be conducted under natural scattered light or white light transmitted through light without reflected light.
2) Appearance Quality: The plating layer should be fine and uniform in crystallization, and should not have the following defects:
a) Surface roughness, particles, scorching, cracks, blistering, peeling, or falling off.
b) Dendritic crystallization.
c) Local absence of plating layer or exposure of intermediate layer.
3) Allowed Defects: The plating layer is allowed to have the following defects:
a) Slight rough surface that does not affect assembly at the chamfer.
b) Dark plating layer at the weld seam.
c) Pitting or pinholes caused by defects in the base metal, sand holes, and the electroplating process, the diameter and quantity of which should meet the following requirements:
① For zinc-plated parts, less than 5 points/dm², and the pore diameter should not be greater than 0.2mm.
② For chromium-plated parts, less than 5 points/dm², and the pore diameter should not be greater than 0.2mm.
③ For copper-plated parts, less than 5 points/dm², and the pore diameter should not be greater than 0.2mm.
4) Surfaces Not Assessed: Plating layer defects caused by welding-allowed defects are not assessed; the quality of the plating layer on the surface of the retreat groove is not assessed.
5) Sand Marks on the Piston Rod Travel Surface: The sand marks on the piston rod travel surface are specified as follows:
a) There should not be more than two sand marks on the same circumferential line of the piston rod travel surface.
b) The length of sand marks should not exceed 6mm, and the depth should not be greater than 0.02mm.
c) The interval between two sand marks should not be greater than 20mm.
d) The number of sand marks should not exceed 10/m².
3. Specifications for Electroless Nickel-Phosphorus Alloy Plating Layer (Excerpt from GB/T 1393-2008)
Electroless nickel-phosphorus alloy plating layer is usually obtained by catalytic reduction of nickel metal ions in a hot weakly acidic solution using sodium hypophosphite as a reducing agent. Since the deposited nickel-phosphorus alloy is a catalyst for the reaction, the reaction proceeds automatically. As long as the electroless plating solution circulates freely through all surfaces of irregularly shaped parts, a uniform deposited layer of the plating layer can be obtained.
The obtained plating layer is a thermodynamic metastable alloy of nickel-phosphorus supersaturated solid solution with a phosphorus content of up to 14% (mass fraction). The structure, physical and chemical properties of electroless nickel-phosphorus depend on the composition of the plating layer, the chemical composition of the electroless nickel bath, the pretreatment of the substrate, and the post-plating heat treatment.
Electroless nickel-phosphorus plating layer can improve corrosion resistance and provide wear resistance. Generally, when the phosphorus content in the plating layer increases to more than 8% (mass fraction), the corrosion resistance will be significantly improved; while as the phosphorus content in the plating layer decreases to less than 8% (mass fraction), the wear resistance will be improved. However, through appropriate heat treatment, the microhardness of the high-phosphorus content plating layer will be greatly improved, thereby improving the wear resistance of the plating layer.
(1) Wear Resistance, Thickness, and Application Conditions of Nickel-Phosphorus Plating Layer
Table 1-133 lists the minimum thickness of nickel-phosphorus plating layer with sufficient wear resistance under different usage conditions. In order to obtain the best wear resistance with the minimum thickness of nickel-phosphorus plating layer, the surface of the substrate material should be flat and free of pores. The substrate material with a surface roughness value Ra < 0.2μm can be used as a template.
Since the electroless nickel-phosphorus deposition process can be controlled to obtain a nickel-phosphorus plating layer with characteristics that meet different usage requirements, engineering technicians can specify the characteristics of the plating layer according to special requirements. Table 1-134 lists the types and phosphorus contents of nickel-phosphorus plating layers recommended for use under different conditions.

Double slashes (//) will be used to indicate that a step or operation has not been listed or has been omitted. The marking includes the following contents: a) The term "electroless nickel-phosphorus coating". b) National standard number, i.e., GB/T 13913. c) Hyphen. d) Chemical symbol of substrate metal (see marking of substrate metal). e) Slash separator (/). f) Symbol of electroless nickel-phosphorus coating (see marking of coating type and thickness), and symbols of coatings before and after electroless nickel-phosphorus (see marking of coating type and thickness), with each level in the coating sequence separated by separators in the order of operations. The coating marking should include the thickness of the coating (μm) and heat treatment requirements (see marking of heat treatment requirements). Example of Marking: An electroless nickel-phosphorus coating with phosphorus content of 10% (mass fraction) and thickness of 15μm is deposited on a 16Mn steel substrate, requiring stress relief treatment at 210℃ for 22h, followed by electroplating of 0.5μm thick chromium on its surface. After chromium plating, another heat treatment for hydrogen embrittlement relief is performed at 210℃ for 22h. The specific marking is as follows: Electroless Nickel-Phosphorus Coating GB/T 13913-Fe<16Mn>[SR(210)22]/NiP(10)15/Cr0.5[ER(210)22] 1) Marking of Substrate Metal. The substrate metal should be marked with its chemical symbol, and if it is an alloy, it should be marked with its main components. For special alloys, it is recommended to mark them with their standard names. For example, fill in its steel number or corresponding national standard in the <> symbol. Fe<16Mn> is the national standard name for low-alloy high-strength steel. 2) Marking of Heat Treatment Requirements. Heat treatment requirements should be marked in brackets according to the following contents. a) SR indicates stress relief heat treatment; HT indicates heat treatment to increase coating hardness or bonding force between coating and substrate metal; ER indicates hydrogen embrittlement relief heat treatment. b) The minimum temperature (°C) of heat treatment should be marked in parentheses. c) The duration of heat treatment (h) should be marked. 3) Marking of Coating Type and Thickness. Electroless nickel-phosphorus coating should be marked with the symbol NiP, and the phosphorus content value should be filled in parentheses immediately after it, followed by the minimum local thickness of the electroless nickel-phosphorus coating in μm. The underlying layer should be marked with the chemical symbol of the deposited metal, followed by the minimum local thickness of the coating in μm. For example, the symbol Ni indicates a nickel electroplated layer. Other coatings deposited on the electroless nickel-phosphorus coating, such as chromium, 601 Hydraulic Cylinder Manual

The marking method is to use the chemical symbol of the electroplating layer plus the minimum local thickness of the coating, in units of μm.
(3) Technical requirements for nickel-phosphorus plating
1) Appearance of the coating. The appearance of the chemical nickel-phosphorus plating on the important surface of the coating should be bright, semi-bright or matte as specified by the demander, and there should be no pinholes, bubbles, peeling, spherical growths, cracks and other defects harmful to the final finishing when inspected by naked eyes (unless otherwise required).
Bubbles or cracks that are visible to the naked eye, as well as defects caused by heat treatment, should be regarded as waste products.
2) Surface roughness of the coating. If the demander specifies the requirements for the final surface roughness, its measurement method should be carried out in accordance with the provisions of GB/T10061.
Note: The final surface roughness of chemical nickel-phosphorus plating is not necessarily better than the surface roughness of the substrate before plating. Unless the bottom layer of the plating is particularly smooth and polished.
3) Coating thickness. The specified coating thickness in the marking part refers to its minimum local thickness. In the absence of special instructions from the demander, the minimum local thickness of the coating should be measured at any point on the important surface of the workpiece (which can be tangent to a sphere with a diameter of 20 mm).
4) Coating hardness. If a hardness value is specified, it should be measured according to the method specified in GB/T9790. The hardness of the coating should be within ±10% of the hardness value specified by the demander.
5) Adhesion of the coating. Chemical nickel-phosphorus coating can adhere to metals with and without coating layers. According to the requirements of the demander, the coating should be able to pass one or several adhesion tests specified in GB/T5270.
6) Porosity of the coating. If required, the maximum porosity of chemical nickel-phosphorus coating should be determined jointly according to the requirements of the demander and the test method for porosity.
7) Corrosion resistance of the coating. If required, the corrosion resistance of the coating and its test method should be specified by the demander according to the standard consistent with GB/T6461. The test methods of GB/T10125, acetic acid salt spray test, copper accelerated salt spray test, etc. can be specified as the test methods to evaluate the spot corrosion resistance of the coating.
8) Heat treatment to eliminate internal stress before plating. When the demander specifically indicates [see 4.1 b) in GB/T13913-2008], steel parts with a tensile strength greater than or equal to 1000 MPa, as well as parts containing tensile stress caused by processing, friction, straightening or cold processing, need to undergo heat treatment to eliminate internal stress before cleaning and depositing metal. The heat treatment process and type to eliminate internal stress shall be specially specified by the demander, or the demander shall select a suitable process and type according to GB/T19349. The heat treatment process to eliminate internal stress shall be carried out before any acid or cathodic electrolysis.
9) Heat treatment to eliminate hydrogen embrittlement after plating. Steel parts with a tensile strength greater than or equal to 1000 MPa, as well as parts that have undergone surface hardening treatment, need to undergo heat treatment to eliminate hydrogenation after plating according to GB/T19350 or the relevant process specified by the demander [see 4.1 b) in GB/T13913-2008].
All heat treatments to eliminate hydrogen embrittlement after plating should be carried out in a timely manner, preferably within 1 hour after surface finishing and before grinding and other machining, and should not exceed 3 hours at most.
The effectiveness of the hydrogen embrittlement elimination treatment should be determined through the test method specified by the demander or the test method described in the relevant standard. For example, ISO10587 describes a test method for hydrogen embrittlement of residual stress in threaded parts, while ISO15724 describes a test method for the concentration of diffused hydrogen in steel.
10) Heat treatment to improve coating hardness. The provisions for using heat treatment methods to provide the hardness (and wear resistance) of chemical nickel-phosphorus plating are shown in Table 1-135 [see Section 12 below].

(4) Information to be provided by the buyer to the manufacturer

1) Essential information. When the workpiece to be ordered requires coating according to the requirements of GB/T13993-2008 standard, the buyer should provide the following information in writing in the engineering drawing, buyer's order, and detailed production schedule for all important items:

a) Coating name.
b) Tensile strength of the part and any heat treatment requirements before and after coating deposition.

e) Location, type, and dimensions of defects.
f) Surface roughness requirements.

i) Standard methods and special test conditions for coating thickness, hardness, adhesion, porosity, corrosion resistance, wear resistance, and weldability testing.
j) Any special requirements for stress relief treatment, such as shot peening hardening before coating.
k) Special requirements for pretreatment or restrictions on pretreatment.
l) Special requirements for heat treatment or restrictions on heat treatment.
m) Special requirements for maximum coating thickness, especially for parts subject to wear or machining. These requirements must be strictly followed whether the thickness is measured before or after coating the part.

a) Steel parts should be demagnetized before coating to minimize the entry of magnetic particles or iron filings into the coating.
b) Final surface roughness of the coating.
c) Any special requirements for the chemical composition of the coating.

Chapter 2 Design of Hydraulic Cylinders and Their Components
2.1 Classification and Structure of Hydraulic Cylinders
2.1.1 Types and Classification of Hydraulic Cylinders

According to their purpose or task (function or effect), hydraulic cylinders provide mechanical energy for driving linear mechanical motion.

Further classification (subdivision) of hydraulic cylinders is very difficult. So far, only JB/T10205-2010 contains a clear classification. Other standards, such as JB/T21184-2007, list seven types of hydraulic cylinders; GB/T17746-2012 and GB/T17746-1998 (which has been superseded) define more than 20 types of hydraulic cylinders; GB/T9094-2006 stipulates 64 types of hydraulic cylinder mounting styles, etc.

GB/T13342-2007 stipulates that commonly used marine hydraulic cylinders have the following two types: plunger-type hydraulic cylinders and double-acting piston-type hydraulic cylinders. However, its scope of application should only be limited to marine reciprocating hydraulic cylinders, not all hydraulic cylinders.

JB/T12706.1-2016 stipulates round-head hydraulic cylinders and square-head hydraulic cylinders; JB/T12706.2-2017 stipulates compact square-head hydraulic cylinders.

Hydraulic cylinders can be classified by working method into two categories: single-acting cylinders and double-acting cylinders. Single-acting cylinders are cylinders where fluid can only act on the piston (or piston rod) in one direction; double-acting cylinders are cylinders where fluid force can be applied to the piston in two directions.

Hydraulic cylinders that have been defined in various standards (including superseded standards) are shown in Table 2-1.

Table 2-1 Hydraulic Cylinders Previously Defined in Various Standards

No. Name Definition
1 Adjustable stroke cylinder A cylinder whose stroke stop position can be changed to allow variation in stroke length
2 Cylinder with cushioning A cylinder with a cushioning device
3 Cylinder with non-rotatable piston rod A cylinder that prevents relative rotation between the cylinder body and piston rod
4 Diaphragm cylinder A cylinder where fluid acts on a diaphragm to generate mechanical force
5 Differential cylinder A double-acting cylinder where the effective areas on both sides of the piston are different. A double-acting cylinder where the ratio of effective areas at both ends of the piston plays a major role in the circuit
6 Double piston rod cylinder A cylinder with two mutually parallel-acting piston rods
7 Double-acting cylinder A cylinder where fluid force can be applied to the piston in two directions
8 Impact cylinder A double-acting cylinder with an integrally configured tank and valve seat, providing rapid acceleration for the piston and piston rod assembly during extension
9 Magnetic piston cylinder A cylinder with a permanent magnet on the piston, which can be used to operate a position sensor along the stroke length
10 Multiposition cylinder A cylinder that provides at least two separated positions in addition to the static position. At least two pistons are installed on the same axis moving within a common cylinder body, which is divided into several separately controlled chambers, allowing selection of different positions
11 Multiple rod cylinder A cylinder with more than one piston rod on different axes
12 Plunger cylinder A single-acting cylinder without a piston inside the cylinder barrel, where pressure acts directly on the piston rod
13 Servo cylinder A cylinder that can take a specific stroke position in response to a variable control signal
14 Single-acting cylinder A cylinder where fluid force can only act on the piston or piston rod in one direction
15 Single rod cylinder A cylinder that extends the piston rod from only one end
16 Tandem cylinder A cylinder where at least two pistons move in separated chambers of the same cylinder on the same piston rod

2.1.2 Basic Structure of Standard Hydraulic Cylinders

1. Model Representation Methods for Standard Hydraulic Cylinders

The model of a hydraulic cylinder usually consists of two parts, with the first part representing the name and structural characteristics, and the second part representing the pressure parameters, main parameters, and connection and installation methods. A third part can be added in the hydraulic cylinder model to represent other characteristics and detailed descriptions.

JB/T 2 1 8 4—2 0 0 7 stipulates that the main parameter of a hydraulic cylinder is the cylinder bore × stroke, with both units in mm; QC/T4 6 0—2 0 1 0 stipulates that the main parameter code of a hydraulic cylinder is expressed as bore × stroke, with both units in mm. The bore of a piston cylinder refers to the inner bore of the cylinder, the bore of a plunger cylinder refers to the plunger diameter, and the bore of a sleeve cylinder refers to the diameter of the first-stage sleeve extended, and the stroke refers to the total stroke.

2. Servo hydraulic cylinder model representation method
G B / T 3 2 2 1 6—2 0 1 5 is applicable to proportional/servo-controlled piston and plunger hydraulic cylinders using hydraulic oil as the working medium (hereinafter referred to as hydraulic cylinders or piston cylinders, plunger cylinders). Taking the piston cylinder as an example, its composition generally should include cylinder body (barrel), piston, piston rod, cylinder head, cylinder bottom, guide sleeve, sealing device, cushioning device, exhaust device, locking and anti-loosening device, built-in (type) or external (type) sensor, etc. If the electro-hydraulic servo valve is integrated on the piston cylinder, it should also include electro-hydraulic servo valve, manifold block and piping.
The model numbers of hydraulic components are uniformly formulated using Chinese phonetic letters and Arabic numerals. The servo hydraulic cylinder model is proposed to consist of three parts, with the front part indicating the name and structural characteristics of the servo hydraulic cylinder, the middle part indicating the parameters of the servo hydraulic cylinder, and the rear part indicating other characteristics and details of the servo hydraulic cylinder.
(1) Specific content of the front part of the servo hydraulic cylinder model
1) According to J B / T 2 1 8 4—2 0 0 7, the first part (number) uses Arabic numerals to indicate the number of piston rods of the servo hydraulic cylinder. For example, double rod servo hydraulic cylinder and constant velocity servo hydraulic cylinder use Arabic numeral "2" to indicate the number of piston rods, and the first number of single piston rod cylinder is omitted.
2) According to J B / T 2 1 8 4—2 0 0 7, the code D C※G is used to indicate the name of the servo hydraulic cylinder, with the specific meaning of electro-hydraulic servo control (D C)※ hydraulic cylinder (G). The specific meaning of ※ G can refer to the provisions of J B / T 2 1 8 4—2 0 0 7.
3) According to J B / T 2 1 8 4—2 0 0 7, for servo hydraulic cylinders integrated with electro-hydraulic servo valves, the composite element composed is indicated by the code D C, separated by a slash from the servo hydraulic cylinder code. If there is no electro-hydraulic servo valve, it is omitted.
4) Referring to the provisions of J B / T 2 1 8 4—2 0 0 7 on structural codes, the piston rod sealing type is used as the structural characteristic. The gap seal code is specified as 0 1, the seal (ring) seal code is 0 2, and the code for other seal types is 0 3, but the current formulation does not follow the order of servo hydraulic cylinder finalization.
(2) Specific content of the middle part of the servo hydraulic cylinder model
1) According to J B / T 2 1 8 4—2 0 0 7, the rated pressure or nominal pressure value of the servo hydraulic cylinder should generally comply with G B / T 2 3 4 6, and the code should follow J B / T 2 1 8 4—2 0 0 7, with special provision 2 1 M P a indicated by code F 1.
2) According to J B / T 2 1 8 4—2 0 0 7, the bore×stroke of the hydraulic cylinder is its main parameter. However, in the servo hydraulic cylinder numbering, the bore/piston rod diameter×maximum cylinder stroke value (Arabic numerals) is used to indicate, and it should generally comply with G B / T 2 3 4 8 and G B 2 3 4 9.
3) According to J B / T 2 1 8 4—2 0 0 7, the connection and installation method should be indicated by uppercase Chinese phonetic letters. However, in the servo hydraulic cylinder numbering, the installation code should generally follow G B / T 9 0 9 4—2 0 0 6, instead of J B / T 2 1 8 4—2 0 0 7.
(3) Specific content of other characteristics of the rear part of the servo hydraulic cylinder model
1) Referring to the provisions of J B / T 2 1 8 4—2 0 0 7 on the stroke end damping code, the code Z C is used to indicate that a fixed cushioning device is installed at the stroke end of the servo hydraulic cylinder, and the code Z T is used to indicate that an adjustable cushioning device is installed. If no cushioning device is installed at the stroke end of the servo hydraulic cylinder, it is omitted.
2) The Chinese phonetic letter N Z is used to indicate a servo hydraulic cylinder with a built-in (type) sensor, and the letter W Z is used to indicate a servo hydraulic cylinder with an external (type) sensor.

3. Hydraulic Cylinder Structural Features
(1) Hydraulic Cylinder Structural Features
In the first part of the hydraulic cylinder model composition, the first digit indicates the number of piston rods or the number of stages of a telescopic cylinder (omitted for single piston rod cylinders).
Hydraulic cylinders with the same name and main parameters but different structures are represented by sequential Arabic numerals based on the order of finalization. Generally including:
1) Cylinder end connection structure.
2) Piston structure and connection structure.
3) Piston rod structure.
4) Cylinder head structure.
5) Cylinder bottom structure.
6) Guide sleeve structure.
7) Sealing structure.
8) Cushioning structure.
9) Exhaust gas structure.
10) Locking and anti-loosening structure.
11) Connection and installation structure.
12) Oil port structure.
13) Other structures, such as travel (external extension) limit, positioning, adjustment, as well as integrated transmission, control, sensing, signal, medium pollution degree control, energy conversion and other components, accessories, assemblies or devices.
For hydraulic cylinders, its control mainly targets the working chamber (such as rodless and rod cavities) pressure, movable parts (such as pistons and piston rods) speed (including direction), cylinder stroke (such as maximum stroke and adjustable stroke) (or including direction) control; energy conversion includes gas-liquid and electro-hydraulic conversion.
More detailed structural features may also include material and mechanical properties, heat treatment, surface treatment, corrosion prevention, anti-pollution, etc.
