2.10 Design of hydraulic cylinder seals

2.10.1 Introduction to hydraulic cylinder seals

1. Leakage and sealing

A hydraulic cylinder is a special closed pressure vessel. It drives the piston (piston rod) to move relative to the cylinder body (tube) by changing the volume of the hydraulic working medium enclosed in the rodless cavity and/or rod cavity (taking a piston-type single piston rod double-acting hydraulic cylinder as an example), converting hydraulic energy into mechanical energy. The hydraulic working medium is under pressure, and sometimes the pressure can be very high, meaning there are ultra-high pressure hydraulic cylinders with a nominal pressure exceeding 32 MPa. Generally speaking, the higher the pressure of the hydraulic working medium, the more severe the leakage, and the more difficult the sealing. However, the pressure of the hydraulic working medium in low pressure (0～2.5 MPa) and medium pressure (2.5～8.0 MPa) should not be ignored. In practice, there have indeed been cases where hydraulic cylinders do not leak at high pressure (16.0～31.5 MPa) and ultra-high pressure (≥32 MPa), but leak at medium and low pressure. The leakage of hydraulic cylinders refers to the phenomenon of the hydraulic working medium flowing out from the high-pressure side to the low-pressure side across the boundary of the cavity. Leakage is generally divided into internal leakage and external leakage. For example, the hydraulic working medium in the rodless cavity of the hydraulic cylinder leaks to the rod cavity, or the hydraulic working medium in the rod cavity leaks to the rodless cavity, which is called internal leakage (inter-cavity); the leakage of the hydraulic working medium to the surrounding environment of the hydraulic cylinder is called external leakage, such as oil leakage at the weld of the bottom of the welded hydraulic cylinder, and oil on the extended piston rod, etc. GB/T17446-2012 defines leakage as the relative small amount of fluid flow that does not do useful work and causes energy loss.
171:
leakage, and defines external leakage as the leakage from the inside of a component or pipe to the surrounding environment. The main causes of hydraulic cylinder leakage are: (1) gaps between mating parts; (2) pressure differences (pressure) on both sides of the mating surfaces. Internal leakage affects the efficiency, speed, and cylinder travel and/or return output force of the hydraulic cylinder, and also causes further heating of the hydraulic working medium, which may lead to accidents; external leakage wastes the hydraulic working medium, pollutes the environment, and is prone to causing accidents. Therefore, for hydraulic cylinders, whether internal or external leakage exceeds the standard, it may be a very serious accident. Internal leakage (volume) and external leakage (volume) are mandatory inspection items for hydraulic cylinder factory testing. Please refer to JB/T 10205—2010 and GB/T 15622—2005 and other standards for details. The leakage of hydraulic cylinders is mainly leakage (through, bypassing).

Devices that can prevent or reduce leakage are generally called seals or sealing devices. A sealing device is a device composed of one or more sealing elements and supporting parts (such as retaining rings, springs, metal shells). The elements in the sealing device used to prevent leakage and/or prevent contaminants from entering are called sealing elements. Some also refer to sealing rings, retaining rings, guide rings (support rings), and dust rings as sealing elements (see MT/T11642011). The function of sealing is to seal the gaps between mating surfaces, cut off leakage channels or increase the resistance of leakage channels, so as to reduce or prevent leakage. The main indicators for measuring the quality of sealing performance are leakage rate (leakage volume/time or leakage volume/cumulative stroke, etc.), service life, and service conditions (pressure, speed, temperature, etc.). Now, due to the great progress in China's hydraulic cylinder sealing design standards and levels, processing technology and equipment, sealing element structural types and parameters, sealing (rubber and plastic, etc.) materials and additives, and testing, etc., the sealing performance of hydraulic cylinders has also been greatly improved. In short, the technical performance of hydraulic cylinders such as pressure, speed, temperature, product grade, service life (durability), and reliability largely depends on the sealing device (system) of the hydraulic cylinder and its design.

In addition to the above-mentioned meaning that sealing is a measure (behavior or practice, i.e., treatment method) to prevent or reduce leakage, "sealing" also has another meaning opposite to the phenomenon or state of leakage.

Author's note: 1. A super high-pressure hydraulic press is a hydraulic press with a working medium pressure not lower than 32 MPa. Please refer to GB/T8541—2012 for details. Hydraulic cylinders with a nominal pressure ≥32 MPa can also be called super high-pressure hydraulic cylinders.

2. "Sealing" is the antonym of "leakage", but "sealing" is not defined in GB/T17446—2012.

3. In GB/T50670—2011 "Terminology Standard for Mechanical Equipment Installation Engineering", the term "sealing" is defined, which is the general term for measures to prevent medium leakage.

2. Classification of Sealing

Sealing is divided into dynamic sealing and static sealing. In dynamic sealing, there is relative motion between the sealing mating (matching) parts; in static sealing, there is no (obvious) relative motion between the sealing mating (matching) parts. Due to these two different sealing working states, there are many differences in the requirements for sealing elements. In addition to bearing the pressure of the hydraulic working medium, dynamic sealing elements must also withstand friction and wear (or abrasion) caused by the relative motion of the mating parts; they must ensure a certain sealing performance and meet the requirements of various motion performances, including the support and guiding requirements of motion parts. According to whether the relative motion between the sealing mating parts is sliding or rotating, dynamic sealing is further divided into reciprocating (motion) sealing and rotary motion sealing. The sealing between the cylinder body (tube) and piston, and between the piston rod and guide sleeve in hydraulic cylinders are all reciprocating motion sealing. According to the contact relationship between the sealing element and the sealing surface of the mating parts, reciprocating motion sealing can be further divided into bore sealing (or outer diameter sealing, piston sealing) and shaft sealing (or inner diameter sealing, piston rod sealing). In bore sealing, the sealing element has relative motion with the bore; in shaft sealing, the sealing element has relative motion with the shaft, as shown in Figure 2-5. Static sealing can also be divided into plane static sealing (axial static sealing), cylindrical static sealing (radial static sealing), and angular static sealing (see Figure 2-6). Their leakage gaps are axial gaps and radial gaps.

According to whether the hydraulic working medium pressure acts on the inner or outer diameter of the sealing ring, axial static sealing is further divided into internal pressure and external pressure. The one where the hydraulic working medium may leak from inside to outside is called internal pressure axial static sealing (external flow type), and the one where the hydraulic working medium may leak from outside to inside is called external pressure axial static sealing (internal flow type), as shown in Figure 2-6a,b. Cylindrical static sealing (radial static sealing) refers to Figure 2-5.

According to the shape and sealing type of the sealing element, seals can be classified into molded packing (molded products or molded sealing elements) seals and rubber seals, belt seals, packing seals. Molded packing seals (elements) generally refer to annular sealing rings molded from materials such as rubber and plastic, such as O-ring rubber seals, Y-ring rubber seals, etc. They have a simple and compact structure, a wide variety of specifications, a wide range of working parameters, and convenient installation and use.

Dynamic seals can also be classified into contact and non-contact seals according to the contact type of the mating surfaces of the mating parts. Contact seals rely on the sealing element being tightly attached to the sealing surface of the mating part under the action of forced pressure, with the sealing surface and the sealing element being in a state of frictional contact separated by only a very thin layer of hydraulic medium. This sealing method has good sealing performance, but is limited by friction and wear conditions, so the relative moving speed of the sealing surface cannot be too high, and most reciprocating dynamic seals in hydraulic components belong to this type. Contact seals can be further divided into compression seals and pressure-energized seals. Compression seals rely on squeezing the sealing packing installed in the sealing groove to make it expand radially and press tightly on the shaft or hole to achieve sealing; pressure-energized seals are a type of seal with self-sealing ability, and O-ring rubber seals, Y-ring seals, etc. in molded seals all belong to this type of seal. The working principle of these seals is to install the seal ring into the sealing groove and assemble it with the mating part, so that the seal element applies a pre-pressure to the mating part through elastic deformation. When the seal element is subjected to the pressure of the sealing working medium in one direction, the seal element is further deformed, and the contact pressure (stress) of the sealing surface (line) increases to adapt to the increase in the pressure of the sealing working medium, ensuring sealing. Pressure-energized seals can be divided into two categories: extrusion type and lip type. The representative of the extrusion type is the O-ring rubber seal, and the representative of the lip type is the Y-ring seal. Non-contact seals are a type of clearance seal, such as piston clearance seal. Since there is no contact and friction between the sealing mating surfaces, this type of seal has small friction and wear, low starting pressure, and long service life, but its sealing performance is poor.

According to the role of the sealing element in the sealing device, there are main seals and auxiliary seals. The role of auxiliary seals is to protect the main sealing element from damage, extend the service life of the main sealing element, and improve its sealing performance, such as dust seals, retaining rings, buffer rings, and anti-pollution protection rings.

In addition, sealing elements can also be classified according to the sealing working medium, sealing material, the different pressure of the sealed working medium, etc.

(1) Molded Extruded Seals
Among extruded seals, rubber extruded seals are the most widely used and have the most types. Others found in samples from various seal manufacturers include angle-O rubber seals, square rectangular rubber seals, triangular rubber seals, T-type rubber seals, heart-shaped rubber seals, dumbbell-shaped rubber seals, and polygonal rubber seals.

1) O-ring rubber seals.
① A rubber seal with an O-shaped cross-section. O-ring rubber seals are generally made of synthetic rubber through molding and are a type of rubber sealing component with a cross-sectional shape of O in natural state (or called a rubber seal ring with a circular cross-section). O-ring rubber seals (hereinafter referred to as O-rings) have good sealing performance and can be used in static or dynamic conditions. They can be used alone, capable of sealing bidirectional fluid; their structure is simple, compact in size, easy to install and disassemble, and have low technical requirements for installation; when there is wear on the working surface, high pressure and/or large gaps require the use of (installing) retaining rings to prevent extrusion damage; O-rings can form seals on their inner diameter, end face, or other arbitrary surfaces during operation. Therefore, their applicable working parameter range is wide, and the working pressure can reach 261 in static conditions.
174:
6.3 MPa or higher (referenced literature mentions it can reach 200 MPa), and can reach 35 MPa under reciprocating motion conditions; with different sealing material selections, the working temperature range is -60~200°C; the linear velocity can reach 3 m/s (generally limited to below 0.5 m/s); the shaft diameter can reach 3000 mm.

When O-rings are used as reciprocating motion seals, they have the disadvantages of large starting friction resistance and being prone to twisting and rolling, especially when used in cases of uneven gaps, large eccentricity, and high reciprocating motion speeds, they are more likely to twist and break. As the coupling's diameter (inner diameter) increases, the tendency to twist also increases. Therefore, O-rings used for dynamic sealing are only reasonable when used in light load conditions or internal (piston seal) reciprocating dynamic sealing. Specifically, it is more suitable for applications with small diameter pistons, short strokes, and medium-low pressure conditions.

O-rings can also be used for low-speed rotating motion and short running cycle swing shaft seals.

② Non-standard cross-section rubber O-rings. Other special cross-sectional shapes different from O-ring cross-sections, which are extrusion-type sealing rings, or can be called non-standard cross-section O-rings. The commonly used ones are X-rings, also known as star rings.

The development and use of non-standard cross-section O-rings are mainly to overcome the disadvantages of O-rings, such as rolling, twisting, and large starting friction force. Taking the 4-lip X-ring as an example, compared with O-rings, since two of the sealing lips that contact the moving surface in the X-ring can form a lubrication cavity, it has smaller friction resistance and starting resistance. Since the parting surface of the molding die is opened at the concave part of the cross-section (similar principle to the 45° parting surface O-ring), the sealing effect is good. Its non-circular cross-section can avoid rolling during reciprocating motion, and there are now series of products that can generally be used in standard O-ring sealing grooves. Based on the above characteristics of X, X-rings are mainly used for dynamic sealing, but can also be used for static sealing, such as their application in low-leakage coaxial sealing components. In addition to X-rings and dumbbell-shaped rings, which will be introduced in detail later, other non-standard cross-section O-rings are rarely actually used on hydraulic cylinders, so only some simple introductions are provided below.

a. Square (rectangular) ring: It is easy to form, difficult to install, has poor sealing performance, and large friction resistance, and is often used as a static sealing component. But there is one special case, which is the use of hydraulic cylinder seals in automotive disc-type hydraulic brakes.

b. D-ring: It is stable in position during work, suitable for bidirectional sealing alternating pressure conditions, and mainly used for reciprocating motion seals. High pressure may cause seal failure due to extrusion damage.

c. Triangular ring: It is stable in position during work, but has relatively large friction resistance, short service life, and is generally only suitable for special-purpose seals.

d. T-ring: It is stable in position during work, resistant to vibration, has small friction resistance, and can achieve sealing with a 5% groove compression rate, generally used in medium-low pressure and vibration conditions. High pressure may cause extrusion damage.

e. Heart-shaped ring: Its cross-section is similar to that of an O-ring, but its friction coefficient is smaller than that of an O-ring, and it is generally suitable for sealing low-pressure rotating shafts.

f. X-ring: It resembles two O-rings, has four protruding sealing parts in the cross-section, is stable in position in the groove, has small friction resistance, can achieve sealing with a 1% groove compression rate, and allows a higher working linear speed. It can be used for sealing shafts with rotating and reciprocating motion that require low friction resistance. X-rings can also be used for static sealing, but are mainly used for dynamic sealing.

g. Corner-O-ring: It resembles three O-rings, has three protruding parts, the two protruding parts on the outside are higher, making it stable in position in the groove and having a large compression rate. Referenced literature mentions that its working pressure can reach 210 MPa.

Author's note: The above "can reach 210 MPa" expression is mentioned in both reference [46] and its previous edition, but the author has not conducted practical machine testing.

h. Dumbbell-shaped ring: It can replace O-rings with retaining rings for static sealing, is very resistant to extrusion and twisting, has a long service life, and the maximum working pressure can reach 50 MPa. It is suitable for working conditions with pressure pulsation and contamination intrusion, and is used on hydraulic cylinders of construction machinery, etc., and its application is becoming more and more widespread.

i. Polygonal ring: Its friction resistance is smaller than that of an O-ring, and its leakage is also less than that of an O-ring. The working pressure can reach 14 MPa, and it is used for plunger seals of hydraulic cylinders.

2) Non-rubber O-ring seals. Common non-rubber material O-rings are PTFE O-rings (including PTFE-coated O-rings) and stainless steel hollow tube O-rings. Due to the characteristics of PTFE that are not possessed by other materials, such as a wide working temperature range, strong resistance to working media, and low friction coefficient, it is also made into O-rings for use in some special occasions. The elasticity of PTFE is inferior to that of rubber. When using standard O-ring sealing grooves, it is necessary to redesign and test. Generally, the compression rate should not exceed 7%, and it is mainly used for static sealing.

3) Coaxial sealing components. It is a combined sealing assembly, whose characteristics are to obtain a compact, low-friction, lightweight, and long-life sealing assembly by combining sealing components of different materials and different functions. General coaxial sealing components are composed of plastic sliding rings and rubber elastic bodies, so this combined sealing component is also defined as a sliding ring combined seal. Since the sliding ring is made of materials with low friction coefficient or self-lubricating plastic, it has the above advantages. Its disadvantages are that the leakage is generally larger than that of lip seals, installation is more difficult, and special tools and specified process methods are often required for installation.

① National standard parts I. G B/T15242.1-2017 specifies three types of coaxial sealing components: square for holes, combined for holes, and stepped for shafts, which are suitable for dynamic sealing of reciprocating motion of hydraulic cylinder pistons and piston rods using water-based or oil-based transmission media.

The replaced standard G B/T15242.1-1994 stipulates: It is suitable for reciprocating motion hydraulic cylinder pistons and piston rods (plungers) with hydraulic oil as the working medium, working pressure ≤40 MPa, speed ≤5 m/s, and temperature range -40~200°C.

b. Combined coaxial seal for holes. It is a piston combination seal composed of a sealing ring, a mountain-shaped elastomer, and two retaining rings.

c. Stepped coaxial seal for shafts. It is a piston rod combination seal with stepped cross-section of the sealing ring and O-ring as the elastomer.

b. Toothed multi-piece combined ring. It is a coaxial seal composed of multiple plastic rings and rubber parts with sawtooth-shaped cross-sections, with the middle plastic ring serving as the friction sealing surface. It only has a definition but no product standard.

4) Bidirectional sealing rubber seals. GB/T10708.2—2000 specifies bidirectional sealing rubber seals for reciprocating motion (bellows rubber seals and mountain-shaped rubber seals) and their plastic support rings.

GB/T36520.1—2018 also specifies single-body bidirectional seals (single-body bellows seals and single-body mountain-shaped seals) and sealing structural types. However, it lacks the types and dimensions of plastic supports.

It is worth noting that the friction sealing surfaces of bellows rubber seals and mountain-shaped rubber seals are both rubber, not (plastic) sealing rings. Their sealing principle is similar to that of special-shaped cross-section O-rings.

(2) Lip-shaped rubber seals

Lip-shaped rubber seals have at least one flexible sealing (dust-proof) protrusion, and the pressure of the fluid on one side of the lip keeps it in close contact with the mating surface on the other side to form a seal. More directly described as: in their cross-sectional profiles, they all contain one or more angular so-called lips (or edges) with waists. Lip-shaped rubber seals named according to their (transverse) cross-sectional shapes include: Y-shaped rubber seals, Yx-shaped rubber seals, V-shaped rubber seals, U-shaped rubber seals, L-shaped rubber seals, J-shaped rubber seals, etc., among which Yx is not defined in the standard GB/T5719.

GB/T36520.1—2018 and GB/T36520.2—2018, issued on 2018-07-13 and implemented on 2019-02-01, respectively specify single-body Y×D seals and single-body Y×d seals.

Furthermore, some rubber dust seals can also be classified as lip-shaped rubber seals.

1) Y-shaped rubber seals. Y-shaped rubber seals (hereinafter referred to as Y-shaped seals) include equal-height lip Y-shaped seals and unequal-height lip (high-low lip) Y-shaped seals; according to their cross-sectional width (different proportions of cross-sectional height and width), there are also wide-section Y-shaped seals and narrow-section Y-shaped seals. Generally, the equal-height lip wide-section Y-shaped seal is simply called a Y-shaped seal; the equal-height lip narrow-section Y-shaped seal is called an EY-shaped seal.

The Y-shaped seal is a one-way seal. The equal-height lip Y-shaped seal is universal for shafts and holes, and there are also two types of shaft and hole types like the unequal-height lip Y-shaped seal. Although the cross-sectional shapes of the equal-height lip Y-shaped seals for shafts and holes are not much different, they are indeed divided into shaft and hole types, such as the piston Y-shaped seal. The equal-height lip Y-shaped seal for holes is marked as Y80×65×9.5; the piston rod Y-shaped seal, the equal-height lip Y-shaped seal for shafts, is marked as Y70×85×9.5, which can be found in GB/T10708.1.

The service life and sealing performance of the Y-shaped seal are both higher than those of the O-ring. Since the lip of the Y-shaped seal is wider than that of the single V-shaped seal, its sealing performance is better. The static and dynamic friction forces of the Y-shaped seal change little, and in hydraulic cylinders 461 Hydraulic Cylinder Manual.

The most commonly used reciprocating motion sealing device in sealing systems. However, since it is a one-way seal, if it is used in situations where pistons require two-way sealing, a pair of Y-rings must be used, which increases the axial size and also makes installation difficult, and sometimes it is necessary to make the groove in a split (open) form.

The characteristics of the Y-ring are that a single seal ring can only achieve one-way sealing, and it can be used under more demanding working conditions. When the reciprocating motion speed is 0.5 m/s and the gap f is 0.2 mm, the working pressure range is 0-15 MPa; when the gap is 0.1 mm, the working pressure range is 0-20 MPa; when the reciprocating motion speed is 0.15 m/s and the gap is 0.2 mm, the working pressure range is 0-20 MPa; when the gap is 0.1 mm, the working pressure range is 0-25 MPa. Generally, the sealing materials used to manufacture Y-rings are nitrile rubber, polyurethane rubber, and fluorine rubber. Y-rings made of these three sealing materials can be used without problems in the temperature range of -20-80°C.

Regarding whether the Y-ring needs to be equipped with a support ring and a retaining ring, GB/T10708.1-2000 does not mention it, but some reference materials introduce that when the pressure fluctuates greatly, an equal-height lip Y-ring needs to use a support ring, while an unequal-height lip Y-ring does not need to use a support ring. When the Y-ring made of nitrile rubber is used, when the working pressure is 14-31.5 MPa, a Y-ring made of polyurethane rubber is used; when the working pressure is >31.5-70 MPa, a retaining ring must be used. The author has no experience in using a support ring for Y-rings, but has practical experience in using a retaining ring, that is, it is decided whether to install a retaining ring according to the conditions for using a retaining ring for Yx-rings, that is, when the working pressure is >16 MPa, it is advisable to install a retaining ring; when the working pressure is >25 MPa, a retaining ring must be installed, and the actual effect is very good.

2) Yx sealing ring. The Yx sealing ring (hereinafter referred to as Yx ring) is also a lip-shaped rubber sealing ring, which is divided into shaft type and hole type, and has the following standards: JB/ZQ4265-2006 "Shaft Yx Sealing Ring" and JB/ZQ4264-2006 "Hole Yx Sealing Ring". These two standards respectively stipulate the type, size and limit deviation of the Yx ring sealing groove. The Yx ring is used under the conditions of temperature -20-80°C and working pressure ≤31.5 MPa.

The cross-sectional height of the Yx ring is 1 times or more larger than its thickness. When used, it is not easy to flip over in the groove, and even when the working pressure and motion speed change greatly, it does not need to be equipped with a support ring. Generally, no retaining ring is provided when using the Yx ring. When the working pressure is >16 MPa, or when the motion pair has a large eccentricity and a large gap, a retaining ring can be placed on the support surface of the sealing ring. It should be noted that some reference materials say that the groove specified in the standard GB/T2879-2005 is the groove specified for the use of Yx rings, which is incorrect.

3) Monolithic Y×D sealing ring and monolithic Y×d sealing ring. The monolithic Y×D sealing ring and monolithic Y×d sealing ring respectively specified in GB/T36520.1-2018 and GB/T36520.2-2018 are lip-shaped polyurethane rubber sealing rings. It is suitable for reciprocating speed of 0.5 m/s, maximum working pressure of 35 MPa, use temperature of -40-80°C, and engineering cylinders with mineral oil as the working medium.

4) V-shaped rubber sealing ring. The V-shaped rubber sealing ring (hereinafter referred to as V-ring) is a typical form of lip-shaped rubber sealing ring, and it is also the earliest and most widely used lip-shaped rubber sealing ring. According to the terms defined in GB/T17446-2012, it is now classified as a packing seal. Its characteristics are good pressure resistance and wear resistance, and it can be overlapped and used according to the pressure, but the disadvantage is that it is large in size, has high friction resistance, and must use a split (open) type sealing groove, and the length of the sealing groove is generally adjustable. On hydraulic cylinders, it is mainly used for reciprocating motion sealing of pistons and piston rods, which can seal holes (piston sealing) and shafts (piston rod sealing), but it is rarely used for rotary sealing and static sealing. V-rings are rarely used alone, and they are usually stacked with pressure rings and elastic sealing rings or support rings, called V-shaped combination sealing rings. In specific use, usually 1-6 V-rings are stacked together with pressure rings and support rings (or elastic sealing rings) to form a V-shaped combination sealing ring, forming one or more seals, with a very good sealing effect. The working pressure of such a V-shaped combination sealing ring can reach 60 MPa or higher. The working pressure of the V-ring is: rubber V-ring is generally 31.5 MPa, and the cloth-rubber V-ring can reach 60 MPa or higher; the working temperature range is -30-100°C, or higher.

5) U-shaped rubber sealing ring. The U-shaped rubber sealing ring (hereinafter referred to as U-ring) is one of the most widely used sealing rings in hydraulic cylinder sealing. It is also a lip-shaped rubber sealing ring. Whether it is used for piston or piston rod sealing, it can achieve good sealing effect.

Before July 13, 2018, there was no U-ring in the current domestic sealing standard, but there was a U-ring definition in GB/T5719-2006, while foreign sealing manufacturers' product samples rarely saw Y-rings. Like Y-rings, U-rings also have equal-height lips and unequal-height lips. Generally, equal-height lip U-rings are universal for shafts and holes, that is, they can be used for piston sealing or piston rod sealing; unequal-height lip U-rings are divided into piston sealing and piston rod sealing.

In order to improve the lubrication conditions, reduce the friction force, and increase the service life, there is also a so-called double-lip U-ring (the author believes it should be called double-sealed U-ring). In order to improve the extrusion resistance of the U-ring, there are also U-rings with plastic retaining rings embedded in the bottom of the U-ring, as well as U-rings with both double lips and plastic retaining rings embedded.

The U-ring is a rubber sealing ring with a U-shaped cross section. An O-ring or other shaped elastomer (rubber) is embedded in the U-shape to form another form of U-ring. This U-ring has better performance in sealing low-temperature and low-pressure working media, is impact-resistant, high-pressure resistant, and has stable sealing performance. This manual classifies it as a non-typical U-ring, or a (pre-)loaded U-ring.

4. Operating Conditions for Hydraulic Cylinders
The operating conditions for hydraulic cylinders generally refer to the situation of driving external loads, as well as the working medium and environment. The operating conditions for hydraulic cylinders can generally be divided into light load, medium load, and heavy load.
The hydraulic cylinder and its seals are designed according to the specified operating conditions and should meet the specified conditions. The specified operating conditions for hydraulic cylinders refer to the conditions that the hydraulic cylinder must satisfy during operation and testing. Therefore, the operating conditions for hydraulic cylinders are only a part of the specified operating conditions.
For the design of hydraulic cylinder seals using hydraulic oil, it is necessary to first clarify the pressure, temperature, speed, stroke, and their ranges that the sealing system should be suitable for.

2.10.2 General Technical Requirements for Hydraulic Cylinder Sealing
1. Overview
One meaning of hydraulic cylinder sealing refers to the hydraulic cylinder sealing device, which is one of the important components of a hydraulic cylinder, used to seal all reciprocating motion areas (dynamic sealing) and connection areas (static sealing). Generally, it includes piston seal, piston rod seal, seal between cylinder body (tube) components, seal between piston and piston rod components, seal at port connections, etc. The hydraulic cylinder sealing device also typically includes dust (seal) protection for piston rods, and guidance and support for pistons and piston rods.

Another meaning of hydraulic cylinder sealing is relative to hydraulic cylinder leakage, expressing a meaning opposite to the phenomenon or state of leakage.

Hydraulic cylinder leakage refers to the phenomenon of hydraulic working medium flowing from the high-pressure side to the low-pressure side through the cavity boundary. Leakage is divided into internal leakage and external leakage.

In current hydraulic cylinder standards, the technical requirements for hydraulic cylinder sealing are an important component, and the design and manufacture of hydraulic cylinders must meet these technical requirements.
184:
Some technical requirements. The technical requirements for hydraulic cylinder seals listed in Table 2-67 vary in their expressions, but mainly concern the requirements for static and dynamic sealing performance of hydraulic cylinders.

Under specified conditions, the pressure resistance of hydraulic cylinder seals includes high-pressure resistance, low-pressure resistance, durability, and other performance related to hydraulic cylinder seals, such as starting pressure, minimum speed, and maximum speed. Generally, these must be ensured in hydraulic cylinder design and manufacturing, and for servo hydraulic cylinders, these indicators are also very important.

For the various hydraulic cylinder standards listed in Table 2-67, there are unreasonable or incorrect technical requirements, such as external leakage indicators, minimum speed requirements, and test pressure (nominal pressure or rated pressure) determination, etc. Please note these when determining the technical requirements (conditions) for hydraulic cylinder seals, and you may further refer to reference [102], etc.

GB/T13342-2007 "Technical Conditions for Marine Reciprocating Hydraulic Cylinders"

1) The seals in the hydraulic cylinder should be able to withstand high temperature, corrosion, aging, hydrolysis, and have good sealing performance, satisfying both the sealing of the oil and the requirements of the marine atmospheric environment.

2) The design and manufacturing of various seals and grooves should meet the following requirements:

a) The dimensions of O-ring rubber seals should comply with GB/T3452.1.

b) The appearance of O-ring rubber seals should comply with GB/T3452.2.

c) The groove dimensions for O-ring rubber seals should comply with GB/T3452.3.

d) The groove dimensions and tolerances for dynamic sealing of hydraulic cylinder pistons and piston rods should comply with GB/T2879.

e) The groove size series and tolerances for narrow-section dynamic sealing of hydraulic cylinder pistons and piston rods should comply with GB2880.

f) The groove type, dimensions, and tolerances for piston seals with support rings in hydraulic cylinders should comply with GB/T6577.

g) The groove type, dimensions, and tolerances for dust seals for hydraulic cylinder piston rods should comply with GB/T6578.

h) Other types of seals and grooves should preferably adopt national standards, and the selected seal models should be certified products.

3) For hydraulic cylinders not used for lifting purposes, it is recommended to use a sealing structure with a support ring and dynamic seal, and the support material is recommended to be filled bronze powder PTFE or long-chain molecular reinforced polyoxymethylene.

4) For hydraulic cylinders used for lifting purposes, where oil leakage in the oil chamber may cause the weight to descend, the dynamic seal is recommended to use a rubber-coated fabric V-ring seal.

5) When the ambient temperature is -25 to 65°C, the hydraulic cylinder should be able to work normally.

The so-called normal working (state) refers to the working (state) of the hydraulic cylinder under specified working conditions, where the changes in its various performance parameters (values) are within the predetermined range.

6) When the working medium temperature is -15°C, the hydraulic cylinder should have no sticking phenomenon.

7) When the working medium temperature is +70°C, there should be no leakage at the joints of the hydraulic cylinder.

8) Under 1.5 times the nominal pressure, no damage or permanent deformation should occur in all parts of the hydraulic cylinder, and no leakage should occur in the gaskets and welds.

9) Under 1.25 times the nominal pressure, the internal leakage between the cylinder barrel and the piston should comply with the specified value, as detailed in Table 2-159.

10) The internal leakage of a double-acting piston hydraulic cylinder should not exceed the specified value, as detailed in Table 2-159.

11) There should be no (external) leakage at the seals and during movement of the hydraulic cylinder.

12) For a double-acting piston hydraulic cylinder, after 50,000 reciprocating movements of the piston, the external leakage at the piston rod should not form droplets. After 50,000 reciprocating movements, when the piston moves 100 mm, if the piston rod diameter d ≤ 50 mm, the external leakage should not exceed 0.01 mL; if the piston rod diameter d > 50 mm, the external leakage should not exceed 0.002d mL.

13) For a plunger hydraulic cylinder, after 25,000 reciprocating movements of the plunger, the external leakage at the plunger rod should not form droplets. After 25,000 reciprocating movements, when the plunger moves 100 mm, if the plunger rod diameter d ≤ 50 mm, the external leakage should not exceed 0.01 mL/min; if the plunger rod diameter d > 50 mm, the external leakage should not exceed 0.002d mL.

14) The minimum starting pressure for a plunger hydraulic cylinder should not exceed the values specified in Table 2-67-1.

2. Y-shaped rubber seal rings and their grooves
(1) Sealing mechanism, classification and characteristics of Y-ring
1) Sealing mechanism of Y-ring. As shown in Figure 2-21, the natural state of Y-ring is that the sealing lip is open, and the lip part is large; after being installed into the sealing groove, the lip part becomes smaller, and the lip part is attached to the sealing surface, but the contact force is very small; when the sealed working medium is filled into the lip part, with the increase of pressure, the lip part and the sealing surface contact becomes wider, and the contact force increases, which is also the self-sealing ability of Y-ring mentioned earlier: that is, with the increase of the pressure of the sealed working medium, the sealing ability also increases accordingly. But it does not mean that the working pressure can be increased infinitely, generally the maximum working pressure of Y-ring does not exceed 25 MPa. With the increase of pressure, the friction force and wear are also increasing.
2) Classification of Y-ring. As shown in Figure 2-22, GB/T 10708.1-2000 "Rubber seal rings for reciprocating motion - Part 1: One-way seal rubber seal rings" specifies two types of Y-rings for L1 sealing grooves, namely the piston L1 sealing groove shown in Figure 2-22a and the rod L1 sealing groove shown in Figure 2-22b.
219:
Figure 2-21 Y-ring seal
Use Y-ring for the groove shown in Figure 2-22b for piston rod with L1 seal groove; Y-ring for the groove shown in Figure 2-22c for piston with L2 seal groove; Y-ring for the groove shown in Figure 2-22d for piston rod with L2 seal groove. Y-ring for L1 seal groove is an equal-lip Y-ring, while Y-ring for L2 seal groove is an unequal-lip Y-ring.
(3) Characteristics of Y-ring. Compared with O-ring, the most significant feature of Y-ring is its small starting friction, and its service life and sealing performance are also higher than those of O-ring. Compared with V-ring, its friction is smaller than that of V-ring, and its sealing is better than that of V-ring. In summary, Y-ring has the following characteristics:
a) Y-ring for piston L1 seal groove  b) Y-ring for piston rod L1 seal groove
c) Y-ring for piston L2 seal groove  d) Y-ring for piston rod L2 seal groove
Figure 2-22 Structure types of Y-ring
a) Y-ring for piston L1 seal groove  b) Y-ring for piston rod L1 seal groove
c) Y-ring for piston L2 seal groove  d) Y-ring for piston rod L2 seal groove
① Good sealing performance, reliable sealing.
② Small static friction resistance, smooth starting.
③ Good pressure resistance, wide range of operating pressures.
④ Simple installation with rectangular groove.
(2) Sealing design of Y-ring
The sealing design of Y-ring is mainly the design of sealing groove. According to the working conditions and structural requirements, choose whether to use Y-ring for L1 seal groove or Y-ring for L2 seal groove, and whether to use retaining ring. In practice, Y-ring for L2 seal groove is used more often. There are no relevant standards for Y-ring for L1 and L2 seal grooves with retaining ring, and there are no corresponding standards for Y-ring grooves with retaining ring. Figure 2-23 shows the groove structure type of Y-ring with retaining ring, and the corresponding dimensions are shown in Tables 2-81 to 2-84.
3. Yx rubber sealing ring and its groove
(1) Yx ring and its characteristics
Yx ring is an unequal-lip narrow-section (cut) lip seal ring, which has been introduced before and will not be repeated here. Its sealing mechanism is the same as that of Y-ring.
(2) Sealing design of Yx ring
Since there are standards JB/ZQ4264-2006 "Yx seal ring for hole" and JB/ZQ4265-2006 "Yx seal ring for shaft", in the sealing design of Yx ring, as long as the sealing material of the sealing ring is selected correctly, the requirements of working medium, working temperature, working pressure and speed are met, and it is decided whether to install a retaining ring, the sealing groove can be designed according to the standard. The hole-type Yx seal ring has the following mark at the bottom: YxD50, which is the nominal outer diameter (cylinder inner diameter) D=50mm hole-type Yx seal ring, that is, the Yx seal ring used for piston seal. The shaft-type Yx seal ring has the following mark at the bottom: Yx d50, which is the nominal inner diameter (piston rod diameter) d=50mm shaft-type Yx seal ring, that is, the Yx seal ring used for piston rod seal.
The types of Yx ring and its groove are shown in Figure 2-24 and Figure 2-25. The groove dimensions of hole-type Yx seal ring are shown in Table 2-85.

5. V-shaped rubber sealing rings and their grooves

(1) Sealing mechanism of V-shaped rubber sealing rings
V-shaped rubber sealing rings are also a type of lip seal. Their cross-section is V-shaped (or the cross-section is in the shape of the letter V, hereinafter referred to as V-ring), as shown in Figure 2-28.

V-rings generally cannot be used alone; they must be used together with at least three components: a pressure ring and a support ring (or an elastic sealing ring) to form a combined seal, i.e., a V-shaped combined sealing ring. The included angle of V-rings is generally made 90°, with special cases at 60°. The pressure ring and support ring are also made 90° or slightly larger. Taking a V-ring for piston rod sealing as an example, when the V-ring is in its free state, its outer diameter is larger than the inner diameter of the sealing groove, and its inner diameter is smaller than the piston rod diameter. When the three components are assembled together and installed into the sealing groove, the V-ring undergoes initial deformation. Due to the action of the support ring, this deformation only occurs in the lip portion of the V-ring, generating pressure at the contact points. Even without applying pressure, the lip of the V-ring can seal the working medium with a certain pressure. This is the "self-sealing" effect possessed by V-rings.

When the pressure of the working medium being sealed increases, the lip portion changes its contact shape and increases the contact stress. The lip portion and the contact surface贴合得更紧密，使密封圈与密封面的接触面积增加，提高了密封效果。

2. 密封沟槽的设计

(1) 密封圈的沟槽尺寸

密封圈的沟槽尺寸是根据密封圈的尺寸和公差来确定的。一般情况下，沟槽的尺寸应略大于密封圈的尺寸，以便于安装和拆卸。但沟槽的尺寸也不能过大，否则会影响密封效果。

(2) 密封圈的安装

密封圈的安装是保证密封效果的关键步骤。安装时应注意以下几点：

1) 密封圈的安装方向应正确，不要装反。

2) 密封圈的安装位置应准确，不要偏离中心。

3) 密封圈的安装应平整，不要扭曲或变形。

4) 密封圈的安装应牢固，不要松动或脱落。

5) 密封圈的安装应清洁，不要有杂质或污物。

6) 密封圈的安装应轻柔，不要用力过猛或损坏密封圈。

7) 密封圈的安装应按顺序进行，不要遗漏或重复。

8) 密封圈的安装应检查合格后方可使用。

(3) 密封圈的维护

密封圈的维护是保证密封效果和使用寿命的重要措施。维护时应注意以下几点：

1) 定期检查密封圈的磨损情况，及时更换磨损严重的密封圈。

2) 定期清洁密封圈的表面，保持密封圈的清洁。

3) 定期检查密封圈的安装情况，及时调整或更换安装不当的密封圈。

4) 定期检查密封圈的工作环境，避免密封圈受到高温、高压、腐蚀等恶劣环境的影响。

5) 定期检查密封圈的密封效果，及时发现和解决密封失效的问题。

6) 定期检查密封圈的储存情况，避免密封圈受潮、变形或老化。

7) 定期检查密封圈的配套件，如沟槽、轴、孔等，确保其尺寸和质量符合要求。

8) 定期检查密封圈的使用记录，了解密封圈的使用情况和寿命，为下次更换提供参考。

(4) 密封圈的选择

密封圈的选择是保证密封效果和使用寿命的基础。选择时应考虑以下因素：

1) 工作介质的性质，如液体、气体、固体等。

2) 工作介质的温度、压力、流量等参数。

3) 工作环境的温度、湿度、腐蚀性等条件。

4) 密封圈的材质、硬度、弹性等性能。

5) 密封圈的尺寸、形状、结构等特点。

6) 密封圈的使用寿命、维护成本等经济因素。

7) 密封圈的密封效果、可靠性等技术因素。

8) 密封圈的安装、拆卸、更换等操作因素。

9) 密封圈的环保、安全等社会因素。

10) 密封圈的标准、规范、认证等法律因素。

根据以上因素，选择合适的密封圈，以满足实际工作的需要。

When the pressure of the working medium is very high, several V-rings can be stacked together for combined use. Through the pressing of a set of V-rings by the pressure ring and support ring, their sealing capacity can be enhanced, and it can even reach 60 MPa or higher. The reason for the enhanced sealing capacity is that the working medium will be depressurized every time it passes through each V-ring until the leakage is prevented. After being pressed tightly, 3 to 4 V-rings can seal the ultra-high pressure of 60 MPa. The standard has a maximum of 6 V-rings stacked together as a group.
The V-ring is a one-way seal ring, and its V-ring notch end must face the high-pressure side. When used for the piston seal of a double-acting hydraulic cylinder, since two sets of V-rings must be arranged symmetrically, the length of the piston becomes too long, and the friction force also increases greatly. It is also relatively troublesome that the pressing force of the V-ring is not easy (able) to be adjusted, and only an elastic seal ring is used to apply the pressing force. The friction force of the V-ring seal is greater than that of other seals. The minimum starting pressure reflected on the hydraulic cylinder is also large. In the JB/T10205-2010 "Hydraulic Cylinder" standard, for double-acting hydraulic cylinders with V-ring (combination) seal (both piston and piston rod seals are V-rings) with a nominal pressure ≤16 MPa, the minimum starting pressure is not allowed to be greater than 0.75 MPa; while for double-acting hydraulic cylinders with other seals, the minimum starting pressure is not allowed to be greater than 0.3 MPa. For double-acting hydraulic cylinders with a nominal pressure >16 MPa and V-ring (combination) seal (both piston and piston rod seals are V-rings), the minimum starting pressure is not allowed to be greater than 9% of the nominal pressure; while for double-acting hydraulic cylinders with other seals, the minimum starting pressure is not allowed to be greater than 6% of the nominal pressure.
The material for manufacturing V-rings is most commonly nitrile rubber, and there are also those using cloth-reinforced rubber. Among them, cloth-reinforced fluorine rubber can be used for high temperature or other media (it should be checked according to the working medium when in use). The materials for manufacturing pressure rings and support rings (elastic seal rings) are generally cloth-reinforced rubber, and there are also those using plastics and metals, but now few people make them by themselves, and there is no need to do so.
(2) Use and characteristics of V-ring seal
The V-ring was used earlier, but now it is used less. It is used on some agricultural plunger pumps because its lubrication is poor (water, pesticides or liquid fertilizers, etc.). It is occasionally used on hydraulic cylinders because of the harsh working conditions, and it is hoped that when there is a leak, the pressure cap (generally used to press the V-ring) can still be used after being tightened. When the V-ring is used, it can withstand a certain degree of eccentricity, but don't expect it to have a very long service life in occasions with large eccentricity. The number of V-rings in a group should not be too many. Sealing with 5 or 6 is not possible, and adding more will not be possible. In order to improve the sealing effect and service life, cloth-reinforced and non-cloth-reinforced V-rings can be mixed and installed, and generally the non-cloth-reinforced ones are placed in the middle. When a set of V-rings is sealed, the lubrication is poor, and a spacer ring can be installed to improve the lubrication, or special lubrication can be carried out. Some reference documents introduce that the pressure ring and support ring should be made of tin bronze or aluminum bronze when the pressure is above 8 MPa. The author believes that using tin bronze or aluminum bronze to make the pressure ring and support ring is definitely stronger than cloth-reinforced rubber (or cloth-reinforced reinforced rubber). The geometric shape of the pressure ring and support ring is crucial for the V-ring seal. Metal is smaller than (cloth-reinforced) rubber or plastic in deformation, which is more conducive to ensuring the sealing state of the V-ring.
Characteristics of V-ring seal:
1) Several V-rings can be stacked for use, and the sealing capacity generally increases with the increase of the number of stacks.
2) It has a certain ability to resist eccentricity.
3) Its service life can be improved by increasing the pressing force.
4) It is resistant to high pressure and has reliable performance.
5) When used in stacks, it can be cut and installed.
6) It can be used in occasions with poor lubrication or harsh working conditions.
7) It is especially suitable for use under heavy load conditions.

9) Large friction resistance and large structural dimensions.

(3) Design and selection principles for V-ring seals

The main tasks in designing V-ring seals are: determining the installation structure for V-rings, selecting the material and quantity of V-rings, and selecting or designing the pressure ring and support ring for V-rings.

The maximum working pressure for V-rings can reach 60 MPa or even higher. The working temperature ranges from -30 to 100°C or higher, with a movement speed ≤0.5 m/s.

1) Determination of installation structure. The installation structure of V-rings differs from other seal groove structures in that it must have an adjustable groove length structure, which is necessary to apply pressure to the V-rings. The adjustable part is usually the pressure cover, which is typically pressed onto the pressure ring. Using adjustment shims is the most common method to adjust the pressure.

2) Material selection. V-ring materials are classified into three types: pure rubber, rubber with fabric insert, and rubber-plastic composite. Pure rubber V-rings have excellent sealing performance, while fabric-reinforced rubber V-rings have better pressure resistance and wear resistance than pure rubber V-rings. Some sources recommend that at least one pure rubber ring should be included in a group of V-ring seals under low-temperature conditions to ensure good sealing performance. Fabric-reinforced V-rings can be cut and assembled, while pure rubber V-rings cannot. When cutting fabric-reinforced V-rings, they should be cut at a 45° angle, and each V-ring can only be cut at one break. When installing, the breaks should be staggered by 90° to 180°. This characteristic is very important; the author once used it when handling oil well seals in an oil field. Currently, V-rings are suitable for hydraulic oil and petroleum-based lubricants. If sealing other working media, it is necessary to communicate thoroughly with the seal manufacturer beforehand.

3) Selection of quantity. The number of V-rings in a group depends on the sealing pressure; the higher the pressure, the more rings are needed. However, when the number reaches a certain level, further increases do not significantly improve the sealing effect, while friction force increases sharply. The number of V-rings can be selected from 1 to 6, but 3 to 5 is most common. To improve the overall sealing performance, V-rings of different materials can be installed alternately, or spacer rings can be used.

4) Selection and design of pressure ring and support ring. V-rings sold in the market are usually supplied in sets, including the pressure ring, V-rings, and support ring (or elastic seal ring). Simply select according to the "Piston L3 Seal Groove V-ring, Pressure Ring, and Elastic Ring Dimensions and Tolerances" or "Piston Rod L3 Seal Groove V-ring, Pressure Ring, and Support Ring Dimensions and Tolerances" tables in GB/T10708.1-2000 "Reciprocating Rubber Seal Ring Structural Dimension Series Part 1: Unidirectional Rubber Seal Rings."

If metal retaining rings and support rings are used, they may need to be designed by oneself. To ensure the correct position of the V-ring, the metal rings must be carefully designed and processed. However, the shape and dimensions of the V-ring will have errors, and the metal ring also needs to have a certain elasticity. Therefore, soft metals such as tin bronze and aluminum bronze are generally selected.

If the pressure of the hydraulic medium to be sealed is low and small friction force is required, the angle of the recessed part of the retaining ring can be designed to be slightly larger than the angle of the sealing ring. Some reference literature mentions that it can reach up to 96°.

Finally, it should be noted that the service life of V-ring combined seals (including sealing performance) is closely related to the adjustment of the pressing force. Theoretically, the V-ring will have a longer service life under the optimal pressing force. However, if the pressing force is adjusted to be very large at the first time, its service life will definitely be very low. When adjusting the pressing force on site, it is necessary to tighten it gradually and not be hasty. The author has had many on-site practice experiences in this regard.

6. U-shaped rubber sealing ring and its groove

(1) Characteristics and functions of U-ring

The U-shaped rubber sealing ring (hereinafter referred to as U-ring) is a lip-shaped sealing element with a U-shaped cross-section. It has a pair of flexible sealing protrusions (sealing lips or lip edges, i.e., there is an inner lip and an outer lip, a pair of lips), as shown in Figure 2-30. According to the definition of the U-ring, the pair of sealing lips of the U-ring should be of equal height (symmetrical), and the bottom of the U-ring should be shorter than that of the Y-ring. However, there is no standard for how much shorter it should be to be called a U-ring instead of a Y-ring. In fact, this kind of sealing ring, which is frequently used for sealing hydraulic cylinders, had neither product standards nor sealing groove standards in China before July 13, 2018. However, it is common to see U-rings in the product samples of foreign sealing ring manufacturers. In their product samples, the pair of sealing lips of the U-ring are either of equal height (symmetrical) or of unequal height (asymmetrical). The U-ring with equal height (symmetrical) lips is generally universal for shafts and holes (piston and piston rod seals), while the U-ring with unequal height (asymmetrical) lips is divided into piston seals and piston rod seals, which is similar to the Y-ring standard in China. However, Y-rings are rarely seen in the product samples of foreign sealing ring manufacturers. Therefore, some reference literature points out that the U-ring in foreign countries is the same as the Y-ring in China.

As shown in Figure 2-31, in addition to a pair of (symmetrical or asymmetrical) sealing lips, the U-ring in the samples of foreign sealing ring manufacturers may also have another sealing lip on the side in contact with the mating part, which is called the second sealing lip. According to the definition of related terms, the seal here cannot be called a lip seal, and this sealing type is not a lip seal because it does not have a flexible part. The correct definition should be the second type of extrusion seal, which has the same sealing mechanism as the O-ring seal. Therefore, this kind of sealing ring should be called a double-sealed U-ring.

As shown in Figure 2-32, because the U-ring also has the problem of extrusion, especially under high temperature and high pressure (pressure pulsation or impact), the problem is still very serious. Therefore, there is a combined U-ring, and the bottom of this U-ring is embedded with a plastic retaining ring.

As shown in Figure 2-33, in order to improve the initial sealing ability of the U-ring, there is also a non-typical U-ring with an O-ring or other shapes of elastomer embedded or combined in the U-shaped groove.

The combined elliptical ring specified in GB/T 36520.2-2018 is extremely similar in structure to the combined U-ring shown in Figure 2-32.

The U-ring is a one-way sealing ring, which can be used for piston seals or piston rod seals in reciprocating motion; some reference literature points out that the U-ring can also be used for static seals or low-speed rotating shaft seals. The author has seen physical objects of hydraulic components with U-rings used for static seals and rotating shaft seals, but the author has not

U-ring sealing grooves suitable for static sealing and rotary shaft sealing can be found in domestic standards.
U-ring is most suitable for piston rod sealing.
Basic characteristics of U-ring:
1) Suitable for unidirectional sealing, small in size, simple and generally shallow sealing groove, which can be installed in the integral groove.
2) Small friction force, certain extrusion resistance, good wear resistance and long service life.
3) Supporting ring can be added to improve the pressure resistance.
4) Many product types and specifications, and various sealing materials can be selected.
5) The sealing system combined with C-type dust seal (double-lip rubber seal) may achieve "zero" leakage.
6) Double-sealed U-ring has good lubrication, low friction, small influence by impact load or pressure peak, stable sealing performance, especially good low-pressure sealing performance, and can also prevent external air from entering.
7) It has certain following ability, and is more eccentric resistant than O-ring.
8) Products with pressure relief groove can be selected when installed back to back.
(2) Sealing mechanism of U-ring
As shown in Figure 2-34 and Figure 2-35, because U-ring has a pair of flexible sealing protrusions (sealing lips), the fluid pressure acting on one side of the lips keeps the other side in close contact with the mating surface to form a seal.
Figure 2-34 Piston seal of U-ring
Figure 2-35 Piston rod seal of U-ring
After the U-ring is assembled, the sealing groove and the mating surface radially compress the U-ring, make it contact with the mating surface and generate initial contact stress, block the assembly clearance, and form initial seal; after the working medium to be sealed pressurizes it, a pair of flexible lips radially expand, and the lips are further closely attached to the sealing surface. With the increase of working medium pressure, the sealing contact area and contact stress will also increase, and the sealing ability will be enhanced. Therefore, U-ring is a kind of seal ring with self-sealing effect (ability).
Compared with the extrusion seal, the typical U-ring has weak initial sealing ability. Therefore, it is generally not suitable for static sealing.
The atypical U-ring effectively overcomes the above disadvantages of U-ring because of the elastic body embedded in the U-shaped groove, so that the U-ring has almost the same initial sealing ability as the extrusion seal, and therefore can be used for static sealing.
The sealing mechanism of the atypical U-ring contains the sealing mechanism of the extrusion seal and the lip seal, but the elastic body embedded in the U-shaped groove may affect the excitation ability of the sealing lip, that is, it is insensitive to pressure impact or the self-sealing ability is weakened. The solution is to first vulcanize the bamboo joint-shaped O-shaped straight bar, then bond it into an O-ring, and then embed it into the U-shaped groove of the U-ring to form an atypical U-ring which does not affect the excitation ability of the sealing lip and has good initial sealing ability.
Another atypical U-ring has excellent static and dynamic sealing performance and can also be used for rotary sealing because of the metal spring (usually stainless steel) with U-shaped or oval cross-section embedded in the U-shaped groove. Due to its ability to accurately control the friction force within a wide working temperature range, it is used in switching elements such as pressure switches. This U-ring can be made of various materials and has excellent sealing performance.

7. Rhodoid rubber sealing ring and its groove
(1) Characteristics and function of rhodoid ring
As shown in Figure 2-38, the rubber sealing ring with a cross-section resembling a rhodoid is called rhodoid rubber sealing ring (hereinafter referred to as rhodoid ring). The rhodoid ring is a one-way sealing ring with standards, and the structure type, size, and tolerance of the rhodoid ring are specified in GB/T10708.1-2000 "Structure Size Series of Reciprocating Rubber Sealing Rings Part 1: One-way Rubber Sealing Ring".
The rhodoid ring is generally composed of two parts, the sealing part is made of rubber, and the supporting part is made of cloth-reinforced rubber, and the hardness of the cloth-reinforced rubber is higher than that of the sealing part rubber.
Figure 2-38 Structure type of rhodoid ring
According to relevant definitions, the rhodoid ring does not belong to lip seals. Because its sealing protrusion part (sealing lip or lip) does not have a connected flexible part. One-way sealing is because its structure is combined with a supporting part (ring), when the sealing part is pressurized by hydraulic oil on one side, the other side supporting part can only resist extrusion by leaning against the side of the sealing groove, and vice versa it cannot.
Due to its structural characteristics, when the piston seal of a double-acting hydraulic cylinder adopts a rhodoid ring, it is difficult to solve the pressure relief after oil trapping if it is installed back to back. Therefore, the rhodoid ring is mainly used for piston rod seals rather than piston seals of double-acting hydraulic cylinders.
Due to its structural characteristics, the rhodoid ring can be used for radial static sealing.
The use conditions of one-way sealing rhodoid ring for reciprocating motion are shown in Table 2-96.

Compared with Y-shaped ring, the rhodoid ring has the following characteristics:
1) Reasonable structure type.
2) High sealing pressure and long life.
3) Good sealing performance.
4) Certain self-compensation ability.
5) Certain anti-eccentricity ability.
6) Universal with Y (unequal lip height) shaped ring groove.
7) Can be used for radial static sealing.
When the hydraulic cylinder seal using Y (unequal lip height) shaped ring seal has problems, the rhodoid ring should be considered first, but it is not possible if the cylinder bore is scratched. Because its sealing material is generally NBR, its tear resistance and wear resistance are lower than AU or EU, and the author has practical field experience in this regard.

(2) Sealing Mechanism of U-ring
The sealing mechanism of U-ring is more similar to extrusion type sealing. Its structure can be understood as a combination of an irregular O-ring and a special retaining ring, i.e. the sealing part and supporting part mentioned above. The sealing material used for the sealing part of U-ring should be equivalent to that of O-ring, with hardness lower than 90 HA (or IRHD), generally around 75 HA; the hardness of cloth-inserted rubber used for the supporting part is generally higher than 90 HA, and it is usually molded into one piece with the same rubber. Due to the presence of the supporting part (special retaining ring), it can only be used in one direction, i.e. one-way sealing. After the U-ring is installed into the sealing groove, its sealing part is radially compressed, forming initial sealing against the mating surface and the bottom of the groove; when the sealing part is subjected to the action of hydraulic oil, i.e. under pressure, the supporting part leans against the side of the groove, and the sealing part undergoes further radial expansion and deformation, increasing the sealing contact area and enhancing the sealing capability; as the sealing pressure further increases, both the supporting part and the sealing part will deform together, further increasing the sealing contact area and further enhancing the sealing capability. Due to the presence of the supporting part, although the resilience of the sealing part is enhanced, it also limits the radial expansion and deformation of the sealing part. In addition, the anti-extrusion capability of the supporting part has a certain limit value, so the sealing pressure is also limited, but it is higher than that of Y-ring seal, possibly even twice as high.

Since the sealing capability of U-ring increases with the increase of sealing working medium pressure, U-ring has a self-sealing effect.

The main function of the supporting part is to enhance the strength of the sealing part, especially its anti-extrusion capability. However, the anti-extrusion capability of cloth-inserted rubber is not as good as that of plastic, so it is necessary to additionally install a plastic retaining ring when needed.

After the U-ring is worn out by reciprocating motion, it still has a certain self-compensating effect because it is an extrusion type seal, which is also one of the reasons for its longer service life compared to Y-ring.

8. Drum-shaped and mountain-shaped rubber seals and their grooves
(1) Characteristics and functions of drum-shaped rings and mountain-shaped rings
Drum-shaped rubber seal ring (hereinafter referred to as drum-shaped ring) and mountain-shaped rubber seal ring (hereinafter referred to as mountain-shaped ring) are rubber seal rings suitable for installation on hydraulic cylinder pistons to provide bidirectional sealing. According to GB/T10708.2-2000 "Structure and Dimensions of Reciprocating Rubber Seals Part 2: Bidirectional Sealing Rubber Seals", there are two structural forms, as shown in Figure 2-40. The first type consists of a drum-shaped ring and two L-shaped support rings (see Figure 2-40a); the second type consists of a mountain-shaped ring, two J-shaped rings, and two rectangular support rings (see Figure 2-40b). The sealing groove specified in GB/T6577-1986 "Types, Dimensions, and Tolerances of Sealing Grooves for Hydraulic Cylinder Pistons with Support Rings" is adopted.

When the reciprocating motion speed is not greater than 0.15 m/s, the working pressure range of the drum-shaped ring is 0.10-70 MPa, and the working pressure range of the mountain-shaped ring is 0-35 MPa; when the reciprocating motion speed is not greater than 0.5 m/s, the working pressure range of the drum-shaped ring is 0.10-40 MPa, and the working pressure range of the mountain-shaped ring is 0-20 MPa.

Drum-shaped rings and mountain-shaped rings are assembled bidirectional sealing rings for holes. In a drum-shaped sealing ring composed of a drum-shaped ring and two L-shaped support rings, the drum-shaped ring is generally made of rubber molded with fabric-wrapped rubber, and the two L-shaped support rings are made of plastic; in a set of mountain-shaped sealing rings composed of a mountain-shaped ring, two J-shaped rings, and two rectangular support rings, the mountain-shaped ring is generally made of rubber, and the two J-shaped rings and two rectangular support rings are made of plastic. Specifically, the two J-shaped rings are made of thermoplastic polyester plastic, and the L-shaped and rectangular support rings are made of reinforced phenolic plastic with glass fiber embedded.

This sealing structure has the following advantages:
1) Good sealing performance under low pressure conditions.
2) The piston length can be shorter, and some can be installed on an integral piston.
3) The special structure of the sealing assembly prevents the seal ring from twisting in the groove during installation.
4) High extrusion resistance of the seal ring, good piston guidance.
5) High temperature resistance and wear resistance.

9. Coaxial sealing elements and their grooves
(1) Characteristics and functions of coaxial sealing elements
The term "coaxial sealing element" is defined in JB/T 8241-1996 "Vocabulary of coaxial sealing elements", which refers to a combined sealing element composed of a plastic ring and a rubber ring, with the plastic ring serving as the friction sealing surface.
A coaxial sealing element typically consists of at least one sealing sliding ring (also called plastic ring or sliding ring) and an elastic body. Generally, the material of the sliding ring is made of polytetrafluoroethylene filled with bronze (or molybdenum disulfide, etc.) or high-hardness polyurethane, and the elastic body is made of rubber material. In GB/T 15242.1-2017, square coaxial sealing elements for holes, combined coaxial sealing elements for holes, and stepped coaxial sealing elements for shafts are respectively provided. The square coaxial sealing element for holes is a piston sealing element with a rectangular cross-section sliding ring and an O-ring or rectangular ring as the elastic body; the combined coaxial sealing element for holes is a piston sealing element composed of a sealing sliding ring, a mountain-shaped elastic body, and two retaining rings; the stepped coaxial sealing element for shafts is a piston rod sealing element with a stepped cross-section sliding ring and an O-ring as the elastic body.
Coaxial sealing elements are suitable for dynamic sealing of hydraulic cylinder pistons and piston rods using hydraulic oil as the working medium, with a working pressure ≤40 MPa, reciprocating motion speed ≤5 m/s, and a working temperature range of -40～200℃. After years of development and technological progress, its working pressure can reach 60 MPa, and the reciprocating motion speed can reach 15 m/s, but the working temperature range has not changed much, mainly because the performance of the elastic body (here referring to the commonly used O-ring material) has not changed much. It should be noted that it is not a single O-ring material that can be applied to the working temperature range of -40～200℃, but rather a comprehensive selection of low-temperature nitrile rubber (HNBR) with a working temperature range of -40～100℃, nitrile rubber (NBR) with a working temperature range of -30～120℃, fluoro rubber (FKM) with a working temperature range of -20～200℃, etc.
For special performance coaxial sealing elements, please refer to Section 2.10.5.1.4.
Coaxial sealing elements are divided into double-acting and single-acting types, generally in combination of both, with the elastic body commonly being an O-shaped rubber sealing ring, and also rectangular (square) or mountain-shaped rubber sealing rings; the cross-section shape of the sliding ring is diverse, with square plastic rings and stepped plastic rings being commonly used. Coaxial sealing elements are not only used for piston and piston rod sealing, but also for dust sealing.
In coaxial sealing elements, there is a series of products with independent intellectual property rights in China, called "Che sealing elements".
Due to the significant changes in the structure of coaxial sealing elements, mainly in the sliding ring, several types of coaxial sealing elements are listed below for future unified naming, as shown in Figure 2-45.
From the various structural forms of the listed coaxial sealing elements, the following changes can be observed:
1) There are also bidirectional sealing structural forms for shaft seals, and lightweight structural forms have been developed.
2) There are also unidirectional sealing structural forms for hole seals, and coaxial seals composed of four parts with non-O-ring elastic bodies have been developed. At the same time, there are also lightweight structural forms for hole seals.
3) There are structural forms for rotary sealing for both shaft and hole seals.

1) Small friction force, easy starting at low pressure, smooth operation, no crawling.
2) Suitable for high-speed operation.
3) No danger of O-ring extrusion, long service life.
4) Wide range of applicable working media and working temperature if O-ring material is selected appropriately.

However, common coaxial seals have two disadvantages:
1) Difficult installation.
2) Poor sealing performance.
Special Note: For hydraulic cylinders with dynamic characteristic requirements, such as digital hydraulic cylinders and servo hydraulic cylinders, coaxial seals should be selected first, including coaxial combination dust seals.
Compared with lip seals, the sealing performance of coaxial seals is lower, i.e., there is leakage, especially more obvious at low temperature and low pressure. Therefore, in places where internal leakage of hydraulic cylinders is strictly required, as well as in lifting (or lifting) machinery, coaxial seals are generally not used for sealing or must be used in series with lip seals.

1.0. Several Atypical Sealing Elements and Their Grooves
(1) Piston Rod Combination Seal Ring with Retaining Ring
The piston rod combination seal ring with retaining ring (hereinafter referred to as piston rod combination ring) is a sealing element composed of a sealing ring and a retaining ring made of two different materials.
As shown in Figure 2-51, the piston rod combination ring is a lip-type sealing element. The sealing ring is made of polyurethane rubber (93HA), and its cross-sectional shape is approximately trident-shaped; the retaining ring is made of plastic, with a hardness higher than that of the sealing ring.
Its main advantages are:
1) Excellent wear resistance.
2) Impact resistance.
3) Extrusion resistance.
4) Small axial compression deformation under medium pressure.
5) Can adapt to the harshest (demanding) working conditions.
6) Can be installed in an integral (closed) sealing groove.
7) Compact structure, suitable for installation in international standard grooves.
The piston rod combination ring is suitable for mineral hydraulic oil, with a working temperature range of -35 ~ 110°C. The maximum working pressure can reach 50 MPa (pressure peak can reach 100 MPa), and the maximum speed is 0.5 m/s.
This piston rod combination seal ring with a special structure is mainly used for sealing hydraulic cylinders in walking machinery. Its application in the sealing system of hydraulic cylinders in construction machinery is mainly used as a buffer seal before the main seal, preventing the highest working pressure inside the hydraulic cylinder from directly acting on the main seal.

(2) Piston Unidirectional Seal Ring with Support Ring and Its Groove

The piston unidirectional seal ring with support ring (hereinafter referred to as piston combination seal ring) is a sealing component composed of a seal ring and a support ring made of materials with different hardnesses.

As shown in Figure 2-52, the piston combination seal ring is a lip-shaped sealing component. The seal ring is made of fabric-reinforced rubber with slightly lower hardness, and its cross-sectional shape is approximately trident-shaped. The support ring is also made of fabric-reinforced rubber, with higher hardness than the seal ring.

The piston combination seal ring is installed back-to-back and can be used for piston sealing in double-acting hydraulic cylinders. Due to its sealing material and structural type, it can meet the requirements of harsh working conditions, such as pressure impact, vibration, and eccentricity. The maximum working pressure can reach 60 MPa.

Its outstanding performance characteristics are that the support ring can prevent extrusion and also produce a sealing effect under high pressure, forming a second sealing barrier. Therefore, it is suitable for heavy-duty working conditions.

(3) Coaxial seal with retaining ring
The "coaxial seal with retaining ring" given in Reference [102] has the same structural form as the bore assembly coaxial seal given in GB/T15242.1-2017. However, in addition to providing reciprocating motion coaxial seals for hydraulic cylinder piston dynamic sealing devices suitable for water-based or oil-based hydraulic fluids as the transmission medium, GB/T15242.1-2017 has no other technical conditions available for selection and reference. It is also not as valuable as that given in GB/T15242.1-1994 (which has been superseded), which is suitable for reciprocating hydraulic cylinder pistons with hydraulic oil as the working medium, pressure ≤40 MPa, speed ≤5 m/s, and temperature range of -40～200 ℃. Therefore, the following content is still of certain reference value.
The coaxial seal with retaining ring is different from the two structural forms of coaxial seals given in GB/T15242.1-1994 "Dimension series and tolerances for coaxial seals for dynamic sealing devices for hydraulic cylinder pistons and piston rods". Its elastomeric cross-section shape is not O-ring, but a special shape (such as mountain-shaped) elastomeric power element; its sliding ring is made of PTFE+bronze or PTFE+glass fiber, and there are also some made of hydrolytically resistant thermoplastic polyester TPE, and a POM or PA retaining ring is installed on each side of the sliding ring, as shown in Figure 2-53.
Figure 2-53 Coaxial seal with retaining ring and installation groove
The special-shaped elastomer has a greater squeezing (powering) ability to the sliding ring than the O-ring; the POM retaining ring installed on both sides of the sliding ring can enhance the extrusion resistance of the sliding ring, reduce pressure shock, and also has a certain dirt scraping and dirt holding capacity, which also plays a certain protective role on the sliding ring and elastomer.
This structural form of coaxial seal is mainly used for medium and heavy-duty hydraulic cylinders.
