1. Environmental and working conditions

1) Environmental temperature: 15 to 35°C.

2) Relative humidity: not greater than 75%.

3) Electromagnetic field: there should be no electromagnetic field that affects the test results.

2. Technical requirements

(1) Appearance

The appearance of the sensor should be intact without cracks or scratches; the markings should be clear, complete, and correct.

(2) Markings

The sensor should be fixed with the product markings in an obvious position on the body, and should be marked with the following contents:

1) Model and specifications.

2) Name.

3) Measurement range.

4) Name or trademark of the manufacturer.

5) Factory number.

6) Production date.

When the product size is small, at least the model and specifications and factory number should be marked on the sensor body, and the remaining contents can be indicated on the product packaging.

(3) Weight

The weight of the sensor should meet the requirements of the product detailed specification, such as JB/T9517-1999 "Magnetoelectric Speed Sensor".

(4) Shape and installation dimensions

The shape and installation dimensions of the sensor should meet the requirements of the product detailed specification.

(5) Output resistance

The output resistance of the sensor should meet the requirements of the product detailed specification.

(6) Insulation resistance

When a DC voltage of 500 V is applied, the insulation resistance of the sensor should not be less than 10 MΩ.

(7) Dielectric strength

When an AC voltage of 500 V and a frequency of 50 Hz are applied, there should be no arcing, breakdown, or flickering on the surface of the sensor, and the test voltage should not have a sudden drop.

(8) Reference sensitivity

The error of the reference sensitivity of the vibration speed sensor should be better than ±5%.

(9) Frequency response (when applicable)

The frequency response deviation of the vibration speed sensor should meet the requirements of the product detailed specification.

(10) Amplitude linearity (when applicable)

The amplitude linearity of the amplitude speed sensor should meet the requirements of the product detailed specification.

(11) Transverse sensitivity ratio (when applicable)

The transverse sensitivity ratio of the amplitude speed sensor should meet the requirements of the product detailed specification.

(12) Sensitivity time drift (when applicable)

The sensitivity time drift of the amplitude speed sensor should meet the requirements of the product detailed specification.

(13) Sensitivity thermal drift (when applicable)

The sensitivity thermal drift of the amplitude speed sensor should meet the requirements of the product detailed specification.

(14) High-temperature storage

The upper limit temperature and holding time for high-temperature storage are as follows:

1) Upper limit temperature: 70 ℃, 85 ℃, 100 ℃, 125 ℃, 150 ℃.
2) Holding time: 48 h, 72 h, 96 h, 168 h.
After the sensor undergoes high-temperature storage test, its appearance should meet the requirements of item 2.(1), and the reference sensitivity of the vibration velocity sensor should meet the requirements of item 2.(8).
(15) Low-temperature storage
The lower limit temperature and holding time for low-temperature storage shall be selected from the following conditions.
1) Lower limit temperature: -55 ℃, -40 ℃, -100 ℃, -25 ℃, -10 ℃.
2) Holding time: 24 h, 48 h, 72 h, 96 h.
After the sensor undergoes low-temperature storage test, its appearance should meet the requirements of item 2.(1), and the reference sensitivity of the vibration velocity sensor should meet the requirements of item 2.(8).
(16) Temperature change
The temperature change shall meet the following conditions.
1) Extreme temperature: Select from the upper limit temperature and lower limit temperature specified in clauses (14) and (15).
2) Minimum test time at extreme temperature: Execute according to the provisions of the product detailed specification based on the weight of the sensor.
3) Conversion time: Not greater than 5 min.
4) Number of cycles: 5 times, 10 times.
After the sensor undergoes temperature change test, its appearance should meet the requirements of item 2.(1), and the reference sensitivity of the vibration velocity sensor should meet the requirements of item 2.(8).
(17) Vibration
Under room temperature, apply vibration to the sensor along its three axes (X, Y, Z) respectively, with the vibration level and time conducted according to the provisions of the product detailed specification.
After the sensor undergoes vibration test, its appearance should meet the requirements of item 2.(1), and the reference sensitivity of the vibration velocity sensor should meet the requirements of item 2.(8).
(18) Shock
Under room temperature, apply shock to the sensor along its three axes (X, Y, Z) respectively, with 12 shocks applied in each direction, acceleration of 1000 m/s², waveform of half-sine pulse, pulse duration of 6 ms, or conducted according to the provisions of the product detailed specification.
After the sensor undergoes shock test, its appearance should meet the requirements of item 2.(1), and the reference sensitivity of the vibration velocity sensor should meet the requirements of item 2.(8).
(19) Constant humid heat
The constant humid heat test shall be selected from the following conditions.
1) Temperature: 40 ℃±2 ℃.
2) Relative humidity: 93%±3%.
3) Test time: 48 h, 96 h, 120 h.
After the sensor undergoes constant humid heat test, its appearance should meet the requirements of item 2.(1), insulation resistance should meet the requirements of item 2.(6), and the reference sensitivity of the vibration velocity sensor should meet the requirements of item 2.(8).
(20) Salt spray
The salt spray test shall be selected from the following conditions.
1) Temperature: 35 ℃±2 ℃.
2) Salt water concentration: 5%±1% mass fraction.
3) Test time: 48 h, 96 h.
After the sensor undergoes constant humid heat test, its appearance should meet the requirements of item 2.(1), insulation resistance should meet the requirements of item 2.(6), and the reference sensitivity of the vibration velocity sensor should meet the requirements of item 2.(8).

2.1.3.7 Technical Requirements for Proximity Switches for Hydraulic Cylinders
Proximity switches are position switches that can operate without mechanical contact with moving parts. Proximity switches can be classified according to various basic characteristics, such as inductive type (I), capacitive type (C), ultrasonic type (U), diffuse photoelectric type (D), non-mechanical magnetic type (M), retroreflective photoelectric type (R), and through-beam photoelectric type (T).
Taking Hall proximity switch sensors as an example, the basic operating parameters and technical requirements are given below.
1. Basic Operating Parameters
(1) Operating Voltage
The nominal value of the sensor's operating voltage should comply with the product technical conditions.
337:
( Detailed specifications).
The recommended operating voltage of the sensor shall be selected from DC 2.5V to 40V.
(2) Output type
The output type of the sensor is usually single-pole type, all-pole type, bipolar type, and bipolar latch type.
(3) Maximum load current
The maximum load current of the sensor is recommended to be selected from the following values: 20mA, 50mA, 100mA, 200mA, 300mA, 500mA.
(4) Operating temperature range
The operating temperature range of the sensor shall conform to the provisions of the product technical conditions (detailed specifications).
The recommended lower limit value of the operating temperature range is: -55°C, -40°C, -25°C, -10°C.
The recommended upper limit value of the operating temperature range is: 70°C, 85°C, 100°C, 125°C, 150°C.
(5) Storage temperature range
The lower limit of the storage temperature range of the sensor is usually equal to or lower than the lower limit operating temperature by 10°C, and the upper limit of the storage temperature range is usually equal to or higher than the upper limit operating temperature by 15 to 20°C.
2. Technical requirements
(1) Appearance
The appearance of the sensor should be free from visible defects, corrosion, and damage; the threaded part should be free from burrs; the components should be intact; the markings should be clear, complete, and accurate.
(2) Appearance, installation dimensions, and lead connections
The appearance, installation dimensions, and lead connections of the sensor shall conform to the provisions of the product technical conditions (detailed specifications).
(3) Operating point magnetic induction intensity
The operating point magnetic induction intensity of the sensor shall conform to the range specified in the product technical conditions (detailed specifications).
(4) Reset point magnetic induction intensity
The reset point magnetic induction intensity of the sensor shall conform to the range specified in the product technical conditions (detailed specifications).
(5) Hysteresis
The hysteresis of the sensor shall conform to the range specified in the product technical conditions (detailed specifications).
(6) Cut-off state current
The cut-off state current of the sensor shall conform to the provisions of the product technical conditions (detailed specifications).
(7) On-state voltage drop
The on-state voltage drop of the sensor shall conform to the provisions of the product technical conditions (detailed specifications).
(8) Operating frequency
The operating frequency of the sensor shall conform to the provisions of the product technical conditions (detailed specifications).
(9) Insulation resistance
Under the specified test conditions, the insulation resistance between the terminal and the housing of the sensor shall not be less than 20 MΩ.
(10) Insulation strength
Under the specified test conditions, the sensor shall be able to withstand a sinusoidal AC voltage with an amplitude of 1000V and a frequency of 50Hz for 1 minute without breakdown or arcing.
(11) Low-temperature storage
After low-temperature storage, the appearance of the sensor shall conform to the requirements of 2.(1), and the operating point magnetic induction intensity, reset point magnetic induction intensity, and hysteresis shall conform to the requirements of items 2.(3) to 2.(5).
(12) High-temperature storage
After high-temperature storage, the appearance of the sensor shall conform to the requirements of 2.(1), and the operating point magnetic induction intensity, reset point magnetic induction intensity, and hysteresis shall conform to the requirements of items 2.(3) to 2.(5).
(13) Temperature change
After the temperature change test, the appearance of the sensor shall conform to the requirements of item 2.(1), and the operating point magnetic induction intensity, reset point magnetic induction intensity, and hysteresis shall conform to the requirements of items 2.(3) to 2.(5).
(14) Constant humidity and heat
After the constant humidity and heat test, the appearance of the sensor shall conform to the requirements of item 2.(1), and the operating point magnetic induction intensity, reset point magnetic induction intensity, and hysteresis shall conform to the requirements of items 2.(3) to 2.(5). The insulation resistance shall conform to the requirements of item 2.(9).
(15) Vibration
After the vibration test, the appearance of the sensor shall conform to the requirements of item 2.(1), and the operating point magnetic induction intensity, reset point magnetic induction intensity, and hysteresis shall conform to the requirements of items 2.(3) to 2.(5).
(16) Shock
After the shock test, the appearance of the sensor shall conform to the requirements of item 2.(1), and the operating point magnetic induction intensity, reset point magnetic induction intensity, and hysteresis shall conform to the requirements of items 2.(3) to 2.(5).
(17) Electrostatic discharge immunity (when specified)
During the electrostatic discharge immunity test, the output state of the sensor shall not change.
(18) Electrical fast transient/burst immunity (when specified)
During the electrical fast transient/burst immunity test, the output state of the sensor shall not change.
(19) Service life
The service life of the sensor switch shall not be less than 1 million times.

Non-contact, precise, and absolute measurement are its important characteristics, and linear magnetostrictive magnets are widely used in industrial applications. Non-contact, wear-free operation helps save high maintenance costs and avoids the trouble of failure downtime. This characteristic allows them to be installed in completely sealed housings, as current position information can be transmitted to internal sensor elements through the magnetic field without contact. Theoretically, a measurement system can measure multiple positions simultaneously. Convenient, lightweight, and reliable sealed design enables magnetostrictive displacement measurement systems to achieve IP67~IP67K protection level. Good shock and vibration resistance has enabled their rapid expansion in industrial applications to heavy machinery and system design fields. Many applications require obtaining measurement values and position values, which can be quickly provided in absolute terms after the measurement system is activated. Because reference runs are omitted, machine availability is greatly improved.
Rod-type micro-pulse displacement sensors are mainly used in hydraulic drive applications. When installed on the pressure part of a hydraulic cylinder, the displacement sensor must have the same pressure resistance as the hydraulic cylinder at that time. In fact, the sensor must be able to withstand pressures up to 1000 bar (1 bar = 10^5 Pa). The chip is integrated in an aluminum or stainless steel housing, the waveguide is installed in a high-pressure resistant non-magnetic stainless steel tube, and the front end of the tube is sealed with a welded plug. The high-pressure part is sealed by an O-ring on the flange mounting surface at the other end. The positioning magnet installed on the magnetic ring slides along the tube or rod with the built-in waveguide to mark the detected position.
(2) Technical Parameters
The BTL7 series rod sensors have characteristics of high pressure resistance up to 600 bar, high repeatability, non-contact, and durability, and can form a durable position feedback system in harsh environments, with a detection range of 25~7620 mm.
The measuring section of the sensor is installed in a high-pressure resistant stainless steel metal tube for reliable protection. This system is very suitable for position feedback of hydraulic cylinders, or for liquid level control of corrosive liquids in the food and chemical industries.

4. LWH Series Potentiometer Linear Displacement Sensor
(1) Product Introduction
Different from the rod-type magnetostrictive micro-pulse displacement sensor of the BTL7 series, the LWH series potentiometer linear displacement sensor is a contact-type linear displacement sensor.
This series of sensors is used in measurement and control systems for direct and absolute measurement of displacement and length.
The maximum working range is up to 900 mm, with high resolution (0.01 mm) providing accurate linear displacement measurement.
The inner and outer surfaces of the sensor are specially treated, allowing it to work under high-speed and low-wear conditions. The flexible buffer bearing at the front end of the sensor can overcome some minor lateral stresses of the transmission rod, ensuring normal operation of the sensor. The structural design considers ease of installation and disassembly.
The fixing and structural design of the sensor's conductive material ensure reliable operation even under the harshest conditions.
The sensor has mounting grooves on all four sides, which facilitates installation with the conductive material facing downward as much as possible, avoiding the presence of tiny impurities inside the sensor and thereby affecting its lifespan.
This series of sensors has the following characteristics:
a) Long service life of up to 10×10^7 cycles under different application conditions.
b) Excellent linearity, up to ±0.04%.
c) Resolution higher than 0.01 mm.
d) High operating speed.
e) Equipped with a DIN 4365050 standard plug and socket (pressure connector).
f) Protection class IP55.
In addition, it should be noted that:
a) The housing is made of anodized aluminum.
b) The installation uses a crimped adjustable fixed clamp.
c) The pull rod is made of stainless steel (1.4305), can rotate, and has an M6 external thread.
d) The bearing uses a flexible buffer bearing.
e) The resistance element uses conductive plastic.
f) The brush assembly uses a precious metal multi-arm brush.
g) The electrical connection is a 4-pole socket conforming to DIN 4365050 standard.

2.1.4 Design of Hydraulic Cylinders for Air Release, Anti-Loosening, and Other Components and Devices
2.1.4.1 Technical Requirements for Air Release Devices of Hydraulic Cylinders
1. Technical Requirements for Air Release Devices of Hydraulic Cylinders
Air release is the means of expelling air from a system or component. An air release valve is a component used to expel air or gas contained in the hydraulic system oil. The hydraulic system should be equipped with necessary air release devices (valves) as required and should allow for easy air discharge (release).
"Air release," "air release valve," and "air release" are all terms defined in GB/T 1746-2012. However, "air release" is defined as a term related only to pneumatics. Therefore, this manual often uses the expression "air (gas) release."
GB/T 13342-2007 stipulates that hydraulic cylinders should generally be equipped with air release devices.
GB/T 24946-2010 stipulates that digital cylinders can be equipped with air release devices as required.
GB/T 3766-2015 stipulates that when installing hydraulic cylinders on fixed industrial machinery, they should be able to automatically release air or provide easily accessible external air release ports. During installation, the air release port of the hydraulic cylinder should be positioned at the highest point.
When these requirements cannot be met, relevant maintenance and usage information should be provided; hydraulic cylinders with inflation chambers should be designed or equipped with air release ports to prevent danger. Hydraulic cylinders should be able to safely expel air through air release ports.
GB/T 3766-2001 (which has been superseded) stipulates that single-acting piston-type hydraulic cylinders should be equipped with air release ports, positioned appropriately to prevent danger from oil spray to personnel.
GJ B638A-1997 stipulates that wherever air that has been mixed in would interfere with the normal operation of the hydraulic system, appropriate methods such as installing manual air release valves should be adopted to expel it, rather than disconnecting pipelines or loosening tube nuts; requirements for automatic air release valves can be found in MIL-V-29592.

2.1.4.3 Technical Requirements for Integrated Hydraulic Control Valves in Hydraulic Cylinders

Hydraulic cylinders with integrated hydraulic control valves, including those with cushioning valves, support valves, and proportional/servo valves, should preferably use cartridge valves and/or cartridge valves.

The nominal pressure and other performance indicators of the hydraulic control valves (hereinafter referred to as hydraulic valves) should not be lower than the technical requirements of the hydraulic cylinders; the mounting surfaces for valves or valve blocks installed on the hydraulic cylinders, or the cartridge mounting holes for cartridge valves, should comply with relevant standard specifications.

The protection level, operating voltage, and electrical connections of electrically controlled valves should comply with relevant standard specifications; generally, the electrically controlled valves themselves should also be equipped with manual override control devices.

1. General Technical Requirements for Hydraulic Valves

(1) Selection of Hydraulic Valves
The selection of hydraulic valve types should consider correct functionality, sealing, maintenance and adjustment requirements, as well as the ability to withstand foreseeable mechanical or environmental impacts. In fixed industrial machinery, cartridge valves and/or cartridge valves should be preferred. When isolation valves are required, valves approved by the manufacturer for such safety applications should be used.

(2) Installation of Hydraulic Valves
When installing hydraulic valves, the following aspects should be considered:
1) Independent support, not relying on connected piping or fittings.
2) Ease of disassembly, repair, or adjustment.
3) Effects of gravity, impact, and vibration on the valve.
4) Sufficient space for wrenches, bolt removal, and electrical connections.
5) Avoidance of incorrect installation methods.
6) Prevention of damage from mechanical operating devices.
7) Installation orientation that prevents air accumulation or allows air discharge when used.

(3) Valve Blocks
1) Surface Roughness and Flatness: On valve blocks, the surface roughness and flatness of valve mounting surfaces should meet the manufacturer's recommended requirements.
2) Deformation: During operation within the specified working pressure and temperature range, valve blocks or valve block assemblies should not fail due to deformation.
3) Installation: Valve blocks should be firmly installed.
4) Internal Flow Channels: Internal flow channels should have sufficient cross-sectional area at cross-flow areas to minimize additional pressure drops as much as possible. Cast and machined internal flow channels should be free of harmful foreign objects such as scale, burrs, and chips. Harmful foreign objects can obstruct flow or cause other components (including seals and packing) to malfunction and/or be damaged when moving with hydraulic fluid.
5) Identification: Valve block assemblies and their components should be labeled according to ISO 1087-4 (i.e., GB/T3697-2018) for marking. When not feasible, identification should be provided by other means.

(4) Electrically Controlled Valves
1) Electrical Connections: Electrical connections should comply with relevant standards (such as GB/T5226.1 or the manufacturer's standard) and be designed with appropriate protection levels (such as GB/T4208).
2) Solenoids: Appropriate solenoids (such as switching frequency, temperature ratings, and voltage tolerance) should be selected so that they can operate the valve under specified conditions.
3) Manual or Other Override Control: When power is unavailable, if operation of electrically controlled valves is necessary, an override control method should be provided. When designing or selecting an override control method, the risk of accidental operation should be minimized; and after the override control is released, automatic reset should be implemented unless otherwise specified.

(5) Adjustment
When allowing adjustment of one or more valve parameters, the following provisions should be considered as appropriate:
1) Safe adjustment methods;
2) Methods to lock adjustments if unauthorized changes are not permitted;
3) Methods to prevent adjustments beyond safe ranges.

2. Technical Requirements for Pressure Control Valves
Valves whose function is to control pressure are called pressure control valves.

Pressure control valves specified in standards include proportional pressure pilot valves, hydraulic relief valves, hydraulic solenoid relief valves, hydraulic unloading relief valves, hydraulic solenoid unloading relief valves, hydraulic reducing valves and one-way reducing valves, internally controlled hydraulic sequence valves and one-way sequence valves, externally controlled hydraulic sequence valves and one-way sequence valves, electrically modulated (proportional) relief valves, electrically modulated (proportional) reducing valves, digital relief valves, hydraulic pressure relays, as well as other types such as bidirectional relief valves (groups) (brake valves) and balance valves.

Different from hydraulic control of hydraulic control valves, this is a control method that operates by changing the hydraulic pressure in the control circuit, but it itself does not have the ability to control the hydraulic pressure in the control circuit.

(1) Technical Requirements for Hydraulic Relief Valves and Solenoid Relief Valves

① The nominal pressure of relief valves should comply with the provisions of GB/T2346 "Nominal Pressure Series for Hydraulic Transmission Systems and Components."

④ Manufacturers should indicate the applicable conditions and environmental requirements of their products in product samples and related materials.

4. Technical Requirements for Directional Control Valves

A valve whose main function is to control the direction of oil flow, connecting or blocking one or more flow paths, is called a directional control valve.

The directional control valves specified in the standard include hydraulic ordinary (straight-through, right-angle) check valves and hydraulic control check valves, hydraulic solenoid directional valves, hydraulic manual and roller directional valves, hydraulic electro-hydraulic directional valves and hydraulic directional valves, hydraulic solenoid directional seat valves, hydraulic multi-way directional valves, electro-modulated (proportional) three (four-way) directional flow control valves, dual-speed directional combination valves, as well as high-pressure manual ball valves, hydraulic control shut-off valves, shut-off check valves, butterfly valves, ball valves, etc.

The minimum control pressure of hydraulic electro-hydraulic directional valves and hydraulic directional valves, as well as the minimum control pressure for reverse opening of hydraulic control check valves, are defined differently from the minimum control pressure of flow control valves.

5. General Technical Requirements for Electrohydraulic Servo Valves

An electrohydraulic servo valve is a servo valve whose input is an electrical signal and output is hydraulic energy. Among them, the flow control electrohydraulic servo valve is an electrohydraulic servo valve whose main function is to control the output flow.

The current standard G B/T1 0 8 4 4—2 0 0 7 stipulates marine electrohydraulic servo valves, G B/T 1 3 8 5 4—2 0 0 8 stipulates jet pipe electrohydraulic servo valves, G J B3 3 7 0—1 9 9 8 stipulates aircraft electrohydraulic servo valves, G J B4 0 6 9—2 0 0 0 stipulates ship electrohydraulic servo valve specifications, and Q J 5 0 4 A—1 9 9 6 stipulates flow electrohydraulic servo valves, etc.

1) Types. Electrohydraulic servo valves can be classified into single-stage, two-stage (or secondary, double-stage), three-stage or four-stage electrohydraulic servo valves according to the number of hydraulic amplifier stages.

(2) Mechanical Design Requirements for Electrohydraulic Servo Valves

1) Design Layout. According to the different requirements of the controlled object, electrohydraulic servo valves can be designed in different types. Some feedback structures can be adopted from the output-stage hydraulic amplifier to the electrical-mechanical converter (such as torque motor) to improve the performance of the valve, such as force feedback, electrical feedback, etc.

2) Interchangeability Requirements.

(1) Installation Requirements. The external outline dimensions of newly developed electrohydraulic servo valves shall be equal to or smaller than those of electrohydraulic servo valves of the same type and specification that are currently in service. When modifying the design of the valve's parts or components, the structural elements of the installation shall not be arbitrarily changed.

The electrical connector shall be the same as that of the electrohydraulic servo valve currently in service. It is recommended to select the plug socket specified in G J B5 9 9 A.

(4) Hydraulic Design Requirements for Electro-Hydraulic Servo Valve

1) Working Pressure. The rated supply pressure and return pressure should comply with the provisions of Table 2-232 and meet the pressure class specified in GB/T23346-2003 or GJB456-1988.

2) Pressure Resistance. The pressure oil port P, working oil ports A and B, and (external) pilot supply port X of the electro-hydraulic servo valve should be able to withstand 1.3 times the rated supply pressure (return port T open); the return port T should be able to withstand 1.3 times the rated supply pressure of the return port T. Under the application of positive and negative rated currents, each maintained for 2.5 minutes, the valve should not have obvious external leakage (moistening allowed, dripping not allowed) or permanent deformation. During and/or after the test, the valve's rated flow, hysteresis, and zero offset should comply with the requirements of detailed industry specifications. Pressure resistance testing should not be performed on the valve's (external control) drain port Y.

Note: Regarding external leakage, reference can be made to the provisions of GB/Z18427-2001, which is expressed as not worse than Grade 3 (fluid formation without dripping droplets).

3) Destructive Pressure. Apply 2.5 times the rated supply pressure to the pressure oil port P, working oil ports A and B (return port T open); apply 1.5 times the rated supply pressure to the return port T, each maintained for 30 seconds. The electro-hydraulic servo valve should not be damaged, and there is no requirement for the valve to restore working performance. Valves that have undergone destructive pressure testing cannot be used as products again.

4) Pressure Pulse. If detailed industry specifications require pressure pulse testing of the electro-hydraulic servo valve, the electro-hydraulic servo valve should be able to withstand 2.5×10⁵ cycles of pulse under rated pressure at positive and negative rated currents. After the test, its performance should comply with the requirements of detailed industry specifications.

5) Working Medium. Should comply with the provisions of detailed industry specifications. Generally, petroleum (mineral) based hydraulic oil conforming to GB11118.1 should be used, or aviation hydraulic oil No. 10, No. 12, and No. 15 conforming to SH0358, Q/SY11507, GJB1177A.

The oil used for filling and the oil filled in protective packaging generally should be consistent with the actual working medium of the electro-hydraulic servo valve.

6) Working Medium Temperature. The working medium temperature class should comply with the provisions of detailed industry specifications. For example, meeting the requirements of GJB456 -55 (54)-135°C.

Note: 1. The temperature class III in GJB456 is different from the temperature class III in GB/T30206.3.

2. The operating temperature range of petroleum-based aviation hydraulic oil specified in GJB1177A is -54-134°C.

3. In ISO10770-1:2009, the output flow or valve core position - oil temperature is 94.3 Chapter 2 Design of Hydraulic Cylinders and Their Components.
361:
Temperature Characteristic Test The oil temperature should reach 70°C.
7) Contamination Resistance. The electro-hydraulic servo valve should operate normally when the solid particle contamination level of the oil is no worse (higher) than GB/T14039 grade 16/14.
In GB/T33370-1998, for nozzle flapper servo valves, the acceptance level of solid contamination in the working fluid used for performance testing, acceptance testing, and internal oil seals should be no higher than class 6/A specified in GB/T4206, and the control level should be no higher than 7/A; for other tests, the solid contamination level of the working fluid should be no higher than 8/A. For jet pipe and direct drive servo valves, the requirements may be appropriately reduced, and should comply with the detailed specifications.
8) Filtration Precision. When the electro-hydraulic servo valve is used conventionally, a filter with nominal filtration precision of no less than 10μm should be installed before the oil inlet (pressure oil port).
When the electro-hydraulic servo valve is used for long life, a filter with nominal filtration precision of no less than 5μm should be installed before the oil inlet (pressure oil port).
During electro-hydraulic servo valve testing, it is recommended to install a filter with nominal filtration precision of 3μm as close as possible to the oil inlet (pressure oil port) of the electro-hydraulic servo valve.
9) External Sealing. The electro-hydraulic servo valve should not have obvious external leakage under all specified operating conditions and throughout the entire working period (moistening is allowed, but oil droplets dripping is not allowed).

2.14.4 Technical requirements for hydraulic filters
To maintain the required hydraulic oil contamination level, the hydraulic system and circuit should provide filtration. If the main filtration system (such as supply or return line filters) cannot achieve the required hydraulic oil contamination level or there are higher filtration requirements, a bypass filtration system can be used. Filters should be installed as needed in the pressure line, return line, and/or auxiliary circulation circuit to achieve the system's required oil contamination level. All filters should be equipped with indicators to provide indication when the filter needs maintenance. The indicator should be easily observable by the operator or maintenance personnel. If this requirement cannot be met, the operator's manual should specify regular replacement of the filter. The filter should be installed in an easily accessible location, with sufficient space left for replacing the filter element. The selected filter should meet the requirement of not exceeding the initial pressure drop recommended by the filter manufacturer at the predetermined flow rate and highest hydraulic oil viscosity. Due to the area ratio of the hydraulic cylinder and the influence of decompression, the maximum flow through the return line filter may be greater than the maximum flow of the pump. When the maximum pressure difference generated by the system across the filter may cause damage to the filter element, a filter bypass valve should be installed. In the pressure circuit, the bypass flow of contaminants through the filter should not cause harm downstream. It is not recommended to install a filter in the pump's suction line, and it is not advisable to use it as the main system filtration. A suction strainer or coarse filter can be used.
Malfunction of proportional valves or servo valves caused by contamination may lead to danger, so it is advisable to install an additional full-flow filter with a non-bypass and easily observable clogging indicator near the proportional valve or servo valve in the supply line. The burst pressure rating of the filter element should exceed the highest working pressure of the system. The blockage of the liquid flow through the non-bypass filter should not cause danger.
1. Basic technical parameter requirements
1) The filtration accuracy of the filter should meet the requirements of the product technical documentation.
The filtration accuracy (μm) should be selected from 3, 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 40. When the filtration accuracy is greater than 40μm, it should be determined by the manufacturer.
2) The rated flow (L/min) of the filter should be selected from the following grades: 16, 25, 40, 63, 100, 160, 250, 400, 630, 800, 1000. When the rated flow is greater than 1000 L/min, it should be determined by the manufacturer.
3) The nominal pressure of the pressure line filter should be in accordance with GB/T23461
363:
4) The dirt-holding capacity of the filter under rated flow should be specified in the technical file of the product.  
5) For filters equipped with an indicator, the pressure drop of the indicator should be indicated in the technical file of the product.  
6) For filters equipped with a bypass valve, the opening pressure drop should be marked in the technical file of the product. When the pressure drop of the bypass valve reaches 80% and the specified opening pressure drop of the bypass valve, the leakage should comply with the provisions of Table 1 in GB/T 20079-2006. The closing pressure drop of the bypass valve should not be less than 65% of the specified opening pressure drop. When the flow through the bypass valve reaches the rated flow of the filter, its pressure drop should not be greater than 1.7 times the opening pressure drop.  
7) When the filter is equipped with both an indicator and a bypass valve, it should meet the following formula requirement, i.e., 65% of the opening pressure drop of the bypass valve ≤ the pressure drop of the indicator ≤ 80% of the opening pressure drop of the bypass valve.  
8) The initial pressure drop of the filter under rated flow should be specified in the technical file of the product.  
9) The flow-pressure drop characteristic curve of the filter under test conditions should be provided in the technical file of the product.  
2. Material Requirements  
1) The materials selected for the filter should comply with the relevant material standards or technical agreements.  
2) The selected materials should be compatible with the working medium.  
3) Metal materials should be corrosion-resistant or protected to ensure that the filter has good resistance to salt spray, humidity, and other harsh conditions during normal storage and use.  
3. Performance Requirements  
1) Low-pressure sealing: There should be no oil leakage on the outside of the filter under a pressure of 1.5 kPa.  
2) High-pressure sealing: There should be no oil leakage or permanent deformation on the outside of the filter under 1.5 times the nominal pressure.  
3) Burst pressure: The filter should not burst under 3 times the nominal pressure.  
4) Pressure drop flow characteristics: The pressure drop flow characteristics of the filter should be specified in the technical file of the product.  
4. Connection Dimensions  
When there are no technical specifications, the connection dimensions between the filter and the pipeline should be selected from Table 2 in GB/T 20079-2006 according to the connection method.  
5. Design and Manufacturing  
1) The filter should be manufactured according to the product drawing and technical file, and its technical requirements should comply with the provisions of GB/T 20079-2006.  
2) The filter should be designed in a structural form that allows the filter element to be replaced without disassembling the pipe fittings or fasteners.  
3) The filter should be designed in a structural form that can effectively prevent incorrect installation of the filter element.  
4) When the filter is equipped with a bypass valve, the design structure should prevent pollutants deposited from directly passing through the bypass valve.  
5) The surface of the filter should not have defects such as dents, cracks, corrosion, and burrs. The surface coating should not crack, peel, or flake during normal storage, transportation, and use.  
6) The cleanliness index of the filter should be specified, and all oil ports should be equipped with dust caps when leaving the factory.  
6. Instructions  
1) When choosing to comply with GB/T 20079-2006 "Technical Conditions for Hydraulic Filters", it is recommended that manufacturers use the following instructions in test reports, product samples, and sales documents: The hydraulic filter complies with GB/T 20079-2006 "Technical Conditions for Hydraulic Filters".  
2) Hydraulic filters with special (product) standards are excluded.  
3) The above documents are often used as one of the technical documents for exchanging information between the supply and demand parties of hydraulic filters.  
2.1.4.5 Technical Requirements for Hydraulic Isolated Accumulators  
In hydraulic systems and circuits with inflatable accumulators, when the system is shut down, the hydraulic system should automatically release the liquid pressure of the accumulator or completely isolate the accumulator. In special cases where pressure is still required after the machine is shut down or the potential energy of the hydraulic accumulator will not cause any danger (such as clamping devices), it is not necessary to comply with the requirements for pressure release or isolation. Inflatable accumulators and any matching pressure-bearing components should be used within the rated limits of pressure, temperature, and environmental conditions. In special cases, protective measures may be needed to prevent overpressure on the gas side. If damage to components and pipe fittings in the inflatable accumulator system may cause danger, appropriate protection should be taken for them. The inflatable accumulator and all matching pressure-bearing components should be supported according to the instructions of the accumulator supplier. The inflatable accumulator should not be modified by machining, welding, or any other means without authorization. The output flow of the inflatable accumulator should be related to the predetermined working requirements and should not exceed the rated value specified by the accumulator manufacturer.  
1. Scope of Application  
Applicable to accumulators with a nominal pressure not exceeding 63 MPa, a nominal volume not exceeding 250 L, a working temperature of -10 to 70°C, and nitrogen/petroleum-based hydraulic oil or emulsion as the working medium.  
2. Technical Requirements  
(1) General Technical Requirements  
1) The nominal pressure and nominal volume (series) of the accumulator should comply with the provisions of GB/T 2352.  
2) The type of the accumulator should comply with the provisions of JB/T 7035 or JB/T 7034.  
3) The type and size of the bladder of the accumulator should comply with the provisions of HG 2331.

2.1.5.2 Installation and Connection Forms of Hydraulic Cylinders for Hydraulic Presses

In hydraulic presses, hydraulic cylinders are installed in two ways: some have the cylinder body directly set on the crossbeam, such as in rubber vulcanizing hydraulic presses. However, most hydraulic cylinders are designed as independent hydraulic components or units, serving as functional parts of the hydraulic transmission system.

Although installing the hydraulic cylinder as an independent unit in the hydraulic press may reduce the strength and stiffness of the crossbeam, it also has its advantages:

a) The hydraulic cylinder can be manufactured by specialized factories, and the main machine manufacturer can purchase it externally.
b) It reduces the difficulty of processing and manufacturing the hydraulic press frame.
c) The design, manufacturing, testing, acceptance, and replacement of hydraulic cylinders are simple and convenient.
d) It better meets the requirements of standardization, serialization, and modular design for hydraulic presses.

There are various installation forms of hydraulic cylinders in hydraulic presses. Although GB/T 9094-2006 specifies 64 installation forms, it still does not cover all existing hydraulic cylinders.

1. Installation Forms with Flange or Boss on Cylinder Body

The front or rear flange or boss for installation of hydraulic cylinders for hydraulic presses is generally directly set (designed) on the cylinder body, rather than on the cylinder end cover. Although the following description still uses front or rear flange or boss, it differs from general hydraulic cylinders and those specified in GB/T 9094-2006.

The cylinder body of hydraulic cylinders has three installation forms: front flange, rear flange, and intermediate flange. The flanges also have three types: circular flange, square flange, and rectangular flange. The flange connection holes are generally through holes, and threaded holes are less common.

(1) Front Circular Flange Installation Form

The far datum face of the front flange is tightly fitted to the inner surface of the crossbeam, and the hydraulic cylinder is fastened to the crossbeam through bolts. During operation, since the two fixed mating surfaces usually squeeze each other, the flange needs to transmit force, resulting in stress concentration at the transition between the flange and the cylinder body (tube), which is prone to fatigue failure. Additionally, the presence of connecting holes in the flange also accelerates this type of failure.

There are also designs where the near datum face of the front flange is tightly fitted to the outer surface of the crossbeam. During operation, the two fixed mating surfaces usually tend to separate, causing a significant increase in the force on the connecting bolts, a decrease in the ability to resist eccentric loads, and no improvement in the stress condition of the cylinder body (tube).

(2) Rear Circular Flange Installation Form

The far datum face of the rear flange is tightly fitted to the inner surface of the crossbeam, and the hydraulic cylinder is fastened to the crossbeam through bolts. During operation, although the two fixed mating surfaces usually squeeze each other and the flange needs to transmit force, the force direction is different from the front flange installation form. Therefore, there is generally no stress concentration problem at the transition between the flange and the cylinder body (tube) for rear flange installation, improving the stress condition of the cylinder body. From the perspective of the stress on the cylinder body (tube), it is a selectable installation form. However, it also has issues such as a larger maximum equivalent stress on the inner wall of the cylinder tube, reduced stability of the hydraulic cylinder, and increased frame height.

There are also designs where the near datum face of the rear flange is tightly fitted to the outer surface of the crossbeam. During operation, the two fixed mating surfaces usually tend to separate, causing a significant increase in the force on the connecting bolts, and the stress condition of the bottom of the rear hydraulic cylinder tends to deteriorate.

(3) Front Boss Installation Form

The far datum face of the front boss is tightly fitted to the inner surface of the crossbeam. A pressure ring fixes the boss, a large nut at the far end of the datum point fastens the cylinder tube, and the pressure ring is fastened to the cylinder bottom through bolts or other forms to ensure this tight fit.

This installation form is the most common and is widely used in medium and small hydraulic presses. However, it is not given in GB/T 9094-2006.

The stress condition of this installation form is similar to that of the front flange installation form, but it is generally slightly improved due to the absence of flange connecting holes. However, the stress concentration problem at the transition between the boss and the cylinder body (tube) still exists.

2. Connection Forms between Piston Rod and Slide Block

GB 28241-2012 and JB/T 4174-2014 define the term "slide block," which is the main component of a hydraulic press that completes the stroke movement and installs the upper die. The piston rod connects to the slide block to transfer energy to it.

GB 2350-1980 specifies three forms of piston rod threads (one internal thread, two external threads). GB/T 9094-2006 provides the end dimensions of piston rods with external threads, the end of piston rods with wrench faces (with internal threads), the end of piston rods with pin holes, the end of piston rods with flanges, and the end dimensions of piston rods with internal threads. However, the length of the external thread at the end of the piston rod differs from the length of the (external) thread of the piston rod specified in GB 2350-1980.

In some designs, a spherical surface is made at the end of the piston rod, and it is fastened by screws through the central threaded hole at the end of the piston rod, the side threaded holes, or a pressure ring. A spherical pad is clamped between the end of the piston rod and the slide block, forming a ball joint connection between the piston rod and the slide block.

(1) Rigid Connection

The rigid connection between the piston rod and the slide block is the most common connection form. Generally, the piston rod is connected to the slide block through accessories.

Due to the different types of piston rod ends and the variety of accessories, there are also various connection forms between the piston rod and the slide block of hydraulic presses. However, it must be ensured that the connection is safe, reliable, and has a long service life. Any components or parts connected to the hydraulic cylinder should be firm to prevent loosening due to impact and vibration. Especially for slide blocks with the risk of accidental falling, a risk assessment should be conducted.

The rigid connection forms between the piston rod and the slide block are as follows:

a) Connection through threaded flange
b) Connection composed of key and pressure ring
c) Direct fastening connection with screws
d) Positioning sleeve connection

In GB/T 9094-2006, the threaded flange is also called piston rod flange.

(2) Swivel connection
When the connection between piston rod and slide block is in the form of pin, ear ring and universal joint bearing, the piston rod and slide block can swing or rotate. This connection form is also relatively common. However, due to the high precision requirements and large nominal force of general hydraulic presses, the above-mentioned swivel connections are not actually used much in hydraulic presses for metal cold working. Instead, a ball joint bearing connection is widely used in hydraulic presses.

The ball surface at the end of the piston rod of the ball joint bearing connection is generally a concave ball surface with material removed, and a center hole with internal thread is generally made in the center; The ball surface at the end of the piston rod and the ball pad block form a pair of ball joints, which should be in a compression state during the working stroke of the hydraulic press. The ball joint bearing connection mainly aims to minimize the eccentric (load) force transmitted from the slide block to the piston rod, or to adapt to the small amount of position change of the slide block during the working stroke.

There is also a special structure of double ball joint bearing connection for hydraulic cylinders used in hydraulic presses, which is characterized by the fact that the piston rod does not directly transmit force to the slide block, but uses an intermediate connecting rod, that is, the piston rod transmits force to the intermediate connecting rod through a ball joint bearing connection, and the other end of the intermediate connecting rod transmits force to the slide block through the ball joint bearing surface. Therefore, there are two double ball joint bearing connections between the piston rod and the slide block. This connection has better elimination of eccentric (load) force effect than a single ball joint bearing connection, so the service life of the hydraulic cylinder is longer. The end parts of the intermediate connecting rod are generally still concave ball surfaces with material removed, but this hydraulic cylinder structure is relatively complex and difficult to achieve in small hydraulic cylinders. At the same time, there are also certain difficulties in the lubrication of the ball surface.

According to the reference materials, the hydraulic cylinder with double ball joint bearing connection has good application effect on large hydraulic presses.

On the oil pump direct drive double column inclined free forging hydraulic press, the main (side) cylinder is generally a plunger type, and its connection mode with the movable crossbeam or the overall frame mostly adopts a double ball joint connecting rod shaft structure.

2.15.3 Metric installation dimensions of 16 MPa series medium single rod hydraulic cylinder

The metric installation dimensions of 16 MPa series medium single rod hydraulic cylinder are specified in JB/T12706.1-2016 to meet the interchangeability requirements of common hydraulic cylinders, which are applicable to round head hydraulic cylinders with cylinder diameters of 25-500mm and square head hydraulic cylinders with cylinder diameters of 200-500mm.

JB/T12706.1-2016 only provides a basic principle. In order to not limit technical applications, hydraulic equipment manufacturers are allowed to flexibly apply it in the design of 16 MPa hydraulic cylinders.

2.15.8 Double-ended stud and tightening torque for cylinder assembly
The cylinder assembly pull rod installation defined in GB/T 17446-2012 is a cylinder installation method that uses the extended part of the cylinder assembly pull rod parallel to the outer side of the cylinder body and is installed from one end or both ends of the cylinder. However, the cylinder assembly should not use pull rods or steel pull rods, but should use double-ended studs.
For electro-hydraulic servo valve controlled hydraulic cylinders, double-ended studs are mainly used for clamping between cylinder head, cylinder body and cylinder bottom, that is, the installation and connection of the hydraulic cylinder itself. This type of hydraulic cylinder with pull rod is still widely used.
The existing standards stipulate that the length of double-ended studs (Grade B) generally does not exceed 500 mm, and lacks necessary technical conditions. If spring washers or elastic washers are used, it is also difficult to determine the tightening torque of the nut.
As shown in Figure 2.16.1, it is a double-ended stud with a transition fit thread at the end screwed into the cylinder head or cylinder bottom end and a fine ordinary thread at the end screwed into the nut, which is for reference only during design.

In the electro-hydraulic servo valve controlled hydraulic cylinder system, there is often relative motion between the hydraulic cylinder and the load it drives. The "Welded End Straight Pipe Joint" has been replaced by the "Cylinder End Straight Through Joint ZZ J" (standard figure 17) in JB/T 966-2005. The main difference between the two is whether there is a cylindrical step on the fixed cylinder end side. The joint body specified in the original JB/T 984-1977 has no cylindrical step, while the cylinder end straight through joint ZZ J specified in JB/T 966-2005 has a cylindrical step.

When using the joint body specified in JB/T 984-1977 and sealing with the "Combination Sealing Washer" specified in JB/T 982-1977, the aperture (countersink) plane diameter of the oil port specified in GB/T 2878.1-2011 is small, and the combination sealing washer may not fit or there may be interference between the joint body specified in JB/T 984-1977 and the upper plane of the aperture of the oil port, making it impossible to seal at the oil port connection. When using the cylinder end straight through joint ZZ J specified in JB/T 966-2005, although there is generally no interference problem with the upper plane of the aperture of the oil port, some specifications of the combination sealing washer may still not fit, causing the same problem, i.e., it is impossible to seal at the oil port connection.

Therefore, if the combination sealing washer specified in JB/T 982-1977 is used to seal the oil port specified in GB/T 2878.1-2011, the corresponding cylinder end straight through joint ZZ J specified in JB/T 966-2005 should be used, and the aperture (countersink) plane diameter of some oil ports should be increased; if the welded straight through pipe joint body specified in JB/T 984-1977 or the welded end straight pipe joint specified in JB/T 966-1977 is still used, the aperture (countersink) plane diameter of the oil port specified in GB/T 2878.1-2011 must be increased. 2.17 Technical Requirements for Hydraulic Cylinder Assembly
Hydraulic cylinder assembly is the process of combining parts that constitute a hydraulic cylinder into components, subassemblies, and assemblies according to the technical requirements (conditions) and precision requirements of the hydraulic cylinder design, until the hydraulic cylinder product is formed. Hydraulic cylinder assembly is a later-stage work in hydraulic cylinder manufacturing and is a key link in forming the hydraulic cylinder product.
A good hydraulic cylinder is not only designed but also assembled.
The assembly of servo hydraulic cylinders should refer to relevant standards such as QJ 14999A and QJ 24778, and the environment of the (servo) hydraulic cylinder assembly site should meet cleanliness requirements.
2.17.1 General Technical Requirements for Hydraulic Cylinder Assembly
1. Technical requirements for assembly in GB/T 7935-2005 "Hydraulic Components - General Technical Conditions"
1) Components should be assembled using qualified parts and purchased parts according to the provisions and requirements of relevant product standards or technical documents. Parts and purchased parts that are deformed, damaged, or rusted shall not be used for assembly.
2) Parts should be cleaned before assembly and should not contain any contaminants such as iron filings, burrs, or fibrous debris.
3) When assembling components, cotton yarn, paper, and other fibrous materials that are prone to shedding should not be used to wipe the inner cavity of the housing, mating surfaces of parts, and inlet/outlet passages.
4) When assembling components, sealing elements that are defective or have exceeded their effective service life shall not be used.
5) Symbols indicating the function of oil ports should be marked near all connecting oil ports of the component.
6) The coating of the exposed non-machined surface of the component should be uniform and consistent in color. Putty shall not be applied before spraying.
7) After the component passes factory inspection, all oil ports should be sealed, dust-proof, and leak-proof.
Here it should be noted that:
1) Articles 4.4 to 4.10 in GB/T 7935-2005 are cited by standards such as JB/T 10205-2010 "Hydraulic Cylinders", JB/T 11588-2013 "Large Hydraulic Cylinders", and DB 44/T 11691-2013 "Servo Hydraulic Cylinders Part 1: Technical Conditions".
2) Generally, sealing elements should not be cleaned.
3) Except for hydraulic cylinders with special structures and special purposes, oil port symbols and reciprocating motion arrows are generally not marked on ordinary hydraulic cylinders.
2. Technical requirements for assembly in JB/T 18292-2014 "Press Machinery - General Technical Conditions"
1) When assembling subassemblies or the entire assembly, gaskets not specified in the technical document are not allowed to be installed.
2) The cleanliness of press machinery assembly should comply with the provisions of the technical document.
3) During the assembly process, machined parts should not be bumped, scratched, or rusted.
4) After assembly, the heads of screws and bolts and the end faces of nuts should be in uniform contact with the plane of the fastened part, without tilting or gaps. The lengths of screws installed in the same position should generally be the same. There should be no loosening of fastened screws, bolts, and nuts, and the fastening force of screws that affect precision should be consistent.
5) Sealing elements should not have damage. Before assembly, sealing elements and sealing surfaces should be coated with grease. When assembling overlapping sealing rings, the rings should be pressed tightly against each other.
3. Technical requirements for assembly in JB/T 38181-2014 "Hydraulic Press - Technical Conditions"
1) The hydraulic press should be assembled according to the assembly process specification. Parts and their surfaces, as well as the lips of seals, should not be damaged due to assembly. All assembled parts (including purchased parts and outsourced parts) should meet the requirements.
2) Important fixed mating surfaces should fit tightly. After being securely fastened, they should be inspected with a 0.05mm feeler gauge, and the depth to which the feeler gauge can be inserted should not exceed 1/4 of the contact surface. The total length of the areas where the feeler gauge can be inserted on the contact surface should not exceed 1/10 of the circumference.
3) For hydraulic cylinders with support ring sealing structures, the support ring should be moderately tight and securely locked. Moving parts that slide down quickly by their own weight (including pistons, movable crossbeams, or sliders) should not have any obstruction during rapid downward movement.
4) All pipelines, pipe joints, flanges, and other fixed and movable connection sealing points should be reliably connected, well sealed, and should not have any external leakage of oil.
4. Technical requirements for assembly in JB/T 10205-2010 "Hydraulic Cylinders"
1) Cleanliness requirements: The solid particle contamination level of the hydraulic oil inside the hydraulic cylinder body shall not be higher than Grade -/19/16 specified in GB/T 14039-2002.
2) The assembly of hydraulic cylinders should comply with the provisions of Articles 4.4 to 4.7 in GB/T 7935-2005. After assembly, the hydraulic cylinder should move freely, and there should be no damage to all external connecting threads, edges of oil ports, etc.

(3) Appearance requirements: The appearance should comply with the provisions of 4.8 to 4.9 in GB/T7935-2005.

The appearance inspection of the cylinder should meet the following requirements:

a) For cylinders with flange structure, the radial misalignment of the mating surfaces of the two flanges should be ≤0.5 mm.

b) The surface of cast and forged parts should be smooth and free of defects.

c) The welding should be flat, uniform, and aesthetically pleasing, without welding slag, spatter, etc.

2) Parts should be cleaned and washed before assembly, and should be free of burrs, flash, oxide scale, corrosion, chips, oil stains, colorants, rust preventive oil, and dust.

2.17.2 Specific Technical Requirements for Hydraulic Cylinder Assembly

1. Assembly preparation

1) According to the production order, prepare drawings, technical documents, and job guidance documents.

2) According to the assembly batch, prepare all parts and components once according to the detailed list or detailed table in the assembly drawing.

3) Recheck the main matching dimensions of parts and components. When using the grouping selection assembly method, parts and components can be grouped at this time; check the certificates of conformity of outsourced and purchased parts and components to ensure that all parts and components entering the assembly are qualified products within the effective service life.

4) The working of the stroke adjustment mechanism of the adjustable stroke cylinder should be sensitive and reliable and meet the accuracy requirements.

5) The working surfaces and mating surfaces of the main parts and components are not allowed to have defects such as rust, scratches, and knocks. All seals (including dust seals, retaining rings, support rings, etc.) should not have any damage.

6) Before assembly, burrs should be removed from each part, and sharp corners and edges not shown in the drawing should be rounded and blunted.

7) Clean each part and component carefully and achieve the cleanliness requirements, but generally do not include seals.

8) The cleaned parts and components should be dried before assembly and should be assembled in time; parts and components that cannot be assembled in time should be wrapped or covered with plastic cloth (film).

9) Make a good inventory and registration of tools, process fixtures, and low-value consumables used for assembly.

2. Assembly

(1) General technical requirements for seal assembly

The function of seals is to prevent leakage or make the leakage amount meet the design requirements. Reasonable assembly process and method can ensure the reliability and durability (life) of seals.

1) Check each part and component according to the drawing, especially the chamfers, lead-in chamfers, and fillets (blunting). There should be no burrs, flashes, etc., and the surfaces of grooves on mating (matching) parts and seals should not have tool marks (such as spiral marks, cross-cutting marks, trembling-cutting marks, etc.), scratches, knocks, or rust.

2) Before assembly, each part and component must be carefully and thoroughly cleaned.
435:
Cleaning, and drying or wiping, especially the grooves of each seal must not retain cleaning liquid (oil) or other residues.

3) After cleaning, each component should be assembled in time; if it cannot be assembled in time, it should be wrapped or covered with plastic cloth (film).

4) Check the specifications, dimensions, and surface quality of the seals according to the drawing, and take them out in the required quantity at one time; seals contaminated on the surface (such as with oil stains, debris, dust, or sand, etc.) cannot be directly used for assembly.

5) Seals that have been disassembled or used generally cannot be used again for assembly, especially O-rings, coaxial seals, dust seals, and support rings (except for pre-assembly), retaining rings, etc.

6) An appropriate amount of lubricating oil (grease) should be applied to the mating surfaces of each matching (mating) part before assembly.

7) The lubricating oil (grease) applied during assembly must not contain solid particles or mechanical debris, including graphite, molybdenum disulfide grease, etc. It is best to use the special lubricating oil (grease) specified by the seal manufacturer.

8) Rubber seals are best assembled at a temperature of 23°C±2°C to 27°C±2°C; seals stored at low temperature must reach room temperature before assembly; seals (or parts with grooves) that need to be heated for assembly should be heated with hydraulic oil not exceeding 90°C, and should be assembled after returning to room temperature and cooling to shrink and set.

9) Various seals must not be overstretched during assembly, nor rolled for installation, or subjected to local strong pulling, pressing, twisting (rotating), folding, or strong compression (squeezing), etc.

10) For repairing surface damage of components, sandpaper (cloth) must not be used for grinding. Fine oilstone can be used for grinding, and it should be cleaned after repair.

11) Seals must not be omitted or over-installed. The installation direction and position of the seals must be correct, and the assembled components should be assembled as a whole in time.

12) During final assembly, if the piston or cylinder head (guide sleeve) needs to pass through oil (flow) holes, key slots, threads, or tool withdrawal slots, necessary protective measures must be taken to protect the seals (parts) from damage.

13) After final assembly, dust plugs (caps) should be used to seal the oil ports of each component, and seals, installation tools, including special tools and other low-value consumables, such as wiping cloths, should be counted.

(2) Technical requirements for O-ring assembly

1) Ensure that the shaft and hole of the mating parts have good coaxiality, so that the clearance around the circumference is uniform.

2) During the assembly process, prevent the O-ring from being scratched, abraded, or cut. When inserting it into the hole or the end of the shaft, there should be a sufficiently long guide cone (incline chamfer), and the intersection of the cone surface and the cylindrical surface should be rounded and smoothly transitioned.

3) If the O-ring needs to pass through oil holes, threads, tool withdrawal slots, elastic retaining ring grooves, or other seal grooves that may scratch, cut, or squeeze it during assembly, necessary protective measures must be taken, such as plugging, filling, shielding, or isolating, to ensure that the O-ring is not damaged during the assembly process. If necessary, special assembly tools should be designed, manufactured, and used.

4) An appropriate amount of grease should be applied to the groove first, and then the O-ring should be installed. Before assembly, an appropriate amount of lubricating oil (grease) should be applied to the mating surfaces of each mating (mating) part; after assembly, the mating parts should be able to move freely, and prevent the O-ring from twisting or rolling.

5) For O-rings installed in a stretched or compressed state, in order to restore the cross-section to a circular shape after pre-stretching or pre-compression, after the O-ring is installed in the groove, it should be left for a proper time before assembling the mating (mating) parts.

6) When installing and removing O-rings, installation and removal tools should be used. The material and style of the installation and removal tools should be selected appropriately, and the end and cutting edge should be blunt. It is forbidden to use sharp and hard tools such as steel needles to pry the O-ring to avoid damaging its surface.

7) O-rings and retaining rings that have been installed, removed, or used must not be used again for assembly.

8) Ensure that the retaining ring for the O-ring and the O-ring are in the correct relative position.

(3) Technical requirements for lip seal assembly

1) Check the specifications, dimensions, and surface quality of the seal, especially the lips (seal edges) must not have defects such as damage; at the same time, check the dimensions and tolerances of each component, surface roughness, chamfers (guide) angles, and fillets, and there must be no burrs or flashes.

It is particularly emphasized that the piston seal and piston rod seal must be clearly distinguished, especially the YX-shaped seal ring for holes and the YX-shaped seal ring for shafts.

2) When assembling the lip seal, the direction must be correct; for the lip seal with a retaining ring, the relative position of the retaining ring and the seal must be correct.

3) Before installation, an appropriate amount of lubricating oil (grease) should be applied to the surface of the mating parts, an appropriate amount of grease should be applied to the seal groove, and the groove at the end of the lip seal should also be filled with grease, and the air should be discharged.

4) Special tools are generally required to install lip seals, and they can be made according to the type recommended by the seal manufacturer. If the lip seal needs to pass through oil holes, threads, tool withdrawal slots, or other seal grooves during installation, special measures must be taken to protect the seal from damage. The usual practice is to first install a special sleeve at the through part, or install 3 (4) petal retaining rings in the seal groove.

5) Lip seals (or parts with grooves) that need to be heated for assembly should be heated with hydraulic oil not exceeding 90°C, and should be assembled with the mating (mating) parts after returning to room temperature and cooling to shrink and set; water must not be used to heat lip seals, especially seals made of polyurethane and polyamide materials.

6) The pressure ring of the V-shaped seal, the V-shaped ring (with or without fabric), and the support ring (elastic seal ring) must be arranged and combined correctly, and must not be adjusted too tightly during initial adjustment.

7) Generally, a pre-assembly should be carried out after only the support ring is installed to check the coaxiality of the mating parts and the assembly of the support ring, and check the movement of the piston and piston rod if possible to avoid 424 Hydraulic Cylinder Manual
436:
To prevent rigid interference.
8) After assembly, there should be no jamming or uneven resistance during the reciprocating motion of the piston and piston rod throughout their full stroke.
(4) Technical Requirements for Assembling Coaxial Seals
Coaxial seals are composite seals composed of a plastic ring and a rubber ring, with the plastic ring providing the entire friction sealing surface. Therefore, they need to be assembled in steps.
The rubber ring must be assembled first. Please refer to the technical requirements for assembling O-rings mentioned above.
1) For piston seals, coaxial seals generally require heating for assembly. It is advisable to heat the plastic ring in hydraulic oil at a temperature not exceeding 90°C until it becomes highly elastic and stretchable. It may be necessary to heat the piston as well, which facilitates the cooling, shrinking, and shaping of the plastic ring.
2) For piston seals, coaxial seals generally require specialized installation tools and shrinking/shaping tools, which can be manufactured and used according to the type recommended by the seal manufacturer.
If it needs to pass through other seal grooves, relief grooves, etc., it is best to consider them in the installation tool.
The surface roughness of the contact surface between the shaping tool for the plastic ring and the plastic ring should be comparable to the surface roughness of the mating part.
3) Coaxial seals assembled after heating must be cooled to room temperature together with the piston before being assembled into the cylinder (tube). If coaxial seals for piston rods are installed using heating, they must also be cooled to room temperature before being assembled with the piston rod.
4) For piston rod seals, coaxial seals can also be assembled after heating, but the plastic ring needs to be bent into a concave shape before assembly. After assembly, a tapered mandrel shaping tool is generally used for shaping. Common issues include forgetting to install the rubber ring and incorrect installation direction of the plastic ring. For example, stepped coaxial seals are unidirectional seals and have specific directional requirements during installation.
5) Before installing the piston into the cylinder (tube) or the piston rod into the guide sleeve or cylinder head, the angle and length of the chamfer at the end of the cylinder (tube) and piston rod must be checked. The intersection between the tapered surface and the cylindrical surface must be rounded and smoothly transitioned, and the surface roughness must meet the requirements specified in the drawing.
6) Generally, coaxial seals should be installed first in a set of seals.
7) Pay attention to lubrication and strictly prohibit dry assembly.
(5) Technical Requirements for Assembling Support Rings
The support rings commonly used now are made of wear-resistant plastic materials and serve to support the piston or piston rod of the hydraulic cylinder, preventing direct contact and collision between moving metal parts, and providing radial support and (axial) guiding functions.
In a certain sense, support rings can be considered as non-metallic bearings.
1) Check the dimensions and tolerances of the groove according to the drawing, especially the fillet at the bottom and edge of the groove. If possible, perform a pre-assembly to inspect the concentricity and movement of each component.
If the end of the hydraulic cylinder is equipped with a cushioning device, it is necessary to check whether the cushioning plunger interferes or collides with the cushioning hole.
2) Support rings with cut-type notches need to be cut and trimmed according to Appendix A of the GB/T15242.2-2017 standard, but the width of the cut notch of the support ring generally cannot be less than the specified value.
3) For batch products, a pre-shaping tool for the support ring should be made.
4) Generally, the support ring should be installed last in a set of seals. If there are multiple support rings in a set of seals, their notch positions should be staggered during installation.
5) Fix the support ring in the groove by applying an appropriate amount of grease. Note that applying too much grease is not conducive to fixing the support ring.
6) Before installing the piston into the cylinder (tube), the angle and length of the chamfer at the end of the cylinder (tube) must be checked. The intersection between the tapered surface and the cylindrical surface must be rounded and smoothly transitioned, and the surface roughness must meet the requirements specified in the drawing. Otherwise, the most likely issue during piston installation is the support ring falling out of the groove.
7) The support ring should be installed with the same precision as a bearing, and methods such as hammering, pressing, or using sandpaper (cloth) to grind and reduce the thickness of the support ring are not allowed. Additionally, using thin sheets (films) between the bottom of the groove and the support ring to reduce the fitting clearance is not allowed.
8) Support rings that have been used for pre-assembly should not be used again for assembly in other situations.
(6) Other Assembly Technical Requirements
1) Ensure the correct positioning of each component of the hydraulic cylinder according to the drawings and technical documents.
2) All threaded connections should be tightened according to the torque specified in the design. For those with specified requirements, follow the regulations, such as the tightening torque of screws for the CD250 and CD350 series heavy-duty hydraulic cylinders (see Table 2-337); for those without specified requirements, refer to Table 2-316 (fine-pitch bolts or nuts) and Table 2-332 (coarse-pitch bolts, screws, and nuts).
3) Important fixed mating surfaces should fit tightly; any components installed or connected to the hydraulic cylinder should be secure.
4) After assembly, ensure that the hydraulic cylinder moves freely, especially for those designed with end cushioning plungers, there should be no interference or collision during movement; there should be no damage to external threaded connections, port edges, etc.
5) Unless otherwise specified, the tolerance for the stroke length of a general hydraulic cylinder should comply with the provisions in Table 9 of JB/T10205.
6) For hydraulic cylinders with stroke positioning or limit devices, the deviation of the stroke positioning or limit should comply with the technical (accuracy) requirements or relevant standard regulations.
7) The surface of the hydraulic cylinder should be clean, with smooth and natural rounded corners, flat welds, and no burrs or sharp edges.
8) The nameplate should be clear and correct, and the installation should be secure and flat.
9) The painting of the hydraulic cylinder should comply with the provisions of JB/T5673, and the color of the topcoat can be determined according to user requirements. The surface of the piston rod and positioning valve rod should not be painted.

2.18 Technical Requirements for Hydraulic Cylinder Operation
The technical requirements for trial operation and/or operation of hydraulic cylinders are expressed differently in the relevant standards for hydraulic cylinders, as shown in Table 2-338.
For hydraulic presses (machines), technical requirements are generally provided for no-load operation. For example, JB/T12996.2-2017 states: "There should be no sticking, crawling, or jumping phenomena during the operation of the ram and worktable."
Considering the above standards comprehensively, the starting and operating states of hydraulic cylinders that have passed factory tests should be described according to Table 2-339. If conditions permit, high-temperature, high-pressure, and their combined operating conditions should also be tested according to the standard. The test results should comply with the standard requirements.
Hydraulic cylinders are usually just a component in a hydraulic system or a part in a hydraulic press (machine). The trial operation and/or operation of hydraulic cylinders must meet the technical conditions of the hydraulic press (machine). Please refer to Chapter 4 for details.
