Chapter 3 Manufacturing of Hydraulic Cylinders
3.1 Commonly Used Machine Tools and Equipment for Manufacturing Hydraulic Cylinders
3.1.1 Overview
This section mainly introduces metal cutting machine tools, which can be classified into general-purpose machine tools, specialized machine tools, dedicated machine tools, and combined machine tools.
Commonly used metal cutting machine tools for manufacturing hydraulic cylinders include lathes, milling machines, drilling machines, boring machines, grinding machines, sawing machines, thread processing machine tools (pipe thread lathes), and machining centers. CNC machine tools are now widely used. CNC machine tools are machine tools that process workpieces according to digital information instructions issued by the control system based on pre-programmed programs. They mainly include CNC hydraulic cylinder lathes, CNC scraping and rolling lathes, CNC deep hole honing machines, vertical internal cylindrical honing machines, external cylindrical grinding machines, their types and parameters, technical conditions, and accuracy inspections.
The types and parameters of machine tools determine their main purposes and generally limit the workpieces that can be processed, as well as their sizes, shapes, and even surface accuracy. They are the main basis for selecting workpiece manufacturing methods and determining workpiece machining processes, and also an important guarantee for the feasibility and economy of workpiece manufacturing. The technical conditions of machine tools are not only the basis for machine tool manufacturing and acceptance, but also the basis for troubleshooting when machine tools or products have problems.
The geometric accuracy, positioning accuracy and repeatability, working accuracy requirements, inspection methods, and corresponding tolerances of machine tools are the main basis for judging whether the mechanical machining process of workpieces is reasonable. The accuracy of workpiece machining generally cannot exceed the accuracy that can be achieved by the test pieces during the accuracy inspection of the machine tool's working accuracy.
Some machine tools are hydraulically driven, and their technical conditions clearly specify requirements for hydraulic systems and hydraulic cylinders, etc., so they can be used as the basis for designing and manufacturing hydraulic cylinders for these machine tools. The positioning accuracy and repeatability of the linear axes of these hydraulic transmission manual or automatic control machine tools can also be used as a reference for inspecting proportional/servo control hydraulic cylinders.
3.1.2 CNC Hydraulic Cylinder Lathe
JB/T 13092.1-2017 "CNC Hydraulic Cylinder Lathe Part 1: Accuracy Inspection" stipulates the geometric accuracy, positioning accuracy and repeatability, working accuracy requirements, inspection methods and corresponding tolerances of CNC hydraulic cylinder lathes; JB/T 13092.2-2017 "CNC Hydraulic Cylinder Lathe Part 2: Technical Conditions" stipulates the manufacturing and acceptance requirements of CNC hydraulic cylinder lathes, applicable to CNC hydraulic cylinder lathes with a maximum turning diameter of the bed body up to 1250 mm and a maximum workpiece length up to 5000 mm (hereinafter referred to as the machine tool).

7. No-load test

(1) Temperature rise test

The main moving mechanism of the machine tool shall start from the lowest speed and run at each level of speed in turn (run at low, medium and high speeds for stepless speed change mechanism). The running time at each speed shall not be less than 2 min, and the running time at the highest speed shall not be less than 1 h, so that the spindle bearing reaches a stable temperature. Check the temperature and temperature rise of the spindle bearing. The temperature shall not exceed 70 ℃, and the temperature rise shall not exceed 40 ℃.

(2) Inspection of main motion and feed motion

1) For the moving parts on each linear axis, carry out no-load test at low, medium, high and fast feed speeds respectively. The motion shall be stable and reliable, with no vibration at high speed and no obvious crawling at low speed.

2) The actual deviation of spindle speed and feed speed shall not exceed ±5% of the instruction value or the value indicated on the nameplate.

(3) Function test

1) Use buttons, switches or manual operation to carry out the following action tests on the machine tool to test the flexibility and reliability of the actions.

① Select any spindle speed to start the spindle for forward rotation, reverse rotation, stop (including braking) continuous operation test, with no less than 10 times of continuous operation.

② The spindle shall be tested for speed conversion at low, medium and high speeds.

③ Select any feed speed (or feed amount), and continuously operate the start, feed and stop actions. On the full stroke of Z axis and X axis, carry out work feed and fast feed tests. The fast feed test of Z axis and X axis can be carried out on more than 1/2 of the full stroke. The continuous operation in forward and reverse directions shall not be less than 7 times.

④ On the full stroke of Z axis and X axis, carry out the conversion test of low, medium and high feed speeds (or feed amounts).

⑤ Use a hand pulse generator or single-step to test the feed of the slide plate and slide plate.

⑥ Use manual or automatic operation to test the movement of the tailstock and tailstock sleeve on its full stroke.

⑦ For the moving parts with locking mechanism, carry out the locking test at any position on the full stroke. The slide plate of inclined and vertical guide rails shall not fall after cutting off the power.

⑧ Carry out the operation test of the chip removal device.

⑨ Carry out the function test of various indicator lights, control buttons, DNC communication transmission equipment and temperature regulating device of the numerical control device.

⑩ Carry out the function test of the safety, insurance and protection devices of the machine tool.

 〓 〓 Carry out the sealing, lubrication and cooling performance test of the hydraulic, lubrication and cooling systems, which should be easy to adjust, flexible in action, well lubricated, well cooled, and no leakage in each system.

2) Use numerical control instructions to carry out the following action tests on the machine tool to test the flexibility and reliability of the actions.

① Carry out the forward rotation, reverse rotation, stop and speed change test of the spindle (for mechanical stepped speed change, carry out the speed conversion test at each level of speed; for stepless speed change, carry out the low, medium and high speed change test).

② Carry out the low, medium and high feed speed (feed amount) and fast feed change test of the feed mechanism.

③ Carry out various positioning tests of the rotary tool post.

④ Test the reliability and flexibility of the functions of overtravel protection of feed coordinates, manual data input, coordinate position display, return to reference point, program sequence number indication and retrieval, program pause, program end, program elimination, individual part feed, linear interpolation, circular arc interpolation, linear cutting cycle, taper cutting cycle, thread cutting cycle, circular arc cutting cycle, tool position compensation, pitch compensation, gap compensation, etc.

(4) No-load power test (spot check)

The no-load power of the main transmission system shall meet the requirements of the design document.

(5) No-load time

Use the numerical control program to simulate the working state without cutting for continuous no-load test. No fault shall occur during the whole operation process of the machine tool. The continuous no-load time is 36 h, and the time of each cycle shall not exceed 15 min. The stop time between each cycle shall not exceed 1 min.

(3) Technical requirements for main components
1) Requirements for hydraulic system components are as follows:
① The design of the hydraulic system should comply with the provisions of GB/T 3766.
② All used hydraulic components should comply with the provisions of GB/T7935.
③ The technical requirements for hydraulic cylinders should comply with the provisions of JB/T10205. When installing the hydraulic cylinder, if the structure allows, the inlet and outlet positions should be on the top or other easy-to-install surfaces.
2) Technical requirements for hydraulic stations are as follows:
① The pump and motor spindle should rotate flexibly without any jamming.
② The hydraulic station should be tested in conjunction with the electrical device, and the actions of all hydraulic components should be correct and without jamming. A pressure test should be conducted at 1.5 times the working pressure, and the sealing condition of all hydraulic components should be good.
③ The hydraulic station should operate smoothly without any abnormal sounds, noise, or vibration.
3) Requirements for mechanical structure components are as follows:
① The selected high-quality carbon structural steel and carbon structural steel materials should comply with the provisions of GB/T 699 and GB/T 700 respectively; the selected low-alloy high-strength steel should comply with the provisions of GB/T15591; the selected cast carbon steel parts should comply with the provisions of GB/T11352; the selected alloy tool steel should comply with the provisions of GB/T1299.
② The chemical composition content and porosity of the bed casting should comply with the provisions of GB/T9439; the surface hardness of the guide rail after high-frequency induction hardening should reach 50-55 HRC, and the effective hardness depth should be 1.5-2.5 mm. The casting should undergo annealing treatment and comply with the provisions of JB/T7711.
③ The straightness error of the bed guide rail in the height direction and front-rear direction (with the operator's side as the front) should not be greater than 0.01/1000.
④ The saddle of the spindle box should be lined with plastic and scraped.
⑤ After installing the workpiece head, pressure head, and spindle box, the position tolerance of their centers relative to the bed guide rail surface should be less than 0.02 mm, and the concentricity tolerance between the three centers should be less than ф0.01 mm.
⑥ After installing the ball screw and trapezoidal screw, the position tolerance of their centers relative to the bed guide rail surface should be less than 0.02 mm.
⑦ The oil tank should not have any leakage.
⑧ The lubrication system piping should not be blocked, and the joints should not have any oil leakage.
4) Requirements for electrical control components are as follows:
① The operating mechanism and its accessories should operate flexibly, and the contacts of various auxiliary switches should be correctly and reliably closed and opened; before use, a simulated operation test should be conducted, and the actions of all electrical components (including electromagnets) should be correct and reliable.
② The continuity of the protective grounding circuit of the electrical control components should comply with the provisions of 18.2.2 in GB 52261-2008 (2019); the insulation resistance should comply with the provisions of 18.3 in GB/T52261-2008 (2019); the withstand voltage should comply with the provisions of 18.4 in GB/T52261-2008 (2019).
(4) Requirements for installation foundation
The ground foundation should be flat, with a flatness error less than 2 cm/10 m, and the thickness of the cement foundation should be greater than 200 mm.
(5) Safety protection
1) Couplings and exposed rotating parts should be equipped with protective covers.
2) Cables and wires should be equipped with protective conduits.
3) The mechanical equipment should be equipped with an emergency automatic shutdown switch for fault states; the electrical equipment should be equipped with an automatic alarm signal and an automatic power-off shutdown program for emergency states.
4) The program should include overload protection and interlock protection.
5) Warning signs should be posted on moving parts.
(6) Appearance requirements
1) The coating should be flat, smooth, and uniform in color, without sagging, peeling, missing coating, scratches, or other defects.
2) Hydraulic components and electrical components should have clear and durable markings.
3) The surface of the weld seam should be flat and smooth, without defects such as incomplete welding, missing welding, or slag inclusion. Important parts should undergo non-destructive testing.

6. No-Load Operation Test of Machine Tool 
(1) Temperature Rise Test and Inspection of Main Motion and Feed Motion 
1) The main motion (including grinding rod box) mechanism of the machine tool should start from the lowest speed, and run in sequence. For the machine tool with stepless speed change, no less than 1 0 kinds of speeds including low, medium and high speeds should be run; for the machine tool with stepped speed change, no-load operation test should be carried out from the lowest to the highest level by level. The running time of each gear speed should not be less than 2 min, and the running time at the highest speed should not be less than 1 h, so that the spindle bearing reaches a stable temperature, and the temperature and temperature rise are measured near the spindle center bearing, and the temperature should not exceed 6 0 ℃, and the temperature rise should not exceed 3 0 ℃. During operation at various speeds, the operation should be stable, and the working mechanism should be normal and reliable. 
2) The moving parts on each linear axis are respectively subjected to no-load operation test at low, medium and high feed speeds and fast speed, and the movement should be stable and reliable, with no vibration at high speed and no obvious crawling at low speed. 
3) Under no-load operation conditions, the actual deviation of spindle speed and feed speed at each level of stepped transmission should not exceed -2 %~6 % of the set value; the actual deviation of spindle speed and feed speed of stepless transmission should not exceed ±1 0 % of the set value.

⑥ For the machine tool's safety, insurance, and protection devices, as well as the control, interlocking, and protection functions of the electrical system, necessary tests should be conducted. The functions should be reliable, and the operation should be flexible and accurate.
⑦ For the machine tool's hydraulic, lubrication, cooling, and pneumatic systems, operation tests should be conducted. The machine tool should be well-sealed, adequately cooled, and well-lubricated, with flexible and reliable operation. No leakage should occur in any of the systems.
⑧ For the machine tool's various auxiliary devices, tests should be conducted. The operation should be flexible and reliable.
2) Numerical Control Function Test (Using numerical control programs to operate the machine tool's components for testing).
① Using medium speed, continuous start-stop (including braking) and positioning operation tests should be conducted 10 times in both forward and reverse directions for the spindle. The operation should be flexible and reliable.
② For a continuously variable speed spindle, speed change operation tests should be conducted at low, medium, and high speeds. For a stepped speed spindle, tests should be conducted at each speed level. The operation should be flexible and reliable.
③ For the moving parts along each linear axis, continuous start-stop and incremental feed operation tests should be conducted in both forward and reverse directions at medium feed rate. The operation should be flexible, reliable, and accurate.
④ For the feed system, at least low, medium, and high feed rate and rapid traverse speed change operation tests should be conducted. The operation should be flexible and reliable.
⑤ For the various instructions that the machine tool is capable of, such as program pause and emergency stop, as well as the clamping and unclamping of related components and tools, and the start and stop of hydraulic, cooling, pneumatic, and lubrication systems, numerical control function tests should be conducted one by one. The functions should be reliable, and the operation should be flexible and accurate.
(3) Continuous No-Load Operation Test for the Machine Tool
1) The continuous no-load operation test should be conducted after the manual function test and numerical control function test, and before the precision inspection.
2) The continuous no-load operation test should use a numerical control program that includes various main functions of the machine tool to operate the machine tool's components for continuous no-load operation. The total continuous no-load operation time should not be less than 48 hours.
3) Throughout the entire continuous no-load operation process, the machine tool's operation should be normal, smooth, and reliable, without any malfunctions. Otherwise, the operation should be repeated.
4) The continuous no-load operation program should include the following content:
① The spindle speed should include more than 5 types of forward rotation, reverse rotation, stop, and positioning at low, medium, and high speeds. Generally, the high-speed operation time should not be less than 10% of the time used by each cycle program.
② The feed rate should combine the movement of components along each axis at low, medium, and high speeds and rapid traverse in both forward and reverse directions, running within the full stroke range. Arbitrary points can be selected for positioning. The use of the magnification switch is not allowed during operation. The time for high feed rate and rapid traverse should not be less than 10% of the time used by each cycle program.
③ Coordinated operation of each linked axis.
④ Operation of special attachments.
⑤ The pause time for each cycle program should not exceed 0.5 minutes.
7. Load Test for the Machine Tool
(1) Test of Maximum Torque of the Main Drive System
1) Within the constant torque speed range of the machine tool spindle, select an appropriate spindle speed and conduct the test using the grinding method. Change the feed rate or grinding depth to make the main drive system of the machine tool reach the maximum torque specified in the design.
2) The test piece material is 45 steel, and the cutting tool is a honing head.
3) During the test, the transmission system and speed change mechanism of the machine tool should work normally and reliably, with smooth and accurate operation. For machine tools produced in batches, the test can be conducted at 2/3 of the maximum cutting torque, but periodic spot checks of the maximum torque should be conducted.
(2) Test of Main Drive System Reaching Maximum Power (Spot Check)
1) Within the constant power speed range of the machine tool, select an appropriate spindle speed and conduct the test using the grinding method. Change the feed rate or grinding depth to make the main motor of the machine tool reach the rated power or the maximum power specified in the design.
2) The test piece material is 45 steel, and the cutting tool is a honing head.
3) During the test, the transmission system and speed change mechanism of the machine tool should work normally and reliably, with smooth operation and no obvious vibration.
8. Minimum Setting Unit Test
(1) Test Method
First, use rapid traverse to move the moving parts along the linear axis a certain distance in the positive (or negative) direction, stop, then give a number of instructions for the minimum setting unit in the same direction, and stop again. Use this position as the reference position, give one instruction each time, and give a total of 20 instructions for the minimum setting unit in the same direction, moving the parts. Measure the stopping position of each instruction. From the final position mentioned above, continue to give a number of instructions for the minimum setting unit in the same direction, stop, then give a number of instructions for the minimum setting unit in the negative (or positive) direction to make the moving parts return to approximately the above final measurement position. The stopping positions of these positive and negative instructions for the minimum setting unit are not measured. Then, starting from the above final position, give one instruction each time, and give a total of 20 instructions for the minimum setting unit in the same direction, moving the parts. Measure the stopping position of each instruction.

1) Test Method. The moving parts of each linear axis perform 5 return-to-origin Po tests at high speed in the same moving direction from any point on the stroke. ② The inspection and acceptance of the machine tool include the following contents:

2) Empty Running Test of Machine Tool

① All joints or exposed joints of the hydraulic, pneumatic, cooling, and lubrication systems and other parts of the machine tool should not leak (seep) oil, leak (seep) water, or leak (seep) air. The coolant should not be mixed into the hydraulic system and the lubrication system.

② The main motion mechanism of the machine tool should run from the lowest speed in sequence, and the running time of each speed level should not be less than 2 min. JB/T7418.1—2019 "External cylindrical grinder Part 1: Type and parameters" specifies the type and parameters of general-purpose external cylindrical grinder, which is applicable to the newly designed worktable mobile and grinding wheel frame mobile external cylindrical grinder. 1. Type and parameters
1) According to the overall layout, the external cylindrical grinder can be divided into two types: worktable mobile and grinding wheel frame mobile.
2) According to the performance characteristics, the external cylindrical grinder can be generally divided into:
① External cylindrical grinder (ordinary type).
② Universal external cylindrical grinder (universal type).

2. Technical conditions
(1) General requirements
1) J B / T 7 4 1 8.2—2 0 1 5 is the concretization and supplement of G B / T 9 0 6 1—2 0 0 6 "General technical conditions for metal cutting machine tools", G B / T2 5 3 7 6—
2 0 1 0 "General technical conditions for machined parts of metal cutting machine tools", G B / T 2 5 3 7 3—2 0 1 0 "General technical conditions for assembly of metal cutting machine tools" and other standards. When accepting the machine tool according to J B / T 7 4 1 8.2—2 0 1 5, the remaining acceptance items not concretized by J B / T 7 4 1 8.2—2 0 1 5 in the above standards should be inspected at the same time.
2) External cylindrical grinder (hereinafter referred to as the machine tool) should be divided into accuracy grades according to the provisions of G B / T 2 5 3 7 2—2 0 1 0 "Accuracy grading of metal cutting machine tools", ordinary grade is grade IV accuracy machine tool, precision grade is grade III accuracy machine tool, high precision grade is grade II accuracy machine tool.
(2) Accessories and tools
1) The machine tool should be equipped with accessories and tools to ensure basic performance, which should be specified by design according to the structural characteristics of the machine tool.
2) According to user requirements, special accessories should be provided according to the provisions of the agreement (or contract).
(3) Safety and hygiene
1) The reciprocating moving parts such as worktable or pallet and grinding wheel frame with inertial impact should be provided with limit insurance devices to prevent collision, and safety measures should be taken to prevent collision for fast approach of grinding wheel frame (such as setting buffer devices, etc.).
2) Safety interlock devices should be set for workpiece rotation, tailstock foot pedal hydraulic cylinder or motorized tailstock sleeve movement, grinding wheel frame fast movement, etc. to control the action sequence.
3) Bed guide rail, grinding wheel frame pad plate guide rail should be provided with safety protection devices to prevent chips and cutting fluid from splashing into the guide rail surface.
4) There should be no abnormal sharp noise and impact noise when the machine tool is running. Under no-load running conditions, the noise of the machine tool should be tested according to the provisions of G B / T1 6 7 6 9—2 0 0 8 (has been repealed), and the noise sound pressure level of the machine tool should not be greater than the provisions of Table 3.2.7.

④ Mating surfaces between the internal grinding tool support and its mating parts.
⑤ Mating surfaces between the headstock housing and its mating rotating base.
⑥ Mating surfaces between the wheel spindle housing and its mating rotating base.
⑦ Mating surfaces between the upper and lower worktables.
⑧ Mating surfaces between the upper worktable pressure plate and the upper and lower worktables (except for special structures).

5) The guide rails of the worktable or pallet, wheel spindle guide, and their mating parts should be assessed according to the requirements of "Hydrostatic, Sliding Guide Rails" in G B/T2 5 3 7 3—2 0 1 0.

(5) Bench Lathe No-Load Test
1) Temperature and Temperature Rise Test of Lathe.
① The spindle of the wheel frame (with wheel) should undergo a no-load test run, starting from the lowest speed and running sequentially to the highest speed or the highest speed specified in the design. It should run for at least 1 h at the highest speed to stabilize the temperature of the spindle bearing of the wheel frame. For ordinary precision lathes, the temperature and temperature rise of the spindle sliding bearing should be checked in the oil pool of the wheel frame, and the temperature should not exceed 55°C, and the temperature rise should not exceed 25°C. The temperature and temperature rise of the bearing should be checked at the outer shell near the rolling bearing of the spindle of the wheel frame, and the temperature should not exceed 65°C, and the temperature rise should not exceed 35°C. The temperature and temperature rise of precision and high-precision lathes are specified by the design.
② In the temperature rise test of the hydraulic system, the method of measuring the temperature and temperature rise of the oil in the bed body oil pool (or separate oil tank oil pool) should conform to G B/T 2 3 5 7 2—2 0 0 9.
2) Test of Main Motion and Feed Motion.
① The speed deviation of the grinding wheel spindle under no-load condition should not exceed -5% to 0% of the design specified value.
② The speed deviation of the main shaft of the headstock and other parts under no-load conditions: For stepless speed change transmission, it is ±5% of the design specified value (speed label) (sampling inspection); for stepless speed change transmission, it is ±10% of the design specified value (speed table has digital position point).
③ The operation status of the main shaft of the headstock and other parts under no-load conditions: There is no impact and abnormal vibration during high-speed operation; there is no crawling and oscillation during low-speed operation.
④ The linear motion parts of the lathe should undergo a no-load test run at low, medium, and high feed speeds respectively. When the moving parts move, they should be stable, flexible, and reliable, without obvious crawling and vibration.
⑤ The relative error of the lateral feed of the non-CNC wheel frame generally should not exceed the provisions of Table 3-33.
Table 3-33 Feed Relative Error

Test Conditions:
a) The indicator is fixed on the measuring bridge plate on the workbench or workpiece bed body, and its stylus axis is roughly in the same horizontal plane as the spindle axis of the wheel frame.
b) Feed with the minimum nominal feed amount, continuously 10 times.
c) The calculation formulas are shown in equations (3-11) and (3-12).

Where δ每次 is the relative error per feed;

3) Power Test of Wheel Frame No-Load. The power of the wheel frame (with wheel) no-load should not exceed 115% of the wheel frame motor no-load power index. When the wheel frame motor no-load power index has not been determined, the wheel frame motor no-load power can be assessed as not greater than 25% of the rated power, or it can be specified by the design.
Ten sets of wheel frames with better assembly support can be selected to measure their no-load power (the motor no-load power should be deducted during measurement level inspection), and the average value is taken as the wheel frame motor no-load running power index.
4) Test of Lathe Function.
① Manual Function Test (test of each part of the lathe operated manually or by CNC manual mode).
a) The spindle of the headstock or wheel frame is subjected to a manual operation test of 10 starts and stops at medium speed or the designed speed, and the action should be flexible and reliable; for the spindle with stepless speed change, the speed change operation test should be performed at the low, medium, and high speeds specified in the design, and the action should be flexible and reliable.
b) The workbench or carriage and other linear motion parts are subjected to 10 consecutive starts and stops in the forward and reverse directions at medium speed. The flexibility and reliability of the test action.
c) Each control button corresponding to the manual function of the lathe numerical control system should be tested one by one, and the action should be flexible and reliable, and the indicator light should display correctly and reliably.
② Automatic Function Test (test of each part of the lathe operated by automatic program).
a) The spindle of the headstock or wheel frame is subjected to an automatic operation test of 10 starts and stops at medium speed or the designed speed, and the action should be flexible and reliable. For the spindle with stepless speed change, the speed change automatic operation test should be performed at the low, medium, and high speeds specified in the design, and the action should be flexible and reliable.
b) For each linear motion part, an automatic operation test of starting, stopping, and incremental feeding in the forward and reverse directions should be performed continuously at medium feed rate or the designed speed; the automatic operation test of speed change of the feed system at low, medium, and high feed speeds and fast speed should be performed, and the action should be flexible, reliable, and correct.
c) Each function of the lathe linkage, positioning, and numerical control system linear compensation, grinding cycle, etc. should be tested, and its action should be reliable, flexible, and correct.

In GB/T24738-2009 "Integrity of Mechanical Manufacturing Process Documents", according to the production type and product complexity, the integrity requirements of commonly used process documents are specified, which are applicable to the process management of mechanical manufacturing enterprises.

1. General Requirements
1) Process documents are the main basis for guiding workers' operations and for production and process management. They should be correct, complete, unified, and clear.
2) The types and contents of process documents should vary according to the production characteristics, production type, and product complexity.
3) The production characteristics of products include prototype trial production, small batch trial production, and formal mass production. Prototype trial production mainly verifies the product design structure, and the integrity of process documents is not required. Each enterprise can determine according to specific conditions; small batch trial production mainly verifies the process, so the process documents of small batch trial production should be basically the same as those of formal mass production, except that the latter is more perfect after being modified and supplemented through the small batch trial production process.

3. Basic Requirements for Designing Process Specifications

1) Process specifications are important technical documents that directly guide on-site production operations. They should be correct, complete, unified, and clear.
2) Based on full utilization of the existing production conditions of the enterprise, adopt advanced process technologies and experiences from both domestic and international sources as much as possible.
3) While ensuring product quality, strive to improve productivity and reduce consumption.
4) Designing process specifications must consider safety and industrial hygiene measures.
5) Parts with similar structural characteristics and process characteristics should be designed with typical process specifications as much as possible.
6) Process specifications from various specialties should be consistent and coordinated during the design process, without contradictions.
7) The format, layout, and filling method of process specifications should comply with the provisions of JB/T 9165.2—1998 "Format of Process Specifications".
8) The terms, symbols, and codes used in process specifications should comply with the relevant standards.
9) The units of measurement in process specifications should all use legal units.
10) The numbering of process specifications should comply with the provisions of JB/T 9166—1998 "Numbering Method for Process Documents".

6. Approval Procedures for Process Programs
(1) Review
1) The review of process procedures is generally conducted by the product's chief process engineer or the process group leader. For critical process procedures, the review can be conducted by the chief of the process department (section).
2) The main contents of the review:
   a) Whether the arrangement of processes and process requirements are reasonable.
   b) Whether the selected equipment and process tooling are reasonable.
(2) Standardization Review
Refer to JB/T9169.7-1998 "Guidelines for Process Management - Standardization Review of Process Documents" for standardization review.
(3) Joint Review
1) After the process procedure has been reviewed and subjected to standardization review, it should be sent to the relevant production workshop for joint review.
2) The main contents of the joint review:
   a) Based on the production capacity of the workshop, review whether the processing or assembly content arranged in the process procedure can be realized in the workshop.
   b) Whether the equipment and process tooling selected in the process procedure are reasonable.
(4) Approval
After the joint review, the complete set of process procedures is generally approved by the chief of the process department (section). For process procedures of products produced in batches and critical products produced individually, approval should be given by the chief process engineer or chief engineer.

2. Design description of adjustable stroke hydraulic cylinder
The WC67Y-100T hydraulic cylinder is designed to be used with the WC67Y-100T/(2500, 3200, 4000) synchronous hydraulic up-moving plate bending machine. According to the provisions of JB/T2184-2005 "Model Compilation Method for Hydraulic Components", the model of this hydraulic cylinder should be: SG1-G180×120Q-160C120-※※2WS100/(2500, 3200, 4000), where ※※ is the manufacturer's code.
(1) Main design basis
The design of this hydraulic cylinder is mainly based on the following standards:

9) Design of the impact block (trapezoidal nut).
During the cylinder's travel, when the piston end cover's lower plane approaches and impacts the upper plane of the impact block, the cylinder's travel is limited, creating a dead point in the travel. The impact block is driven by input torque and speed through the trapezoidal thread shaft. The axial position of its upper plane relative to the positioning boss of the trapezoidal thread shaft and the amount of change relates to the accuracy of the hydraulic cylinder. Therefore, it is required to have precise positioning, repeatable accurate positioning, and long service life.

1. The trapezoidal thread transmission pair requires high transmission accuracy and axial positioning requirements. T80×3.7 (JB/T2886) is selected.
2. There are requirements for its geometric tolerances. The impact end face must be perpendicular to the centerline of the trapezoidal thread hole (thread pitch diameter).
3. The trapezoidal thread has sufficient strength, stiffness, and service life.
4. The impact plane has sufficient compressive strength and service life.
5. The guiding key has high guiding accuracy, requiring a small clearance and being parallel to the centerline of the trapezoidal thread shaft.
6. During transmission, it cannot drive the piston rod to rotate together, meaning it cannot follow rotation.
7. When the piston rod moves, the hydraulic oil above and below the impact block can pass through smoothly without causing abnormal noise.
8. No abnormal noise is generated when the impact block is impacted and separated.

10) Design of adjustment shim.
1. Reasonable material selection.
2. After heat treatment, it requires high hardness and must prevent deformation during storage and use.
3. Verification of planar compressive strength.
4. Determination and provision of dimensions, but mainly requires accurate measurement.
5. Reasonable processing technology.
6. Reasonable installation technology.
7. Long service life.

11) Design of retaining key.
1. Sufficient compressive and shear strength, meeting the structural performance requirements.
2. Axial movement should be minimized, which relates to the axial positioning accuracy of the trapezoidal thread shaft.
3. Reasonable heat treatment and technology.
4. Convenient installation and removal.
5. Design of reducer mounting flange and pressure sleeve.
6. Reasonable positioning design, convenient installation and removal.
7. Ensure coaxiality and perpendicularity requirements.
8. The direction of the reducer input shaft can be adjusted to allow one drive shaft to drive two reducers.
9. There is an outlet for rotational seal leakage, and an oil filling hole for lubrication.

3.3.2 Design accuracy and machining accuracy analysis of adjustable stroke hydraulic cylinder
The adjustable stroke hydraulic cylinder for hydraulic up-moving plate bending machine, in addition to having the general structure of a double-acting single piston rod hydraulic cylinder, also has the special structure of an "adjustable stroke cylinder" whose stroke stop position can be changed to allow changes in stroke length.
The positioning accuracy of the stroke and the repeated positioning accuracy of the stroke of the adjustable stroke cylinder to a certain extent indicate the level of domestic hydraulic cylinder design and manufacturing. Taking the WC67Y-100T hydraulic cylinder as an example, the positioning accuracy of the stroke and the repeated positioning accuracy of the stroke of the adjustable stroke cylinder in China can reach ≤±0.080 mm and ≤0.080 mm in the hydraulic test bench detection, while a patent design of the adjustable stroke cylinder can reach ≤±0.015 mm and ≤0.010 mm in the hydraulic cylinder test bench detection.
Since the positioning accuracy of the stroke and the repeated positioning accuracy of the stroke of this adjustable stroke hydraulic cylinder are the main performance parameters that distinguish it from other hydraulic cylinders, the following focuses on analyzing it in terms of design accuracy and manufacturing accuracy.
1. Design accuracy analysis
Since the hydraulic cylinder is a special pressure vessel, it is required that the designed structure itself has stability under the pressure test (or rated) pressure, that is, the assembly and parts must have sufficient strength, rigidity and impact toughness. Design accuracy is given under steady-state working conditions, and design accuracy analysis is based on the premise of structural stability.
Design accuracy is the degree of conformity between the geometric parameters (dimensions, shapes, positions and surface structures, etc.) given in advance in the design and the ideal geometric parameters. Design accuracy analysis is mainly to analyze the necessity of the accuracy level of the geometric parameters given in the drawing, that is, whether it meets the functional and performance requirements of the product, including the compliance with some design specifications, principles and criteria, such as whether it conforms to the current product geometric technical specifications, tolerance principles, the selection principles of geometric tolerances and surface roughness parameters and their values, the structural design criteria for tolerance requirements, etc.
Generally, design accuracy analysis can be carried out in the following aspects:
1) Dimensional accuracy design analysis, including the analysis of the selection of datum, matching system, standard tolerance (dimensional element accuracy) level, tolerance and fit, etc. Among them, dimensional elements refer to geometric shapes determined by linear dimensions or angular dimensions of a certain size.
2) Geometric accuracy design analysis, including the analysis of the selection of datum, geometric (shape, direction, position and runout) tolerances and tolerance principles, etc.
3) Surface structure accuracy analysis, including the analysis of surface roughness parameters (arithmetic average deviation of profile R a, maximum height of profile R z, sampling length of profile R3, etc.)

The following is an analysis of the design accuracy of the main cylinder components of the WC67Y-100T hydraulic cylinder (except for surface roughness, all linear dimensions in the following text are in mm).

(1) Design accuracy analysis of the cylinder body

Figure 3-5 shows the cylinder body (right) of the WC67Y-100T hydraulic cylinder. The cylinder body is the main body of the hydraulic cylinder and one of its main components. Other components and the host are installed on it, and oil ports for connecting pipelines are also set on the cylinder body.

The cylindrical surface of the cylinder bore serves as a guide rail for the piston and piston rod (since the piston rod and piston are coaxial and combined into one). It is more appropriate to use the axis of the inner hole of the cylinder body (cylinder) as the design datum during design, as shown in Datum A.

As shown in Figure 3-4, since the hydraulic cylinder is a special pressure vessel, it is divided into a rodless cavity and a rod cavity through the piston, piston rod, and sealing device or system, and the piston and piston rod reciprocate within it. Therefore, the bore should ensure certain dimensional tolerances and geometric accuracy. In Figure 3-5, the cylinder bore is designed as ф180H8, and straightness, roundness, and cylindricity tolerances are given, which can ensure movement and sealing; to ensure the maximum cylinder stroke, relevant dimensions of 310±0.20 are given; to install the piston sealing device or system, chamfers for installation and lead-in are provided, and it is required that the lead-in chamfer intersect with the cylindrical surface of the cylinder bore with a rounded corner; to ensure the sealing performance and durability of the sealing device or system, the surface roughness value of the cylinder bore surface is selected as Ra0.4μm, but Rz and Rmr are not further specified; the rod cavity flow channel is set at the retraction groove of the cylinder bore, which not only facilitates the uniform action of the oil liquid in the rod cavity on the effective area of the rod end of the piston but also eliminates the sharp edge chamfer like the rodless cavity flow channel.

The piston rod sealing groove, including the bearing ring groove, is all set on the cylinder body. To ensure the concentricity of all groove bottom surfaces with the inner hole axis of the cylinder, all of them use the inner hole axis of the cylinder as the design datum and give concentricity tolerances, including the hole (or coupling hole) ф170.6H9 that generally does not contact the piston rod; the rounded corners at all parts of the groove are all given rounded corner radii on the drawing and in the technical requirements, and the groove bottom surface and side surface are all given surface roughness requirements.

The installation surface of the hydraulic cylinder is set on the cylinder body. When installed with the host, it must ensure that the axis of the reciprocating motion of the piston and piston rod is parallel to the installation surface of the host and perpendicular to the worktable of the host, and it bears the reaction force of the cylinder output force. In Figure 3-5, geometric tolerances are given for both the two-step contact surface and the step clamping surface, especially the intersection of the step contact surface and the step clamping surface, which is prone to fatigue failure. Therefore, referring to the crossing groove of the external cylindrical grinding wheel (see Figure 1-21, Table 1-85), an alternating load is given for the plane grinding wheel crossing groove. The 8×M20-6H threaded hole on the installation surface is used for installation with the host, and position tolerance is given for it.

Each oil port is designed according to relevant standards, but the WC67Y-100T hydraulic cylinder adopts a combined sealing washer for oil port sealing. Therefore, no further requirements are given for the O-ring angular sealing at the end of the oil port, and only a perpendicularity tolerance is given for the sealing surface.

Other parts such as the threaded connection and positioning stop between the cylinder body and the end cover, the chamfer for installing the sealing ring, and the outer shape of the cylinder body are all given dimensions and tolerances, geometric tolerances, and surface roughness requirements according to relevant standards and technical requirements. The edges of the cylinder body are not marked with chamfers of 2×45°, and the technical requirements state that the surface of the cylinder body can be surface-coated or pre-treated according to user requirements.

See Figure 3-5 for specific geometric accuracy levels and surface roughness at each location.

For linear dimensions without marked tolerance levels, the tolerance level is grade m; for rounded corner radii and chamfer height dimensions without marked dimensions, the tolerance level is grade m; for angles without marked angles, the tolerance level is grade m; for geometric tolerances without marked tolerance levels, the tolerance level is grade K.

The position of the oil port on the cylinder body (left) of the WC67Y-100T hydraulic cylinder is different from that on the cylinder body (right) of the WC67Y-100T hydraulic cylinder.

(2) Design accuracy analysis of the cylinder end cover

In Figure 3-4, since the cylinder end cover, together with the cylinder body and other cylinder components, forms the rodless cavity of the hydraulic cylinder, its sealing performance must be ensured, especially the rotary shaft seal composed of the ф85f8 cylindrical surface with the trapezoidal thread shaft.

Figure 3-6 shows the design datum of the cylinder end cover of the WC67Y-100T hydraulic cylinder as the axis of the ф85H8 hole, as shown in Datum A, which should be in a straight line with the axis of the inner hole of the cylinder body (cylinder body design datum A) during assembly.

To ensure that all sealing groove bottom surfaces are in a straight line with the axis of the inner hole of the cylinder body during assembly, geometric tolerances are given for all sealing groove bottom surfaces relative to the design datum of the cylinder body end cover.

Similarly, the threaded connection with the cylinder body, the positioning boss, the bottom surface of the keyway, the stop surface of the installation flange of the reducer, and the cylindrical surface that cooperates with the cylinder body where the O-ring static seal is located, etc., are all given dimensions and tolerances, geometric tolerances, etc.

To ensure that the axis of the trapezoidal thread shaft installed on the cylinder end cover can be in a straight line with the axis of the inner hole of the cylinder body, in addition to ensuring the fitting accuracy of ф85H8/f8 between the cylinder end cover and the trapezoidal thread shaft, it is also necessary to ensure that the bottom surface of the axial positioning boss on the trapezoidal thread shaft is perpendicular to this axis and has a small assembly clearance with other cylinder components. Therefore, the relevant surfaces and keyway of the cylinder end cover are all given dimensions and tolerances and geometric accuracy requirements.

The lower end surface of the cylinder end cover involves the eccentricity problem of the cylinder return end, and the upper end surface is related to the concentricity of the installation flange of the reducer. Both are given perpendicularity tolerances on the drawing.

Chamfers at each location, especially rounded corners at each sealing groove, are given chamfer dimensions and rounded corner radii. The maximum chamfer at each threaded hole is 1.05D×120°.

The tightening and anti-loosening between the cylinder end cover and the cylinder body are very important. First, the accuracy of the M195×3-6h thread should be ensured.

See Figure 3-6 for specific geometric accuracy levels and surface roughness at each location.

For linear dimensions without marked tolerance levels, the tolerance level is grade m; for rounded corner radii and chamfer height dimensions without marked dimensions, the tolerance level is grade m; for angles without marked angles, the tolerance level is grade m; for geometric tolerances without marked tolerance levels, the tolerance level is grade K.

(3) Design accuracy analysis of the piston rod

In Figure 3-4, the piston, piston rod, and sealing device or system divide the cylinder body into rodless and rod cavities, with the piston and piston rod moving reciprocally within.

As shown in Figure 3-7, the WC67Y-100T hydraulic cylinder's piston rod and piston form an integrated structure with a hollow piston rod. Due to structural limitations, the hollow opening faces the cylinder bottom side, increasing the rodless cavity (inner cavity) wet volume.

To ensure the sealing and reciprocating movement precision of the piston and piston rod, the centerline of the piston rod outer cylindrical surface φ17.0f7 is determined as the design datum for the piston rod, specifically shown as datum A, which should align with the cylinder bore centerline (cylinder body design datum A) during assembly.

The piston rod end cap (or piston rod end cap) is screwed onto the piston rod end and directly contacts the stroke limiter component of the cylinder. The cylinder stroke (unidirectional) positioning accuracy and cylinder stroke (unidirectional) repeated positioning accuracy are the most important precision requirements for the adjustable stroke hydraulic cylinder used in hydraulic up-motion plate bending machines. Therefore, the precision of the piston rod (piston end) end face and threads is crucial. Additionally, a guide key groove is set in the hollow piston rod to prevent the collision block from rotating during axial movement, with the guide key groove also specifying dimensions, tolerances, geometric accuracy requirements, and surface roughness.

To ensure the sealing of the piston and piston rod, geometric accuracy requirements such as straightness, roundness, and cylindricity are specified for the piston rod outer cylindrical surface. Concentricity tolerances are given for the piston seal groove bottom surface and other related cylindrical surfaces relative to the design datum, along with surface roughness for each cylindrical surface.

The precision of the spherical surface SR70mm and 2×M6-6H threaded holes used for connecting the piston rod is also important. To ensure that the reaction force from the driven slider acts on the centerline of the cylinder bore, concentricity tolerance is specified for the intersection circle between the spherical surface and the piston rod end face.

The piston rod is subjected to alternating loads, and fatigue failure is likely to occur at the relief groove or grinding wheel exit groove locations. The drawing specifies chamfer dimensions and fillet radii at these locations. The seal groove bottom fillet radius and groove edge fillet radius R=0.2mm are not specified for each seal groove.

Specific geometric accuracy levels and surface roughness are shown in Figure 3-7. Tolerance grades for unmarked linear dimensions are m-level, for unmarked fillet radii and chamfer heights are m-level, for unmarked angles are m-level, and for unmarked geometric tolerances are K-level.

(4) Design Precision Analysis of Piston End Cap

In Figure 3-4, the piston end cap is threadedly connected and tightened with the piston rod (piston end), moving reciprocally together, and contacts the collision block at the dead point of cylinder travel, serving as the stroke limiter component of the adjustable stroke hydraulic cylinder.

As shown in Figure 3-8, the piston end cap of the WC67Y-100T hydraulic cylinder, to ensure the perpendicularity of each end face (three locations), takes the axis of the threaded minor diameter on the piston rod end (piston end) as the design datum, specifically shown as datum A.

The thread design for screwing and tightening with the piston rod end is M130×3-6H/6h, which is a medium-precision preferred tolerance and fit. To ensure that the thread minor diameter axis can align with the piston rod design datum during assembly, a perpendicularity tolerance is given for the contact surface after screwing and tightening the piston end cap with the piston rod end; to avoid cylinder misalignment at the return limit dead point, a perpendicularity tolerance is given for the top of the piston end cap; to ensure unidirectional positioning accuracy and unidirectional repeated positioning accuracy of cylinder travel, a perpendicularity tolerance is given for the bottom of the piston end cap.

The piston end cap is subjected to alternating loads, and fatigue failure is likely to occur at the relief groove locations. The drawing specifies chamfer dimensions and fillet radii at these locations.

Specific geometric accuracy levels and surface roughness are shown in Figure 3-8. Tolerance grades for unmarked linear dimensions are m-level, for unmarked fillet radii and chamfer heights are m-level, for unmarked angles are m-level, and for unmarked geometric tolerances are K-level.

(5) Design Precision Analysis of Trapezoidal Thread Shaft

As shown in Figure 3-4, the trapezoidal thread shaft is an important cylinder component in the travel adjustment device of the adjustable stroke hydraulic cylinder. Its design precision, machining precision, and assembly precision directly affect the unidirectional positioning accuracy and unidirectional repeated positioning accuracy of the adjustable stroke hydraulic cylinder. The trapezoidal thread shaft requires rotary shaft sealing with the cylinder end cap and forms the generalized cylinder body together with other cylinder components.

As shown in Figure 3-9, the trapezoidal thread shaft of the WC67Y-100T hydraulic cylinder, to ensure connection, sealing, positioning accuracy, and transmission precision, takes the φ28f7 and T80×4-7 trapezoidal thread (major diameter) axis as the combined datum elements, specifically shown as datum A and datum B. Its left end (see Figure 3-9) has a keyed shaft φ28f7 connected to the reducer, φ125×23 is the positioning boss of the trapezoidal thread shaft itself, a section of φ85f8 shaft (or cylinder) fits with the hole φ85H8 in the cylinder end cap to form rotary shaft sealing (seal groove is set on the cylinder end cap). To ensure that the trapezoidal thread shaft design datum aligns with the cylinder body design datum during assembly and to meet other technical requirements, the drawing therefore specifies the rotary shaft dimensions and fit φ85H8/f8 and other dimensions and tolerances, geometric accuracy, and surface roughness requirements.

The precision of the trapezoidal thread affects the setting of various target positions and target reference points of the adjustable stroke hydraulic cylinder, so the drawing provides detailed information about the trapezoidal thread T80×4-7 (JB/T2886-2008) details, which can also be seen in Table 3-49.

The trapezoidal thread shaft is subjected to variable loads during testing and use, and may be subjected to large impact loads in special situations. Fatigue failure is likely to occur at the relief groove or grinding wheel exit groove locations on the shaft, so the drawing specifies chamfer dimensions and fillet radii at all relief groove or grinding wheel exit groove locations. Chamfers at other locations are also detailed in the drawing, especially the installation lead-in chamfer and the fillet at the intersection with the φ85f8 shaft.

The trapezoidal thread shaft requires center holes for external turning and fine trapezoidal thread cutting, so the drawing specifies center holes that need to be ground, with a surface roughness of Ra0.2μm, and requires protection of these two center holes during all process steps including assembly. (2) Analysis of Piston Rod Processing Accuracy

Generally, the processing accuracy of piston rods mainly depends on before and after hard chromium plating, but the piston rod of W C 6 7 Y - 1 0 0 T hydraulic cylinder shown in Figure 3-7 is different from general piston rods, which is an open hollow piston rod facing the cylinder bottom.

The reasons for the difficulty in ensuring the processing accuracy of this piston rod are: ① When finishing, hard chromium plating before and after hard chromium plating, and grinding the outer circle including polishing the outer circle, the direct top-clamping method cannot be used for processing; ② The workpiece must be turned around during processing; ③ There are key grooves in the inner hole (non-through hole).

In order to realize the processing by the top-clamping method, the inner hole of the piston rod should be processed first except for the key grooves, and then a 90° tapered center plug should be used.

After turning around, the piston end is clamped with a self-centering chuck, and the center hole and various parts such as S R7 0 are processed. The main problems are the accuracy of the machine tool and chuck itself, such as the two center holes (the center hole at the piston end is on the 90° center plug) are not on the same straight line. The center hole being processed can be corrected by grinding, but the S R 7 0 center point is difficult to correct.

If a one-time 90° tapered center plug is used, it can only be removed after hard chromium plating and polishing, and key slot processing will become the last process.

(3) Analysis of Trapezoidal Thread Shaft and Block Processing Accuracy

The processing accuracy of the trapezoidal thread shaft mainly lies in the processing of the trapezoidal thread, and the block is the same.

Before finishing the trapezoidal thread shaft, the center hole should be ground, and the surface roughness should be Ra0.2μm, and the top-clamping method should be used to finish the trapezoidal thread. There are certain difficulties in processing T 8 0×4.7 (JB/T2886-2008) trapezoidal thread on an ordinary lathe. First, whether the accumulated error of the pitch of the ordinary lathe can reach δ P 60≤0.010, secondly, the consistency of the pitch diameter of the trapezoidal thread, and thirdly, the surface roughness of the trapezoidal thread.

When turning trapezoidal threads, a clamped hard alloy thread forming turning tool is generally used now.

The accuracy of the two center holes is related to the accuracy of the trapezoidal thread. After grinding, the center hole must ensure that the contact surface is not less than 85% when matching with the standard center. When grinding the outer circle of the major diameter of the thread, the cylindricity tolerance must be ensured.

The processing technology of trapezoidal thread accuracy is very important. Choosing the correct processing technology and process parameters, under the condition that the geometric accuracy and working accuracy of the processing machine tool are qualified, a trapezoidal thread with 7-level accuracy can be turned.

3.4.2 Methods to Meet the Closed Loop Tolerance Requirements of Assembly Dimension Chains
According to product design requirements, structural characteristics, tolerance sizes, and production conditions, different methods can be adopted to meet the closed loop tolerance requirements. Commonly used methods include interchangeability, grouping, repair fitting, and adjustment.
1. Interchangeability Method
Depending on the degree of interchangeability, it can be divided into complete interchangeability and large number interchangeability.
(1) Complete Interchangeability Method
During assembly of all products, the component rings do not need to be selected or their sizes or positions changed. After assembly, the closed loop tolerance requirements can be met. This method uses the extreme value formula for calculation.
(2) Large Number Interchangeability Method
In the vast majority of products, the component rings do not need to be selected or their sizes or positions changed during assembly. After assembly, the closed loop tolerance requirements can be met. This method uses the statistical tolerance formula for calculation.
The large number interchangeability method is based on a certain confidence level. Generally, the closed loop tends to follow a normal distribution, with a confidence level P = 99.73%. At this time, the relative distribution coefficient k0 = 1. Under certain production conditions, if it is required to appropriately enlarge the component ring tolerance, a lower P value can be taken. The relationship between confidence level and relative distribution coefficient is shown in Table 3-57.

When using the large number interchangeability method, appropriate process measures should be taken to exclude individual products that exceed the tolerance range or limit deviation.
2. Grouping Method
The component rings are divided into several groups according to their actual sizes, and corresponding groups are assembled together. Parts in the same group have interchangeability. This method usually uses the extreme value tolerance formula for calculation.

3.5 Design and Use of Process Equipment for Hydraulic Cylinders

3.5.1 Significance of Using Process Equipment for Cylinder Processing

Professional cylinder manufacturers produce honed, rolled, cold-drawn seamless steel pipes or cylinders that meet the requirements of JB/T11718-2013 "Technical Conditions for Hydraulic Cylinder Cylinders." These are frequently used by hydraulic cylinder manufacturers for hydraulic cylinder body manufacturing. For the manufacturing of single-piece or small-batch hydraulic cylinders, they have the advantages of being simple, fast, and low-cost, so they have been widely used in recent years.

Cylinders processed on CNC scraping and rolling machines using combined tools (rough boring, scraping, and rolling) can be classified as rolled cylinders.

In cylinder body manufacturing, since the purchased seamless steel pipes have only the inner hole precision machined, the outer circle and both end faces are generally not machined or precision machined. Moreover, the connections between the cylinder and the cylinder bottom, cylinder cap, etc. (including welding bevels) have not been machined either. Therefore, secondary machining is required to meet the various design and process requirements for hydraulic cylinder bodies.

The above-mentioned seamless steel pipes with honed, rolled, cold-drawn (or hot-rolled) inner holes or cylinders are semi-finished products for hydraulic cylinder bodies. They are collectively referred to as cylinders below.

To ensure the coaxiality, perpendicularity, and other geometric tolerance requirements of each machining surface to the cylinder's inner hole axis during secondary machining, it is now generally necessary to turn a section of outer cylindrical surface on the cylinder's outer circle that is coaxial with the cylinder's inner hole. Then, use a center frame to support this section of the outer circle for further machining.

The processing of this section of the outer circle is purely a process requirement for the process datum, not a product design datum. However, if this section of the cylinder's outer circle is not machined, it would be almost impossible to complete the subsequent processes. Machining this section of the cylinder's outer circle not only affects the appearance of the product but also weakens the cylinder's strength. Therefore, some users explicitly require that this section of the cylinder's outer circle must not be machined.

Machining this section of the cylinder's outer circle also faces difficulties in clamping and alignment, such as using a self-centering chuck to expand and clamp one end of the inner hole, then aligning the other end's inner hole. Although this clamping and alignment method is widely used, it is very difficult to implement in practice, time-consuming, and the quality is not guaranteed. Using a single-action chuck to clamp the outer circle and aligning the other end's inner hole also faces the same problems. Moreover, since it is necessary to simultaneously determine the centers of the two end inner holes coinciding with the machine tool's centerline, the alignment is even more difficult. The above two clamping and alignment methods share a common problem, that is, the chuck jaws must be in line contact with the workpiece; otherwise, it will be impossible to align the other end. Regardless of how this clamping may damage the inner hole, in terms of machining, line contact clamping has very low resistance to cutting forces and other external forces.

To improve resistance to cutting forces and other external forces, it is often necessary to first machine the cylinder's end face, then use the tailstock center to support the cylinder before machining this section of the cylinder's outer circle. However, machining also faces the same problem, that is, low resistance during end face machining.

The most reliable method for machining this section of the cylinder's outer circle is to use a cylindrical mandrel, especially using a centering clamping mandrel for machining, which is most reasonable in theory. However, it has the following problems in practice:

1) Although seamless steel pipes of the same inner hole diameter have different lengths, different lengths of centering clamping mandrels are needed.

2) Because the centering clamping mandrel must pass through the entire length of the seamless steel pipe's inner hole, it is very difficult to ensure that it does not damage the inner hole surface.

3) Due to its structural reasons, large-diameter centering clamping mandrels are too heavy.

There is also a simple centering clamping mandrel, but the problem is that the inner hole surface is almost damaged after clamping. Sometimes, it cannot be removed after clamping. Moreover, different lengths of simple centering clamping mandrels are also needed.

The centering expansion sleeve designed by the author is to solve the above problems and provide a kind of process equipment for turning processing centering fixtures for cylinder processing.

This centering expansion sleeve can process the other end of the cylinder according to the hydraulic cylinder design requirements under the conditions of one end of the cylinder's inner hole being expanded and clamped by a self-centering chuck and the tailstock extended center supporting and positioning the centering expansion sleeve. It does not need to process an additional process datum, that is, it does not need to machine a section of the outer cylindrical surface on the cylinder's outer circle that is coaxial with the cylinder's inner hole and use a center frame to support and position this section of the outer circle for further machining. Instead, it can directly machine to meet the hydraulic cylinder design requirements, and the same inner hole diameter cylinders can use one (type) of centering expansion sleeve, which can be reused.

Using the centering expansion sleeve as process equipment for cylinder processing is not only because using process equipment can ensure product quality, improve productivity, reduce costs, accelerate production cycles, and increase economic benefits, but also because it is necessary in some cases. For example, for the hydraulic cylinders of RAS series gate-type hydraulic shearing machines produced by a certain company, when the host manufacturer does not allow processing the process datum on the cylinder's outer circle, it is almost impossible to ensure the coaxiality or perpendicularity of the machined part of the cylinder to the cylinder's axial direction by aligning the inner hole. At the same time, without the support and positioning of the center frame, turning machining of the cylinder's end is also very difficult. Moreover, when the outer shape of the cylinder body is not circular (such as square or rectangular cylinder bodies, etc.) and has a certain length, even if the headstock end of the cylinder body is positioned using a center plug and tightened with threads, it is still difficult to perform turning machining on the other end due to excessive overhang length, especially for long cylinders, or even impossible. Therefore, using the centering expansion sleeve as process equipment for cylinder processing is necessary in this case.

2. Working Principle of Centering Expansion Mandrel
During the process of tightening the threaded end hexagon adjustment rod 6 with an extended hexagon wrench through the hexagon socket wrench hole 21, the movable plate 10 and a group of steel balls 1 and 13 push the steel balls along the left conical surface of the double-cone sleeve 3 to the right, generating radial displacement and expanding the left end diameter of the thin-walled sleeve 14. Simultaneously, the locating seat 5 and another group of steel balls 16 and 24 push the steel balls along the right conical surface of the double-cone sleeve 3 to the left, generating radial displacement and expanding the right end diameter of the thin-walled sleeve 14. Since both ends of the thin-walled sleeve 14 are expanded, the centering expansion mandrel automatically centers and expands (tightens) within the cylinder bore.

When loosening the threaded end hexagon adjustment rod 6 with an extended hexagon wrench through the hexagon socket wrench hole 21, the steel balls are squeezed back to their initial positions by the thin-walled sleeve 14's own elasticity, completing the release of the expansion (tightening) of the cylinder bore.

3. Use of Centering Expansion Mandrel
After cleaning the cylinder bore to be processed, the centering expansion mandrel is lifted into the cylinder bore using two lifting eye bolts 20, leaving sufficient length (depth) for processing. Using an extended hexagon wrench through the hexagon socket wrench hole 21 to tighten the threaded end hexagon adjustment rod 6, the centering expansion mandrel automatically centers and expands (tightens) within the cylinder bore. After removing the lifting device and lifting eye bolts, the cylinder with the centering expansion mandrel is lifted onto the lathe for clamping. The cylinder end without the centering expansion mandrel uses a self-centering chuck to expand and clamp the bore. When using an extended center to tighten the 60° C-type center hole 22, the cylinder is clamped with a self-centering chuck, completing the cylinder tube clamping for the boring process.

Note that pads or wooden blocks should be placed on the machine tool guideways beforehand to prevent the cylinder from accidentally falling and causing injury to personnel and damage to the machine tool. Before clamping the cylinder, the pads or wooden blocks should not be removed, and the lifting device should not be released. Before processing after clamping, the pads or wooden blocks and lifting device must be removed and released.

After completing this process, the centering expansion mandrel is removed following the above process in reverse. However, note that when the cylinder is placed vertically with the top end removed, the centering expansion mandrel is removed.

When centering the expansion mandrel, the lifting tool must be installed first and the centering expansion mandrel must be in a suspended state before loosening the internal hexagonal adjustment rod 6. Otherwise, the centering expansion mandrel may slip and fall, causing damage to the cylinder tube and the centering expansion mandrel.

4. Characteristics of the centering expansion mandrel

The centering expansion mandrel has the following characteristics in cylinder tube processing:

1) There is no need to manufacture centering clamping mandrels or simple centering clamping mandrels for individual products, which reduces the difficulty of cylinder body processing, saves manufacturing costs, and shortens the manufacturing cycle.

2) There is no need to machine an outer circle on the outer surface of the cylinder tube as a process reference, which eliminates one process step and avoids introducing process reference errors into subsequent processing steps, while also improving the appearance quality, strength, and stiffness of the cylinder tube.

3) A centering expansion mandrel can be used to process cylinder tubes with the same inner diameter, without any requirements on the length of the cylinder tube, and has good versatility.

4) Two centering expansion mandrels can be used simultaneously to clamp and expand a cylinder tube for double-end processing, which not only further reduces working hours and improves efficiency, but also expands the application range of the centering expansion mandrel.

5) Using the centering expansion mandrel can maximize the elimination of the influence of human factors on product quality, ensuring the consistency of the geometric accuracy of the cylinder tube.

6) According to relevant standards, the centering expansion mandrel can be designed and manufactured in a standardized and serialized manner.

In summary, the application of the centering expansion mandrel in cylinder tube processing can make single-piece and small-batch cylinder tube processing easier, improve the structural processability of the cylinder tube, and may further transform special process equipment into general-purpose process equipment, or even standard process equipment.

3.6 Several Process Issues in Rolling and Honing of Cylinder Tubes

3.6.1 Process Quality Issues in Rolling Holes

Rolling holes is generally arranged as the final finishing process for the inner diameter of hydraulic cylinder tubes, but poor surface quality is found after rolling the inner diameter of the cylinder tube, and only then do people think of pursuing the quality of the inner hole before rolling, which happens frequently.

Rolling is a processing method that applies pressure to a metal blank or workpiece using a rolling tool to cause plastic deformation, thereby forming the blank or rolling the surface of the workpiece. Rolling holes is a chip-free finishing processing method that utilizes the plasticity of the material, uses a rolling head to roll the processed surface, causing plastic deformation on the surface to form a hardened layer and produce residual compressive stress.

The plastic deformation in rolling follows three principles: the yield principle, the flow principle, and the strengthening principle.

Note: In GB/T 4863—2008, the definition of the term "rolling holes" is: "Processing the holes of a workpiece using the rolling method."

(1) The role of rolling holes

Rolling holes generally has the following roles:

1) Reduce the surface roughness value. Rolling can improve surface quality, i.e., surface integrity. Generally, the surface roughness value can be reduced by at least two levels, for example: carbon steel (45 steel) has a roughness of Ra3.2μm before rolling → about Ra0.2μm after rolling; cast iron (HT150～HT330) has a roughness of Ra3.2μm before rolling → about Ra0.8μm after rolling.

2) Correct the roundness. If the process parameters are selected correctly, the roundness of the hole after rolling is improved.

3) Improve surface hardness. Generally, it can improve the surface hardness by 15% to 30%, for example: carbon steel (45 steel) has a hardness of 197HBW before rolling → 240HBW after rolling; cast iron (HT150～HT330) has a hardness of 180HBW before rolling → 198HBW after rolling.

4) Improve wear resistance. Generally, the wear resistance of the surface can be improved by about 15% after rolling.

5) Improve fatigue strength. Generally, the fatigue strength of the surface can be improved by about 30% after rolling, and the notch fatigue strength (45 steel sample) can be improved by 78% to 121%.
