3.6.2 Issues with Honing Texture of Cylinder Tubes

Vertical internal cylindrical honing machines are mainly used for honing cylinders. If used for hydraulic cylinder tubes,
492:
The honing of hydraulic cylinder tubes, how to choose the process parameters and honing effect, even some honing machine manufacturers can't explain clearly, mainly because of the texture problem. This is still a test question that some hydraulic cylinder manufacturers often use to examine whether engineering technicians are proficient in the design and manufacture of hydraulic cylinders.

Honing is a method of finishing by applying a certain pressure to the surface of the workpiece using a honing tool, while the honing tool performs relative rotation and linear reciprocating motion, and cuts off an extremely small amount of excess on the workpiece. Honing is a special form of grinding, belonging to finishing. The principle of honing is that under a certain pressure, a complex relative motion is generated between the abrasive strip and the machined surface of the workpiece, and the abrasive particles of the abrasive strip play the roles of cutting, scraping, and squeezing, cutting off a very thin metal layer from the machined surface.

During honing, the abrasive strip expands and contracts radially, and contacts the hole surface with a certain pressure; the abrasive strip has three movements: rotational movement, reciprocating movement, and radial movement under pressure; the rotational movement and reciprocating movement make the cutting trajectory of the abrasive particles on the hole surface form a cross-shaped and non-repeating mesh pattern, which is conducive to storing lubricating oil and reducing the wear of the part surface. In order to prevent the motion trajectory of the abrasive particles of the abrasive strip from repeating, the number of revolutions per minute of the honing head and the number of reciprocating strokes per minute of the honing head should be mutually prime.

Honing can be divided into three stages: the first stage is the falling cutting stage; the second stage is the broken cutting stage; the third stage is the blocked cutting stage (equivalent to polishing). Honing can be divided into constant pressure honing and constant quantity honing.

Honing can improve the dimensional accuracy, roundness, straightness, cylindricity, and surface roughness of holes. For small and medium-sized hydraulic cylinder tubes, cold drawing-floating boring-rolling-honing is the most economical, efficient, and reasonable.

Honing has the following characteristics:
1) The abrasive particles of the abrasive strip have a small load and a long service life.
2) The speed is low, generally below 100 mm/min.
3) A large amount of cutting fluid is injected during honing, which can wash away the fallen abrasive particles, fully cool the machined surface, generate little heat in the workpiece, and have an extremely thin deformation layer, thereby obtaining a better surface allowance.
4) Honing can generally obtain holes with IT6~IT7 accuracy, Ra0.025~Ra0.2μm, and shape error is generally less than 0.005 mm.

The process elements of honing processing mainly include the number of honing times, mesh angle α, working pressure, the length of the abrasive strip extending out of the hole, the type and particle size of the abrasive material of the abrasive strip, honing fluid, etc.

The honing of cylinder tubes can be selected according to the following process elements:
1) Honing is divided into rough honing, fine honing, and super fine honing. The honing allowance after boring is 0.05~0.08 mm, the honing allowance after reaming is 0.02~0.04 mm, and the honing allowance after grinding is 0.01~0.02 mm. For allowances that are large or require high accuracy, it can be divided into three times of rough honing, fine honing, and super fine honing.
2) The rotational speed is generally vt=14~48 m/min, and the reciprocating feed speed va=5~15 m/min. The mesh angle α=2arctan(va/vt), and the cross angle is generally 30°~60°, with 45° being the best.
3) The working pressure of honing is selected as follows: 0.5~2.0 MPa for rough honing, 0.2~0.8 MPa for fine honing, and 0.05~0.1 MPa for super fine honing. Generally, 0.2~0.5 MPa can be taken.
4) During honing, the abrasive strip must extend beyond both ends of the hole, which is usually called the "cutting out" length. Some data suggest that a length of 1/3 of the abrasive strip is most suitable.
5) Abrasive materials suitable for grinding carbon steel and ductile iron include brown corundum A (GZ) and microcrystalline corundum MA (GW), etc. Honing abrasive strips should use ceramic binder (V), the hardness of the honing abrasive strip should be selected as K~P, and the particle size of the abrasive strip should be selected as F80 or above.

The honing process for cylinder bore platforms is now very mature and has relevant standards, and its process can be referenced to meet the technical requirements of hydraulic cylinder tubes.

The honing of cylinder bore platforms is generally divided into three processes:
1) The first process is mechanical expansion knife constant quantity honing, which is to eliminate the geometric errors produced by boring the cylinder, so that the roundness and cylindricity of the cylinder meet the requirements, and provide appropriate surface roughness and machining allowance for the next process.
2) The second process is also mechanical expansion knife constant quantity honing, but the feed speed and feed amount are smaller than the first process, which is to form a clear, symmetrical, and uniform mesh pattern on the cylinder bore surface, that is, the groove pulling process.
3) The third process is the fine honing process, which uses constant pressure honing, divided into two levels of pressurization, which is to form a platform, that is, to remove the peaks and retain the valleys, forming a certain width and number of platforms, and retaining a certain depth of grooves.

Three standards have been used for cylinder bores: ZBJ92011-1989 is the mirror honing standard; JB/T9768-1999 is the ordinary honing standard; DIN4776-1990 is the platform honing standard. The current standard is JB/T5082.7-2011 "Internal Combustion Engine Cylinder Liners Part 7: Platform Honing Mesh Technical Specifications and Testing Methods".

Comparing the honing of the inner hole of the cylinder tube with the honing of the cylinder bore, it can be concluded that the main difference is that the honing of the inner hole of the cylinder tube does not have the groove pulling process, and it is not necessary (not allowed) for the inner hole surface of the cylinder tube to form a "clear, symmetrical, and uniform mesh pattern".

3.6.3 The problem of choosing the process of rolling holes and honing holes
What should be the difference between rolling the inner hole of the cylinder tube and honing the inner hole of the cylinder tube (requirements), and under what circumstances (or conditions) should the process of rolling holes or honing holes be chosen for the cylinder tube of the hydraulic cylinder? This is a problem that is often faced.

Rolling holes or honing holes are both methods of finishing the inner hole surface. Without considering other factors (requirements or problems) for the time being, the pros and cons of the above two methods of finishing the inner hole of the cylinder tube are weighed only from the perspective of ensuring the service life of the sealing element, that is, durability.

Comprehensively considering the requirements of sealing, friction, and lubrication, and from the perspective of the applicability of sealing materials, the finishing processing method for the cylinder bore should be selected as follows:

1) Honing or honing plus polishing can be successively applied to nitrile rubber or fluorine rubber, polyurethane rubber, polytetrafluoroethylene (filled) plastic, and polyamide (filled) plastic.

2) Rolling can be successively applied to polytetrafluoroethylene (filled) plastic and polyamide (filled) plastic, polyurethane rubber, fluorine rubber, or nitrile rubber.

3) From the perspective of ensuring the relative bearing ratio Rmr alone, rolling is superior to honing because rolling can achieve an Rmr of up to 70%.

Polishing after honing may not significantly improve the relative bearing ratio Rmr, but it can significantly reduce seal wear including micro-movement wear. Therefore, polishing should be performed after honing the bore, and polishing can also be performed after rolling.

There are doubts about the claims by some scraping and rolling machine manufacturers that scraping and rolling surfaces have the same oil storage capacity as honed surfaces.

For cylinder parts such as guide sleeves or support rings made of metal materials such as cast iron and copper alloys, the inner bore that directly contacts the piston rod and serves guiding and supporting functions can use rolling as one of its finishing processing methods.

3.7 Common Surface Treatment Processes for Piston Rods

3.7.1 Polishing and Inspection Issues Before and After Chrome Plating of Piston Rods

Spiral patterns were found on the surface after chrome plating of piston rods, which was finally determined to be caused by belt polishing before plating by the electroplating factory; roundness, cylindricity, and straightness problems were also found on the workpiece after plating, which was also considered to be caused by belt polishing before and/or after plating. Improper polishing may further increase the waviness of the piston rod surface.

Polishing is a processing method that uses mechanical, chemical, or electrochemical action to obtain a bright and smooth surface on the workpiece. Its characteristic is to reduce the surface roughness value of the polished surface using free abrasive and soft polishing tools to obtain or improve the surface finish. Polishing before chrome plating of piston rods is mainly to improve the brightness of the surface after plating.

Therefore, it is judged that the term "belt polishing" is problematic and should be called "belt grinding".

Belt grinding or polishing cannot be used for piston rod surfaces before chrome plating, especially belt grinding on belt grinding equipment modified from old lathes without strict belt grinding process specifications, because it is very likely to damage the geometric accuracy and surface finish of the surface that has already formed on the external cylindrical grinder.

In order to ensure the surface finish or brightness after plating, the surface roughness value of the piston rod surface must not be higher than Ra0.8μm after external cylindrical grinding, and should be Ra0.4μm or below.

Polishing or grinding must be performed after plating, but the polishing allowance should not be too large; generally, the unilateral allowance should be between 0.01 and 0.02mm. After polishing after plating, straightness, roundness, cylindricity, and surface finish should be inspected.

The polishing or grinding after plating should also pay attention to improving the relative bearing ratio Rmr of the surface structure, because it affects the sealing performance of the piston rod.

Due to the possible unevenness of the chromium coating, there is now also a process of grinding the outer circle and then polishing or grinding after chrome plating with a coating thickness ≥0.10mm, but if the coating is too thick, it will not only increase the cost, but also there is a risk of defects such as peeling or delamination of the coating. Therefore, it is not recommended to use a process with a coating thickness exceeding 0.10mm.

The minimum (maximum) thickness of the hard chromium coating, the hardness of the hard chromium coating, the measurement method, and the inspection rules should be negotiated and determined according to the relevant regulations of the electroplating factory. If necessary, the adhesion strength, dimensional accuracy, and geometric tolerances of the hard chromium coating can also be included.

For the outer surface of the piston rod chrome-plated with hard chromium, the hardness of the hard chromium coating should be greater than or equal to 800HV0.2, and the thickness of the hard chromium coating should be between 0.04 and 0.10mm.

Special reminder: The hard chromium layer is very sensitive to impact, and is easily damaged by local hammering, impact, or knocking, etc. Even if the hard chromium layer is not visibly damaged by impact, it may still affect its performance.
494:
The chrome coating on the piston rod surface may crack or peel off quickly, causing further damage to the sealing device, system, and contacting metal parts. Therefore, it is essential to protect the piston rod surface during post-plating polishing or grinding. The method of using a hammer (small sheet metal hammer) to repair the damaged hard chrome layer on the piston rod is not recommended, as it will inevitably cause local out-of-roundness of the piston rod and may lead to large-scale cracking or peeling of the hard chrome layer, resulting in seal damage and external leakage at the piston rod seal.

3.7.2 Technical Requirements for Thickness and Hardness of Chrome Coating on Piston Rod Surface

A 630T hydraulic press hydraulic cylinder piston rod was scratched, causing external leakage at the piston rod seal. Upon on-site inspection, besides finding problems with the cleanliness of the hydraulic oil used, it was also considered that there were issues with the thickness and hardness of the hard chrome layer (chrome coating) on the piston rod surface, i.e., the coating was too thin and the hardness was too low.

Since some hydraulic cylinder manufacturers do not have professional instruments and equipment to check the thickness and hardness of the chrome coating on the piston rod surface, and some electroplating factories even polish the electroplated surface after plating the piston rod, the piston rod after outsourcing electroplating has become a finished product. Therefore, hydraulic cylinder manufacturers only check the appearance of the chrome coating on the piston rod surface (such as unevenness, darkness, roughness, delamination, peeling, or blistering defects) and neglect the most basic inspection of coating thickness and hardness.

There is now a fast hard chrome plating method in electroplating factories, which has problems when used to plate the piston rod surface.

According to the technical requirements proposed in this manual and referring to the provisions of GB/T 25974.2-2010 and JB/T 5082.5-2018 "Engine Cylinder Liners Part 5: Technical Conditions for Steel Plated Chrome Cylinder Liners," the outer surface of the piston rod should be plated with hard chrome, and the hardness of the chrome coating should be greater than or equal to 800 HV0.2; before polishing or grinding, the thickness of the chrome coating should be between 0.04-0.10 mm, and after polishing or grinding, the chrome coating should generally be within the range of 0.03-0.05 mm.

For some servo hydraulic cylinders (such as high-frequency, short-stroke reciprocating servo hydraulic cylinders) or some hydraulic cylinders with special requirements (such as special environmental requirements), the chrome coating after polishing or grinding should be thicker.

The hardness of the chrome coating can be tested according to the provisions of GB/T 9790-1988 "Vickers and Knoop Microhardness Tests for Metallic Coatings and Other Related Coatings."

Note: In YB/T 0172017, it is stipulated that the detection of coating hardness shall be carried out in accordance with GB/T 4340.1.

The minimum (maximum) thickness of the chrome coating can be obtained by measuring the difference in dimensions before and after plating, or by using GB/T 6462-2005 "Measurement of Thickness of Metallic and Oxide Coatings - Microscope Method," GB/T 4955-2005 "Measurement of Thickness of Metallic Coatings - Coulometric Method by Anodic Dissolution," GB/T 3156.3-2015 "Measurement of Thickness of Metallic Coatings - Scanning Electron Microscope Method," etc.

3.8 Typical Mechanical Processing and Assembly Processes for Hydraulic Cylinders

The mechanical processing process is a processing method and process that transforms various raw materials and semi-finished products into products that meet the drawings and technical requirements by using mechanical force to process them, according to the drawings and technical requirements, etc.

The assembly process is a method and process of assembling and connecting parts or components to make them into semi-finished products or finished products that meet the drawings and technical requirements, according to the drawings and technical requirements, etc.

The mechanical processing process and assembly process generally need to be specific, i.e., documented and standardized. One of the commonly used process documents - the process card, is a process document that briefly explains the processing (or assembly) process of a product or component in terms of work steps. The following mechanical processing and assembly processes are given in the form of process cards, but also include materials and their heat treatment, some surface engineering technologies, such as rolling holes, surface quenching, and surface rust prevention (coating), etc.

In order to standardize the mechanical processing process and assembly process, typical processes can be formulated, i.e., according to the structure and process characteristics of the product or part, they are classified or grouped, and unified processing (assembly) methods and processes are formulated for products or parts of the same type or group. It is very necessary to formulate typical processes for hydraulic cylinders.

Note: In GB/T 4863-2008 "Basic Terms of Mechanical Manufacturing," there are no terms such as "mechanical processing process" and "assembly process," only the term "mechanical manufacturing process," i.e., a general term for various methods and processes of manufacturing machinery.

(3) Trapezoidal Thread Machining Process
1) Trapezoidal Thread Turning Method.
① The general methods for thread turning include radial feed, oblique feed, axial feed, improved oblique feed, and double-edged alternating feed, with the latter
499:
Both are mainly used for CNC machining; the choice of cutting method primarily considers factors such as material, pitch, thread accuracy, and machine tool performance.

② For trapezoidal threads with a pitch P≤8, rough turning followed by finish turning is required. Rough turning can use radial cutting with a tool whose tooth angle is 2° smaller than the thread angle and cut to the minor diameter; finish turning can use a forming tool with the same tooth angle for radial cutting, or use a tool with the same tooth angle but thinner than the forming tool for axial cutting.

③ The tooth angle of the cutting tool is critical, and tool installation is also very important. Radial cutting produces higher thread accuracy but generally results in larger surface roughness values; radial cutting may affect the tooth shape but can produce threads with smaller surface roughness values.

④ On CNC lathes, alternating cutting with double-edged tools results in uniform wear on both cutting edges and can achieve good tooth shapes and lower surface roughness values, but the programming is complex.

2) Thread cutting tools.

① Rough turning can use high-speed steel single-tooth flat thread cutting tools or hard alloy thread cutting tools.

② Finish turning generally uses hard alloy thread forming cutting tools (indexable thread cutting tools).

3) Tool installation methods.

① Rough turning tools can generally be installed perpendicularly, but cutting may produce tooth angle errors.

② Finish turning must use special fixtures to hold the thread cutting tool.

③ Hard alloy tools should be higher than 1% of the thread outer diameter, while high-speed steel tools can be slightly below the workpiece axis.

④ The protrusion of the thread cutting tool from the tool holder should not exceed 1.5 times the height of the tool shank cross-section.

① The semi-finished blank of the lead screw to be cut should have internal stress fully eliminated to ensure stable internal structure. The blank can be spheroidized annealed with a hardness of 180～210 HBW.

② The center holes at both ends of the lead screw to be turned must be on the same straight line, and the center holes must be ground before finish turning, with a surface roughness value Ra≤0.2μm, and when matched with standard center points, the contact surface should be no less than 85%; before finish turning, the outer circle should be finely ground to ensure the outer circle cylindrical error ≤0.01mm; the gap between the outer circle and the follower rest ≤0.01mm.

③ During rough turning, a large amount of emulsion should be poured, and during finish turning, fine 884 Hydraulic Cylinder Manual

Cutting fluid. It can use 30% soybean oil + 20% kerosene + 50% high-speed all-loss system oil (high-speed spindle oil).

④ For precision turning, high-vanadium cobalt or super-hard high-speed steel turning tools can be selected. Fine-grained hard alloy (such as YG6X) forming turning tools should be selected, with high grinding support amount. It is not allowed to have burns, nicks, or burrs on the cutting edge. The blunt radius of the cutting edge R should not be greater than 0.005 mm, and the surface roughness of the cutting edge Ra should be ≤0.1 μm.

⑤ The machining environment should be clean, and the room temperature should be constant. Generally, for machining a 1000 mm long lead screw with 7-level precision, the temperature change should be ≤±1°C.

⑥ Cutting speed.
Rough turning: high-speed steel turning tool, 10 m/min; hard alloy turning tool, 30-50 m/min.
Semi-precision turning: 8-10 m/min.
Precision turning: cutting speed ≤1 m/min.

⑦ Cutting amount.
For rough turning, the cutting amount per pass is about 0.4 mm. For precision turning, the cutting amount per pass is about 0.2 mm (related to material and hardness), but the cutting amount should be gradually reduced.

⑧ Tool geometric parameters.
For precision turning tools, the front angle is 0°, the side cutting edge angle is 10°-12°, and the tool edge angle is taken as 1/4 to 1/3 of the tolerance of the lead screw thread angle.

3.9 Taboos for Design and Manufacturing of Hydraulic Cylinders

Taboos for design and manufacturing of hydraulic cylinders refer to the prohibitions, dangers, disapprovals, non-allowances, impossibilities or impossibilities expressed by "should not (or should not, not allowed)", "not suitable (or not recommended, not suggested)", "not necessary (or not necessary, not needed)", "cannot (or cannot)", "impossible (or impossible)" in the general manufacturing of hydraulic cylinders, etc. The behaviors or things that are tabooed are actually violations of the provisions, recommendations or suggestions in the relevant elements requirements, verification methods, rules, procedures or guidelines contained in the relevant standards of hydraulic cylinders.

In Appendix A of GB/T 3766-2015, as long as they are suitable and may cause serious hazards, they are all taboos for the design, manufacturing, installation and maintenance of hydraulic cylinders.

3.9.1 Taboos for Design and Selection of Hydraulic Cylinders

Since the hydraulic cylinder is a hydraulic actuator that provides linear motion, it is the simplest and most convenient to directly use the hydraulic cylinder to achieve reciprocating linear motion of the machine.

The selection of the type of hydraulic cylinder is one of the prerequisite conditions for the design calculation of the hydraulic cylinder. First, it should be determined whether to use a double-acting piston cylinder, a single-acting piston cylinder, a plunger cylinder, a single or double-acting telescopic sleeve hydraulic cylinder, or other types of hydraulic cylinders.

There are many factors to consider in the design and selection of hydraulic cylinders. For example, if the reciprocating motion speed needs to be the same, it is easier to use a double (output) rod cylinder; if the return speed of the cylinder needs to be greater than the moving speed of the cylinder, it is more appropriate to use a single piston rod piston cylinder; if only one-way drive of the external load is required, and the return trip can be reliably achieved by external force, a plunger cylinder can be selected; if it is necessary to drive the load to rotate, a swing hydraulic cylinder (combined hydraulic cylinder) can also be selected, etc.

Taking the design and selection of the plunger cylinder as an example, because the plunger cylinder usually only has one oil port, it can only drive the resistance load and cannot return by liquid pressure. That is, the plunger cylinder can only be used in occasions where there is external force (such as gravity, overload or a return cylinder) during the return trip, otherwise it cannot return. In addition, the plunger cylinder is not suitable for horizontal placement. Since it can only bear pressure, considering the stiffness, the diameter of the piston rod is relatively large, and its radial support point is also different from that of the piston cylinder, resulting in a relatively large volume and support of the plunger cylinder. If installed horizontally, the piston rod is prone to press on one side, causing unilateral wear of the guide sleeve and seal ring. If it is necessary to install it horizontally, a plunger bracket needs to be installed to prevent the plunger from sagging, causing bending and increasing initial deflection to cause jamming.

The selection of hydraulic cylinders should first be selected from standard hydraulic cylinders. There are now standard hydraulic cylinders, including hydraulic cylinders for metallurgical equipment, dump (low-speed) truck hydraulic cylinders, marine (reciprocating) hydraulic cylinders, marine hatch cover hydraulic cylinders, marine digital hydraulic cylinders, servo hydraulic cylinders (as specified in local standards), double-acting agricultural hydraulic cylinders, tractor steering hydraulic cylinders, large hydraulic cylinders, hydraulic cylinders for mining machinery, hydraulic support columns and jacks for coal mines, etc.

For products within the scope of product standards, it is taboo to design and use non-standard hydraulic cylinders; for products without product standards, it is also taboo to design and use them in violation of JB/T10205-2010.

It is inappropriate for some literature to recommend the use of double piston rod cylinders for occasions requiring the same reciprocating motion speed. In addition, if a symmetrical electro-hydraulic servo valve is used to control an asymmetric servo hydraulic cylinder (differential cylinder), the servo hydraulic cylinder can only withstand pressure and cannot withstand tension, and phenomena such as pressure out of control, cavitation and pressure shock may occur.

3.9.2 Taboos in Hydraulic Cylinder Parameter Design

The basic parameters of hydraulic cylinders in various hydraulic cylinder standards are not completely identical. In JB/T 10205—2010, it is stipulated that: "The basic parameters of hydraulic cylinders should include the cylinder bore, piston rod diameter (outer), nominal pressure, stroke, and installation dimensions."

In addition to the basic parameters of hydraulic cylinders specified in the above standards, there are also those in other hydraulic cylinder and related standards that list the thrust and pull force at nominal pressure, piston speed, rated pressure, minimum piston rod diameter (outer), plunger diameter for plunger-type hydraulic cylinders, limit or maximum stroke, area ratio of two chambers, threaded ports and nominal bore of ports, piston rod thread type and size, mass, installation type, and connection dimensions as basic parameters of hydraulic cylinders.

In JB/T 2184—2007, the main parameters of hydraulic cylinders are specified as: Cylinder bore × Stroke, with the unit being mm.

Since the nominal pressure or rated pressure of a hydraulic cylinder generally depends on the hydraulic system of the host machine, it is taboo for the nominal pressure or rated pressure of the hydraulic cylinder to be higher than the nominal pressure or rated pressure of the hydraulic system and hydraulic pump of the host machine; if it is necessary to use the hydraulic system of the host machine to perform pressure resistance testing on the hydraulic cylinder, the pressure should not exceed the maximum allowable pressure of the hydraulic cylinder.
514: The nominal pressure or rated pressure of the hydraulic cylinder should be less than 2/3 of the nominal pressure or rated pressure of the host hydraulic system and hydraulic pump during testing. The basic parameters, structural form, dimensions, and tolerances of the hydraulic cylinder components should comply with relevant standards, such as the nominal pressure should comply with the provisions of GB/T 23426, the inner diameter of the cylinder and the diameter of the piston rod should comply with the provisions of GB/T 23448, the thread size of the oil port connection should comply with the provisions of GB/T 28778.1, and the sealing groove should comply with the provisions of GB/T 28779, GB/T 34552.1, GB 65777, GB/T 65778, 1524.3 and other standards, and taboo to adopt non-standard structural forms or dimensions. If the hydraulic cylinder is not designed according to relevant standards, it may cause problems with matching the hydraulic pump, and it may also make it difficult to select seals and accessories for the hydraulic cylinder. The dimensions such as the cylinder diameter and piston rod diameter calculated according to the load and nominal (rated) pressure must be rounded to the values specified in the standard, otherwise it may be impossible to select suitable seals. When determining the wall thickness of the cylinder, taboo to ignore the additional dimensions that should be added to the cylinder due to structural elements such as thread processing, grooves, and oil port settings, as well as processability requirements, so as not to cause the actual dimensions to be reduced or stress concentration, resulting in a decrease in the pressure bearing capacity, strength, and stiffness of the hydraulic cylinder. Taboo to have too small a safety factor for the hydraulic cylinder. In order to ensure sufficient load-bearing capacity of the hydraulic cylinder and consider the influence of factors such as the uniformity of the material and stress concentration, the hydraulic cylinder must have sufficient safety factor, which should generally be above 5. At the same time, under the condition of meeting the force and stroke requirements of the driving load, taboo to have an excessively large external contour size of the hydraulic cylinder. 3.9.3 Taboos for Metal Material Selection and Structural Design of Hydraulic Cylinders 1. Taboos for Metal Material Selection of Cylinder Components The reference [99] points out: "When there is severe impact during work, the cylinder and end cover of the hydraulic cylinder cannot use brittle materials such as cast iron." However, it should also be noted that the reference [115] points out: "Low and medium carbon carbon steel and alloy steel have high multiple impact strength after quenching and low and medium temperature tempering. The comprehensive mechanical properties of quenching + high temperature tempering (i.e. quenching and tempering) are the best, although it can withstand a high strength of a single impact, but the strength of small energy multiple impacts is very low." When the cylinder needs to be welded with the cylinder bottom, cylinder head, pipe joint (connecting pipe), or ear ring, etc., 35 steel with good weldability should be used, and tempered after rough machining. For the cylinder (tube) material of a hydraulic cylinder that works in an environment with a temperature lower than -50°C, 35 steel, 45 steel, or low-temperature steel that has been tempered must be selected. The piston rod that works under corrosive conditions should be made of stainless steel as much as possible. 2. Taboo to use a tie-rod structure for hydraulic cylinders under long stroke, large cylinder diameter, and high pressure. Considering the strength and stiffness of the threaded connection, in order to reduce the tensile force and stress amplitude on the bolt, the stiffness of the bolt can be reduced or the stiffness of the connected parts can be increased. A measure to reduce the stiffness of the bolt is given in reference [54], as shown in Figure 3-14. In reference [110], it is pointed out: "Although the tie-rod hydraulic cylinder has the characteristics of good processability and maintainability, when the length of the hydraulic cylinder is 1500-2000mm, due to the action of hydraulic force, it is easy to cause the tie-rod to elongate and deform, resulting in leakage. The troubleshooting method: Avoid using a tie-rod structure for long hydraulic cylinders and choose a flange connection instead." 3. Taboo to have poor stability of the piston rod. Reference [110] lists a case where the hydraulic cylinder is improperly designed, resulting in poor stability of the piston rod. The cause of the failure: The length of the piston rod guide sleeve is too small, resulting in poor guiding ability. The troubleshooting method: The length L of the guide sleeve generally varies depending on the size of the hydraulic cylinder, the type of piston rod seal, and the purpose, but it should generally be more than 3/5 of the piston rod diameter to ensure that the piston rod has sufficient stability. Reference [99] points out: "When using a long-stroke hydraulic cylinder, it is necessary to comprehensively consider selecting a piston rod with sufficient stiffness and installing an intermediate spacer ring." This manual requires that under normal circumstances, taboo to have a guide sleeve guiding length or supporting length B < 0.7d (d is the piston rod diameter). 4. Other taboos in the structural design of hydraulic cylinders 1) Reference [110] points out: "The end cover of the hydraulic cylinder should not be too thin. The end cover of the hydraulic cylinder bears a large liquid pressure. If the end cover is too thin, gaps are likely to occur, leading to leakage; if the bolt spacing is too large and the bolt preload torque is different, gaps are also likely to occur locally under the action of hydraulic force, thereby leading to leakage." 2) If a vent (discharge) valve is installed on the hydraulic cylinder, taboo to not be in the highest position and not easily accessible during installation. 3) If it can be foreseen that the piston rod may be crushed, scratched, and corroded, taboo to not install a protective cover. 4) Taboo to not design or configure a vent (discharge) port for a hydraulic cylinder with an air cavity; taboo that venting through this vent (discharge) port may cause danger. 5) Taboo to not have an anti-loosening design for the adjustable stroke terminal stop installed inside or outside the hydraulic cylinder; taboo to install a safety valve on the hydraulic cylinder or hydraulic system that cannot automatically reset.

1. Design Taboos for Sealing Grooves
Do not use sealing grooves specified outside the declared compliant hydraulic cylinder product standards or JBT 10205-2010 "Hydraulic Cylinders" for hydraulic cylinder product design.

2. Static sealing grooves should also be included in general hydraulic cylinder design, such as O-ring grooves for hydraulic and pneumatic applications, but are missing in JBT 10205-2010.
However, considering current standards, since the sealing grooves provided in JBT 10205-2010 cannot meet the requirements of most hydraulic cylinder seals and their design, if sealing grooves outside these product standards are used, the hydraulic cylinder cannot declare compliance with any product standard, including JBT 10205-2010 "Hydraulic Cylinders", and the designed hydraulic cylinder product will be a non-standard product.
In summary, to avoid designing and manufacturing non-standard products, referring to the provisions on seal and groove selection in GB 13342-2007 "General Technical Conditions for Marine Reciprocating Hydraulic Cylinders", the design taboos for sealing grooves should be further stated as follows: priority should be given to using seals and grooves specified in national standards for hydraulic cylinder product design; non-standard seals and grooves, i.e., those without current international, Chinese, or foreign standards, should not be used for hydraulic cylinder product design.
Hydraulic cylinders designed with non-standard sealing grooves are most likely to fail to find matching seals. Using seals specified outside standard regulations may result in unguaranteed sealing performance; designing and manufacturing seals independently may also have problems with sealing performance including reliability and durability regardless of cost; self-made seals cannot be stored for extended periods, and urgent maintenance and replacement of seals may face situations where no seals are available for replacement.
Various types of standard grooves are composed of various geometric elements, such as dimensional and tolerance elements, geometric tolerance elements, and surface structure elements, etc. Grooves that meet these groove composition elements and are within the applicable range of the groove are standard grooves. Excessive requirements for various elements may also lead to non-standard groove design, such as unrealistically reducing dimensional tolerances to 1/5 or 1/10 of the original tolerance, etc.
Non-standard sealing grooves do not refer to modifications to sealing grooves made to adjust seal compression, adapt to seal material swelling values, and install thicker retaining rings, etc.

Sealing elements or devices incompatible with the working medium should not be selected for hydraulic cylinders.

3. Taboos in Selection of Structural Types of Sealing Components (Rings)

At present, most hydraulic cylinder sealing systems contain polyurethane Y-rings or U-rings. However, with the progress of hydraulic cylinder sealing technology and the improvement of customers' requirements for product quality, their limitations (or defects) have also become increasingly prominent.

From the perspective of material properties, compared with NBR, it has the following limitations:

1) Large permanent deformation under compression. At high temperatures, the permanent deformation under compression of polyurethane Y-rings or U-rings is 1-2 times that of NBR rubber sealing rings.

2) Severe hydrolysis at high temperatures. During the use of hydraulic oil, it is generally inevitable that it is contaminated by water (such as moisture, humidity invasion). The increase of water content and the rise of oil temperature will make the hydrolysis effect on general polyurethane Y-rings or U-rings more serious, and this hydrolysis is irreversible and fatal damage. However, polyurethane materials resistant to hydrolysis have poor elasticity and are rarely used to make Y-rings or U-rings.

3) Large leakage under low pressure or high-speed conditions.

Now, when selecting polyurethane materials to make Y-rings or U-rings, there are generally:

1) Polyurethane materials resistant to high temperatures are often not resistant to low temperatures.

2) If the material hardness is selected to be high, the sealing ring has poor elasticity; if the material hardness is selected to be low, the sealing ring is severely squeezed out.

3) Polyurethane materials with high elasticity have poor high-temperature resistance.

4) Polyurethane materials resistant to hydrolysis have problems with elasticity and low-temperature resistance.

Therefore, manufacturers of sealing components are often in a dilemma of being unable to take care of both sides.

From the perspective of structural type, it has the following defects:

1) Compared with NBR rubber, it has poor conformity and low-temperature follow-up.

2) The large contact area leads to large friction force.

3) It is prone to crawling and abnormal noise problems.

4) Air is easily trapped in the groove at the end of the lip, which may lead to burning of the sealing lip.

5) Insufficient material hardness may lead to extrusion of the base of the sealing ring.

6) When two lip-shaped sealing rings are installed back-to-back, the back pressure generated may damage the lip of the sealing ring.

7) Large-section sealing rings have large friction force, are difficult to install, and have high cost.

8) Small-section sealing rings are prone to flipping and have poor pressure resistance.

Due to the above limitations (defects) of polyurethane Y-rings or U-rings, the problems of hydraulic cylinder sealing systems nowadays are mostly concentrated on them. Therefore, the following taboos (not suitable) are proposed:

1) Hydraulic cylinder sealing systems should not prioritize the selection of polyurethane Y-rings or U-rings.

2) Polyurethane Y-rings or U-rings should not be selected in high-temperature or humid-heat environments.

3) Polyurethane Y-rings or U-rings should not be selected under low-pressure or high-speed conditions.

4) Hydraulic cylinders with low-friction (or dynamic characteristic) requirements should not select polyurethane Y-rings or U-rings.

5) When two lip-shaped sealing rings are installed back-to-back, polyurethane Y-rings or U-rings without pressure relief grooves should not be selected.

The above main viewpoints have been proved by a large number of comparative bench tests on hydraulic cylinder sealing performance conducted by Suzhou Meifurui New Material Technology Co., Ltd.

4. Taboos in Determining Sealing Conditions

Hydraulic cylinder sealing devices or systems whose environmental temperature, working medium temperature, reciprocating motion speed, sealing gap, working pressure range, and working temperature range do not meet the requirements of the standards should not be selected or designed.

Generally speaking, reciprocating motion speed, sealing gap, working pressure range, and working temperature range are performance parameters of hydraulic cylinder sealing components (rings), devices or systems, and all should contain a range expressed by high (large) or low (small), or the highest (large) or lowest (small) (value).

The lowest environmental temperature or the lowest value of the environmental temperature should be equal to the lowest working medium temperature or the lowest value of the working medium temperature.

5. Taboos in Hydraulic Cylinder Seal Design Based on Sealing Performance
1) Hydraulic cylinder seal devices or systems that may cause external leakage when the hydraulic cylinder is stationary should not be selected or designed.
Generally, seals (seal devices) for reciprocating motion that are not specified by standards or have not been verified should not be used for static sealing of hydraulic cylinders. In practice, the author has not only seen adapters seals (rings) specified in JB/T10205—2010 "Hydraulic Cylinders" used for static sealing, but also seen rotary (shaft) seals used for static sealing.
It should be particularly noted that lip packings (various forms such as V-shaped, U-shaped, L-shaped, Y-shaped, etc.) specified in JB/T66122—2008 "Terms for Static Seals and Packing Seals" are mostly not suitable for static sealing of hydraulic cylinders. This is not only because the standard's scope of application does not explicitly include hydraulic cylinder seals, but also because
518:
Frictional resistance caused by the friction between the dynamic sealing device and the mating parts (couplings), and even the metal friction between the piston rod and the guide bushing (cylinder head), and between the piston and the cylinder barrel, results in reduced output force efficiency of the cylinder, increased temperature of the hydraulic oil, and wear of cylinder components. Except for using metal (such as tin bronze) as guide rings or support rings, metal friction between other cylinder components should be avoided as much as possible during the reciprocating motion of the hydraulic cylinder.

1) Do not select or design a hydraulic cylinder sealing device or system that causes the (minimum) starting pressure of the hydraulic cylinder to not meet the standard requirements. A suitable sealing device or system should be selected or designed, especially for hydraulic cylinders with dynamic characteristic requirements, such as digital hydraulic cylinders and servo hydraulic cylinders. Although the standard stipulates the use of V-ring seals on hydraulic cylinders for lifting purposes, when selecting or designing a sealing device or system containing V-ring seals, the (minimum) starting pressure should be estimated to see if it exceeds the standard. Excessive "redundant design" of the sealing system should be avoided, including excessive support and guidance.

2) Do not select or design a hydraulic cylinder sealing device or system that causes insufficient guidance and support for the piston and piston rod of the hydraulic cylinder. When driving the load with the piston rod of the hydraulic cylinder extended, especially when the piston rod of a long-stroke hydraulic cylinder is near the limit extension, the piston rod may bend or become unstable. If the support length or guidance length of the piston and piston rod of the hydraulic cylinder is insufficient, the possibility of the piston rod bending or becoming unstable is greater. The load driven by the hydraulic cylinder may have lateral component forces. In this case, if the support length or guidance length of the piston and piston rod of the hydraulic cylinder is insufficient, severe wear of the cylinder components may occur. If the support length or guidance length of the piston and piston rod of the hydraulic cylinder is insufficient, it may also cause an increase in the eccentricity of the hydraulic cylinder, resulting in local wear of the cylinder components. All these situations may increase the friction force of the hydraulic cylinder when carrying a load to varying degrees.

3) Do not select or design a hydraulic cylinder sealing device or system that causes the output force efficiency (load efficiency) of the hydraulic cylinder to not meet the standard requirements. The friction force when carrying a load directly reduces the output force efficiency of the cylinder. According to the definition and calculation formula of the output force efficiency of the cylinder, if the tested hydraulic cylinder maintains a uniform motion state at different pressures to detect the output force efficiency of the cylinder, then the formula pA=W+F2+F3 must be true, where pA is the theoretical output force of the cylinder, W is the actual output force of the cylinder, F2 is the friction resistance generated by friction, and F3 is the resistance generated by back pressure. According to the provisions of JB/T10205-2010 "Hydraulic Cylinder", the output force efficiency of the cylinder should be η=W/(pA)×100%≥90%. If the back pressure is limited or ignored, the friction resistance generated by friction will be limited.

7. Taboos for Hydraulic Cylinder Sealing Design Based on Hydraulic Cylinder Operating Performance

1) Do not select or design a hydraulic cylinder sealing device or system that causes vibration, sticking, or crawling of the hydraulic cylinder. There are many factors that cause the hydraulic cylinder to vibrate, stick, or crawl. Even hydraulic cylinders that pass factory tests and inspections may exhibit these conditions during use. However, the probability of the sealing system's "redundant design" and the design of sealing rings, support rings, or retaining rings with excessive interference fit may be very high.

2) In a reciprocating motion sealing system, do not select or design a sealing device or system with a large difference between the static and dynamic friction coefficients. If the static and dynamic friction coefficients of the sealing device or system in the hydraulic cylinder differ too much, it may cause the (minimum) starting pressure of the hydraulic cylinder to exceed the standard, crawling, or sudden jumping (instantaneous jumping) of the hydraulic cylinder when starting. The possible reasons for this are:
① Inappropriate selection of sealing materials, including support ring and guide ring materials.
② Problems with the sealing material during use, such as deformation of polyamide when exposed to water.
③ The working environment temperature of the hydraulic cylinder exceeds the allowable use temperature of the sealing components.
④ Unreasonable design or installation of the sealing system, resulting in dry friction.
⑤ Unreasonable selection of sealing components, including support rings, or quality problems with the components themselves.
⑥ Unreasonable design of the sealing groove.
⑦ Inappropriate selection of surface roughness of mating parts or lack of demagnetization.
⑧ Inconsistent surface roughness or surface hardness of mating parts.
⑨ Other reasons such as unreasonable structural design of the hydraulic cylinder, unreasonable design or adjustment of the cushioning device, bending or instability of the piston rod, air in the working medium, or piston seal leakage.

3) Do not select or design a hydraulic cylinder sealing device or system that causes the dynamic characteristics of the hydraulic cylinder to not meet the standard requirements. One of the technical requirements for assembly quality in the JB/T10205-2010 "Hydraulic Cylinder" standard is that "after assembly, the hydraulic cylinder should be guaranteed to move freely." Digital hydraulic cylinders and servo hydraulic cylinders have further requirements for dynamic characteristics (dynamic indicators), such as step response and frequency response for servo hydraulic cylinders. Taking DB44/T11169.1 "Servo Hydraulic Cylinder Part 1: Technical Conditions" as an example, the required "minimum starting pressure" value is so small that it cannot be achieved by merely improving the assembly quality level. Instead, the selected or designed hydraulic cylinder sealing device or system should first have performance that meets the relevant standard requirements.

3.9.5 Taboos for Hydraulic Cylinder Cushioning Device Design

The cushioning of a cylinder with a cushioning device is a means of deceleration when the moving parts are approaching the end of their motion. There are mainly two types: fixed and adjustable.

There are several taboos in the design of fixed hydraulic cushioning devices:
1) Taboo for excessive cushioning length. The cushioning device should be able to absorb the maximum kinetic energy with a shorter cushioning length (also known as cushioning stroke) of the cylinder.
519:
The goal is to completely convert the kinetic energy of the moving parts (including all connecting parts or related parts) into heat energy.

2) During the buffering process, it is forbidden to have excessively high pressure pulses or excessively high peak pressure in the buffering chamber. The change in pressure should be a gradual process.

3) It is forbidden for the peak buffering pressure in the buffering chamber (at the cylinder head end) to exceed 1.5 times the nominal pressure of the hydraulic cylinder.

4) For hydraulic cylinders with buffering devices installed at the rod end, it is forbidden for the (excessively high) buffering pressure to act on the piston rod dynamic sealing system.

5) It is forbidden for the oil temperature to be too high. The conversion of kinetic energy into heat energy causes the temperature of the hydraulic oil to rise, and the maximum temperature of the oil should not exceed the maximum allowable operating temperature of the sealing elements.

6) It is forbidden to install unnecessary buffering devices. According to JB/T10205-2010 "Hydraulic Cylinders", "For hydraulic cylinders that require buffering performance, it shall be determined through consultation between the user and the manufacturer." For hydraulic cylinders that do not require buffering devices, do not add them unnecessarily; for cases where the buffering device of the hydraulic cylinder alone cannot convert all kinetic energy, other deceleration and braking measures should be taken, such as designing braking circuits in the hydraulic system.

7) It is forbidden for the designed buffering device to affect the starting performance of the hydraulic cylinder. The starting performance of the hydraulic cylinder should be considered, and the (minimum) starting pressure of the hydraulic cylinder should not exceed the requirements of relevant standards; abnormal situations such as delayed movement or surging (abnormal movement) and abnormal noise should be avoided when the piston starts or leaves the buffering area.

8) It is forbidden for the nominal flow rate of the check valve in the buffering valve buffering device to be too small. If the designed check valve has too small a nominal flow rate, it may cause the hydraulic cylinder to suddenly stop or retreat when starting.

A case is listed in reference [110]: When the hydraulic cylinder moves at a high speed, it is prone to produce great impact and noise when suddenly stopping at the end of the stroke, causing damage to the hydraulic cylinder, and even damaging various valves, pipes and related mechanical parts. The cause of the fault: As shown in Figure 3-15a, due to the large mass of the load, hydraulic cylinder piston and piston rod itself, the momentum of the movement is very large, so when it suddenly stops at the end of the stroke, it is prone to produce great impact and noise, causing damage to the hydraulic system. The troubleshooting method: In order to eliminate this impact, corresponding components can be installed in the hydraulic circuit to control the speed of the hydraulic cylinder. A buffering device should be installed for the fast-acting hydraulic cylinder, such as a fixed or adjustable hydraulic cylinder buffering device, as shown in Figure 3-15b.

The current problem is that if the speed of the hydraulic cylinder during the entire stroke can be reduced, it can fundamentally solve the impact and noise problems when the hydraulic cylinder reaches the end of its stroke, and the hydraulic cylinder itself may not need to be equipped with a buffering device. However, the example in reference [110] is neither the buffering device design of the hydraulic cylinder itself nor the buffering design of the hydraulic system where the hydraulic cylinder is located.

3.9.5 缓冲机构的选用

缓冲机构的选用应根据液压缸的工作要求、缓冲类型、缓冲形式、缓冲方式、缓冲性能、缓冲机构类型以及液压缸的用途等因素综合考虑。例如，要求速度变换缓慢的液压缸，当活塞速度为0.05～0.12 m/s时，也应采用缓冲装置。

对于缸外制动机构，当vm≥1 m/s时，缸内缓冲机构不可能吸收全部动能，必须要在缸外加装制动机构，如下所述：

1）在外部加装行程开关。当开始进入缓冲阶段时，开关即切断供油，使液压能等于零，但仍可形成压力脉冲。

2）在活塞杆与负载之间加装减振器。

3）在液压缸出口加装液控节流阀。

此外，可按工作过程对活塞线速度变化的要求，确定缓冲机构的类型，如下所述：

1）减速过渡过程要求十分柔和，如砂型操作、易碎物品托盘操作、精密磨床进给等，宜选用近似恒减速型缓冲机构，如多孔缸筒型或多孔柱塞型以及自动节流型。

2）减速机构允许微量脉冲，如普通机床、粗轧机等，可采用铣槽型、阶梯型缓冲机构。

3）减速机构允许承受一定的脉冲，可采用圆锥型或双圆锥型，甚至圆柱型柱塞的缓冲机构。

3.9.6 液压缸上集成的配管选用与油路块设计禁忌

1. 配管选用禁忌

1）禁忌选用M、G、R和NPT以外的连接螺纹，且应首选普通细牙(M)螺纹。

2）禁忌选用的管接头型式达不到液压系统的工作压力或公称压力，或没有相应的规格、产品。

3）禁忌管接头及被连接管的最大工作压力或公称压力超过规定的压力、温度要求。管接头只有在规定的压力、温度(范围)下使用才是安全的。连接管壁厚应足够，特殊场合使用的如舰船上的液压系统(站)连接管(碳钢无缝钢管)应考虑留有腐蚀余量。

4）禁忌管接头及被连接管的通流能力低于液压系统的要求。

5）禁忌管子弯曲半径及偏差、管子弯曲处圆度公差及波纹深度等超出JB/T5000.3的规定，管子冷弯曲壁厚减薄率不得大于15%。

6）禁忌配管的清洁度超标。除镀锌钢管外，所有碳钢钢管(包括预制成型管路)都要进行酸洗、中和、清洗吹干及防锈处理。

7）禁忌泄漏。预制完成的管子焊接部位都要进行耐压试验，试验压力为工作压力的1.5倍，保压10 min，应无泄漏及其他异常现象发生；对装配完成的管路，按液压系统(管子)技术要求进行耐压试验。

8）禁忌在较大通径或一些特殊场合应用管接头连接的硬管总成。一般在公称通径≥40 mm时应采用法兰连接的硬管总成；一些特殊场合应用的配管，如振动、摇摆及冲击严重的场合，可在公称通径≥25 mm时即采用法兰连接的硬管总成。

9）禁忌软管总成在一些特殊情况下的应用。有技术要求或安全技术要求标准规定的一些特殊场合或设备，软管总成不能应用。

2. 油路块设计禁忌

油路块是可用于安装插装阀、叠加阀和板式阀并按液压回路图通过油道使阀孔口连通的立方体基板，归属于配管。在各标准及参考文献中，还有将油路块称为集成块、油路板、安装板、底座、底板、底板块、基础板或阀块的。

油路块设计应遵循一些原则。根据相关标准及实践经验的总结，列出以下若干油路块设计禁忌，供读者参考。

(1) 油路块材料选择禁忌

选用铸铁制造中、高压和较大尺寸的油路块时一定要慎重。首先，较大尺寸的立方体铸件不是任何一家铸造厂都可以铸造合格的；其次，一旦加工时出现问题修复困难。

通常可选用Q235、Q345、20、35或45碳钢钢板或锻件制造油路块。使用钢板制造油路块应注意其各向力学性能的不同及可能存在的质量缺陷。

船用二通插装阀油路块推荐采用中碳钢锻件，且毛坯应消除内应力并进行无损检测。

用于管接头试验的油路块规定不得有镀层，硬度值应为GB/T230.1规定的35～45 HRC。

禁忌用铸铁制造中、高压或中、大型以及在振动场合使用的油路块。

(2) 油路块型式确定禁忌

油路块外形可设计成正方形或长方形六面体，一般应禁忌设计四边带地脚凸缘的油路块。油路块外形尺寸不宜过大，否则加工制造困难；一般确定的三个基准面应相互垂直，且应使设计基准、工艺基准和测量基准重合，三个基准面应留0.3 mm左右的精磨量。

禁忌液压阀安装面超出油路块。

在液压系统较为复杂、液压阀较多的情况下，可采用多个油路块叠加的形式。相互叠加的油路块上下面一般应有公共的P油路、公用的T油路和L油路以及至少四个用于连接的螺钉(通)孔(最下层的为第90页)

Threaded holes, generally the topmost one is a counterbore for cylindrical head screws.

The dimensional tolerance of the manifold's external shape should generally not exceed the requirements for JS grade in GB/T 1804.

The external oil ports of the manifold should be uniformly arranged on one surface; manifolds weighing more than 15 kg should have lifting facilities.

Under the pressure test pressure (or rated pressure) of the manifold and within the specified time, after 1 hour of immersion in 90°C hydraulic oil, no deformation should occur that would cause hydraulic valve malfunction (or stated as "should not cause malfunction due to deformation").

Note that the edges of the hexahedron should be chamfered at 2×45° or 1.5×45°, and the surface can be treated with bluing or chemical nickel plating.

(3) Taboos in dimension marking for manifolds

The dimension marking for a certain surface of the manifold can be marked in the form of dimensions starting from the same reference, or it can be listed in coordinate form. This common reference is generally selected as the lower-left corner of the main view of the manifold as the coordinate origin.

The dimensions of the hydraulic valve mounting surface can be marked as reference dimensions at the same time according to its marking method.

Taboo dimension markings that are not conducive to inspection and verification.

(4) Taboos in the design of flow channel cross-sectional area and minimum spacing for manifolds

Reference literature suggests that for medium and low-pressure hydraulic systems, the minimum spacing between flow channels (oil passages) in the manifold should not be less than 5 mm, and for high-pressure hydraulic systems, it should be larger. Other reference literature suggests determining the minimum spacing between flow channels (oil passages) in the manifold based on the flow channel diameter, i.e., when the diameter is less than or equal to ф2.5 mm, the minimum spacing between flow channels (oil passages) in the manifold should not be less than 5 mm; when the diameter is greater than ф2.5 mm, the minimum spacing between flow channels (oil passages) in the manifold should generally not be less than 10 mm.

For steel manifolds without product standard specifications, the minimum spacing between flow channels (oil passages) (actual) can refer to the wall thickness of corresponding nominal pressure hard pipes (steel pipes), but generally should not be less than 5 mm in design.

The cross-sectional area of the manifold flow channel should be at least equal to the flow area of the relevant components. The recommended pipe flow rate for the nominal diameter of the pressure oil passage can refer to the design of the flow rate limit for oil in system metal piping, such as the recommended oil flow rate values for system metal piping in Table 4-151.

For a flow channel hole drilled from both ends (counter-drilling), the maximum deviation at the joint point should not exceed 0.4 mm.

Taboos include designing the cross-sectional area of flow channels and the spacing between oil passages in the manifold too small.

(5) Taboos in plugging holes in manifolds

Generally, there may be process holes on the manifold, and plugging holes means blocking these process holes according to process requirements. There are three common methods for plugging holes on steel manifolds: welding, ball expansion, and screw plugs.

When using the welding method to plug holes, a cylindrical plug should generally be pre-installed inside the hole, made of low-carbon steel, about 5 mm in length, and tightly fitted with the hole; a welding (seam) thickness of more than 5 mm should be left, and sealed welding should be performed according to the plug welding process, but there should be a certain weld bead height (excess height).

The author disagrees with the suggestion in some reference literature that process holes with a diameter of ф5 mm and below can be directly welded and plugged without pre-installing a cylindrical plug; also disagrees with using steel balls as pre-installed plugs for welding.

When using hydraulic pneumatic ball expansion plugs to plug holes, as long as the dimensions and tolerances of the mounting holes are processed and assembled strictly according to JB/T 9157-2011 "Dimensions and Tolerances for Hydraulic Pneumatic Ball Expansion Plugs", they can generally be used under a maximum working pressure of 40 MPa, and the manifold material can be gray cast iron, ductile iron, carbon steel, or alloy steel.

Note: If there are no technically skilled operators and strict process guarantees, try not to use hydraulic pneumatic ball expansion plugs to plug holes, especially in military products.

When using screw plugs to plug holes, pressure oil passages can only use hexagonal screw plugs specified in GB/T 2878.4-2011 (external and internal).

For test (permanent blocking) oil ports, M14×1.5 hexagonal screw plugs are preferred for plugging.

Process holes on marine two-way cartridge valve manifolds should be blocked using removable methods such as plugs or flanges as much as possible.

For manifolds with pressure passages and process holes, using tapered screw plugs to plug holes is now taboo.

(6) Taboos in surface flatness and surface roughness of manifolds

In addition to ensuring the design and manufacture of corresponding holes on the manifold according to the dimensions and tolerances, position tolerances, etc. specified by the components (hydraulic valves), ensuring the verticality tolerance of threaded (screw) holes is also particularly important.

The flatness tolerance for the contact surface (mounting surface) between the current components (hydraulic valves) and the manifold is generally required to be 0.01 mm/100 mm, and the surface roughness value Ra should be ≤0.8 μm, but should comply with the requirements of the hydraulic valve manufacturer you choose.

Taboos include surface quality defects such as bumps, scratches, scribe marks, nicks, indentations, rust spots, and peeling plating on the component mounting surface.

(7) Taboos in the design of holes and threaded oil ports on manifolds

Try to avoid designing long holes, inclined holes, intersecting holes, and half-intersecting holes. Generally, when the hole depth exceeds 25 times the hole diameter or more, processing becomes difficult; when the eccentricity between two holes of equal diameter exceeds 30%, both the flow area and local resistance will have problems.

Threaded oil ports used for external connections should ensure their verticality. Generally, the verticality tolerance for threaded oil ports with M22×1.5 mm and below is ф0.10 mm, and for threaded oil ports with M22×1.5 mm and above is ф0.20 mm; the thread tapping length for threaded oil ports should be sufficient; the thread accuracy should comply with GB/T 0015 Hydraulic Cylinder Manual.

Considering the assembly and disassembly of pipe joints, sufficient wrench space should be left between adjacent threaded oil ports and between them and other components.
Considering the strength and rigidity of oil ports, the minimum center distance between adjacent threaded oil ports should be 1.5 times the oil port diameter.
It is prohibited to design flow channels in hydraulic blocks that are difficult to process or have poor flow characteristics; it is also prohibited to design piping that cannot be assembled or disassembled.
(8) Taboos for Marking Hydraulic Blocks
The marking of valve mounting surfaces on hydraulic blocks generally used for mounting plate valves and stack valves can be carried out according to the relevant regulations of hydraulic systems. However, GB/T14043-2005 "Identification Symbols for Hydraulic Valve Mounting Surfaces and Cartridge Valve Valve Holes" stipulates the identification symbols for hydraulic valve mounting surfaces and cartridge valve valve holes that comply with national and international standards.
Further reference can also be made to the provisions of GB/T17490-1998 or ISO16874 (i.e., GB/T36997-2018).
Identification marks should be made on the side of each external oil port at a position not less than 6 mm from the edge of the hole and not affecting the sealing.
It is prohibited to omit identification marks on external oil ports of hydraulic blocks.
Using computer-aided three-dimensional software to model hydraulic blocks can display the relative positions of each hole in its internal space and the connection status of each hole, allowing for a three-dimensional and intuitive check of the design results. However, the above taboos are of great significance for the design of hydraulic blocks using computer-aided three-dimensional software.
3.9.7 Taboos for Installation and Connection of Hydraulic Cylinders
Regardless of whether the installation posture of hydraulic cylinders is horizontal, vertical, or inclined, the effects of the weight of the piston rod and its connecting parts, as well as the lateral forces applied externally, on their guidance, support, and movement cannot be ignored, especially for horizontally installed hydraulic cylinders.
For large horizontally installed hydraulic cylinders and long-stroke solid piston rod hydraulic cylinders, the weight of the piston rod and the moving parts it drives can cause an increase in the eccentricity between the piston and piston rod and the cylinder barrel and guide sleeve, resulting in local wear, increased internal and external leakage of the hydraulic cylinder, and a shortened service life of the hydraulic cylinder.
If necessary, additional guidance and support should be provided for the piston rod or moving parts.
For vertically installed hydraulic cylinders with a top-mounted configuration, the weight of the piston, piston rod, and the moving parts it drives is an overrunning load during the cylinder's stroke, affecting the deceleration, braking, stopping, and locking of the hydraulic cylinder; for bottom-mounted installations, it affects the return stroke motion and stopping.
For heavy-load, hollow piston rod, long-stroke, rear lug-mounted piston rod end pin hole or lug-connected hydraulic cylinders, and plunger cylinders, special attention should be paid to their rod stability (instability) issues.
Hydraulic cylinders with inclination and swing requirements should be able to work normally under certain inclination and swing conditions.
It is prohibited to install and connect hydraulic cylinders in an unstable or unreliable manner.
1) It is prohibited to determine the installation and connection method of the cylinder without considering the structural layout of the host machine, installation conditions, motion form, and requirements. Whether the installation and connection method of the hydraulic cylinder is appropriate has a significant impact on the service life and efficiency of the cylinder, and in severe cases, it can lead to abnormal motion.
2) It is prohibited to ignore the geometric tolerances of the hydraulic cylinder barrel, lugs, and pin shafts. In order to reduce the starting pressure of the hydraulic cylinder and ensure that there is no "binding" phenomenon during motion, sufficient attention should be paid to the geometric tolerances of the barrel. Generally, the roundness and cylindricity errors of the inner diameter of the barrel should not be greater than half of the diameter tolerance of the barrel; the straightness error of the barrel axis should not be greater than 0.03 mm per 500 mm length; the axial circular runout error of the end face of the barrel should not be greater than 0.04 mm per 100 mm. For lug-type hydraulic cylinders, the position tolerance error of the lug holes relative to the barrel axis should not be greater than 0.03 mm; for pin-type hydraulic cylinders, the position tolerance error of the pin axis should not be greater than 0.1 mm, and the perpendicularity error should not be greater than 0.1 mm per 100 mm length.
3) Try to avoid the piston rod of the hydraulic cylinder bearing the maximum load in a compressed state to prevent instability of the piston rod.
The installation method and load guidance will directly affect the bending stability of the piston rod. The specific requirements given in reference [99] are as follows:
1) Lug installation: The force acts within a plane, and if the lug is equipped with a ball joint, it can be deflected within a cone angle of ±4°.
2) Pin installation: The force acts within a plane, and the most commonly used types are front pin and intermediate pin. Rear pin is only used for small, short-stroke hydraulic cylinders because of its large support length, which affects the bending stability of the piston.
3) Flange installation: The force and support center are on the same axis, and the connection between the flange and the support seat should allow the flange surface to bear the force, rather than the fixing screws. For example, for front flange installation, if the force is a thrust, the type shown in Figure 3-17a should be adopted, avoiding the type shown in Figure 3-17b; if the force is a pull, the opposite is true; for rear flange installation, if the force is a thrust, the type shown in Figure 3-18a should be adopted, avoiding the type shown in Figure 3-18b; if the force is a pull, the opposite is true.

Chapter 4 Hydraulic Cylinder Design and Selection for Hydraulic Press (Machine)

The hydraulic cylinder in the hydraulic system of a hydraulic press (machine) should comply with the corresponding standard provisions or with the product (design) drawings and technical documents (such as technical conditions, technical requirements) that have been reviewed, approved, and implemented by the relevant departments. The main content of this chapter is to provide a basis for the design and selection of hydraulic cylinders for hydraulic press (machine).

4.1 Design and Selection Basis for Hydraulic Cylinders in Construction Machinery

Construction machinery products specified in JB603032001 "General Safety Technical Requirements for Construction Machinery" include bulldozers, loaders, excavators, backhoe loaders, scrapers, and graders, which are now all classified as earthmoving machinery. Other construction machinery products may also include cranes and hoisting machinery, road construction and maintenance machinery equipment, building construction machinery and equipment, etc.

Earthmoving machinery is wheeled, tracked, or walking self-propelled or towed machinery, equipped with working devices or auxiliary devices (work tools), or both, mainly used for excavation, loading, transportation, drilling, paving, compaction, or trenching operations of soil, rock, or other materials. Hydraulic working devices and auxiliary devices in earthmoving machinery generally contain hydraulic cylinders, and the technical conditions of the entire machine serve as the basis for the design and selection of these hydraulic cylinders.

According to the principle of "Reference documents without a specified date shall be the latest version applicable to this document," the documents cited in the following sections have been updated to current standards. For revoked standards, they have been noted, and some new standards adopted should include the 2018 edition of construction machinery series standards, etc.

Note: Earthmoving machinery includes the following machine families: bulldozers, loaders, excavators, trenchers, dump trucks, scrapers, graders, backfilling compactors, road rollers, pipe-laying machines, horizontal directional drills, etc.

4.1.1 Track-Type Bulldozer

The track-type bulldozer discussed in this section is a self-propelled tracked machine, whose working device can be equipped with a bulldozer attachment, performing earth shoveling, pushing, and leveling of materials through the forward movement of the machine, or equipped with auxiliary devices to generate thrust or traction. GB/T35213-2017 "Earthmoving Machinery - Track-Type Bulldozer - Technical Conditions" stipulates the terms and definitions, classification, requirements, test methods, inspection rules, as well as markings, packaging, transportation, and storage of track-type bulldozers, applicable to crawler-type bulldozers (hereinafter referred to as bulldozers) with engine net power of 60-400 kW that are mechanically driven, hydromechanical, or hydrostatic, derivatives of bulldozers (such as bulldozer rakes), variant products, as well as bulldozers with net power greater than 400 kW, which can also be referenced.

1. Classification

(1) Type and Model

1) Type. Bulldozers can be classified into three types based on the transmission method: mechanically driven bulldozers, hydromechanical bulldozers, and hydrostatic bulldozers.

2) Model. The model of a bulldozer should comply with the provisions of JB/T97252014 "Product Model Compilation Method for Earthmoving Machinery."

(2) Parameters

1) Main Parameter. The engine net power is used as the main parameter for bulldozers.

2) Basic Parameters. The basic parameters of bulldozers can be found in Table A.1 of Appendix A of GB/T35213-2017. The dimensions and symbols of basic parameters should comply with the provisions of GB/T18577.12008 "Definitions of Dimensions and Symbols for Earthmoving Machinery - Part 1: Host" and GB/T18577.22008 "Definitions of Dimensions and Symbols for Earthmoving Machinery - Part 2: Working Devices and Auxiliary Devices."

2. Requirements

(1) General Requirements

1) The engine net power of a bulldozer should comply with the provisions of GB/T169362015 "Engine Net Power Test Specification for Earthmoving Machinery."

2) The assembly quality of a bulldozer should comply with the provisions of JB/T59452018 "General Technical Conditions for Assembly of Construction Machinery."

3) The appearance quality of the paint coating on a bulldozer should comply with the provisions of JB/T59462018 "General Technical Conditions for Coating of Construction Machinery."

4) The structural design of a bulldozer should ensure safety and convenience during use, maintenance, and upkeep.

(2) Performance and Quality Requirements

1) A bulldozer should be able to start and operate normally under environmental temperatures of -15 to 40°C and altitudes not exceeding 2000 m, with smooth starting. If special requirements are needed, they can be specified in the contract between the supplier and the demander.

2) The specific power of a bulldozer should not be less than 5.6 kW/t.

Note: The term "specific power" is defined in GB/T35213-2017 as "the ratio of the engine net power of a bulldozer to the working mass of the entire machine."

3) The side slip of a bulldozer should not exceed 0.5%.

4) The maximum traction force of a bulldozer should not be less than 78% of its own working mass (the ground adhesion coefficient should be greater than 0.81).

5) The maximum traction efficiency of a mechanically driven bulldozer should not be lower than 75%, and the maximum traction efficiency of hydromechanical and hydrostatic bulldozers should not be lower than 70%.
525:
The traction efficiency shall not be less than 65%.
6) After the bulldozer completes a 1000 h reliability test, the reliability evaluation index shall meet the following requirements:
① The mean time between failures (MTBF) shall not be less than 300 h.
② The availability shall not be less than 90%.
7) The solid particle contamination level of the hydraulic system of the bulldozer's working device shall meet the following requirements:
① The contamination level of the plunger pump system shall not be higher than -/18/15.
② The contamination level of the gear pump system shall not be higher than -/20/17.
8) The bulldozer shall be able to climb up a longitudinal slope of 30° smoothly.
9) The sealing performance test of the bulldozer shall be conducted immediately after the bulldozer stops working for 3 h, and no oil or water leakage shall occur at the sealing joints within 15 min.
10) When the bulldozer is on a 30° longitudinal slope, it shall be able to stop reliably when braking uphill; when braking after the vehicle starts sliding down the slope from zero speed and travels 1 m by itself, it shall be able to stop reliably within the ground contact length of the track (except for hydrostatic bulldozers with neutral gear braking).
11) When the bulldozer turns at low speed, the driven wheel on the braking side shall not rotate (except for bulldozers with in-situ turning function).
12) The thermal balance performance achieved during bulldozer operation shall meet the following requirements:
① The outlet temperature of the torque converter shall not be greater than 120°C.
② The oil temperature of the final drive shall not be greater than 100°C.
③ The oil temperature of the working device (hydraulic system) shall not be greater than 90°C.
13) The effective capacity of the fuel tank shall ensure that the entire machine can work continuously for more than 10 h.
14) The lifting speed of the bulldozer's blade shall not be less than 0.3 m/s, and the natural sinking amount of the bulldozer's blade within 15 min shall not be greater than 120 mm.
15) The electrical system of the bulldozer shall comply with the provisions of GB/T3521312017.
16) The hydraulic system shall be safe and reliable, operate smoothly, and shall not have phenomena such as impact, stagnation, crawling, or vibration. The arrangement of various pipelines shall be neat.
(3) Safety and environmental protection requirements
The safety and environmental protection requirements for bulldozers are specified in GB/T3521312017.
3. Test methods, inspection rules, signs, packaging, transportation, and storage
The test methods, inspection rules, signs, packaging, transportation, and storage of bulldozers are specified in GB/T3521312017.
4.1.2 Hydraulic excavator
This section involves hydraulic excavators, unless explicitly marked as mechanical excavators, excavators usually refer to hydraulic excavators. Excavators are self-propelled tracked, wheeled, or walking mechanical equipment with a rotatable upper structure that can carry the working device, mainly using a bucket for excavation operations, and the chassis does not move during its working cycle. The working cycle of an excavator usually includes excavation, lifting, rotation, and unloading of materials, and excavators can also be used for handling (transporting) items or materials. The terms and definitions, classification, requirements, test methods, inspection rules, signs, packaging, transportation, and storage of hydraulic excavators are specified in GB/T91392017 "Earth-moving Machinery - Hydraulic Excavator - Technical Conditions", applicable to wheeled and tracked hydraulic excavators (hereinafter referred to as excavators) with a working mass not exceeding 200000 kg as specified in GB/T84982017 "Earth-moving Machinery - Basic Types - Identification, Terms, and Definitions".

② Wheeled excavators.
③ Walking excavators.
(2) Models

(3) Main parameters

(1) General requirements
1) The excavator driver's manual should be prepared according to GB/T25622-2010 "Earth-moving Machinery Driver's Manual Content and Format".
2) The excavator should be able to operate normally in an environment with an ambient temperature of -15 to 40°C and an altitude not exceeding 2000 m.
