4.3.2 CNC Shearing Machine
The CNC shearing machine is a shearing machine with the tool holder and/or the material blocking device controlled by the CNC system. GB/T28762012 "CNC Shearing Machine" stipulates the terms and definitions, technical requirements, accuracy, test methods, inspection rules, marks, nameplates, packaging, transportation and storage of the CNC shearing machine, which is applicable to the CNC shearing machine. The shearing machine with the CNC feeding device can also be used for reference.
1. Technical Requirements
(1) General Requirements
1) The drawings and technical documents of the CNC shearing machine shall comply with the provisions of GB/T28762012 standard and technical documents, and shall be approved through the prescribed procedures before production.
2) When the CNC shearing machine leaves the factory, it shall ensure its integrity and be equipped with the necessary accessories and tools for normal use and maintenance; the special accessories shall be determined by the user and the manufacturer together and supplied with the machine or ordered separately. The purchased parts (including electrical, hydraulic, pneumatic components, etc.) shall comply with the provisions of the technical documents and must be tested together with the main machine.
3) The actions of the working mechanism and the operation and adjustment mechanism of the CNC shearing machine shall be accurate and coordinated; when an operation cycle is completed, the tool holder shall be reliably stopped at the upper dead point.
637:
(4) The operation of the handle, foot pedal device, etc. should be safe, flexible, and reliable.

(5) When designing the CNC shearing machine, it should meet the requirements of two-shift operation and, under the condition of adhering to the usage rules, the service life before the first planned major overhaul should not be less than 5 years.

(6) The instruction manual should comply with the provisions of GB/T9969, and the content of the instruction manual should include requirements and explanations for installation, transportation, storage, use and maintenance, and safety.

(2) Parameters

The parameters of the CNC shearing machine should comply with the provisions of JB/T1826 or the product technical documentation.

(3) Rigidity

The rigidity of the CNC shearing machine should comply with the provisions of the technical documentation.

(4) Safety and Protection

The safety and protection of the CNC shearing machine should comply with the requirements of GB1720 and JB8781 (already repealed).

(5) Castings, Forgings, and Welded Parts

1) Gray cast iron parts should comply with the provisions of JB/T5775; nodular cast iron parts should comply with the provisions of GB/T13348; welded parts should comply with the provisions of JB/T8609; forgings and non-ferrous metal castings should comply with the provisions of JB/T1829 and the technical documentation. For defects that do not affect usage and appearance, repair is allowed according to the provisions of the technical documentation under the condition of ensuring quality.

2) Important castings, forgings, and welded parts such as the machine frame, tool holder, worktable, cylinder body, piston, adjustment screw, piston rod, and blades should undergo stress relief treatment.

(6) Machining of Parts

1) The machining of components should comply with the requirements of the design and process technical documentation. The machined surfaces should not have burrs, spots, or other mechanical damage. Except for special requirements, sharp edges should be chamfered.

2) Important sliding pairs such as the main guide rails, tool holder, cylinder body, and piston rod of the CNC shearing machine should take wear-resistant measures.

3) Other technical requirements for part machining can be found in GB/T28762-2012.

(7) Assembly

1) The CNC shearing machine should be assembled according to the assembly process specifications. The components assembled onto the CNC shearing machine should all meet quality requirements. It is not allowed to assemble gaskets, sleeves, and other parts that are not specified in the drawings.

2) Other technical requirements for assembly can be found in GB/T28762-2012.

(8) Electrical Equipment and CNC System

1) The electrical equipment of the CNC shearing machine should comply with the provisions of GB5226.1.

2) The CNC system should comply with the provisions of JB/T8832 (already repealed). The mean time between failures of the CNC system should not be less than 5000 hours, and it should have the following basic functions:

① Single-direction positioning function.

② Function to limit the range within which the CNC axis can move.

③ Function to accept compensation data and correct errors.

④ Function to automatically retreat control.

⑤ Safe area settings should be reserved for the minimum and maximum stroke positions of the back gauge. The back gauge should run at low speed within the safe area.

⑥ Function to record the number of processed parts, and the counting direction should be selectable.

⑦ After counting is completed, the processing can be done using one of the following methods:

a. Stop the machine when the count reaches the set value (increment counter).

b. Stop the machine when the count reaches 0 (decrement counter).

⑧ Function to automatically find the reference point, and the speed of finding the reference point should be low.

⑨ Provide teaching function to replace the operation of finding the reference point.

⑩ At least manual and automatic operation modes should be available.

〓〓〓After a power outage, the CNC system should be able to save processing-related data.

〓〓〓Provide a method to monitor the status of digital I/O ports.

〓〓〓At least provide a diagnostic method for the following system components:

a. Input ports.

b. Output ports.

c. Keys.

d. Display components (LED, LCD).

e. Data storage.

(9) Hydraulic and Pneumatic Systems

1) The hydraulic system of the CNC shearing machine should comply with the provisions of GB/T3766, hydraulic components should comply with the provisions of GB/T7935, and the pneumatic system should comply with the provisions of GB/T7932.

2) The working parts should not have crawling, stagnation, or vibration within the specified range, and there should be no obvious impact phenomenon during commutation and depressurization.

3) For hydraulic systems with proportional or servo valves, a high-pressure oil filter should be installed at the outlet of the hydraulic pump.

4) There should be no oil or air leakage in the hydraulic and pneumatic systems.

5) The cleanliness of the hydraulic system of the CNC shearing machine should comply with the provisions of JB/T9954.

6) The oil temperature at the inlet of the hydraulic pump should not exceed 60°C.

(10) Lubrication System

1) The CNC shearing machine should have a reliable lubrication device. The lubrication points of the lubrication pipeline should have corresponding numbered signs to ensure that each moving part receives normal lubrication. The lubrication system should comply with the provisions of GB/T6576.

2) The lubrication of important friction parts should generally adopt a centralized lubrication system. Only when a centralized lubrication system cannot be used can a dispersed lubrication device be adopted. Dispersed lubrication should have a separate lubrication label, and the label should indicate the lubrication parts.

3) There should be no oil leakage in the lubrication system.

4) Oil should not be thrown out from rotating parts. For non-circulating thin oil lubrication parts, an oil collection and recovery device should be provided.

4.3.3 Plate Bending Machine
A plate bending machine is a machine that bends sheet metal through relative motion of dies; a hydraulic plate bending machine is a plate bending machine driven by hydraulic power. JB/T 2257.2-1999 "Plate Bending Machines - Types and Basic Parameters" specifies the types and basic parameters of plate bending machines; JB/T 2257.1-2014 "Plate Bending Machines - Part 1: Technical Conditions" specifies the technical requirements, test methods, inspection rules, packaging, transportation and storage of plate bending machines; GB/T 1434-2011 "Plate Bending Machines - Accuracy" specifies the accuracy inspection, allowable accuracy values and inspection methods for plate bending machines, applicable to plate bending machines or general-purpose plate bending machines.

1. Types
Plate bending machines are divided into three transmission types:
1) Type I: Mechanical upper transmission (suitable for nominal force ≤ 1600 kN), see Figure 1 in JB/T 2257.2-1999.
2) Type II: Hydraulic upper transmission (suitable for nominal force ≤ 10000 kN), see Figure 2 in JB/T 2257.2-1999.
3) Type III: Hydraulic lower transmission (suitable for nominal force ≤ 4000 kN), see Figure 3 in JB/T 2257.2-1999.

1) The main parameters of plate bending machines are nominal force and maximum bending width, see Table 4-141.
2) The basic parameters of plate bending machines should comply with the provisions in Table 4-141.

2) The sheet metal bending machine should conform to the provisions of GB28243.
3) For the adjusting mechanism with electric motor adjusting the closed height of the ram, the upper and lower limit switches should be sensitive and reliable in action.
4) In the pneumatic or hydraulic system, when the air pressure or hydraulic pressure suddenly loses pressure or the air supply or liquid supply is interrupted, protective measures and necessary displays should be provided.
5) Other technical requirements for safety are shown in JB/T22571-2014.
(5) Noise

2) The nameplate should be properly and firmly fixed in an obvious and suitable position.

Cast carbon steel parts should conform to the provisions of GB/T11352. Welded parts should conform to the provisions of JB/T8609. Forgings and non-ferrous metal castings should conform to the relevant standards. If there are no relevant standards, they should conform to the requirements of the drawing and technical documents. For defects that do not affect the use and appearance, repair is allowed according to the provisions of the technical documents, provided that the quality is guaranteed.
2) The machine frame (left column, right column), ram (upper moving type), upper crossbeam (lower moving type), worktable, connecting rod, large gear, flywheel, eccentric wheel, cylinder body, piston, main (crankshaft), adjusting screw, piston rod, die, etc. are important castings, forgings and welded parts, which should be subjected to 926 Section 4 Hydraulic Cylinder Design and Selection for Hydraulic Machines (Machinery)

Processing of Internal Stresses.
(8) Machining
1) The machining of parts shall comply with the requirements specified in the design, process documents and relevant standards. The machined surfaces shall be free from burrs, nicks and other mechanical damage. Except for special requirements, sharp edges shall be chamfered.
2) The machine frame, slide block, main (crank) shaft, piston rod, cylinder body, roll pin, slide pin, sector fork (knife) and other major friction pairs shall be provided with wear-resistant measures.
3) Other technical requirements for machining are specified in JB/T 22571-2014.
(9) Electrical Equipment
The electrical equipment of plate bending machines shall comply with the provisions of GB 5226.1.
(10) Hydraulic, Lubricating and Pneumatic Systems
1) The hydraulic system of plate bending machines shall comply with the provisions of GB/T3766. The hydraulic components shall comply with the provisions of GB/T7935.
2) The pneumatic system shall comply with the provisions of GB/T7932.
3) There shall be no crawling, stagnation and vibration of the working parts within the specified range, and no obvious impact shall occur during direction change and pressure relief.
4) The pressure retention performance of the hydraulic system shall comply with the provisions of the technical documents.
5) The cleanliness of the hydraulic system shall comply with the provisions of JB/T9954.
6) Plate bending machines shall be provided with reliable lubrication devices. The lubrication pipelines and lubrication points shall have corresponding signs to ensure that the rotating parts are properly lubricated.
7) No oil shall be splashed from rotating parts. A collection and recovery device shall be provided for non-circulating thin oil lubricated parts.
8) No oil or gas leakage shall occur in the hydraulic system, pneumatic system and lubrication system.
(11) Assembly
1) Plate bending machines shall be assembled according to the assembly process specifications. The parts assembled on the plate bending machines shall comply with the quality requirements, and no gasket, bushing or other parts not specified in the drawings shall be assembled.
2) Within the same motion pair, the hardness of the removable guide rail shall be lower than that of the non-removable guide rail; the hardness of the small part guide rail shall be lower than that of the large part guide rail.
3) Other technical requirements for assembly are specified in JB/T 22571-2014.
(12) Appearance
1) There shall be no bulges, dents or uneven roughness on the external surfaces of plate bending machines that are not specified in the drawings. The edges of the joint surfaces of parts shall be neat and uniform, and the tolerance of their deviation shall comply with the provisions of relevant standards.
2) The heads of countersunk head screws shall not protrude from the external surfaces of parts. 4.3.4 CNC Press Brake

According to the terms and definitions in GB/T34376-2017, a CNC hydraulic press brake is a hydraulic press brake with CNC control of the slide block and/or back gauge; an electro-hydraulic servo CNC hydraulic press brake is a CNC hydraulic press brake that uses electro-hydraulic proportional or servo valves to drive hydraulic cylinder movement, and controls the synchronous movement of the press brake hydraulic cylinders through displacement sensor detection and feedback; a torsion shaft synchronous CNC hydraulic press brake is a CNC hydraulic press brake that maintains synchronous movement of the press brake hydraulic cylinders through mechanical (or hydraulic) means. GB/T34376-2017 specifies the terms and definitions, requirements, accuracy, test methods, inspection rules, marking, packaging, transportation and storage for CNC press brakes; GB/T33644-2017 specifies the inspection requirements, allowable values and test methods for the accuracy of CNC press brakes (hereinafter referred to as CNC press brakes).

1. Requirements

(1) Drawings and Technical Documents
The drawings and technical documents of CNC press brakes shall comply with the regulations, and shall be approved through the prescribed procedures before production can commence.

(2) Type and Parameters
The basic type and parameters of CNC press brakes shall comply with the provisions of JB/T22572.

(3) Spare Parts and Compatibility
1) When leaving the factory, CNC press brakes shall be guaranteed to be complete, and shall be equipped with special accessories and spare wearing parts required for normal use and maintenance. Special accessories shall be mutually agreed upon by the user and the manufacturer, and supplied with the machine or ordered separately.
2) The manufacturer shall ensure that the purchased components (including electrical, hydraulic, pneumatic components, etc.) of the CNC press brake comply with the current standards and have obtained their qualification certificates, and shall be subjected to operational tests simultaneously with the host machine.

(4) Safety and Protection
The safety and protection of CNC press brakes shall comply with the requirements of GB28243.

(5) Rigidity
The rigidity of CNC press brakes shall comply with the provisions of the technical documents.

(6) Slide Block Stop Position
The actions of the working mechanism and operating mechanism of the CNC press brake shall be coordinated, and when an operating cycle is completed, the slide block shall reliably stop at the upper dead point.

(7) Nameplate
CNC press brakes shall have nameplates and various labels and signs indicating lubrication, operation and safety requirements. The requirements for nameplates shall comply with the provisions of GB/T13306. The graphical symbols on the nameplates shall comply with the provisions of JB/T3240, and the nameplates shall be properly and firmly fixed in an obvious and suitable position.

(8) Castings, Forgings, Welded Parts
1) Gray iron castings shall comply with the provisions of JB/T5775, ductile iron castings shall comply with the provisions of GB/T1348, welded parts, forgings and non-ferrous metal castings shall comply with the provisions of the technical documents. If there are no standards, they shall comply with the technical requirements of the drawings and process documents. Defects that do not affect use and appearance may be repaired according to the provisions of the technical documents, provided that quality is guaranteed.
2) The frame, slide block, connecting beam, worktable, cylinder block, piston, piston rod, adjustment screw, and mold, which are important castings, forgings and welded parts, shall be subjected to stress relief treatment.

(9) Part Processing
1) The processing of parts and components shall comply with the requirements of the design, process and relevant standards. The processed surfaces shall not have burrs, scratches and other mechanical damage. Unless otherwise specified, all sharp edges shall be chamfered.
2) The main guide rails, guide shafts, slide blocks, cylinder blocks, piston rods and other main friction pairs of the CNC press brake shall be provided with wear-resistant measures.
3) Other requirements for part processing are specified in GB/T34376-2017.

(10) Electrical Equipment and CNC System
1) The electrical equipment of the CNC press brake shall comply with the provisions of GB52261.
2) The CNC system shall comply with the provisions of JB/T8832 (which has been repealed) and JB/T11216. The mean time between failures of the CNC system shall be no less than 5000 h, and shall have the following basic functions:
① The CNC system shall have unidirectional positioning function.
② The CNC system shall limit the range within which the CNC axes can operate.
③ The CNC system shall have the function of accepting compensation data and correcting errors.
④ The CNC system shall have automatic retreat control function.
⑤ The CNC system shall reserve a safety zone for the minimum and maximum stroke positions of the back gauge. The back gauge shall operate at low speed within the safety zone.
⑥ The CNC system shall have the function of automatic searching for the reference point, and the searching speed shall be low.
⑦ The CNC system shall provide teaching function instead of searching for the reference point operation.
⑧ The CNC system shall have counting control function.
⑨ The CNC system shall have at least manual and automatic operation modes.
⑩ After power failure, the CNC system shall be able to save processing-related data.
〓〓〓The CNC system shall provide a method for monitoring the status of digital I/O ports.
〓〓〓The CNC system shall provide at least a method for diagnosing the following system components:
a. Input ports.
b. Output ports.
c. Keys.
d. Display components (LED, LCD).
e. Data storage.

4.4 Design and Selection of Hydraulic Cylinders for Heavy Machinery

Basis

4.4.1 Hydraulic System for Heavy Machinery

GB/T37400.16-2019 "General Technical Conditions for Heavy Machinery - Part 16: Hydraulic System" specifies the system design, hydraulic oil, system equipment assembly, quality of castings, forgings, welded parts and pipe fittings, welding, electrical wiring, control, flushing, testing, painting, packaging, transportation and storage requirements for hydraulic systems of heavy machinery (hereinafter referred to as "mechanical equipment"); applicable to hydraulic systems of mechanical equipment with nominal pressure not greater than 40 MPa and hydraulic medium being mineral oil-based hydraulic oil.

Note: 1. Heavy machinery mainly includes metallurgical, rolling and heavy forging machinery and equipment.

2. Heavy products specified in GB/T37400.1-2019 "General Technical Conditions for Heavy Machinery - Part 1: Product Inspection" mainly include: metallurgy, rolling, heavy forging, continuous casting, mining machinery and equipment and supporting machinery.

1. System design

(1) Basic requirements

The content of basic requirements should include:

1) Personnel safety.

2) Equipment safety.

3) Reliable and safe operation.

4) Normal operation.

5) Energy saving and high efficiency.

6) Reliable and complete principle.

7) Convenient maintenance.

8) Low noise.

9) No external leakage.

10) Long system life.

11) Economical cost.

(2) Design conditions

The technical agreement and design task book should include the following contents:

1) Main purpose of the mechanical equipment.

2) Process flow, action and cycle of the mechanical equipment.

3) Climate conditions of the system use area, environmental temperature, humidity, salinity and their variation range around the system.

4) Installation position of hydraulic actuators, hydraulic pump stations, hydraulic valve groups and other hydraulic devices (such as indoor or outdoor installation; fixed mechanical equipment or mobile mechanical equipment installation; installation in basement, ground or elevated location, etc.). The layout drawing of the mechanical equipment should be provided if necessary.

5) Various parameters of the medium used in the cooling system.

6) System design, manufacturing and use requirements for special conditions such as high dust, high temperature, strong radiation, corrosion, flammability, external disturbance (such as impact, vibration, etc.), high altitude (above 1000 m), severe cold areas, and high precision and high reliability.

7) Capability and motion parameters of hydraulic actuators; installation method and relevant special requirements (such as pressure holding, pressure relief, synchronization accuracy and dynamic characteristics, etc.).

8) Degree of automation and interlocking requirements for system operation.

9) Type of working oil used by the system.

10) Clarify user power grid parameters.

(3) Safety requirements

1) The selection, application, configuration and adjustment of system components should consider all possible accidents, with the principle of personnel safety and minimum equipment damage in case of accidents.

2) The system should have overpressure protection.

3) The design and adjustment of the system should consider impact forces. Impact forces should not affect the normal operation of the equipment or cause danger.

4) The design of the system should consider pressure loss and loss of control (such as unexpected power outages, etc.), to prevent the hydraulic actuators from producing uncontrolled movement and causing danger.

5) The use of components should comply with their respective usage characteristics, technical parameters, and performance.

6) The installation position of components should be safe and convenient for adjustment and operation.

7) The operation and adjustment of components must comply with the manufacturer's regulations.

5) To prevent contamination of the system, an air filter should be installed on the open oil tank; a filter should be installed in the system circuit as needed; a filter should be installed at the pressure port of the servo valve and proportional valve.

6) The new hydraulic oil injected into the system should be filtered, and the filtering accuracy should not be lower than the design requirements.

7) The cleanliness level should comply with the provisions of G B/T 1 4 0 3 9.

(9) Basic maintenance requirements

1) Components should be located in easily disassembled areas, with sufficient space to facilitate maintenance.

2) When components in the system are disassembled, the oil tank should not be drained, and

3) Under conditions where the use and installation allow, the system should be equipped with an oil drain pan.
4) Under conditions where maintenance is possible, the number of detachable points in the system piping should be reduced. The piping layout should be convenient for assembly and disassembly, and should not hinder the movement of production personnel or the maintenance and inspection of electromechanical equipment.
5) Large hydraulic devices should be equipped with steps or ladders.
6) Pressure measurement points, air release points, hydraulic oil sampling points, oil filling ports, and oil discharge ports should be set in the system.
7) If the hydraulic device has electrical wiring, a junction box should be provided.
(10) Lifting Measures
Lifting devices should be provided for components and parts weighing over 15 kg.
(11) Installation, Use, and Maintenance Documentation
1) The design unit should provide the user with the civil engineering task list for the system.
2) The design unit should provide the user with the following drawing documents:
   a) System schematic diagram, including a detailed list of component models, names, specifications, quantities, and manufacturers.
   b) Operation time program table for electrical and mechanical control components of the system.
   c) System equipment installation drawing or other drawings as specified in the agreement, along with a drawing index.
   d) Spare parts list.
3) The design unit should provide the user with the system's operating instructions, which should mainly include:
   a) The main purpose of the mechanical equipment.
   b) The main function, composition, and main technical parameters of the system.
   c) The working principle and operating instructions of the system.
   d) Conditions and requirements for the system's normal operation (such as normal operating oil temperature range, oil cleanliness requirements, oil tank filling height, oil type code and working viscosity range, filling requirements, etc.).
   e) Operating requirements and precautions for the system.
   f) The settings of test points, oil filling ports, oil discharge ports, sampling ports, oil filters, etc. for regular testing and maintenance.
   g) Common faults and troubleshooting methods of the system, as well as maintenance methods for special components and parts.
   h) Randomly attached tools.
   i) Detailed list of consumable seals (excluding purchased parts).
(12) Marking
1) Schematic Diagram Marking
   a) The graphical symbols for components should comply with GB/T7 8 6 . 1 or the specifications of the professional component manufacturer.
   b) The units of measurement should comply with GB/T 3 1 0 2 (all parts).
   c) Hydraulic actuators should be represented by schematic diagrams and labeled with names. The corresponding hydraulic cylinders or hydraulic motors should be labeled with specification parameters and port sizes.
   d) Main pipelines (such as pressure pipelines, return oil pipelines, drain pipelines, etc.) and pipelines connecting hydraulic actuators should be labeled with outer diameter and wall thickness.
   e) Pressure control components should be labeled with the set pressure value.
   f) Pressure-charged components or parts should be labeled with the medium type and charging pressure.
   g) Temperature control components should be labeled with the set temperature value.
   h) Motors and electrical contacts, solenoid coils should be labeled with codes.
   i) Each component should be numbered with a part number, and components of the same model should also be labeled with their sequence numbers.
   j) Independent hydraulic circuits within the hydraulic device should be divided into areas and labeled with codes using double dashed lines.
   k) The interface between assembled parts within the system should be labeled with codes.
2) Equipment Marking
   a) When marking components or other parts on the system equipment, the marking should be consistent with the drawing marking.
   b) The main pipelines of pressure oil pipelines, return oil pipelines, and drain pipelines should be marked with the letters "P", "T", and "L" respectively. The pipelines connecting hydraulic actuators should be marked with pipeline codes.
   c) The interfaces of components in the system should be marked with codes (oil filling port codes) according to the manufacturer's specifications.
   d) Identification plates, pressure gauges, and other devices for each function of the hydraulic operation device or the status information of the system's execution function should be marked with functional markings.
   e) The coloring should comply with the design requirements. The outer surface of the main pipelines on non-hydraulic devices should be painted and colored to correspond and match the color rings.
   f) The wiring in the junction box on the hydraulic device should be marked with wire numbers.
   g) The hydraulic device should be marked with a product nameplate, and purchased components should be accompanied by a nameplate.
   h) The hydraulic pump should be marked with a rotation direction mark for the pump shaft.
3) Marking Requirements. The marks on the hydraulic device must be clear, visible, durable, and neat. The printing, spraying, pasting, and binding positions of the marks should ensure that they do not disappear due to the replacement of components.
(13) Operating Force
When designing, the operating force on manual and foot-operated control mechanisms should not exceed the following values:
1) Fingers: 10 N.
2) Wrist: 40 N.
3) Single arm: 150 N.
4) Both arms: 250 N.
5) Foot pedal: 200 N.
(14) Tightening Torque
The tightening torque for joints, plugs, and fasteners of components should comply with GB/T 3 7 4 0 0 . 1 0—2 0 1 9 "Heavy Machinery General Technical Conditions Part 1 0 - Hydraulic Cylinders for Hydraulic Presses (Machines) Selection and Design".

2. Hydraulic Oil
1) When designing the system, the type and characteristics of the hydraulic oil to be used in the system should be specified.
2) When designing the system, the compatibility of the selected hydraulic oil with the following substances should be considered:
  ① Metal materials, sealing materials, and other non-metallic materials in contact with the hydraulic oil in the system.
  ② Protective coating materials and other liquids that may come into contact with the system.
  ③ Materials that come into contact with spilled or leaked hydraulic oil.
3) When using hydraulic fluid as the transmission medium, the general components used in the system should be derated.
4) The use of hydraulic oil in the system should comply with the provisions of GB/T7631.2 or adopt the recommendations of the hydraulic oil manufacturer, considering its temperature, pressure range, and special characteristics.
5) The following points should be noted when using hydraulic oil:
  ① Within the temperature range of the working fluid specified by the system, the viscosity range of the selected oil should meet the usage conditions of the components.
  ② Different types of hydraulic oil should not be mixed. Generally, hydraulic oils of the same grade produced by different manufacturers should not be mixed either; if mixing is necessary, a small sample mixing test should be conducted to check for physical changes and chemical reactions, and confirmation should be obtained from the oil manufacturer.
  ③ During use, the physical and chemical indicators and particulate contamination of the hydraulic oil should be regularly inspected to determine whether the oil can be reused; generally, inspection should be done once every three months, with a maximum interval of six months.
  ④ The viscosity, acid value, cleanliness, and other qualities of the oil in the system should be regularly checked for hydraulic oil maintenance; if the hydraulic oil does not meet quality requirements, it should be completely replaced.
  ⑤ The hydraulic oil manufacturer should provide relevant information such as labor hygiene requirements during use, emergency treatment measures for toxic gases and suffocation hazards in case of fire, and waste liquid disposal methods.
3. System Equipment Assembly
(1) Manufacturing Basis
The manufacturing of the system should comply with the agreement between the supplier and the demander, and meet the requirements of the design drawings, technical documents, and corresponding standards and process specifications that have been reviewed, approved, and implemented by relevant units.
(2) Component Requirements
1) All components, auxiliary components, sealing components, and fasteners in the system should comply with the manufacturer's recommendations or the provisions of product drawings and technical documents approved for production by relevant departments.
2) The quality of purchased parts should comply with the provisions of product drawings and technical documents, and they should have corresponding quality grade certificates.
3) Important purchased parts should be accepted according to performance requirements.
4) Purchased parts that have been affected in quality due to rust, deformation, or other problems caused during storage, transportation, or system assembly should not be put into use.
5) Purchased parts with seal failure and contamination should have their seals replaced and be cleaned before use.
(3) Power Components
1) The type and installation requirements of the coupling between the hydraulic pump and the prime mover should comply with the manufacturer's provisions.
2) Protective covers should be installed on exposed rotating shafts and couplings.
3) The mounting base of the hydraulic pump and the prime mover should have sufficient rigidity to ensure coaxiality during operation.
4) The inlet pipeline of the hydraulic pump should be short and straight to avoid bends and sudden changes in cross-section. Within the specified viscosity range of the oil, the inlet pressure and other conditions of the pump should meet the manufacturer's specified values.
5) The sealing of the inlet pipeline of the hydraulic pump should be reliable and should not allow air to be sucked in.
6) High-pressure, high-flow hydraulic pump units should adopt:
  ① Rubber elastic compensation joints at the pump inlet.
  ② High-pressure hoses at the pump outlet.
  ③ Elastic damping pads on the pump unit base.
(4) Control Components
1) Valves.
  ① Valve Selection. The type of valve selected should consider correct functionality, sealing, maintenance and adjustment requirements, as well as the ability to withstand foreseeable mechanical or environmental influences. In systems used in fixed heavy machinery, cartridge valves or stacked valves should be preferred. When isolation valves are required, valves approved by the manufacturer for such safety applications should be used.
  ② Installation of Hydraulic Valves. The installation of hydraulic valves should comply with the following provisions:
   a. The installation method of the valve should comply with the manufacturer's provisions.
   b. Cartridge valves or stacked valves should have correct orientation measures.
   c. To ensure safety, the installation of the valve should consider the influence of gravity, impact, and vibration on the main parts inside the valve.
   d. The performance grade of the connecting screws for the valve should meet the manufacturer's requirements and should not be arbitrarily replaced.
   e. Attention should be paid to the orientation of the inlet and return ports to avoid installation in the wrong direction, which could cause accidents.
   f. To avoid air infiltration into the valve, the connection should ensure good sealing. For valves installed with flanges, the screws should not be tightened too much, as excessive tightening may cause poor sealing.
   g. The installation of directional control valves should generally have the axis installed in a horizontal position.
   h. Generally, pressure control valves should increase pressure when rotated clockwise and decrease pressure when rotated counterclockwise; generally, flow control valves should decrease flow when rotated clockwise and increase flow when rotated counterclockwise.

2) Manifold Block (Valve Block).
① The manifold block should be made of 35 steel or 45 steel and undergo quenching and tempering treatment. Non-destructive testing should be performed if necessary.
② The surface quality of the mounting surfaces for components on the manifold block should comply with the manufacturer's specifications.
③ The dimensional tolerances between the mounting holes for components on the manifold block should ensure interchangeability of the valves.
④ The internal oil passages in the manifold block should ensure that the pressure drop caused by fluid flow through the passages does not adversely affect system efficiency and response throughout the entire operating temperature range and system flow capacity.

(5) Actuator Components
1) Hydraulic Cylinder.
① When designing or selecting a hydraulic cylinder, consideration should be given to stroke, load, and assembly conditions to prevent abnormal bending of the piston rod when extended.
② The installation of hydraulic cylinders should comply with design drawings and manufacturer specifications.
③ If the structure permits, the inlet and outlet ports of the hydraulic cylinder should be positioned at the top during installation to allow for automatic air bleeding or to be equipped with convenient manual air bleeding valves.
④ The installation of hydraulic cylinders should be firm and reliable; in cases of large strokes and high working temperatures, one end of the cylinder should be kept floating to avoid the effects of thermal expansion.
⑤ Pipe connections should not be loose.
⑥ The parallelism and perpendicularity of the mounting surface of the hydraulic cylinder and the sliding surface of the piston rod should comply with design drawings and manufacturer specifications.
⑦ The installation of seals should comply with the manufacturer's specifications.
2) Hydraulic Motor.
① The type of coupling between the hydraulic motor and the driven device and the installation requirements should comply with the manufacturer's specifications.
② Exposed rotating shafts and couplings should be equipped with protective covers.
③ When using hydraulic motors, consideration should be given to the effects of starting torque, stall torque, load variations, load kinetic energy, and low-speed performance.
3) Mounting Base. The mounting base for hydraulic actuators should have sufficient rigidity to ensure normal operation of the actuator.

(6) Other Auxiliary Devices and Components
1) Oil Tank Device.
① Oil Tank.
a. The design of the oil tank should comply with the following basic requirements:
a) Under normal operating conditions, especially when no cooler is installed in the system, it should be able to adequately dissipate heat from the hydraulic oil.
b) It should have a relatively slow circulation speed to allow for the separation of air mixed into the oil and the settling of heavier impurities in the oil.
c) The return oil port and the pump's suction port should be far apart, and baffles or other measures can be used for isolation, but they should not interfere with cleaning the oil tank.
d) Under normal operating conditions, it should be able to accommodate all the hydraulic oil flowing from the system.
b. General oil tanks should be made of carbon steel plates, while important oil tanks and special oil tanks should be made of stainless steel plates.
c. The structure of the oil tank should comply with the following basic requirements:
a) The oil tank should have sufficient strength and rigidity to prevent significant deformation after installing various components and filling with oil.
b) The bottom of the oil tank should be at least 150 mm above the ground to facilitate handling, draining, and heat dissipation.
c) It should have sufficient support area to allow for adjustment using shims and wedges during assembly and installation.
d) The inner surface of the oil tank should be kept flat with minimal structural parts to facilitate cleaning of internal dirt.
e) To facilitate cleaning the oil tank, one or more handholes or manholes should be provided.
f) The shape of the bottom of the oil tank should allow for complete drainage of the hydraulic oil, and a drain port should be installed at the bottom.
g) The tank cover, handholes, manholes on the side walls, and the mounting holes or base plates for other components should be welded with raised flanges (such as non-through flanges, through flanges, etc.).
h) The structure of removable covers should prevent the entry of contaminants into the oil tank.
i) Pipes passing through the oil tank walls should be effectively sealed.
② Requirements for Oil Tank Accessories. The installation of oil tank accessories should comply with the following requirements:
a) Important oil tanks should be equipped with oil diffusers or defoaming devices.
b) The top of open oil tanks should be equipped with air filters and oil fillers. The filtration accuracy of the air filter should comply with the system cleanliness requirements. The maximum pressure drop of the air filter should not affect the normal operation of the hydraulic system.
c) The oil tank should be equipped with a level gauge, which should be installed near the hydraulic pump's suction port to display the oil level in the tank. Important oil tanks should be equipped with level switches to monitor and signal the high and low limits of the oil level.
d) The oil tank should be equipped with an oil temperature gauge and oil temperature detection element to visually monitor the oil temperature and signal the set oil temperature value.
e) Pressure-type isolated oil tanks should be equipped with low-pressure alarms, and pressure-type pressurized oil tanks should be equipped with pneumatic safety valves, pressure gauges, and pressure alarms.
2) Platform Railings. The design and manufacture of platform railings should comply with the provisions of GB 4053.1-2009 "Safety Requirements for Fixed Steel Ladders and Platforms Part 1: Straight Ladders," GB 4053.2-2009 "Safety Requirements for Fixed Steel Ladders and Platforms Part 2: Inclined Ladders," and GB 4053.3-2009 "Safety Requirements for Fixed Steel Ladders and Platforms Part 3: Industrial Protective Railings and Steel Platforms."

3) Heat exchanger (cooler). The system should be equipped with a heater or cooler according to the usage requirements, and should meet the following basic requirements:

① The surface dissipation power of the heater should not exceed 0.7 W/cm².

② The position of the heater installed on the oil tank should be lower than the lowest liquid level position of the oil tank.

③ When using a heat exchanger, there should be temperature measurement points for hydraulic oil and cooling (or heating) medium.

④ When using a heat exchanger, an automatic temperature control device can be used to keep the temperature of the hydraulic oil within the normal working range.

⑤ The user should use the cooling medium specified by the manufacturer.

Example: If special cooling medium or water is used and the water source is very dirty, the water quality is corrosive, or the water volume is insufficient, it should be proposed to the manufacturer.

⑥ When using an air cooler, prevent the air inlet and outlet channels from being blocked or obstructed, and consider the surrounding air temperature factors.

4) Filter.

① A filter should be installed in the system to eliminate pollutants in the hydraulic oil, and the filtering accuracy of the filter should meet the usage requirements of components and the system.

② A pollution indicator or test device should be installed for timely cleaning of the filter or replacement of its filter element according to the indicator or test results.

③ If the user specifically requests the ability to replace the filter element without stopping the system, the user's requirements should be met.

④ If a magnetic filter is used, care should be taken to prevent the adsorbed impurities from falling into the oil during maintenance and use.

⑤ When using a filter, its nominal flow rate should not be less than the actual flow rate of the filtered oil and should leave a certain margin.

⑥ For large hydraulic pump stations that work continuously, it is recommended to use a separate cooling circulation filtration system.

5) Accumulator.

① A safety shut-off valve block should be installed in the accumulator circuit for charging, maintenance, or long-term shutdown use.

② To prevent the pressure oil in the accumulator from flowing back when the pump stops working, causing the pump to reverse, a check valve should be installed between the accumulator of the hydraulic oil source and the hydraulic pump.

③ When the mechanical equipment is parked, if the system still needs to use the pressurized liquid in the accumulator to work, a safety use instruction should be prominently displayed near the accumulator, which should include the words "Caution, pressure vessel."

④ The discharge rate of the accumulator should be consistent with the system usage requirements and should not exceed the manufacturer's regulations.

⑤ The type of charging gas and installation of the accumulator (including gas-loaded accumulator) should comply with the manufacturer's regulations.

⑥ The accumulator should be installed away from heat sources.

⑦ The accumulator should not be disassembled before depressurization, and welding, riveting, or machining on the accumulator is not allowed.

6) Pressure detection and display elements.

① The range of the pressure sensor should generally be 1.2 to 1.5 times the rated pressure.

② The range of the pressure gauge should generally be 1.5 to 2 times the rated pressure.

③ When using a pressure gauge, a pressure switch and pressure damper should be installed for maintenance, accurate detection, and extended lifespan.

7) Seals.

① The material of the seal should be compatible with the medium it contacts.

② The use pressure, temperature, and installation of the seal should comply with the manufacturer's recommendations.

③ The seals provided with the product should be used within the manufacturer's specified storage conditions and storage validity period.

(7) Piping

1) Pipe fittings material.

① The system piping can be made of steel pipe, copper pipe, rubber hose, or nylon pipe.

② When steel pipe is used for piping, seamless steel pipes such as 10 steel, 15 steel, 20 steel, and Q345 should be used. For special and important systems, stainless steel seamless steel pipes should be used.

2) Pipe fittings precision requirements. The precision level of the pipe should be compatible with the pipe fittings used. The minimum precision of the pipe fittings should comply with the provisions of GB/T 8163-2018 "Seamless Steel Pipes for Fluid Transportation."

3) Piping installation requirements. Piping installation should meet the following requirements:

① Piping laying and installation should be carried out according to relevant process specifications.

② Piping laying and installation should prevent components and hydraulic devices from being contaminated.

③ Piping should be laid in a free state, and after welding, the fixed and connected piping should not be subjected to excessive radial force for forced fixing and connection.

④ The arrangement and orientation of the piping should be neat and consistent, with clear hierarchy, and horizontal or vertical piping should be preferred.

⑤ The distance between the contour edges of adjacent pipe fittings should not be less than 10 mm.

⑥ Piping should avoid unnecessary use of short pipe fittings for splicing.

4) Trench laying. The laying of piping in pipe trenches and the requirements for trenches should comply with the design drawings and GB/T 37400.11.

5) Pipe bending.

① Field-made pipes should be cold-bent using a pipe bender.

② The bending radius of the pipe should comply with the provisions of GB/T 37400.11.

③ The bent part of the pipe should be smooth, without obvious dents, ripples, or flattening (the ratio of short to long axis should not be less than 0.75).

6) Rubber hose.

① The selection of the diameter of the rubber hose should be based on the manufacturer's recommendation.

② The laying of the rubber hose should comply with the drawings or the manufacturer's recommendation, with the following requirements:

a) Avoid severe bending deformation of the rubber hose during the operation of mechanical equipment.

4. Quality of Castings, Forgings, Welded Parts, and Pipe Fittings

(1) Basic Requirements

1) The grade of metal material should meet the design requirements.

2) The chemical composition and mechanical properties of the metal material should comply with GB/T3740003, GB/T3740004, GB/T3740005, GB/T3740006, and GB/T3740008, or adopt the manufacturer's recommendations.

3) The quality of castings, forgings, welded parts, and pipe fittings should comply with GB/T3740003, GB/T3740004, GB/T3740005, GB/T3740006, GB/T3740008, and GB/T3740011, or adopt the manufacturer's recommendations.

(2) Machining Quality

1) Sharp edges and corners that do not require reservation should be chamfered and blunted.

2) The machined surface should not have rust, burrs, knocks, scratches, and other defects.

3) Metal burrs on the ports of hydraulic manifolds, joints, and metal pipes, as well as metal burrs at the intersection of internal channels in hydraulic manifolds, should be removed.

4) For machined parts with no tolerance requirements specified in the drawing, the dimensional tolerances, geometric tolerances, and thread accuracy should comply with the standard level specified by the manufacturer.

(3) Requirements for Welding Blanks and Pipe Fittings

1) The degree of rust on the metal surface of welding blanks should not be lower than Grade B; the degree of rust on the metal surface of hydraulic pipe fittings should not be lower than Grade A specified in Appendix B of GB/T3740012-2019.

2) Welding blanks and pipe fittings must be derusted, and the quality of derusting should comply with the provisions of GB/T3740012. Anti-rust treatment should be carried out according to the corresponding standards and specifications after derusting.

3) The forming geometric tolerances of welding blanks should comply with the provisions of GB/T3740003.

4) The surface roughness Ra value of the cut surface of welding blanks is 25μm.

5) The cut end face of pipe fittings should not have a raised shape, and the end face should be flush, with a perpendicularity tolerance of 1% of the pipe outer diameter relative to the pipe axis.

6) The welding bevels of welding blanks and pipe fittings should be machined and comply with the provisions of GB/T3740003 and GB/T3740011.

7) The forms of welding joints of welded parts should comply with the provisions of GB/T3740003.

(4) Defect Treatment for Castings and Forgings

Under the condition of ensuring the quality of use, defects in castings and forgings that do not affect use and appearance may be repaired by welding according to the provisions of GB/T3740007.

5. Welding Requirements

(1) Basic Requirements

1) The interface of pipe line welding should be flush on the inner wall: for pipes with a working pressure below 6.3 MPa, the misalignment on the inner wall should not exceed 2 mm; for pipes with a working pressure equal to or higher than 6.3 MPa, the misalignment on the inner wall should not exceed 1 mm.

2) The welding of welded parts and pipe lines should respectively comply with the provisions of GB/T3740003, GB/T2740011, and relevant process specifications.

3) The quality of pipe line welds should meet the requirements of BS and BK grades in GB/T3740003-2019.

4) Pipe line pressure tests should comply with the provisions of GB/T3740011.

(2) Welded Parts

1) Oil tank welding.

① The inner wall of an open rectangular oil tank should adopt continuous welds with full penetration; the weld seam on the inner wall of an open cylindrical oil tank should protrude from the inner wall, and the height should comply with the provisions of GB/T3740003. The welding of pressure oil tanks should comply with the provisions of GB150.4-2011 "Pressure Vessels - Part 4: Manufacturing, Inspection, and Acceptance."

② When re-welding a painted oil tank, care should be taken to avoid damaging the paint on the oil tank.

1. Coating peeling off from the inner wall.
2) Other welded parts. Other welded parts should comply with the provisions of GB/T 37400.3.
(3) Pipe welding
1) Steel pipe pipelines should be welded using argon arc welding or argon arc welding bottom sealing with arc welding filling.
2) When pipes are butt-welded, the weld seam on the inner wall should be higher than the inner wall, and its height should comply with the provisions of GB/T 37400.1.1.
3) Repair of pipe weld seams should be formulated with process measures, and the number of repair times for the same part should not exceed 2 times.
4) During pipe welding, sealing rings in the welding heat zone should be removed to prevent overheating and aging.
6. Electrical wiring
1) The electrical wiring on equipment should meet the following basic requirements:
① The type of wiring should comply with the electrical design requirements.
② Junction boxes, wire troughs, and conduits should comply with the manufacturer's recommendations.
2) The laying of circuits should comply with the manufacturer's recommendations or according to the provisions of design drawings and technical documents.
7. Control
(1) Circuit protection devices
1) If the working pressure or flow in the circuit exceeds the specified value and may cause danger or accidents, protective devices should be provided.
2) Control elements for adjusting pressure and flow should be manufactured and assembled to prevent the adjusted value from exceeding the working range marked on the nameplate. The adjusted value of the adjustment device should be maintained until readjustment.
3) When the system is in the parking position, if the hydraulic oil returning to the tank from valves, pipelines, and actuators may cause damage to mechanical equipment or danger, measures should be taken to prevent the hydraulic oil from returning to the tank.
4) The system circuit should be designed to prevent uncontrolled movement and abnormal action sequence (especially when making vertical and inclined movements) under conditions such as starting, stopping, idling, adjusting, and hydraulic faults of hydraulic actuators. Actuators that need to maintain their own position should be equipped with valves that have fail-safe protection.
5) In pressure control and flow control circuits, the selection and setting of components should consider the effects of working pressure, temperature, and load changes on the response, repeatability, and stability of components and circuits.
6) For systems composed of central hydraulic pump stations and multiple independent valve stations, each valve station should be equipped with automatic or manual valves to cut off the main oil flow, to ensure that when a fault occurs in the control area of a certain valve station, the oil supply to that valve station can be cut off in time without affecting the operation of the control areas of other valve stations.
7) When there are more than one interconnected manual or automatic control actions on the entire mechanical equipment, if any action failure may cause personal injury and equipment damage or should be operated according to certain procedures, otherwise the mechanical equipment will interfere, interlocking protection (including operation interlocking protection) should be provided.
(2) Manual control devices
1) For safety reasons, the equipment should have emergency braking or emergency return control.
2) Emergency braking and emergency return control should meet the following requirements:
① It should be easily identifiable.
② It should be installed at each operator's work position and be easy to operate under all working conditions. Additional control devices may be added if necessary.
③ It should act immediately.
④ It should not interfere functionally with the adjustment or throttling devices of other control devices.
⑤ It should not require any actuator to input energy.
⑥ It should only be possible to complete all emergency operations using one manual control device.
⑦ On the actuator pipelines from servo valves, sufficient emergency braking valves may be installed.
3) After emergency braking, the restart of the cycle should not cause equipment damage or danger. If the actuator needs to return to the starting position, a safe manual control device should be provided.
4) The movement setting of manual control levers should not cause operational confusion.
5) For sequential control circuits or automatic control circuits with multiple actuators, separate manual adjustment devices should be provided to adjust the stroke of each actuator.
(3) Control of valves
1) When designing or installing mechanically operated valves, it should be ensured that overload or overtravel will not cause accidents.
2) Foot-operated valves should be equipped with protective covers or other protective measures to prevent accidental contact.
3) The working position of the operating lever of manually operated valves should be clearly marked with signs or symbolic representations.
4) Unless otherwise specified, solenoid valves should be equipped with manual operation buttons, and avoid configuring buttons that may cause misoperation of the facility.
5) The parameters of the electrical control power supply, pneumatic air source, and hydraulic liquid source for valves should comply with the action requirements of the valves.
(4) Installation requirements for control devices
1) The arrangement position of all control devices should prevent the following unfavorable factors:
① Malfunctioning and premonitory accidents.
② High temperature.
③ Corrosive gases.
④ Oil pollution of electrical control devices.
⑤ Vibration and high dust.
⑥ Fire and explosion.
2) Various control devices should be located in places that are convenient for adjustment and maintenance.
3) Manual control devices should meet the following basic requirements:

① Located near the operator's normal working position and within reach.
② The operator should not be required to extend or reach over rotating or moving mechanical equipment or components to operate the control devices.
③ Should not interfere with the operator's normal working activities.
④ Position sequence control should be adopted. When using pressure sequence control or time control alone may cause damage to the equipment due to sequence failure, position sequence control should be adopted.
⑤ Circuit interrelationships. The operating conditions of one part of the system should not adversely affect other parts.
⑥ Servo control loop. The servo valve should be installed close to the related actuator. The installation, arrangement and direction of the valve should comply with the requirements of the valve manufacturer. An independent pump source or a filter should be installed before the servo valve, with a filtration accuracy meeting the manufacturer's requirements.
⑦ Hydraulic power unit control requirements. The automatic control of important hydraulic power units should have the following basic functions:
① Low-level and minimum-level oil tank liquid level automatic alarms, and automatic shutdown of the hydraulic pump drive device.
② Filter contamination alarm.
③ Highest oil temperature alarm.
④ Heat exchanger automatically operates according to the oil temperature signal.
⑤ Main pressure oil pressure loss alarm.
⑥ Hydraulic pump operation signal indication.
8. Flushing
(1) Pipeline flushing
After the pipeline installation is completed, the pipeline should be flushed and should be executed according to the provisions of GB/T2513-2010 "Hydraulic System Assembly Pipeline Flushing Method".
(2) System flushing
System flushing should meet the following requirements:
① The filtration accuracy should be higher than the system design requirements.
② The flushing fluid should be compatible with the system working oil and the materials of hydraulic devices in contact.
③ A low-viscosity flushing fluid should be used to achieve turbulent flow.
④ The temperature of the flushing fluid: The temperature of the hydraulic oil should not exceed GB/T2513-2010 or the manufacturer's recommendation.
⑤ The servo valve and proportional valve should be removed and replaced with a flushing plate.
After flushing is completed, its cleanliness should meet the provisions of Appendix A in GB/T27400.16-2019 or meet the design requirements.
9. Testing
1) The system should be subjected to performance testing according to the test outline and the manufacturer's test specifications.
2) The test should be recorded, and the recorded parameter values should be consistent with the measured parameter values.
10. Painting
Painting should meet the following basic requirements:
1) The paint should be suitable for the working oil and environment.
2) The quality of painting materials should comply with GB/T37400.12 or adopt the manufacturer's recommendation.
3) The painting method and steps should comply with the provisions of the painting process specification or adopt the manufacturer's recommendation.
4) The coating thickness and adhesion of the painting should comply with the provisions of GB/T37400.12.
11. Packaging, Transportation and Storage
1) The packaging, anti-rust measures, date, and packaging, storage and transportation signs of hydraulic equipment should comply with the agreement between both parties, GB/T19191-2008 "Packaging Storage and Transportation Signs", GB/T4879-2016 "Anti-rust Packaging", GB/T13384-2008 "General Technical Conditions for Packaging of Electromechanical Products", GB/T37400.13 and the design requirements.
2) The basic requirements for packaging, transportation and storage:
① When the hydraulic equipment is transported in sections, the disassembled pipelines and their end holes or joints should be marked with identification signs.
② The working oil in the hydraulic equipment and the water in the cooler should be drained.
③ The hydraulic equipment should be protected against rust as required (including the internal cavities of the equipment).
④ Important instruments and scattered parts should be individually packaged and then placed in the packaging box.
⑤ The exposed openings of the hydraulic equipment should be sealed with sealing caps or sealed with plastic film.
⑥ The exposed threads and glass instruments of the hydraulic equipment should be protected.
⑦ The scattered parts, components, etc. of the hydraulic equipment should have labels, which should be clear, correct, durable and long-lasting, and should correspond to the drawings.
⑧ Before packaging and transportation, the gas-filled accumulator should discharge high pressure and maintain a residual pressure of 0.15-0.3 MPa.
3) The packaging of hydraulic equipment should consider the impact of vibration and impact during transportation and loading/unloading on the equipment, and the equipment should not move during handling.
4) The packaging of hydraulic equipment should be intact to prevent damage, deformation and paint scratches.
5) The rust inhibitor should meet the following requirements:
① The quality of the rust inhibitor should comply with GB/T4879 or adopt the manufacturer's recommendation.
② The type and chemical properties of the rust inhibitor used for rust prevention in the internal cavities of the hydraulic equipment should be compatible with the hydraulic oil to be used and the materials in contact.

3) Hydraulic cylinders should comply with the provisions of JB/T 6134.

5) Adjust the buffer valve at the end of the rodless chamber of the rotary hydraulic cylinder so that the hydraulic cylinder has a clear buffer when retracting to the end of the stroke, allowing for smooth stopping without impact.
(4) Hydraulic, Lubrication, and Electrical Equipment
1) The hydraulic mud gun hydraulic system should comply with the provisions of JB/T 6996.
2) The basic parameters of the hydraulic mud gun lubrication system and components should be implemented according to JB/T 7943.1.
3) The hydraulic mud gun electrical system should comply with the provisions of GB5226.1 and GB50058.
4) The random hydraulic press lubrication pipeline should ensure unobstructed cleaning. The hydraulic pipeline should be cleaned and rust-proofed separately according to JB/T50000.11 before being used to ensure cleanliness meets the drawing requirements. If the drawing does not specify requirements, it should reach NAS 8 level.
5) The pipes used in the hydraulic pipeline need to be pickled, flushed, and blown.
6) The high-pressure hoses in the hydraulic pipeline need to be armored or protected with heat-resistant sleeves.
7) Rotary joints with high precision and high reliability are recommended for articulated parts in the hydraulic pipeline.
8) Except for self-lubricating bearings, each bearing must have a lubrication device. A single-machine centralized lubrication scheme is adopted, with individual points using single-point lubrication. Centralized lubrication operation can be performed manually, electrically, or automatically. Single-point lubrication should be marked with a lubrication point sign. The lubrication of the slewing support should be centralized lubrication.
9) When the hydraulic control circuit of the rotary hydraulic cylinder is not manually operated, it is recommended to use a differential circuit to reduce the demand for the main pump displacement. Under the condition of meeting the normal working flow rate requirements, the system should be equipped with a backup pump of the same specification.
10) The hydraulic system should have the function of maintaining and replenishing pressure for the rotary hydraulic cylinder. At the same time, the pressure-maintaining circuit should be used for the mud striking hydraulic cylinder circuit to prevent the mud striking piston from retreating in a clogged state.
11) The rotary hydraulic cylinder should be equipped with a pressure balance control circuit, which can adopt a balance valve or a pilot-operated check valve circuit to prevent the mud gun from diving during downhill travel when allowed on a sloping base, and also to prevent violent shaking when the mud gun suddenly stops during rotation.
12) The running time of the hydraulic mud gun is 12-15s for forward movement and 30-40s for backward movement.
13) Before the test run, the hydraulic press lubrication pipeline should be tested at 1.25 times the rated working pressure (when the system working pressure is 16-31.5MPa) or 1.15 times (when the system working pressure is greater than 31.5MPa). There should be no leakage anywhere.
(5) Important Components
1) The fire-facing surface of the mud striking hydraulic cylinder and mud cylinder should be protected by heat-insulating filler guard plates or water-cooled guard plates.
2) The piston rod adopts a deep hole structure, using centralized piping to reduce strength weakening. The exposed piston rod needs to be protected by a protective cover.
3) When the material of the mud cylinder is ZG35CrMo, its inner wall should be finely processed and then subjected to ion nitriding, with a nitriding layer depth of 0.40-0.45mm, surface hardness not lower than 560HV, and non-uniformity less than 30HV.
4) When the mud cylinder is formed by welding 35 steel, CO2 gas shielded welding should be used, and the weld seam should undergo ultrasonic testing to meet the Class II requirements of NB/T47013.3-2015. Its inner wall should be hard chrome plated, with a plating thickness of 0.10-0.15mm and surface hardness not lower than 900HV.
5) The inner wall of the hydraulic cylinder and the outer surface of the piston rod should be hard chrome plated, with a plating thickness of 0.03-0.05mm.
(6) Assembly
1) The assembly of the hydraulic mud gun should be carried out in accordance with the provisions of JB/T50000.10.
2) The slewing bearing should be installed strictly according to the requirements of the use, with the soft strip direction, applying anti-loosening glue on the plane and bolt tightening glue, and tightening the bolts in sequence and according to the torque requirements.
3) During the assembly of the hydraulic cylinder, the iron filings in the deep hole of the piston rod should be cleaned, the sharp edges of the seal ring groove should be rounded, and special tools should be used to install special seal rings.
4) Check and adjust the coaxiality error of the assembly of the mud striking hydraulic cylinder and the mud cylinder, which should not be greater than 0.25mm.
5) The assembly of hydraulic cylinders with a nominal pressure PN≤25MPa should comply with the requirements of JB/T6134. The allowable deviation of the overall dimensions of the assembled hydraulic cylinder is: basic length ±1.5mm, stroke ±1.5mm, extended length ±1.5mm.
6) Strength test should be conducted after the hydraulic cylinder or rotary joint is installed.
(7) Painting
1) The surface treatment before painting should be carried out in accordance with the provisions of 4.1 in JB/T50000.12-2007.
2) The equipment painting needs to be temperature-resistant 200-400℃. The painted surface must undergo rust removal treatment to meet the corresponding requirements, with two coats of anti-rust paint on the inner surface and two coats of heat-resistant paint on the outer surface. If no requirements are specified by the client, the total film thickness should be 40-70μm. The exposed surface should undergo anti-rust treatment.
3) The grid test result grade of the paint film should meet the Class II quality requirements specified in Table C.1 of JB/T50000.12-2007.
(8) Installation
1) Installation shall be carried out in accordance with GB50231-2009 "General Code for Construction and Acceptance of Mechanical Equipment Installation Engineering", GB50372-2006 "Installation Acceptance Code for Ironmaking Machinery Equipment Engineering", and GB/T50387-2006 (2017) "Installation Engineering for Hydraulic, Lubrication and Pneumatic Equipment in Metallurgical Machinery".

The relevant provisions of the acceptance specifications shall be followed.
2) Welding and grounding are strictly prohibited through hydraulic cylinders and bearings during installation.
3) The allowable deviation of the foundation installation dimensions of the mud cannon should meet: the coordinate deviation in the direction parallel to the iron hook is ±10mm, the coordinate deviation in the direction perpendicular to the iron hook is ±5mm, and the elevation deviation is ±5mm.
4) The rotation radius of the rotation mechanism should be the theoretical dimension ±10mm, and the rotation angle should be the theoretical value ±1°.
5) The position of the nozzle center and the angle of the mud spraying mechanism should have allowable deviations: horizontal ±10mm, height ±5mm, mud spraying angle ±0.5°, and the angle between the projection of the centerline of the mud spraying mechanism and the centerline of the iron hook ±0.5°.
6) When the position of the nozzle deviates from the theoretical taphole position, there should be no interference between the mechanisms. The deviation value shall be subject to the provisions of Table 5 in YB/T01713-2017, and the deviations in various directions shall not reach the maximum value at the same time.
(9) Repair of products
1) The hydraulic mud cannon is an important large-scale equipment. After normal wear and tear or local damage, it has replaceable and repairable properties. The repair should be carried out in accordance with the principle of "repairing the old as new", but unnecessary excessive repair and repair with excessive cost should not be pursued.
2) When repairing, the newly manufactured parts shall be executed according to the standard. Connecting and fastening parts, bearings, copper sleeves, seals, and hydraulic and lubrication pipelines shall be updated in principle. Parts that can be directly used shall be cleaned and necessary painting and protection shall be applied.
3) During the repair, the dimensions and structures that are not critical or have little impact on the use performance can be modified, but it should be ensured that the safety is not reduced and the production requirements are met.
4) After the repaired product is assembled, it shall be tested according to the trial operation procedure of the new product.
3. Test method
(1) Nitriding treatment
The method for determining the depth of the nitrided layer shall be carried out in accordance with the relevant provisions of GB/T11354-2005 "Determination of the depth of the nitrided layer of steel parts and metallographic examination". The detection of the hardness of the nitrided layer shall be carried out in accordance with GB/T4340.1-2009 "Metallic Materials - Vickers Hardness Test - Part 1: Test Method".
(2) Coating inspection
1) The thickness of the coating can be obtained by reading the difference in size before and after plating, or measured by the method of GB/T4955-2005 "Metallic Coatings - Measurement of Coating Thickness - Coulometric Method of Anodic Dissolution" or GB/T4956-2003 "Non-magnetic Coatings on Magnetic Substrates - Measurement of Coating Thickness - Magnetic Method".
2) The coating hardness test shall be carried out in accordance with GB/T4340.1.
(3) Non-destructive testing
1) Ultrasonic testing shall be carried out in accordance with NB/T47013.3.
2) Magnetic particle testing shall be carried out in accordance with NB/T47013.4.
3) Non-destructive testing of cast steel parts shall be carried out in accordance with JB/T50000.14.
4) Non-destructive testing of forged steel parts shall be carried out in accordance with JB/T50000.15.
(4) Strength test
1) Hydraulic press lubrication pipeline: The test of the hydraulic press lubrication pipeline shall be carried out in accordance with Chapter 7 of GB50387-2006 (2017).
2) Hydraulic cylinder and rotary joint: The strength test shall be carried out after the hydraulic cylinder or rotary joint is installed. The test pressure shall be 1.25 times of its working pressure, and the pressure shall be maintained for 20 minutes. If the pressure drop is not greater than 2.5% of the working pressure, it is qualified.
3) Water cooling system: When the mud cylinder and the driving cavity adopt water cooling protection, the pressure test of the water cooling protection plate shall be carried out. The test pressure shall be 1.5 times of the working pressure, and the pressure shall be maintained for 10 minutes without leakage.
(5) Trial operation of the whole machine
1) The hydraulic mud cannon shall be trial-operated with the supporting hydraulic equipment, electrical equipment, and the same-side taphole machine at the supplier's factory to check the matching between these devices. If it is not possible to conduct a joint trial operation due to the supplier's working conditions, the trial operation shall be conducted after being transported to the site.
2) Move the mud cannon to the working position, adjust the control connecting rod and buffer, and make the nozzle in the theoretical mud spraying position. Measure the center position of the nozzle and the angle of the mud spraying mechanism.
3) Adjust the position of the nozzle to the extreme deviation from the theoretical taphole position for trial operation. There should be no interference between the mechanisms.
4) After the hydraulic mud cannon is assembled, perform a no-load trial operation. The mechanisms should act back and forth 10 times, and the actions should be accurate, flexible, and without jamming. The running speed should meet the requirements.
(6) Painting
1) The quality and paint film thickness inspection of the painting shall be carried out in accordance with the provisions of Chapter 5 of JB/T50000.12-2007.
2) The evaluation of the resistance of the coating to separation from the substrate (adhesion of the paint film) shall be carried out in accordance with the provisions of Chapter 6 of JB/T50000.12.

4.4.3 Six-roll Cold Rolling Mill
The six-roll mill is a mill with six horizontal rolls arranged vertically in the same window, with two supporting rolls arranged on the left and right of the upper and lower work rolls, mainly used for rolling non-ferrous metal plates and cold-rolled steel strips. J B/T 11593—2013 "Six-roll Cold Rolling Mill" stipulates the structural types, basic parameters, technical conditions, test methods, inspection and packaging of six-roll cold rolling mills, applicable to six-roll cold rolling mills with automatic thickness control, intermediate roll lateral movement, and hydraulic roll bending (hereinafter referred to as six-roll mills).
1. Structural Type and Basic Parameters
(1) Structural Type
The six-roll mill is a fully hydraulic mill, with a closed frame structure frame. The intermediate roll can be driven laterally by a hydraulic cylinder, and the work roll has positive and negative bending roll devices, while the intermediate roll has a positive bending roll device. The rolling line elevation adjustment adopts a worm gear pair electric pressure reduction or a hydraulic cylinder (or hydraulic motor) driven wedge adjustment mechanism; It is a six-roll mill with hydraulic pressure reduction, automatic thickness AGC system, tension closed-loop and speed closed-loop control (see Figure 1 in J B/T 11593—2013).
