4.5 Design and Selection Basis for Hydraulic Cylinders for Metal Cutting Machine Tools

4.5.1 Hydraulic System for Metal Cutting Machine Tools

GB/T23572-2009 "General Technical Conditions for Hydraulic Systems of Metal Cutting Machine Tools" stipulates the technical requirements, assembly requirements, safety requirements, test methods, inspection rules and other requirements for hydraulic systems of metal machine tools. It is applicable to hydraulic transmission and control systems of metal cutting machine tools that use hydraulic oil as the working medium.

1. Technical Requirements

(1) Basic Requirements

The design, manufacture and use of the hydraulic system should comply with the provisions of GB/T3766, and should ensure long service life of the equipment and convenient maintenance.

(2) Hydraulic Components and Parts

Hydraulic components used in the hydraulic system should comply with the provisions of GB/T7935, and other parts should comply with the requirements of the corresponding standards.

(3) Hydraulic Oil

1) The hydraulic oil used in the hydraulic system should comply with the provisions of GB/T3766 and GB7632-1987 "Selection and Use of Lubricants for Machine Tools". The hydraulic system should be equipped with a liquid filter device in a position convenient for replacement and maintenance. The oil should be fully filtered before being injected into the hydraulic system oil tank.

2) The oil used in the hydraulic system and the oil used in the guide rail or other mechanical parts should be separated from each other.

(4) Pipelines, Joints and Channels

1) The material of the pipe joints in the hydraulic system is generally metal. The material of the pipeline is generally metal, oil-resistant rubber braided hose, resin high-pressure hose and other materials compatible with the working medium. The pipe wall should be able to work normally when subjected to 1.5 times the maximum working pressure of the system.

2) There should be no leakage at all joints and exposed joints of the hydraulic system. Sealing packing or sealing glue can be used at joints and other joints, but miscellaneous materials such as hemp and silk should not be used instead.

3) The bent part of the oil pipe should be smooth, and there should be no obvious dents or bias (flattening). The ratio of the short and long axes should not be less than 0.75.

4) Before assembly, the joints, pipelines, channels (including cast core holes, machined holes, etc.) and oil tanks of the hydraulic system should be cleaned.

5) The oil channels of the hydraulic system should have sufficient flow area.

6) The pipeline should be set safely and reasonably, and the arrangement should be neat, which is convenient for adjusting, repairing and replacing components. In order to avoid vibration and collision of the pipeline, there should be a certain gap between the pipelines. When the pipelines are long or the pipelines vibrate and collide, resulting in noise, pipe clamps should be used for fixing. The distance between the pipe clamps can refer to the value in Table 4-166.

Table 4-166 Distance Between Pipe Clamps

7) The pipe clamp should not be welded to the pipe, nor should it damage the pipeline.

8) Generally, the pipeline should not be used to support components or support the oil circuit board.

9) The hose is generally used between movable parts and is convenient for replacing parts, suppressing the transmission of mechanical vibration or noise. Its length should be as short as possible to avoid severe bending and deformation of the hose during equipment operation. If necessary, a hose protection device should be installed.

10) When the pipeline needs to be suspended and crossed, its height should be convenient for maintenance and ensure the safety of personnel, and the support should be reliable.

11) The pipeline should be marked. Pressure pipelines, control pipelines, oil return and leakage pipelines should use different signs.

12) There should be signs at both ends of the pipeline connection to facilitate recovery after disassembly.

(5) Hydraulic System Oil Tank

1) The nominal volume of the oil tank of the hydraulic system should comply with JB/T7938-2010 "Hydraulic Pump Station Oil Tank Nominal Volume Series" (already abolished).

2) During the entire working cycle, the oil level in the oil tank should be kept at a safe working height. The oil tank should have sufficient space to allow thermal expansion of the oil and separation of air. Under normal circumstances, the oil tank should be able to accommodate all the oil returned from the system. Spills or leaks of contaminated oil should be prevented from flowing directly back into the oil tank.

3) Where conditions permit, the bottom of the hydraulic station can be raised 150 mm above the installation surface to facilitate handling, oil discharge and heat dissipation.

4) The detachable cover plate should be able to prevent impurities from entering the oil tank in its structure.

5) Use baffles or other measures to separate the return oil from the inlet of the hydraulic pump. The adopted measures should not hinder the cleaning of the oil tank.

6) The shape of the bottom of the oil tank should allow the hydraulic oil to be drained. The oil tank should be equipped with an oil drain hole, a sampling hole, an oil filling port and a cleaning port. The oil drain hole should be located at the lowest position of the bottom of the oil tank. The sampling hole can also be set on the working pipeline. The oil tank should be equipped with one or more cleaning ports to clean the entire interior of the oil tank.

7) Tubes passing through the tank top cover should be sealed, and the terminal of the return oil line should be below the lowest liquid level of the tank.

8) A level gauge should be installed next to the oil filling port, and an air filter should be provided on the upper part of the vented tank.

9) The tank material should be compatible with the oil. For tanks made of ordinary steel plates, the inner surface can be treated with methods such as phosphating after pickling, shot peening or sandblasting followed by spraying, which have excellent chemical and physical stability, or it can be coated with a rust-proof coating that does not peel off and is compatible with the oil.

(6) Pressure Gauge

1) Pressure gauges installed in hydraulic systems should be installed in conspicuous and easily observable positions.

2) The range of the pressure gauge should be 1.5 to 2 times the pressure being tested.

3) Pressure gauges should generally be equipped with a pressure relief device, or use shock-resistant pressure gauges with dampers added externally.

4) When measuring multiple pressures, a multi-point measurement device consisting of one pressure gauge and one selector valve can be used.

2. Assembly Requirements

1) The interfaces between the separated parts of the hydraulic system pipeline and the host should be numbered and marked, and the pipeline numbering, marking, and relevant technical documents should be consistent.

2) When installing the hydraulic pump, ensure that the pump shaft is concentric with the drive motor transmission shaft. For rigid coupling, the concentricity tolerance is ф0.05 mm; for flexible coupling, the concentricity tolerance is ф0.1 mm.

3) Other assembly and trial operation requirements should comply with the provisions of GB/T3766.

3. Safety Requirements

1) The safety requirements for the design, manufacture, and use of hydraulic systems should comply with the provisions of GB/T3766.

2) The action sequence between moving parts should be equipped with interlocking safety devices. When using a static pressure device, to ensure that the hydraulic system or other mechanical movements can only be driven after establishing static pressure, interlocking safety devices should generally also be provided.

3) When the hydraulic system of the machine tool loses normal pressure and may cause unsafe factors, necessary alarm devices, indication signals, and protective measures should be set in the system.

4) When the connection between the hydraulic pump and the drive motor is exposed, a safety guard should be installed.

5) When the machine tool is stopped, the hydraulic circuit equipped with an accumulator should be able to automatically release the pressure in the accumulator, or reliably isolate the circuit from the accumulator.

6) When the machine tool is stopped, if the hydraulic circuit still needs to use the pressurized oil in the accumulator to work, safety usage instructions should be marked on the accumulator or in a conspicuous place near the accumulator, including the words "Caution, Pressure Vessel".

7) All components or equipment with a mass exceeding 15 kg should be easily liftable or equipped with lifting devices.

4. Test Methods

(1) Preparations Before the Test

Before the test, the hydraulic system should be circulated and filtered. During circulating filtration, servo valves, proportional valves, accumulators, etc. in the hydraulic system should be short-circuited.

4.5.3 High-speed Machine Tool Rotating Hydraulic Cylinder
In the typical structure of hydraulic cylinders in reference [15], general hydraulic cylinder typical structures, special-purpose hydraulic cylinder typical structures, and piston-type rotating hydraulic cylinder typical structures (including gear-rack rotating hydraulic cylinders, parallel piston gear-rack hydraulic cylinders, roller rotating hydraulic cylinders, ball screw rotating hydraulic cylinders, and single screw rotating hydraulic cylinders) are listed respectively. It is pointed out that: "Piston-type rotating hydraulic cylinders are a combination of hydraulic cylinders and rotating mechanisms. The rotating mechanism is usually a gear-rack pair or a screw-nut pair. This is an element that lies between hydraulic cylinders and hydraulic motors and possesses the function of oscillating motors. Because its output is torque, the rotation angle is a limited ±θ° oscillating angle."

According to the definition of cylinders or hydraulic cylinders, some hydraulic cylinders listed in the typical structures of piston-type rotating hydraulic cylinders in reference [15] do not belong to hydraulic cylinders, but some belong to combined hydraulic cylinders, such as gear-rack rotating hydraulic cylinders and parallel piston gear-rack hydraulic cylinders.

The machine tool rotating hydraulic cylinders listed in this section differ in principle from the typical structures of piston-type rotating hydraulic cylinders listed in reference [15]. The rotational motion between the cylinder body and piston of these hydraulic cylinders is driven by an external force rather than produced by the hydraulic cylinder itself.

4.6.1 Hydraulic parts for coal mining machinery
In M T / T 4 5 9—2 0 0 7 General technical conditions for hydraulic parts for coal mining machinery, the technical requirements, safety requirements, test requirements, markings and packaging for hydraulic components of coal mining machinery are stipulated, applicable to all kinds of hydraulic components (hereinafter referred to as components) for coal mining machinery using hydraulic oil (liquid) as the working medium, and also applicable to hydraulic auxiliary parts for coal mining machinery.
1. Technical requirements
1) Basic parameters, graphic symbols and installation and connection dimensions of the components shall generally comply with the provisions of the relevant national standards. However, when the main machine of coal mining machinery has special requirements, the basic parameters and installation and connection dimensions may also be determined according to the requirements of the main machine.
2) All parts shall be manufactured according to the prescribed drawings and technical documents, and their materials shall comply with the provisions of the drawings. The performance of materials shall comply with the provisions of the relevant standards.
Materials may be replaced on condition that the product quality is not reduced.
3) The shell of the component shall be treated accordingly to eliminate internal stress. The shell shall be free of process defects affecting the use of the component and meet the strength requirements of the component. The surface of the shell shall be flat and smooth, and shall not have process defects affecting the appearance quality. The casting shall be cleared of sand, and there shall be no residue in the internal channels and cavities.
The inspection of flaws shall be carried out for complex castings.
4) The components shall be assembled according to the provisions of the relevant product standards or technical documents. All parts and purchased parts shall be products inspected and qualified by the quality inspection department.
5) Parts shall be cleaned before assembly, and shall not contain any contaminants (such as iron filings, burrs, fibrous impurities, coal chips, coal ash, etc.).
6) During the assembly of the component, cotton yarn, paper and other fibrous materials that are easy to fall off shall not be used to wipe the inner cavity of the shell, the mating surfaces of the parts and the inlet and outlet flow channels.
7) During the assembly of the component, seals with defects and beyond the effective service life shall not be used.
8) Symbols indicating the function of the oil port shall be clearly marked near all oil connection ports of the component. Except for special provisions, the symbols of oil ports are as follows:
① P— — —pressure oil port.
② T— — —return oil port.
③ A, B— — —working oil port.
④ L— — —drain oil port.
⑤ X, Y— — —control oil port.
9) The coating of the exposed non-machined surface of the component shall be uniform with consistent color. No putty shall be applied for pretreatment before spraying.
10) After the component passes the factory inspection, sealing, dustproof and leakage prevention measures shall be taken for all oil ports.
2. Safety requirements
1) All kinds of light metal, light alloy materials and non-metallic materials shall comply with the relevant provisions of G B3 8 3 6 . 1—2 0 0 0 (2 0 1 0) Explosive atmospheres—Part 1: Equipment—General requirements.
2) Explosion-proof components shall comply with the relevant requirements of G B3 8 3 6 . 2—2 0 0 0 (2 0 1 0) Explosive atmospheres—Part 2: Equipment protected by flameproof enclosures "d".
3) Intrinsically safe components shall comply with the relevant requirements in G B 3 8 3 6 . 4—2 0 0 0 (2 0 1 0) Explosive atmospheres—Part 4: Equipment with type of protection "i".
4) Components with explosion-proof requirements shall be provided with "product qualification certificate", "explosion-proof certificate" issued by the national designated explosion-proof inspection station and "mark certificate for coal mine products" issued by the authorized institution of the national safety production supervision department.
The G B3 8 3 6—2 0 0 0 series of standards have been abolished. The above-mentioned names of standards are the names of the current (2 0 1 0 edition) standards, and some standards have been updated to the 2 0 1 7 edition.

4.7 Marine Hydraulic Cylinders: Design and Selection Basis
4.7.1 Marine Hydraulic Systems
CB/T1102-2008 "General Technical Conditions for Marine Hydraulic Systems" stipulates the requirements for marine hydraulic systems, the application of components and accessories, piping and cleaning, etc., and is applicable to the design and manufacture of hydraulic transmission and control systems for ship machinery and equipment, including the hydraulic systems of the entire ship and supporting equipment.
1. Design
(1) Design Principles
1) The design of hydraulic systems should consider personnel safety and possible accidents, and take the following safety measures:
① Pressure, position, and speed limits.
② Overload protection.
③ Reduction of system impact pressure, which should not cause danger due to impact pressure.
④ Provision of system back pressure.
⑤ Guarantee of hydraulic pump suction conditions.
⑥ The filtration accuracy of the hydraulic oil should meet the requirements of various components in the system.
⑦ Provision of alarm signals, such as low oil level, high or low oil temperature, filter blockage, pressure loss, overload, etc.
⑧ Clear specification of the quality and performance of the recommended working oil.
⑨ Safety protection when the hydraulic energy source or pipeline of the system suddenly fails. Such as setting hydraulic lock valves, anti-burst valves, hydraulic brakes or locking mechanisms, etc.
⑩ Formulation of safe operating procedures and setting of operating procedure nameplates.
2) The working temperature of the system should match the allowable operating temperature of the components.
3) The system design should consider avoiding heat generation.
4) When the oil temperature in the system is too high, an oil cooler (air-cooled or water-cooled) set in the system should be used.
5) When the oil temperature in the system is too low, an oil heater (electric heating or steam heating) set in the system should be used.
6) When starting under low ambient temperature conditions, methods such as oil circulation, throttling, and overflow should be used for warm-up. The system can only be put into operation after warming up to a certain temperature.
7) The installation of components and pipelines should consider reducing the generation and transmission of noise.
8) Noise reduction measures should be taken, such as elastic through-cabin pipe fittings, accumulators, hoses, etc.
9) Collection facilities should be set up for parts prone to oil leakage, and oil pollution collection work should be done well to prevent oil pollution from harming the environment.
10) Equipment layout should consider the following disassembly and installation measures:
① When disassembling individual components or pipelines in the system, adjacent components or parts should not be disassembled in large quantities.
② When carrying out maintenance work, a large amount of working oil loss should not be caused.
③ Unless the system needs to replace the working oil, the maintenance oil tank generally does not need to drain oil.
11) Components that need debugging, replacement, and regular cleaning should be arranged in easily operable locations.
12) Vent or drain points should be set at appropriate parts of the system, paying attention to not causing air accumulation.
13) Components, parts, or equipment weighing more than 15 kg should be easy to lift or have lifting devices.
(2) Components and Accessories
1) Hydraulic Cylinders
① The load, stroke, and installation of hydraulic cylinders should not subject them to abnormal lateral forces.
② The exhaust port of the hydraulic cylinder should be arranged upward.
2) Working Hydraulic Oil
① The type and characteristics of the working hydraulic oil used should be suitable for all components and accessories in the system. The solid particle contamination level code of the working hydraulic oil should meet the requirements of GB/T14039.
② When extracting liquid samples from the working system pipeline for hydraulic particle contamination analysis, it should be carried out according to the provisions of GB/T17489.
③ When the working oil is filled into the system, it should be filtered, and the filtration accuracy should not be lower than the system requirements.
3) Seals and Sealing Elements
① The seals of components and accessories should adopt pressure sealing seals.
② Mechanical seals should meet the requirements of GB/T6556.
③ O-ring rubber seals should meet the requirements of GB/T3452.1.

4) Block. The block shall not deform under the specified working pressure and temperature.
(3) Piping
1) Flow velocity in pipelines. The general flow velocities are: 1 m/s for suction pipelines, 3 to 6 m/s for pressure pipelines, and 1.5 to 2.5 m/s for return oil pipelines.
2) Pipeline strength. The strength of the pipeline system should be able to withstand the highest peak pressure that may occur in the system.
3) Pipeline and its fittings.
① Galvanized pipes or joints should not be used, nor should brass pipes be used.
② The welds between pipes and joints, flanges, etc. should be subject to non-destructive testing.
4) Pipeline layout.
① The routing and layout of the pipeline should minimize the number of elbows and joints.
② Where small diameter pipes for remote control or braking are relatively weak, protective measures such as baffles or protective covers should be installed.
③ The pipeline layout should not interfere with the adjustment, repair, disassembly, and assembly of components or equipment.
④ Fittings should be easy to disassemble and assemble, without affecting other fittings or components, and without requiring special tools.
⑤ Where pipeline deformation may occur due to changes in oil temperature and air temperature, larger elbows or expansion joints should be installed.
⑥ The highest points in different areas of the pipeline system should be equipped with venting points. At the same time, venting points should be provided at the lowest positions.
⑦ Deck pipelines should be laid along the hatch coaming, and should be protected from sunlight exposure or equipped with sunshades.
⑧ Pipelines in cabins should be kept away from heat sources and have improved ventilation.
⑨ Leaking oil, return oil from pilot control, and return oil pipelines should be separately connected to the oil tank.
⑩ Fittings should not be used to support equipment or oil blocks.
⁂⁂⁂ Pipelines should not pass through freshwater tanks. If unavoidable, they should pass through oil-tight tunnels or sleeves. When passing through fuel oil tanks, the pipe wall should be thickened and should not have detachable joints.
⁂⁂⁂ When pipelines pass through watertight or airtight structures, they should be equipped with through fittings or base plates.
5) Pressure measurement interfaces.
① If there is no pressure measurement interface on the pressure control component, a pressure measurement interface should be installed on the corresponding pipeline.
② A pressure measurement interface for the supply oil pressure should be installed between the actuator and its corresponding control component.
③ When using a multi-point pressure gauge switch and a pressure gauge to form a pressure measurement device, each pressure measurement point should be marked.
2. Process
(1) Bending pipes
1) The bending radius of pipes should generally be greater than 3 times the outer diameter of the pipe. At the same time, bending should start at a distance greater than 0.5 times the outer diameter of the pipe from one end of the pipe.
2) No creases should appear when bending the pipe. The ratio of the minor axis to the major axis of the elliptical cross-section at the flattened area of the bent pipe should not be less than 0.75.
3) The sand-filled hot bending process should not be used.
4) Flanges or pipe joints should be installed near elbows and branch pipes.
5) Heat treatment and non-destructive testing should be performed after bending the pipes.
6) Attention should be paid to the following when configuring hoses:
① The arrangement of hoses should avoid twisting.
② Hoses should be fixed in position or protected.
③ If the weight of the hose may cause tension, supports should be installed and brackets or drag chains should be configured.
④ If a hose rupture would endanger safety, the hydraulic system should be protected with a cover.
(2) Support of pipeline systems
1) Supports should be installed at both ends of the pipeline system and along its length.
2) The support of the pipe should be close to the elbow.
3) If there are no special requirements for the spacing of pipeline system supports, it should be less than the recommended values in Table 4-185.
Table 4-185 Spacing of Pipeline System Supports

4) Supports such as brackets, hangers, and pipe clamps should not be welded to the pipe, nor should they damage the pipe.
5) Vibration-damping pads should be installed between the pipe clamp and the pipe.
(3) Cutting and drilling of pipes
1) Pipes should be cut and drilled using machining methods, avoiding gas cutting.
2) Burrs and chips should be removed after cutting and drilling pipes.
(4) Welding
1) Pipes should not be lengthened by butt welding. Welding is only applicable to the connection of pipes with flanges, pipe joints, branch pipes, etc.
2) After welding, the inside of the pipe in the welded area should be cleaned of welding slag, spatter, and oxide scale.
3) The distance from the weld to the open end of the pipe should not exceed 5 times the inner diameter of the pipe.
4) There should be no dead corners at any welded joint.
5) Electric welding should not be used for welding construction, and argon arc welding should be used instead.
3. Requirements
(1) Marine environmental conditions
1) Atmospheric environment. The hydraulic system should be able to work normally under the following atmospheric environmental conditions:
① The temperature range for ships sailing unlimited sea areas is -25 to 55°C.
② The relative humidity of the air is 95%, with dew formation.
③ There is salt spray, oil mist, and mold.

(2) Product marking
1) The graphic symbols used in the simplified schematic diagram of the hydraulic system should comply with the requirements of G B/T 7861.
2) Each component should have a code, such as a number or letter, and should be marked near the corresponding component on the equipment.
3) The oil ports of each component, such as the working oil inlet and outlet, pilot control port, test port, drain port, etc., should all have markings.
4) The control valve should have markings for its operating form and function.
5) Integrated or assembled components, such as cartridge valves, combination valves, etc., can be marked as a whole.
6) The marking of electric actuators should be consistent with the marking on the electrical and hydraulic system diagrams.
7) The identification symbols and colors of pipelines should comply with the requirements of G B 3033-1982 (which has been invalidated).
4. Testing
(1) Test pressure
The hydraulic test should be conducted before and after the installation of the pipelines. The system pressure test pressure should not be lower than 1.5 times the design pressure, and the sealing test pressure should be 1.25 times the design pressure, but should not exceed the design pressure plus 7 MPa.
(2) Test requirements
1) The hydraulic test of pipelines should comply with the requirements of CB/T 3616-1994 (2017) "Requirements for Hydraulic Test of Pipelines".
2) The installation and sealing test of pipelines should comply with the requirements of CB/T 3619-1994 "Quality Requirements for Installation and Sealing Test of Ship Systems and Power Pipelines".
3) During the test, the pressure should be increased in steps of 25% of the nominal pressure until the test pressure is reached, and the holding time should not be less than 5 min.
4) The hydraulic system of ship machinery and equipment should be tested together with the corresponding equipment.
5) The hydraulic system of the whole ship should be tested together with the mechanical equipment being driven or controlled.
6) The following matters should be noted during the hydraulic test:
① Pressure gauges with a pressure range exceeding the effective range, automatic control components, and pressure valves that have been adjusted should be isolated or removed.
② Before pressurizing, the air stored in the system should be fully eliminated.
③ During the test, the pressure should be increased to the test pressure in steps of 25% of the nominal pressure, and the holding time for each level should generally be 10 min.
(3) Test content
The main contents of the hydraulic system test are as follows:
① The function of transmission or control.
② Performance parameters, such as working oil pressure, speed of the actuator, etc.
③ The effectiveness of safety protection measures.
④ Overload capacity, etc.
5. Cleaning
(1) General requirements
1) Blind plates, plugs, etc. should be installed at all oil ports of hydraulic components and auxiliary parts in the system. If any problems are found, they should be disassembled and maintained in a timely manner.
2) The oil tank (cabinet) is usually not filled with hydraulic oil when it is installed on the ship. Before filling with oil, its internal cleanliness should be rechecked.
3) All pipelines (including cross-connected pipelines for cleaning) should be chemically cleaned.
4) If the pipelines after chemical cleaning are not cleaned with oil in time, oil filling should be used to form a complete oil film on the inner surface of the pipelines, and pipe plugs should be used to seal the ports. The oil used should be compatible with the working oil.
5) When installing the hydraulic system on the ship, operations such as air cleaning, grinding, or painting that may pollute the system should not be carried out nearby.
6) Equipment (including integrated blocks) and pipeline systems that are assembled as a whole and shipped should be cleaned in advance, and the open oil ports should be sealed.
7) The pipeline system should be cleaned with oil after being installed on the ship.
8) Special equipment should be used for hydraulic pumps, filters, oil tanks, etc. for cleaning.
9) Temporary cross-connected pipes should be set up to short-circuit the pipeline system into a loop, without allowing the cleaning oil to flow through hydraulic pumps, control components, and actuator components, etc.
10) When setting up cross-connected pipes, the pipeline system can be short-circuited into one or several loops as needed and for convenience.
11) For pipelines that do not constitute a loop, such as expansion oil pipes and drain pipes, they should be handled separately.
678:
, they should be connected into loops for cleaning. Otherwise, anti-pollution measures should be taken during installation.
(2) Cleaning of piping systems by filling with oil
1) Flow rate of hydraulic pump set for cleaning. The flow rate of the hydraulic pump set for cleaning should be the same as or slightly greater than the working flow rate of the hydraulic system. However, it is recommended that the flow rate of the hydraulic pump set for cleaning should ensure that the Reynolds number in the pipe fittings is not less than 4000.
2) Filters for cleaning.
① The accuracy of the filter can be determined according to the actual situation. At the beginning of cleaning, a coarse filter of 150-200 mesh is usually used, and then the accuracy is gradually increased. Finally, its accuracy should be consistent with or slightly higher than the requirements of the hydraulic system.
② The filter for cleaning should be full-flow.
③ The filter for cleaning should be easy to disassemble, inspect, or replace the filter element.
3) Oil for cleaning.
① The oil for cleaning should have the same oil base as the working oil.
② The oil for cleaning is usually of low viscosity.
③ If the working oil is used for cleaning, the oil after cleaning is generally not suitable for use as working oil again.
④ Soluble chemical cleaning agents should not be used.
4) Temperature of cleaning oil.
① It is recommended to use hot oil for cleaning. When the oil temperature is limited by the cleaning equipment and the oil used, the maximum oil temperature should not exceed the specified value, and the recommended oil temperature is 50°C.
② The oil temperature can be increased by using an oil heater or throttling.
③ Oil pipes should not be directly heated.
5) Operational requirements.
① The cleaning by filling with oil should be carried out continuously, and the pipes should be lightly tapped with a wooden hammer (or other effective methods) along the pipeline multiple times, especially at welded parts or pipe joints.
② After the pipe fittings are cleaned by filling with oil, the time interval for inspecting the filter should not be too long. It is recommended to perform the first inspection 10 minutes after cleaning.
③ The time interval for inspecting the cleaning filter can be gradually extended according to the actual situation, and the maximum recommended interval is 1 hour.
④ The total cleaning time should be determined according to the length and complexity of the piping system loop. Generally, each loop requires 10-24 hours.
⑤ After the cleaning meets the quality requirements, the piping system can be purged with clean and dry compressed air or nitrogen to remove the cleaning oil from the piping system.
(3) Cleaning of the system by filling with oil
1) The system cleaning by filling with oil is carried out after the installation of the hydraulic system and mechanical equipment is completed. The system cleaning by filling with oil usually uses the working oil.
2) The oil filling and air exhaust should be operated according to the following requirements:
① During the oil filling process, the hydraulic oil should be prevented from being stirred.
② The oil filling process should be continuous, and air should not be filled in at the same time.
③ The new oil injected into the system should be filtered.
3) The control elements and actuator elements should be operated one by one in steps. It is recommended that each element should be operated no less than 6 times, and the duration should be no less than 15 minutes.
4) During the system cleaning by filling with oil, the actuator elements are usually in an unloaded state. If cleaning is carried out under load, it should be operated according to the requirements of equipment trial operation.
5) The cleaning process should be operated according to the following requirements:
① The oil temperature during the cleaning process should be below 60°C.
② There should be no leakage during the cleaning process.
③ After the system starts cleaning by filling with oil, the time interval for inspecting the cleaning filter should not be too long. It is recommended to perform the first inspection 30 minutes after cleaning.
④ The time interval for inspecting the cleaning filter can be gradually extended according to the actual situation.
⑤ The oil level in the oil tank should be checked frequently. When the oil level reaches the minimum allowable level, oil should be added to the oil tank in time.
(4) Quality inspection of cleaning
1) Quality inspection of cleaning should be carried out after cleaning of the piping system by filling with oil and cleaning of the system by filling with oil.
2) According to the importance and composition of the mechanical equipment, the components of the system should meet the following requirements for the contamination level of solid particles in the oil:
① For general medium and low-pressure hydraulic systems, the contamination level code of solid particles should not be higher than --/20/16 in GB/T14039-2002, and the contamination level code of solid particles in high-pressure hydraulic systems should be higher than --/18/15 in GB/T14039-2002.
② For general medium and low-pressure proportional hydraulic systems, the contamination level code of solid particles should not be higher than --/17/14 in GB/T14039-2002, and the contamination level code of solid particles in high-pressure proportional hydraulic systems should be higher than --/16/12 in GB/T14039-2002.
③ For servo hydraulic systems, the contamination level code of solid particles should not be higher than --/15/12 in GB/T14039-2002.
3) The following inspection methods are recommended:
① Inspect the filter.
② Inspect the quality of the oil.
③ Analyze and determine the contamination degree of the oil.
4) The oil sample for oil quality inspection should be taken according to the following regulations:
① When used for inspecting the oil quality, the sample should be taken from the oil tank or the release point of the system 6 hours after the cleaning work is stopped.
② When used for determining the contamination degree of the oil, three samples should be taken continuously and randomly during the cleaning process, with a time interval of 10 seconds.
5) Other matters.
① When the hydraulic system is officially put into use, the filter should be replaced with a new or clean filter element.
② After completing the above work, the outer surface of the pipe fittings that need to be protected from rust should be coated with oil-resistant paint.
The use instructions, packaging, and transportation of the hydraulic system can be found in CB/T11102-2008.

4.7.2 Marine Reciprocating Hydraulic Cylinder
The scope and normative references of G B/T 13342-2007 "General Technical Conditions for Marine Reciprocating Hydraulic Cylinder" are shown in Table 1-30.
1. Classification
(1) Type
There are two common types of marine hydraulic cylinders:
1) Plunger-type hydraulic cylinder: The plunger only extends outward in one direction, and the reverse retraction is completed by external force.
2) Double-acting piston-type hydraulic cylinder: The piston moves in both directions, and both extension and retraction strokes are realized by fluid pressure.
(2) Basic Parameters
The basic parameters of hydraulic cylinders can be found in G B/T13342-2007 or Table 2-14.
(3) Graphic Symbols
The graphic symbols of hydraulic cylinders shall be in accordance with the provisions of G B/T 7861.
2. Requirements
(1) Appearance
1) The hydraulic cylinder shall be free from defects such as burrs, bruises, and rust, and the coating shall be free from peeling and bubbles.
2) The outer surface of the hydraulic cylinder shall be free from defects such as folds, obvious waves, and cracks.
3) Exposed components shall be treated for rust prevention, and may also be protected by coatings, passivation layers, paint layers, etc. When painting, apply anti-rust primer first, then topcoat.
4) The outer surface of the hydraulic cylinder shall be free from oxide scale and rust pits before painting. The paint layer shall be free from defects such as blisters.
(2) Materials
1) The materials selected for the main parts of the hydraulic cylinder are shown in Table 4-189, and materials with performance higher than those specified in Table 4-189 may also be selected.

2) After 100% non-destructive testing of the cylinder barrel, it should reach Grade I specified in J B/T 4730.3-2005 (already obsolete).
(3) Structure
1) The hydraulic cylinder should generally be equipped with a buffer device, and there should be no metal impact sound when the stroke reaches the end.
2) The connecting screws and bolts used in the hydraulic cylinder shall not be lower than Grade 8.8 specified in G B/T 3098.1-2000.
3) The hydraulic cylinder should generally be equipped with an exhaust device.
4) The hydraulic cylinder, piston rod or plunger should have anti-corrosion measures.
5) The strength of the weld seam should not be lower than the strength index of the parent material, and the quality of the weld seam should reach Grade II specified in G B/T 3323-2005.
6) The performance of seals, the design and manufacture of each sealing ring and groove can be found in G B/T 13342-2007 or Table 2-67.
(4) Temperature
The temperature requirements of the hydraulic cylinder can be found in G B/T13342-2007 or Table 2-67.
(5) Working Medium
The solid particle contamination degree code of the working medium in the cavity of the hydraulic cylinder shall not be higher than that specified in G B/T 14039-2002 -/19/16.
(6) Pressure Resistance
The pressure resistance requirements of the hydraulic cylinder can be found in G B/T13342-2007 or Table 2-67.
(7) Sealing
Under 1.25 times the nominal pressure, the internal leakage between the cylinder barrel and the piston should comply with the values specified in Table 2 or Table 2-159 of G B/T13342-2007, and there should be no external leakage at other mating surfaces.
(8) Internal Leakage
The internal leakage of a double-acting piston-type hydraulic cylinder should not be greater than the value specified in Table 2 or Table 2-159 of G B/T13342-2007.
(9) External Leakage
The external leakage requirements of the hydraulic cylinder can be found in G B/T13342-2007 or Table 2-67.
(10) Minimum Starting Pressure
1) The minimum starting pressure of the plunger-type hydraulic cylinder should not be greater than the value specified in Table 3 or Table 2-67 of G B/T13342-2007.
2) The minimum starting pressure of the double-acting piston-type hydraulic cylinder should not be greater than the value specified in Table 4 or Table 2-158 of G B/T13342-2007.
(11) Minimum Stable Speed
The requirements for the minimum stable speed of the hydraulic cylinder can be found in G B/T13342-2007 or Table 2-67.
(12) Load Efficiency
The load efficiency of the hydraulic cylinder should not be lower than 90%.
(13) Pressure Resistance
The pressure resistance requirements of the hydraulic cylinder can be found in G B/T13342-2007 or Table 2-67.
(14) Internal Cleanliness
The quality of internal pollutants in the hydraulic cylinder (when the stroke is 1 m) should be lower than the limit value in Table 5 of G B/T13342-2007, as detailed in Table 5-15.
3. Test Methods
The test methods for hydraulic cylinders can be found in G B/T 13342-2007.
4. Inspection Rules
The inspection rules for hydraulic cylinders can be found in G B/T 13342-2007.

The marking requirements for hydraulic cylinders can be found in G B/T13342-2007, and the product nameplate is shown in Table 2-324.
(2) Packaging
The packaging requirements for hydraulic cylinders can be found in G B/T 13342-2007.

The hydraulic cylinder should operate smoothly without sticking, crawling, or external leakage when unloaded throughout the entire stroke.

The starting pressure of the piston cavity for the column under no-load, no-back-pressure conditions should be less than 3.5 MPa. The starting pressure of the piston rod cavity should be less than 7.5 MPa.

4) Sealing Performance of Piston Rod Cavity
The piston rod cavity of the hydraulic cylinder should not leak externally under a pressure of 2 MPa and 1.1 times the supply pressure.
5) Pressure Relief Performance
The column and supporting jack should have bearing capacity while moving and possess pressure relief characteristics:
① The force measured during central pressure relief should be less than 1.1 times the rated force and not less than the rated force.
② The force measured during eccentric pressure relief should not exceed 110% of the maximum force measured during central pressure relief and should not be less than the rated force.
Note: In GB/T 2974.2-2010, the term "pressure relief" is defined as: "The process of the hydraulic cylinder length change caused by external forces exceeding the safety valve opening pressure."
6) Overload Performance in Center
The overload performance in center includes:
① The column (including the extension section) and supporting jack should not experience functional failure when subjected to a static load of 1.5 times the rated force and a dynamic load from mechanical impact reaching 1.5 times the rated working pressure. The residual deformation of the cylinder barrel expansion should be less than 0.02% of the cylinder diameter.
② The column and supporting jack that have not been subjected to mechanical impact dynamic load should be able to withstand a static load pressure of 2 times the rated force. After the loading test, the function of the column and supporting jack should no longer be considered, but the base material should not produce cracks, nor should weld seam cracks occur.
③ The supporting jack that has not been subjected to mechanical impact dynamic load should be able to withstand a static tensile force of 2 times the rated force.
④ The column and supporting jack in a fully retracted state should be able to withstand 2 times the rated force, and there should be no plastic deformation after the test.
⑤ The jack should not experience functional failure when loaded with 1.5 times the rated tensile force or rated working pressure.
7) Eccentric Loading Performance
After being subjected to eccentric force and lateral force, the column (including the extension section) and supporting jack should not experience functional failure. The deflection at the transition between stages should be less than 0.1% of the test length.
8) Durability
After 21,000 loading cycles, the column (including the extension section) and supporting jack should not experience functional failure.
After 10,000 loading cycles, the jack should not experience functional failure.

The column and supporting jack should extend towards the external stop block using at least 0.8 times the rated working pressure, remain stationary for at least 3 minutes, and the external stop block should not be damaged.

4.9 Reference Drawings for Hydraulic Cylinder Design and Selection
All the hydraulic cylinder drawings involved in this section are hydraulic cylinder product drawings designed, reviewed, approved, (re)manufactured, used, tested, accepted and repaired by the author in the past decade or so. The original drawings have been deleted according to relevant requirements including the protection of patent technology.

Due to the large time span, the author's cognition and understanding of hydraulic cylinder design and manufacturing technology, the update of standards, the progress of technology, the improvement of design and manufacturing level, as well as the accumulation and summary of experience, these drawings are not perfect when examined with the current perspective. However, the actual service life of the hydraulic cylinders designed and manufactured by the author has been verified by practical machine verification (or demonstrative test).

Only some common and representative hydraulic cylinder drawings are selected in this section, and some products produced by professional manufacturers are not selected, such as automobile full hydraulic steering gear, coal mine hydraulic support, etc. designed and manufactured by the author.

This manual does not involve the so-called hydraulic cylinder or hydraulic device in which the piston and piston rod move spirally.

The focus of this section is to describe the structural design characteristics of hydraulic cylinder, and the seals in all drawings are simplified, and the nameplates, marks, etc. of each hydraulic cylinder are deleted.

5.1 Test Methods for Hydraulic Cylinders

5.1.1 Summary and Application of GB/T15622-2005 "Test Method for Hydraulic Cylinders"

1. Summary
GB/T15622-2005 "Test Method for Hydraulic Cylinders" was issued on July 11, 2005 and implemented from January 1, 2006, replacing GB/T15622-1995 "Test Method for Hydraulic Cylinders". This standard is not only normatively referenced by JB/T10205-2010 "Hydraulic Cylinders" but also normatively referenced by other hydraulic cylinder product standards. To apply this standard well, the following is a summary of some of its contents.

1. Scope
This standard specifies test methods for hydraulic cylinders.
This standard applies to type tests and factory tests for hydraulic cylinders (including double-acting and single-acting hydraulic cylinders) using hydraulic oil (liquid) as the working medium.
This standard does not apply to combined hydraulic cylinders.

2. Normative References
The following documents contain provisions that, through reference in this text, constitute provisions of this standard. For dated references, subsequent amendments to, or revisions of, any of these publications do not apply. However, parties to agreements based on this standard are encouraged to investigate the possibility of applying the most recent editions of the normative documents indicated below. For undated references, the latest edition of the normative document referred to applies.
GB/T14039-2002 Hydraulic Fluid Power - Fluids - Code for Levels of Contamination by Solid Particles
GB/T17446 Fluid power systems and components - Vocabulary (GB/T17446-1998)

3. Terms and Definitions
The following terms and definitions apply to this standard in addition to those given in GB/T17446.
3.1 Minimum Starting Pressure
The minimum pressure at which a hydraulic cylinder starts to move.
3.4 Load Efficiency
The ratio of the actual output force of a hydraulic cylinder to its theoretical output force.
The symbols and units used in this standard are shown in Table 5-1.
6.7 Load Efficiency Test
Install a force gauge on the piston rod of the hydraulic cylinder being tested, keep the hydraulic cylinder moving at constant speed, and calculate the load efficiency at different pressures using the following formula...
η=W/(pA)×100%

To determine the scope of application specified in the standard GB/T15622-2005, it is necessary to define the term "combined (type) hydraulic cylinder." Here is a tentative definition of the term "combined hydraulic cylinder": a hydraulic cylinder composed of two or more hydraulic cylinders assembled together as a single unit.

Based on this definition, a spring-return single-acting cylinder is not a combined (type) hydraulic cylinder; while a swing hydraulic cylinder is a combined (type) hydraulic cylinder, but does not include devices or parts that convert the reciprocating linear motion of the hydraulic cylinder into the reciprocating rotary motion of gears, etc.

There are also cases where combined (type) hydraulic cylinders are referred to as compound hydraulic cylinders.

In some literature, the definition of compound hydraulic cylinder has been proposed, i.e., a compound hydraulic cylinder is a hydraulic cylinder assembled from different hydraulic cylinders or other hydraulic components. If this definition is followed, the same servo hydraulic cylinder, if the servo valve is installed on its cylinder body, can be called a compound hydraulic cylinder after being assembled into a single hydraulic cylinder; while if the servo valve is connected to it through pipelines, this type of hydraulic cylinder cannot be called a compound hydraulic cylinder, which obviously presents a problem.

For the types and classification of hydraulic cylinders, please refer to Section 2.1.1 of this book.

(2) Minimum starting pressure and load efficiency

The study of the terms "minimum starting pressure" and "load efficiency" is to enable non-professional personnel who have not participated in the compilation of the standard to clearly understand, correctly apply, and cite the national standard GB/T15622-2005.

In both GB/T15622-2005 and JB/T10205-2010, the terms "minimum starting pressure" and "load efficiency" are defined.

In the normative references of GB/T15622-2005, GB/T17446-2012 (1998), there are two terms: "starting pressure" and "cylinder output force efficiency," which are defined as the minimum pressure required to initiate motion (action) and the ratio between the actual (effective) output force of the cylinder and the theoretical output force, respectively.

Comparing the definitions of "minimum starting pressure" with "starting pressure" and "load efficiency" with "cylinder output force efficiency" in GB/T15622-2005 and GB/T17446, the following can be found:

a) Using "minimum" to define "minimum," the concept and term are the same, which is equivalent to not defining it.

b) Different terms but the same definition do not conform to the uniqueness of terms.

c) It violates the statement: "The following terms and definitions given in GB/T17446 as well as the following are applicable to this standard."

In GB/T15622-2005, the term "minimum starting pressure" and its definition do not follow the method of selecting terms and writing definitions as "terms expressing more specific concepts can usually be composed of terms expressing more general concepts"; "load efficiency" not only does not conform to the requirement that terms should have uniqueness but also does not comply with the principle of not repeating the definition of terms that have been defined in other authoritative vocabularies.

Therefore, it is unnecessary to reselect and define the terms "minimum starting pressure" and "load efficiency" in GB/T15622-2005.

GB/T1.1-2009 "Guidelines for Standardization Part 1: Structure and Drafting of Standards" stipulates that synonymous terms should be avoided for concepts that have already been defined. Further references can be made to GB/T20000.1-2002 "Guide to Standardization Part 1: General Vocabulary of Standardization and Related Activities," GB/T101112-2019 "Terminology Work Principles and Methods," and GB/T15237.1-2000 "Terminology Work Vocabulary Part 1: Theory and Application" and other related standards.

(3) Effective area of piston rod

The study of the name and symbol of the "effective area of piston rod" is mainly to solve the calculation problem of load efficiency or cylinder output force efficiency.

In the normative references of GB/T15622-2005, GB/T17446, there is no term and definition of "effective area of piston rod," but there is the term and definition of "piston rod area."

In GB/T17446-1998 and GB/T17446-2012, the term "piston rod area" is defined as "the cross-sectional area of the piston rod" and "the cross-sectional area of the piston rod," respectively.

As a normative reference file of GB/T15622-2005, although JB/T10205-2010 is consistent with the referenced file in "quantity, symbol, and unit," it later changes "effective area of piston rod" to "numerical value of effective area of piston" in "load efficiency test," with the symbol still being "A."

The term "effective area of piston" only appears in GB/T17446-1998, with its definition being: the area that generates mechanical force under the action of fluid force.

It seems that neither GB/T15622-2005 nor JB/T10205-2010 can calculate the load efficiency or cylinder output force efficiency of single-acting and double-acting hydraulic cylinders specified in the standard scope.

(4) Calculation and test of load efficiency

If the issues of the name and symbol of the "effective area of piston rod" mentioned above are not resolved, the calculation of load efficiency or cylinder output force efficiency of double-acting hydraulic cylinders and single-acting hydraulic cylinders specified in GB/T15622-2005 cannot be carried out.

1) According to "symbols and units" and "load efficiency test" in GB/T15622-2005, only the load efficiency or cylinder output force efficiency of plunger cylinders can be calculated, while the load efficiency or cylinder output force efficiency of double-acting piston cylinders and single-acting piston cylinders cannot be calculated.

2) According to "quantity, symbol, and unit" and "load efficiency test" in JB/T10205-2010, due to inconsistency before and after, the load efficiency or cylinder output force efficiency cannot be calculated.

3) According to "load efficiency test" in JB/T10205-2010, only the load efficiency or cylinder output force efficiency of piston cylinders can be calculated, while the load efficiency or cylinder output force efficiency of plunger cylinders cannot be calculated.
737:
The load efficiency of a cylinder or the output force efficiency of a cylinder cannot be calculated.

Based on the above analysis, in the "Symbols and Units" or "Quantities, Symbols and Units" of GB/T15622-2005 or JB/T10205-2010, "Piston (Effective) Area" can be added, or "Piston Rod Effective Area" can be deleted, and "Cylinder Effective Area" can be added. Otherwise, the load efficiency of single and double-acting piston cylinders specified in the standard range cannot be calculated.

It should be noted that if the hydraulic cylinder type test hydraulic system given in Figure 4 of GB/T15622-2005 is used for load efficiency testing, some small-sized hydraulic cylinders may not be able to proceed due to the maximum speed during testing exceeding the designed maximum speed and/or excessive back pressure; general hydraulic cylinders will also fail to achieve the purpose of verifying the load-bearing static friction force of the hydraulic cylinder through load efficiency testing due to the inability to limit the back pressure.

In addition, there are issues of confusion and misuse of terms such as trial operation and trial running, nominal pressure and rated pressure, double-rod cylinder (double-rod cylinder) and double piston rod (hydraulic) cylinder, leakage and seepage, stroke and maximum stroke, etc. in GB/T15622-2005, as well as some other issues, which are worth further discussion.

5.1.2 JB/T10205-2010 "Hydraulic Cylinder" Summary and Its Application

JB/T10205-2010 "Hydraulic Cylinder" was issued on February 11, 2010 and implemented on July 1, 2010, which has been over 10 years. Compared with other hydraulic cylinder product standards, it has a wider applicable range, so it is widely followed by other hydraulic cylinders without product standards in design and manufacturing.

The study of JB/T10205-2010 "Hydraulic Cylinder" standard is to better comply with this standard, and to design and manufacture better hydraulic cylinders by applying or referring to this standard.

1. Scope

(1) Summary

1. Scope

This standard specifies the classification and basic parameters, technical requirements, test methods, inspection rules, packaging, transportation and other requirements for single and double-acting hydraulic cylinders.

This standard applies to single and double-acting hydraulic cylinders with a nominal pressure of 31.5 MPa or less, using hydraulic oil or other mineral oil with comparable performance as the working medium. For hydraulic cylinders with a nominal pressure higher than 31.5 MPa, this standard may be referred to. Special requirements other than those specified in this standard shall be negotiated between the hydraulic cylinder manufacturer and the user.

(2) Application

Based on the writing characteristics of the standard, the standard lacks hydraulic cylinders with a nominal pressure of 31.5 MPa.

According to the provisions of GB/T81702008, the correct statement should be: This standard applies to single and double-acting hydraulic cylinders with a nominal pressure less (lower) than or equal to 31.5 MPa, using hydraulic oil or other mineral oil with comparable performance as the working medium.

It can also be expressed as: This standard applies to single and double-acting hydraulic cylinders with a nominal pressure not greater (higher) than 31.5 MPa, using hydraulic oil or other mineral oil with comparable performance as the working medium.

According to the rules given in GB/T1.12009 "Standardization Work Guide Part 1: Structure and Writing of Standards", the standard writing in the above abstract does not meet the "uniformity" requirement, that is, similar clauses should be expressed using similar wording, and the same clauses should be expressed using the same wording; at the same time, the limits specified in the "Scope" of the standard are incomplete.

(2) Application

JB/T10205—2010 "Hydraulic Cylinders" replaced JB/T10205—2000 "Technical Conditions for Hydraulic Cylinders" which was first published in August 2000. In JB/T10205—2000, the internal leakage of double-acting hydraulic cylinders (Table 5) and the internal leakage of single-acting hydraulic cylinders (Table 6) differ from Tables 5-7 and 5-8 only in the "Notes", indicating that there has been no change in the performance indicators for internal leakage of piston-type single and double-acting hydraulic cylinders in factory tests over the past 20 years.

In JB/JQ20301—1988 "Grading of Product Quality for Medium and High-pressure Hydraulic Cylinders (Trial Implementation)", Table 1 lists the inspection items and key items for quality grading. The internal leakage indicators for medium and high-pressure hydraulic cylinders with cylinder bores of 40-250 mm are also the same as in Table 5-7, but there is no distinction made between the internal leakage of piston-type double-acting and single-acting hydraulic cylinders, nor are there any "Notes" regarding checking internal leakage by settling amount.

Based on the above summary and the distribution of versions of this standard that it has replaced, the following points should be noted when applying the performance indicators for internal leakage of piston-type single and double-acting hydraulic cylinders in JB/T10205—2010:

1) Internal leakage of piston-type single-acting hydraulic cylinders. In Table 7 of JB/T10205—2010, the internal leakage (values) listed for piston-type single-acting hydraulic cylinders is twice or more than that listed in Table 6 for double-acting hydraulic cylinders.

Table 6 of JB/T10205—2010 can be traced back at least to JB/JQ20301—1988, and its evolution is clear, indicating industry consensus; however, Table 7 of JB/T10205—2010 is not in JB/JQ20301—1988 and can only be traced back to JB/T10205—2000.

Considering factors such as the sealing structure and mechanism of hydraulic cylinders and test conditions, the internal leakage (values) listed for piston-type single-acting hydraulic cylinders in Table 7 of JB/T10205—2010 are not entirely reasonable.

2) Checking internal leakage of piston-type double-acting hydraulic cylinders by settling amount. Since internal leakage of piston-type single-acting hydraulic cylinders can be checked (measured) by settling amount, then piston-type double-acting hydraulic cylinders should also be able to use settling amount to check (measure) their internal leakage. In standards such as JB/T9834—2014 "Technical Conditions for Agricultural Double-acting Hydraulic Cylinders" and JB/T11588—2013 "Large Hydraulic Cylinders", it is stipulated that the internal leakage of double-acting hydraulic cylinders can be measured or calculated by settling amount.

When using settling amount to measure or calculate the internal leakage of double-acting hydraulic cylinders, testing (trial) methods should be specified.

There is a one-to-one correspondence between settling amount and internal leakage, and the values are basically equivalent after conversion, as shown in Table 5-7 above. If it is confirmed that the internal leakage of double-acting hydraulic cylinders given in Table 6 of JB/T10205—2010 is reasonable, then the settling amount of double-acting hydraulic cylinders can only be around 0.025 mm/min.

3) Internal leakage of hydraulic cylinders and technological progress. Despite the JB2146-237 Hydraulic Cylinder Handbook

1977 "Hydraulic Component Factory Test Technical Indicators" and JB/JQ20301-1988 "Medium and High Pressure Hydraulic Cylinder Product Quality Classification (Trial)" and JB/T10205-2000 "Hydraulic Cylinder Technical Conditions" and JB/T10205-2010 "Hydraulic Cylinder" have no substitution or reference relationship, but because it is stipulated in JB214-1977 that the allowable value of internal leakage is calculated based on the cylinder sinking amount of 0.5mm/5min (0.1mm/min). This not only shows that the sinking amount can be used to detect the internal leakage of piston-type double-acting hydraulic cylinders, but also shows the technical progress of the internal leakage performance index of hydraulic cylinders.

Standards should fully consider the latest technical level and provide a framework for future technological development. In terms of the internal leakage of double-acting hydraulic cylinders, a performance index of hydraulic cylinders, JB/T10205-2010 "Hydraulic Cylinder" has not changed since JB/JQ20301-1988 "Medium and High Pressure Hydraulic Cylinder Product Quality Classification (Trial)" implemented in October 1988, and the standard cannot reflect that it is based on a summary of modern science, technology and experience.

Technology is always progressing. In Table 7 of JB/T11588-2013 "Large Hydraulic Cylinder", there is a note: "For special specifications of hydraulic cylinders, the internal leakage is calculated based on the displacement of 0.01mm/min when the rodless chamber is pressurized." The above statement in JB/T11588-2013 is not entirely correct. In general hydraulic cylinders, the piston of single and double-acting piston cylinders and the piston rod head of single-acting plunger cylinders are often used as limiters. When the piston or piston rod head contacts other cylinder parts, it is one end of the cylinder stroke (the terminal position of the cylinder process or the terminal position of the cylinder return stroke).
In high-pressure and high-speed (high-speed return stroke of the cylinder) hydraulic cylinders, the piston diameter (or cylinder bore) and piston rod diameter, and the piston rod head diameter and piston rod diameter are not much different. In this case, if the working chamber is subjected to hydraulic oil with a pressure of 1.5 times the nominal pressure for a pressure test at the terminal position of the cylinder process, the cylinder parts may be damaged. Therefore, in some other hydraulic cylinder product standards, there are: "During the pressure resistance test of the hydraulic cylinder to be tested, the piston of the hydraulic cylinder to be tested should be stopped at both ends of the stroke (cannot contact the cylinder cover)" or "(During the pressure resistance test of the double-acting piston hydraulic cylinder) When pressurizing from the rodless end, fix the piston near the end of the stroke for the test; when pressurizing from the rod end, fix the piston near the starting position of the stroke for the test". 6.1 Trial Operation
Adjust the test system pressure to start the hydraulic cylinder under no-load conditions and reciprocate it through its full stroke several times to completely eliminate air from the hydraulic cylinder.

Under rated pressure, make the hydraulic cylinder run continuously at the highest speed required by the design (±10% speed error), for more than 8 h continuously. During the test, no adjustment of hydraulic cylinder parts is allowed. Record the cumulative stroke.

Supply oil to the working chamber of the hydraulic cylinder, pressurize to rated pressure or user-specified pressure, and measure the leakage amount through the piston to the unpressurized chamber.

When the hydraulic cylinder bore is greater than 32 mm, at a minimum pressure of 0.5 MPa (5 bar); when the hydraulic cylinder bore is less than or equal to 32 mm, at 1 MPa (10 bar) pressure, make the hydraulic cylinder reciprocate through its full stroke at least 3 times, staying at the stroke ends for at least 10 s each time.

During the test, perform the following checks:
a) Check if the hydraulic cylinder vibrates or crawls during movement.
b) Observe if there is oil leakage at the piston rod seal. When the test ends, the oil film on the piston rod should not be sufficient to form oil drops or rings.
c) Check all static seals for oil leakage.
d) Check the throttling and/or cushioning components installed on the hydraulic cylinder for oil leakage.

Fully loosen the cushioning valve of the working chamber of the hydraulic cylinder under test, adjust the test pressure to 50% of the nominal pressure, run at the highest designed speed, and detect the cushioning effect when the cushioning valve is fully closed.

Install a dynamometer on the piston rod of the hydraulic cylinder under test, keep the hydraulic cylinder moving at constant speed, and calculate the load efficiency at different pressures using the formula shown in Figure 6 (omitted), then draw the load efficiency characteristic curve.

Under rated pressure, input hydraulic oil at 90°C to the hydraulic cylinder under test, and reciprocate through full stroke for 1 h.

Stop the piston or plunger of the hydraulic cylinder under test at both extreme positions of the stroke, and measure the stroke length.

When applying or referencing test items and methods in various standards, the following points should be noted.
(1) Pressure Test (Test) Pressure
In the pressure test, the pressure test (test) pressure is specified differently in various standards, such as nominal pressure, rated pressure, nominal working pressure, and rated working pressure.
Only "Nominal Pressure" and "Rated Pressure" are defined in GB/T17446—2012.
The pressure test represented by nominal pressure or rated pressure has a specific meaning, while others may be ambiguous.
In the standards listed in Table 5-10, the highest is "1.5 times the nominal pressure" for the pressure test (test) pressure. In hydraulic transmission systems and components, the pressure test pressure is second only to the burst pressure. Generally, only the pressure test (performance) test can be conducted under the pressure test pressure, and other performance tests cannot be performed. The pressure test is a static pressure test. This point is particularly important for cylinders.
In pressure tests, the specification of "holding pressure for 10 seconds during factory testing" is the most scientific. Other specifications such as holding pressure for 2 minutes (or even 5 minutes in some cases) at 1.5 times the nominal pressure, even if the hydraulic cylinder being tested passes the test, may cause irreparable damage to the cylinder.
"Nominal pressure" and "rated pressure" are also used in sealing tests. In any case, the test pressure for hydraulic cylinder sealing tests should not be higher than or equal to the pressure test pressure, and the corresponding holding time for static sealing factory tests should also be reasonably specified. Otherwise, after factory testing, the hydraulic cylinder being tested will be scrapped.
(2) Piston and Piston Rod
The piston and piston rod are cylinder components that can perform reciprocating motion relative to the cylinder body (barrel), and the piston and piston rod are coaxial and connected as one unit.
In some hydraulic cylinder test standards, the states of hydraulic cylinder operation and stopping are often described by the relative position between the piston and the cylinder body (barrel). Such descriptions are mostly necessary, but since the piston is hidden inside the cylinder body (barrel) and cannot be directly observed, only the exposed piston rod can be visually judged during hydraulic cylinder testing. Therefore, the descriptions of piston position during hydraulic cylinder operation and stopping lack simultaneous descriptions of the piston rod.
In DB44/T11692013, regardless of whether the specified test methods are correct and feasible, only in the general provisions for eccentricity test "detecting the eccentricity of the piston rod during piston movement for hydraulic cylinders with piston diameter greater than 500mm under loaded conditions," the word "所" (meaning "during") in "piston movement 所 piston rod" is difficult to understand.
Even for hydraulic cylinders with built-in displacement sensors or servo hydraulic cylinders, there is still the issue of simultaneous description of the piston and piston rod when the hydraulic cylinder is running and stopping.
Additionally, plunger cylinders do not have pistons, only piston rods, so describing the state of the hydraulic cylinder using the piston rod is more accurate.
(3) Placement of Hydraulic Cylinder
GB/T15622-2005 provides two placement methods for hydraulic cylinder testing: horizontal placement and inclined placement.
During hydraulic cylinder testing, it is generally impossible to simulate actual working conditions, i.e., it is impossible to simulate the installation type, connection type, and force conditions on the host machine. Therefore, the tested hydraulic cylinder generally does not bear lateral loads or perform lateral force loading.
Different placements of the tested hydraulic cylinder may directly affect test results, and some performances may not even be testable, such as the settlement of the hydraulic cylinder.
JB/T10205-2010 also stipulates: "The test device for hydraulic cylinders should generally adopt a plane device with a horizontal foundation as the standard."
(4) Internal Leakage Test
Most hydraulic cylinder tests require "stopping the piston of the tested hydraulic cylinder at both ends of the stroke" respectively, and measuring the leakage amount leaking through the piston to the unpressurized chamber.
Without discussing whether the two ends are the (stroke) limit positions or other positions, but conducting internal leakage tests by "stopping the piston at both ends and the middle of the hydraulic cylinder respectively" is more reasonable, especially for hydraulic cylinders with a stroke exceeding 1000mm, this specification is even more reasonable.
During internal leakage testing, the temperature of the hydraulic oil (fluid) input to the tested hydraulic cylinder cannot be lowered, otherwise the test measurement values will be inaccurate. More importantly, the viscosity of the test hydraulic oil must comply with regulations or be agreed upon by the manufacturer and user. Otherwise, internal leakage tests conducted at the user's site, including settlement tests, may exceed standards.
(5) Settlement Measurement Method
The internal leakage factory test method given in Table 6 of JB/T98342014 is not entirely reasonable (see Table 5-10). For example, oil supply to both chambers of the tested cylinder is required, but it should be stipulated that the hydraulic cylinder cannot operate at high speed; closing the shut-off valve on the supply oil chamber can only be a shut-off valve installed in the rodless chamber, not a shut-off valve installed in the rod chamber; using a loading cylinder to make the supply chamber oil pressure reach the test pressure, but it must be stipulated that it is the rodless chamber.
The correct method for settlement testing to check internal leakage should be: supplying oil to both chambers of the double-acting hydraulic cylinder respectively, allowing it to run at low speed; under the condition of ensuring the rodless chamber is free of air, and the amount of air mixed in the test oil meets the regulations, closing the shut-off valve near the oil port of the rodless chamber, making the piston and piston rod stop at a certain distance from the cylinder return stroke limit position or a specified position (generally should include the cylinder stroke limit position and the middle position of the cylinder stroke), and opening the oil port of the rod chamber, allowing it to communicate directly with the atmosphere; through external loading (force), the pressure in the rodless chamber should always be maintained at the test pressure (nominal pressure), and the displacement of the piston (piston rod) should be measured after 1 minute.
According to the settlement measurement method given by the author above, the hydraulic system schematic diagram for type testing of hydraulic cylinders shown in Figure 5-1 and the hydraulic system schematic diagram of the loading device for digital hydraulic cylinder type testing shown in Figure 5-2 do not have the function of active loading with fixed direction and fixed pressure, and cannot be used to complete this test.

2. Test Equipment

The factory test equipment for hydraulic cylinder sealing performance should generally consist of a loading test equipment and a hydraulic cylinder test operation table (including hydraulic system, testing instruments, meters, devices, and/or electrical control, operating devices, and other control equipment).
