Composition of the device.

According to the relevant standards for hydraulic cylinder testing, the factory sealing performance test device of hydraulic cylinders should have the following performance:

1) It should be equipped with a device for applying external loads to the tested hydraulic cylinder, and the load should act along the centerline of the hydraulic cylinder. It should be able to generate a pressure greater than or equal to 1.5 times the nominal pressure in each working chamber of the tested hydraulic cylinder, and can serve as an actual stopper for the tested hydraulic cylinder at various positions of the stroke, including the two extreme positions of the hydraulic cylinder stroke (i.e., the so-called stroke ends). It can also be equipped with a device for applying lateral force (load) to the tested hydraulic cylinder. The installation, connection, and placement of the hydraulic cylinder (type) test should be consistent with the actual working conditions.

2) The hydraulic system should be equipped with a relief valve to prevent the tested hydraulic cylinder from bearing a pressure exceeding 1.1×1.5×nominal pressure, especially to prevent the pressure increase in the rodless cavity of the hydraulic cylinder due to the piston area difference from exceeding the above-mentioned pressure; a manual pressure relief device for each chamber of the tested hydraulic cylinder should be set up; necessary safety devices should be set up, and reliable protective measures should be adopted to ensure the safety of equipment and personnel.

3) The hydraulic system should be able to apply a pressure of 0 to 1.5 times the nominal pressure or higher to the tested hydraulic cylinder; it should be able to make the hydraulic cylinder run continuously (reversing) stably at the nominal pressure (or rated pressure) and 0 to the highest design speed; it should be able to apply a back pressure of 0.2 MPa to the tested hydraulic cylinder; it should be able to make the oil temperature in the oil tank and the input port of the hydraulic cylinder reach and maintain +50℃±4℃ or +90℃±4℃; the solid particle contamination level code of the oil in the oil tank and the input port of the hydraulic cylinder should not be higher than 19/15 or —/19/15 specified in GB/T 14039.

4) Both chambers (oil ports) of the tested hydraulic cylinder should be able to be connected to the system, cut off from the system, and also open to the atmosphere after being cut off from the system; the pressure measurement point should be set at a distance of about 2d to 4d from the oil port of the tested hydraulic cylinder (d is the inner diameter of the connecting pipeline), and the temperature measurement point should be set at a distance of 2d to 4d from the pressure measurement point (d is the same as above).

5) The allowable system error of the measurement system and the allowable variation range of the average display value of the controlled parameters should be specified according to the relevant standards. It should be able to detect a pressure of 0.03 MPa (the minimum starting pressure of the servo hydraulic cylinder) up to 1.1×1.5×nominal pressure, and the range of the (pressure gauge) should generally be (1.5 to 2.0)×1.5×nominal pressure; it should be able to detect an input flow rate of 0.02 mL/min up to the flow rate that enables the tested hydraulic cylinder to run at the highest design speed; it should be able to detect a force greater than or equal to the theoretical output force of the tested hydraulic cylinder; it should be able to detect the stroke and deviation of the tested hydraulic cylinder; or it should be able to accurately detect the cylinder stroke positioning accuracy and stroke repeated positioning accuracy of the tested hydraulic cylinder with special technical requirements or special structures.

It should also be able to automatically accumulate the number of reversals (counting), timing, ambient temperature measurement, etc. The measurement of the inclination, rocking, vibration, and eccentricity of the hydraulic cylinder should be carried out according to the relevant standards.

6) The electrical control voltage should be DC 24V, and it should be equipped with reliable grounding connection. The electrical operation device (station) should be set independently and can be moved. The environmental pollution degree, background noise level, power capacity and quality, fire protection facilities, safety protection measures, etc. of the installation site of the test device should all comply with the relevant standards.

Taking the "Figure 3 Factory Test Hydraulic System Schematic Diagram" (see Figure 5-1) given in GB/T 15622-2005 "Hydraulic Cylinder Test Method" as an example, according to the mandatory inspection items, rules (methods or steps) for hydraulic cylinders specified in JB/T 10205-2010 "Hydraulic Cylinders" and the corresponding mandatory test items and rules for the sealing performance of hydraulic cylinders, the following points should be noted when applying GB/T 15622-2005 "Figure 3 Factory Test Hydraulic System Schematic Diagram":

(1) Oil Tank
Since there is no heat exchanger designed and installed in the oil tank shown in Figure 3 of GB/T 15622-2005, the oil temperature in the oil tank and the input port of the hydraulic cylinder cannot be guaranteed to reach and maintain the specified temperature and allowable variation range. Therefore, all the mandatory inspection items specified in JB/T 10205 and all the mandatory test items specified in the hydraulic cylinder sealing performance test cannot obtain accurate test measurement values and converted values, that is, they do not meet the test conditions specified in JB/T 10205.

(2) Filter
Since only a coarse filter is allowed on the hydraulic pump suction pipeline, the filter shown in Figure 3 of GB/T 15622-2005 can only be a coarse filter. The oil filtered by the coarse filter cannot guarantee that it meets the test oil contamination level specified in JB/T 10205 and in the hydraulic cylinder sealing performance test, that is, the solid particle contamination level code of the oil in the input port of the hydraulic cylinder should not be higher than 19/15 or —/19/15 specified in GB/T 14039, that is, it does not meet the test conditions specified in JB/T 10205.

(3) Hydraulic Pump
Since there is only one fixed displacement hydraulic pump and one relief valve in Figure 3 of GB/T 15622-2005, and it is a return throttling, no bypass throttling speed control system, this system cannot achieve (obtain) stable operation (condition) under no-load conditions with low pressure and low speed, that is, it cannot carry out the mandatory inspection items specified in JB/T 10205 and the mandatory test items "test run" specified in the hydraulic cylinder sealing performance test, that is, "starting pressure characteristic test"; or it cannot carry out the test items of "low pressure and low speed test" and "leakage under low pressure".

(4) Relief Valve
Since there is only one relief valve in Figure 3 of GB/T 15622-2005, if the hydraulic system is to be able to adjust out a stable pressure condition between less than 0.3 MPa (or 0.03 MPa) and greater than or equal to 1.5×31.5 MPa (or 1.1×1.5×nominal pressure), it is almost impossible in terms of the performance (such as pressure regulating range) of the existing relief valve.

Moreover, to prevent the pressure increase in the rodless cavity of the tested hydraulic cylinder due to the piston area difference, a relief valve should be set in the rodless cavity.

5.1.4.2 Hydraulic Cylinder Sealing Performance Test Method and Inspection Rules

1. Technical Requirements for Hydraulic Cylinder Sealing Performance

In all the following tests, there should be no damage to any components (including sealing elements).

In all the following tests, except for the piston rod seal, there should be no external leakage or seepage at other locations; there should be no external leakage when the hydraulic cylinder is stationary at the piston rod; there should be no seepage on the outer surface of the hydraulic cylinder body (barrel).

In low-pressure, low-speed tests and internal leakage tests, the internal leakage should not exceed the standard specified values.

When checking (measuring) the internal leakage amount by the settlement method, the settlement amount should not exceed the standard specified value.

During operation, the hydraulic cylinder should not exhibit vibration, abnormal noise, sudden rushing, jamming, or crawling.

If necessary, environmental adaptability tests are recommended.

The operating conditions should generally include combinations of high and low pressure, high and low temperature, and high and low speed.

For hydraulic cylinders with lateral deviation performance requirements, the lateral deviation value should not exceed the specified value.

For the description of the starting and operating states of hydraulic cylinders, refer to Section 2.18 of this manual.

2. Factory Test Method for Hydraulic Cylinder Sealing Performance

(1) Trial Operation (Mandatory Test)

The hydraulic cylinder is started under no-load conditions and reciprocated several times along the full stroke to completely expel air from the hydraulic cylinder.

(2) Low-Pressure, Low-Speed Test (Mandatory Test)

1) Pressure adjustment range: 0 to 0.5 MPa or 0 to 1.0 MPa.

2) Speed adjustment range: 0 to 4.0 (8.0) mm/s or 0 to 5.0 (10.0) mm/s.

Adjust the pressure and speed, and finally select a pressure of 0.5 MPa or 1.0 MPa and a speed of 4.0 (5.0) mm/s or 5.0 (10.0) mm/s. The cylinder should reciprocate along the full stroke at least 3 times (6 times), with each end of the stroke being held for at least 10 s.

The minimum stable speed index should be determined through agreement with the user and should be stipulated in the contract. Additionally, the two groups of minimum speed indexes are specified in GB/T13342 and CB/T3812, respectively.

(3) High-Speed Test (Sampling Test)

Under the rated pressure, the hydraulic cylinder operates continuously at the design-required highest speed (highest speed index should be determined through agreement with the user and should be stipulated in the contract) under the specified conditions or rated conditions, with a speed error of ±10%. Each test should run continuously for more than 8 hours.

The high-speed test (sampling test) is also known as the durability test.

(4) Pressure Resistance Test (Mandatory Test)

Except for hydraulic cylinders where the technical requirements explicitly prohibit using cylinder components as actual limiters, for other hydraulic cylinders undergoing the pressure resistance test, the hydraulic cylinder piston should be stopped at both ends of the stroke (single-acting hydraulic cylinder at the extreme position of the stroke), and hydraulic oil at 1.5 times or 1.25 times the rated pressure should be applied to the working chamber. The factory test should maintain pressure for 10 s.

(5) Internal Leakage Test (Mandatory Test)

The hydraulic cylinder should be stopped at both ends of the stroke or at a position 10 mm from the end of the stroke (endpoint), and hydraulic oil at the rated pressure (or rated pressure) should be applied to the working chamber for testing.

For hydraulic cylinders with a stroke exceeding 1 m, in addition to the internal leakage test (mandatory test), the hydraulic cylinder should also be stopped at the middle of the stroke for the aforementioned internal leakage test (mandatory test).

It is recommended to determine through negotiation between the manufacturer and the user that the internal leakage test pressure uses the "rated pressure."

(6) High-Temperature Test (Sampling Test)

Under the rated pressure, hydraulic oil at 90°C is input into the hydraulic cylinder, which should reciprocate along the full stroke for 1 hour.

The high-temperature test should only be conducted on hydraulic cylinders if high-temperature performance is required for the product. Whether to disassemble and inspect or replace sealing elements after the test should be determined through negotiation between the manufacturer and the user.

(7) Buffer Test (Sampling Test)

Under a pressure of 50% of the rated pressure or the highest working pressure, the hydraulic cylinder should operate several times at the highest speed required by the design (under the specified conditions or rated conditions).

The buffer test should only be conducted on hydraulic cylinders if buffer performance is required for the product. This test mainly examines the sealing performance of the hydraulic cylinder under the action of "buffer pressure" or "peak buffer pressure."
759:
(8) Dynamic Characteristics Test (Sampling)
For hydraulic cylinders with dynamic characteristic requirements, the dynamic characteristics test shall be conducted according to the provisions of their product standards, such as digital hydraulic cylinders and servo hydraulic cylinders. For hydraulic cylinders without product standard provisions but with dynamic characteristic requirements, inspection shall be conducted at least according to the special technical requirements (conditions or indicators) agreed upon between the manufacturer and the user.

It is recommended that manufacturers draft and formulate product enterprise standards based on their products.

During dynamic characteristics testing, extreme conditions beyond the specified operating conditions may occur.

(9) External Leakage Test (Mandatory)
The external leakage test is included in all the above tests; at the end of the above tests, the oil film on the piston rod should be insufficient to form oil droplets or oil rings.

For hydraulic cylinders that have not undergone sampling test items, the external leakage should be checked after reciprocating the full stroke more than 20 times under nominal pressure (or rated pressure), with the same requirements as above.

The installation positions (surfaces) of the inlet and outlet ports, exhaust (relief) devices, cushioning (valve) devices, stroke adjustment devices (mechanisms), input devices (including speed reduction devices and drive devices, etc.), hydraulic valves or manifold blocks, and instruments, sensors, etc., should not have external leakage.

3. Inspection Rules for Hydraulic Cylinder Sealing Performance Factory Test

Hydraulic cylinders must undergo individual sealing performance factory tests before leaving the factory. The inspection results (test measurement values) of mandatory inspection items and sampling inspection items agreed upon with the user shall comply with the relevant standard provisions.

For hydraulic cylinders that have passed type tests and are already standardized or in mass production, sampling inspection items should also be conducted periodically.

4. Precautions for Hydraulic Cylinder Sealing Performance Testing

1) The hydraulic cylinder test should be operated by specially trained personnel with professional knowledge.

2) There are dangers in hydraulic cylinder testing, such as possible cylinder body rupture, connection (including welding) failure, piston rod disconnection (ejection), and seal device (system) failure, etc. Necessary protective measures should be taken, including installing and using protective covers, etc., to avoid possible injuries to personnel caused by high-pressure and/or high-temperature oil splashing or spraying.

3) For hydraulic cylinders designed with exhaust (relief) devices, the air in the hydraulic cylinder should be completely expelled during trial operation, and the danger of oil splashing or spraying to personnel caused by exhaust should be avoided.

4) For hydraulic cylinders (including test systems) without exhaust (relief) devices, the full stroke should be reciprocated several times during trial operation to completely expel the air in the hydraulic cylinder, and then placed for a period of time before conducting other test items, so that the air mixed in can be separated from the oil in the oil tank.

5) The oil used for hydraulic cylinder sealing performance testing should be consistent with the type and viscosity grade of the working medium of the hydraulic system or host it is matched with; otherwise, it may cause batch non-conformance of the product.

6) Except for high and low temperature tests, other hydraulic cylinder sealing performance inspections should be conducted when the working medium temperature in the working chamber is 52°C ± 4°C (considering the system error allowed by the measurement system); otherwise, it may cause batch non-conformance of the product.

7) In the single-acting hydraulic cylinder specified in JB/T10205, the settling amount refers to the displacement of the cylinder (piston and piston rod) in the return direction caused by the leakage of the oil in the rodless cavity through the piston seal device (system) to the rod cavity. The settling (amount) of the double-acting hydraulic cylinder installed on the host may be either the displacement (amount) of the cylinder in the return direction or the displacement (amount) in the advance direction. Therefore, attention should be paid to the conversion relationship between the settling amount of the double-acting hydraulic cylinder in the advance direction and the internal leakage amount, and at the same time, attention should be paid to the fact that the settling amount of the hydraulic cylinder is caused by external loading, and the test bench without loading test devices cannot detect this item.

8) During testing, the hydraulic cylinder should be loaded (pressurized) and unloaded (depressurized) slowly and in stages. During the pressure test, the holding time specified in the standard should not be exceeded (10 s for factory test holding).

9) In JB/T10205, the internal leakage amount (specified value) of double-acting hydraulic cylinders and the internal leakage amount (specified value) of single-acting hydraulic cylinders have at least one group of questionable values, and further consultation with the user should be conducted before testing to determine.

10) When visually checking the external leakage at the piston rod, it is advisable to wipe it clean again after trial operation and then check to avoid false "leakage" being misjudged as leakage.

11) For checking seepage or external leakage, the method of attaching clean absorbent paper (for fixed cylinder parts surface, such as cylinder body surface) or laying white paper along the path (for moving cylinder parts along the path, such as piston rod reciprocating path) can be used to check, with oil traces or oil spots on the paper indicating seepage or external leakage.

12) All sampling test items may cause certain damage to the hydraulic cylinder seal. It is recommended that the first hydraulic cylinder that has undergone sampling test items be disassembled and inspected after the test.

The following points should be noted when applying them.

(1) Hydraulic System Schematic Diagram

In CB/T3812-2013, the hydraulic system schematic diagram for hydraulic cylinder testing is specified according to GB/T13342. GB/T13342-847 Hydraulic Cylinder Manual

(2) Material Test, Cleanliness Test and Environmental Adaptability Test

The test method in CB/T 38112-2013 includes material test, cleanliness test (test) and environmental adaptability test (test), which are not included in GB/T 15622-2005 and JB/T 10205-2013. Specifically:

1) Material Test. Check the material certificates of each part.

2) Cleanliness Test. Clean the inner cavity of the hydraulic cylinder, then slowly pour the cleaning liquid onto the filter membrane (accuracy 0.8μm) placed on the funnel orifice for filtration. 3) Environmental Adaptability Test. When the ambient temperature is 65°C ± 5°C, keep the temperature of the test hydraulic fluid at 70°C ± 2°C. "Test" has a clear definition. Checking the material certificates of each part cannot be called a "material test". However, before the hydraulic cylinder test, it is necessary to check and verify the grades and material specifications of the materials used.

Although this standard provides a cleanliness test method, which is feasible and may facilitate the use of the standard, it must be complete, accurate, and comply with the relevant standard regulations. (3) Hydraulic Cylinder Performance Test Method

1) Compared with the other two standards (GB/T 15622-2005 and JB/T 10205-2013), CB/T 38112-2013 adds two test items, minimum stable speed and disassembly inspection, in the hydraulic cylinder performance test method, and omits the stroke inspection. The disassembly item is only carried out during type inspection. Stroke should be a basic parameter of the hydraulic cylinder. It is also included in the product identification specified in CB/T 38112-2013, but this standard has neither technical requirements nor inspection methods for stroke.

2) The technical requirements and test methods for "load efficiency" are included in these standards, but the test method given in CB/T 38112-2013 is: Install a dynamometer on the piston rod of the tested hydraulic cylinder, gradually increase the pressure in the working chamber of the tested hydraulic cylinder, and calculate the efficiency of each point according to formulas (2) and (3). This is different from the other three standards, lacking the test condition of "keeping the tested hydraulic cylinder moving at a constant speed" or "keeping the tested hydraulic cylinder moving at a constant speed", that is, it may not measure and record various parameters under steady-state operating conditions. Therefore, there are deficiencies in the test method for "load efficiency" given in CB/T 38112-2013.

In addition, the calculation formula (2): η=WF×100 given by it is wrong and should be η=WF×100%.

3) The technical requirements and test methods for buffering are not included in GB/T 13342-2007, but are included in the other three standards. In CB/T 38112-2013, the test method for "buffering effect" is: Test the tested hydraulic cylinder at a designed maximum speed when the input pressure is 50% of the nominal pressure, and observe the movement of the piston. Compared with the "buffering test" given in GB/T 15622-2005, which is to fully loosen the buffer valve in the working chamber of the tested hydraulic cylinder, adjust the test pressure to 50% of the nominal pressure, run at the designed maximum speed, and detect the buffering effect when the buffer valve is fully closed, its applicable range may be wider. However, the piston is not visible, and it is impossible to determine the buffering effect by "observing the movement of the piston".

4) The test method for "durability" given in CB/T 38112-2013 is different from the other three standards. It is to continuously operate the test for a cumulative reciprocating motion of 5000 times under nominal pressure, requiring normal operation, no replacement of parts (including seals), and checking external and internal leakage; and it gives the continuous operation time based on the working temperature of the hydraulic oil entering the hydraulic cylinder being 50°C ± 2°C. The test shall be stopped when the oil temperature is lower or higher than this temperature, and the test shall be continued after the temperature returns to normal until the 5000 times are completed, but the continuous operation time for each time shall not be less than 6 hours.

It is not a problem to check the "durability" of the hydraulic cylinder by cumulative reciprocating motion times of continuous operation, but if there is no specified speed for the reciprocating motion of the hydraulic cylinder, disputes may arise in the inspection results. In addition, there are also some problems in the expression of continuous operation time in this standard.

5) In the "disassembly inspection" given in CB/T 38112-2013, there is a provision for "checking the appearance... and the outer diameter of the guide plug...", but the "guide plug" is not defined in GB/T 17446-2012.

Other items such as operation and operation, load, oil pressure, and horizontal safety position are also involved.

Comparing only the cleanliness indexes of double-acting hydraulic cylinders with a 1 m stroke in the two tables, the index of the mass of contaminated particles in the hydraulic cylinder cavity given in CB/T 3812-2013 far exceeds the cleanliness index given in JB/T 10205-2010, with the highest exceeding more than four times.

GB/T13342-2007 is included in the normative references of CB/T 3812-2013, and JB/T 7858-2006 is included in the normative references of GB/T13342-2007, but CB/T 3812-2013 does not give the cleanliness index according to JB/T 7858-2006.

2) Cleanliness Test Method. The detection procedure and single filter membrane mass analysis procedure given in JB/T7858-2006 are as follows:

① Measure and record the magnetism of the tested component, and demagnetize to 12 Gs (Gauss, 1 Gs=10^-4T) or below if necessary.

② Clean the outer surface of the tested component.

③ Determine the wet volume of the inner cavity of the tested component.

④ Disassemble the tested component (components with process plugs and interference fits are not disassembled).

⑤ Remove the sealing elements on the mating surfaces (except for the piston sealing elements of hydraulic cylinders), and wipe the parts of the sealing surfaces that do not contact the working medium with white silk cloth.

⑥ Put all the internal parts after disassembling the component into a clean container.

⑦ Spray wash the parts that contact the working medium with clean washing liquid. For the parts that partially contact the working medium, only wash the parts that contact the working medium. For the parts that do not contact the working medium (such as the flange of the pump), only wipe the parts that contact the working medium with clean cloth.
762:
Parts, valve handles, cylinder ear rings, etc.) are not cleaned. The amount of clean cleaning solution used is 2-5 times the wet volume of the inner cavity of the component being tested.

⑧ Collect the cleaning solution from step ⑦ into a container that meets the cleanliness requirements and mark the container number (e.g., sample No. 1).

⑨ Repeat steps ⑥-⑧, with the container numbers being sample No. 2 and sample No. 3 in sequence.

⑩ Perform mass analysis on samples No. 1, No. 2, and No. 3 according to the single filter membrane or double filter membrane mass analysis procedure.

Note: Single filter membrane and double filter membrane mass analysis methods are two selectable mass analysis methods. When it is certain that the filter membrane can be sufficiently rinsed, the single filter membrane analysis method can be selected.

⑾ Single filter membrane mass analysis procedure:

a) Take an appropriate amount of spare filter membrane (0.8μm) and place it in a Petri dish, cover it halfway, and put it into a drying oven. Keep it at a constant temperature of 80℃ (or the temperature specified for the filter membrane) for 30 min. After taking it out, cover it and cool for 30 min. During this process, the filter membrane should remain flat and undeformed.

b) Take out one filter membrane that has been dried from the Petri dish and weigh its initial mass GA.

c) Fix the filter membrane on the filtration device. After fully stirring the sample to be tested, pour it into the filtration device. Then use 50 mL of clean cleaning solution to rinse the sample container and pour it into the filtration device. Cover the funnel lid and perform vacuum filtration. When there is about 2 mL of residual liquid left in the filtration, remove the funnel lid and rinse the side wall of the funnel with clean cleaning solution, then cover the funnel lid and continue vacuum filtration until the cleaning solution on the filter membrane is completely filtered.

d) Use a syringe to draw clean cleaning solution and inject it along the wall of the funnel for rinsing until there is no cleaning solution on the filter membrane.

e) Stop vacuum filtration. Carefully remove the filter membrane and place it in a Petri dish. Place the Petri dish with the lid half-open into a drying oven and keep it at a constant temperature of 80℃ (or the temperature specified for the filter membrane) for 30 min. Take it out, cover it, and cool for 30 min, then weigh the mass GB.

f) The mass of contaminants in the sample being tested is Gn=GB-GA.

Comparing the testing procedures and single filter membrane mass analysis procedures given in JB/T7858-2006 with the cleanliness test methods given in CB/T3812-2013, the problems are obvious at a glance. Tests that are not conducted according to the procedures or methods specified in the standard are invalid.

(2) Environmental Adaptability

1) Environmental adaptability indicators. The environmental adaptability requirements in CB/T3812-2013 are: the environmental temperature, etc. should comply with the relevant provisions of GB/T13342. In GB/T13342-2007, the temperature requirements are specified as: 5.4.1 When the ambient temperature is -25-65℃, the hydraulic cylinder should be able to work normally. 5.4.2 When the working medium temperature is -15℃, the hydraulic cylinder should have no jamming phenomenon. 5.4.3 When the working medium temperature is 70℃, there should be no leakage at the mating surfaces of the hydraulic cylinder.

In CB114612-1996 "Environmental Test and Engineering Guide for Ship Equipment - Low Temperature", the severity level (test temperature) of low-temperature operation test is specified; in CB114613-1996 "Environmental Test and Engineering Guide for Ship Equipment - High Temperature", the severity level (test temperature) of high-temperature operation test is specified. Among them, the requirement in CB/T3812-2013 that "when the ambient temperature is 65℃±5℃, the temperature of the test hydraulic oil should be maintained at 70℃±2℃" does not comply with the provisions of CB114613-1996, and it is also very difficult to achieve in actual operation.

2) Environmental adaptability test method. Taking the high-temperature operation test - intermediate inspection (excerpt) specified in CB114613-1996 as an example: "5.2.4.3 For communication navigation equipment, navigation equipment, and radar equipment installed on the open deck of ships, when the temperature rises to 70℃±2℃ and is maintained for 10 h, the various temperature control devices equipped by the test specimen itself can be turned on, and within 30 min, the temperature of the test box (chamber) should be reduced to 55℃±2℃ at the specified rate [not greater than 1℃/min (average value within 5 min)], then start the test specimen to work continuously for 2 h, and perform relevant performance tests under the environmental conditions of 55℃±2℃, and the performance should be within the specified range." Compared with the environmental adaptability test method specified in CB/T3812-2013, there are significant differences.

a) The ambient temperature and the working medium temperature are the same, both are 70℃±2℃.

b) The test specimen (hydraulic cylinder) does not work under the environmental conditions of 70℃±2℃.

c) The operation test - intermediate inspection is conducted under the environmental conditions of 55℃±2℃.

d) The continuous working (continuous reciprocating operation) time is 2 h.

In summary, the author believes that when formulating standards, it is necessary to consider the requirements related to health and safety, such as whether it is appropriate to conduct environmental adaptability inspection when the ambient temperature is 65℃±5℃. Environmental testing should follow the standards, otherwise the test results may not be valid.

5.3 Test Methods for Large Hydraulic Cylinders

1. Comparison of Test Methods for Large Hydraulic Cylinders

The test methods for large hydraulic cylinders specified in JB/T11588-2013 "Large Hydraulic Cylinders" differ from the test methods for hydraulic cylinders specified in GB/T15622-2005 "Test Methods for Hydraulic Cylinders" and JB/T10205-2010 "Hydraulic Cylinders" in many aspects, mainly including:

1) JB/T11588-2013 does not provide a test device.

2) JB/T11588-2013 states: "The ambient temperature for the test is room temperature." The other two standards do not directly state this.

3) JB/T11588-2013 lacks a title like "Test Hydraulic Oil", so the description (requirements) about the test hydraulic oil below may be misunderstood. The other two standards all provide the description about hydraulic oil under the title "Test Hydraulic Oil".

4) In JB/T 11588-2013, the statement "Cleanliness: The internal cleanliness should not be higher than 19/15 or 19/15 specified in GB/T 14039-2002" (requirement) contains errors. See section 6.1.2, item 15 for the citation and application of GB/T 14039-2002 standard.

5) JB/T 11588-2013 specifies the accuracy of the test pressure gauge: 0.5 grade for type testing; 1.0 grade for factory testing; range is 140%-200% of the maximum test pressure. Unlike the other two standards, it does not specify the allowable error of the measurement system and the allowable variation range of the average display value of the controlled parameter.

6) JB/T 11588-2013 divides the test into static pressure test (method) and dynamic load test for hydraulic cylinders, while the other two standards do not make such test classification.

7) The issue of mixed use of "trial operation" and "trial run" exists in all three standards, but in JB/T 11588-2013, it states "Before the test, preparation operation should be performed first. Start under no-load condition, and reciprocate the full stroke several times to completely eliminate air in the hydraulic cylinder, and the operation should be normal." Such statement (requirement) at least has problems of inconsistent use of terms (trial operation and trial run), non-standard use of terms (such as state, load), and putting forward performance requirements (such as operation should be normal) under the title of test method.

8) In JB/T 11588-2013, "Minimum starting pressure: Without load, the hydraulic pressure is gradually increased from zero until the piston rod moves smoothly, measure the minimum starting pressure at three points near the two ends and the middle of the piston in the cylinder, and take the maximum value." Such statement is different from the other two standards in several aspects, such as gradually increasing the hydraulic pressure from zero until..., when the piston rod moves smoothly..., measure the minimum starting pressure at three points of the piston..., take the maximum value. "When the piston rod moves smoothly, measure the minimum starting pressure at three points of the piston" does not conform to the definition of "minimum starting pressure" in the other two standards, nor does it conform to the definition of "starting pressure" in GB/T 17446-2012; "Hydraulic pressure" is generally not an abbreviation of liquid pressure, and cannot be used interchangeably with "pressure".

9) The internal leakage and external leakage in JB/T 11588-2013 are also different from the other two standards, such as explicitly mentioning "holding pressure for 30 min", and conducting internal leakage test and external leakage test separately.

10) JB/T 11588-2013 provides a cleanliness test method for hydraulic cylinders, which is to pressurize one cavity and drain oil from the other cavity, and use an oil contamination detector to detect the oil discharged from the hydraulic cylinder. The other two standards do not provide this.

11) JB/T 11588-2013 requires "Dynamic load test of hydraulic cylinder should be conducted at the user's site" and requires "Observe whether the action is smooth and flexible." This still has the problem of inconsistent use of terms (such as action).

12) In "Stroke test" of JB/T 11588-2013, since there is no requirement for "stroke" in this standard, it cannot perform the so-called "stroke test"; and in "Stop the piston of the tested hydraulic cylinder at the extreme positions at both ends of the stroke,...". "Extreme positions at both ends of the stroke" appears again, which is inconsistent with the previous multiple expressions of "both ends of the stroke".

13) Compared with the other two standards, JB/T 11588-2013 does not have regulations and requirements for "steady-state operating conditions", requirements and test methods for "durability", requirements and test methods for "load efficiency", requirements and test methods for "high-temperature performance", etc.

14) JB/T 11588-2013 does not have regulations and requirements for "environmental test".

2. Application of Test Methods for Large Hydraulic Cylinders

(1) Standard Citation

JB/T 11588-2013 does not normatively cite the two standards GB/T 15622-2005 "Test Methods for Hydraulic Cylinders" and JB/T 10205-2010 "Hydraulic Cylinders", but through the above comparison, it is found that the content of "test methods" in JB/T 11588-2013 is basically similar or identical to the other two standards.

Without normatively citing the above two standards, the following problems cannot be solved:

1) GB/T 15622-2005 was published and implemented earlier, and a large amount of content from GB/T 15622-2005 is cited in JB/T 11588-2013, but GB/T 15622-2005 is not listed as a normative reference document, so that people who have not participated in the drafting of the standard may have many objections to this standard, or cannot use more authoritative normative reference documents to clarify these objections.

2) At least the schematic diagram of the hydraulic system for factory test is no longer available for reference.

If a "test method" does not have a test device and a schematic diagram of the test device, it is indeed difficult to clearly describe or provide the test method, and it is very prone to problems.

3) Standards can be revised and trimmed, but they must develop towards a more standard and more applicable direction, not the opposite.

(2) Pressure Resistance

The "pressure resistance" test specified in JB/T 11588-2013 is: Stop the piston of the tested hydraulic cylinder at both ends of the stroke respectively, and apply 1.5 times the nominal working pressure to the working chamber respectively, hold pressure for 2 min for type test, and hold pressure for 10 s for factory test. The biggest difference between the "pressure resistance test" in this standard and the "pressure resistance test" in the above two standards is "nominal working pressure".

The "nominal working pressure" is used multiple times in this standard, such as in internal leakage and external leakage tests, and is different from "nominal pressure", because this standard also uses "nominal pressure" in the cushioning test.

It is not important whether "nominal working pressure" is first used in this standard, but what pressure it is has not been clearly defined. Because in GB/T 17446-2012, there are only "nominal pressure" and "maximum working pressure".
764:
The terms "nominal working pressure" and "maximum pressure" are defined, which may lead to a series of problems:

1) The standard lacks normative references for terms and vocabulary, and does not specify the terms and definitions used in the standard. It is impossible to determine this "nominal working pressure," and consequently, it is also impossible to perform a "pressure test."

2) If "nominal working pressure" and "nominal pressure" are treated as synonyms, then due to the special structure of large hydraulic cylinders, performing a pressure test at the extreme position of the cylinder stroke may pose a risk of damaging the hydraulic cylinder.

3) If "nominal working pressure" and "maximum working pressure" are treated as synonyms, then performing a pressure test at the extreme position of the cylinder stroke may pose a slightly lower risk of damaging the hydraulic cylinder.

(3) Operating State
The operating state of the hydraulic cylinder is one of the technical requirements for the hydraulic cylinder, as mentioned in Section 2.1.8 on the technical requirements for the operation of hydraulic cylinders.

There are multiple descriptions of operation in JB/T 11588-2013, such as "operation should be normal," "smooth movement," "whether there is vibration or crawling," "whether the movement is smooth and flexible," etc.

The current problem is how to determine whether "the piston rod moves smoothly" during the minimum starting pressure test. Generally, a lower starting pressure is better, especially for hydraulic cylinders with dynamic characteristics. The following issues may exist with this standard's provisions:

1) Under the same test conditions, different testers and both parties may obtain inconsistent test results, and it is easy to raise objections to the test results.

2) For large hydraulic cylinders, the attitude of the hydraulic cylinder during the test will have a significant impact on the starting pressure. If the attitude of the hydraulic cylinder during the test is not specified, it may lead to greater controversy.

3) For large hydraulic cylinders, the minimum starting pressure may be related not only to the type of seal used in the hydraulic cylinder but also to the cylinder bore and piston rod diameter.

Additionally, it is unclear where the definitions of "M type as standard seal" and "T type as low-friction seal" originate.

2) Safety requirements. The test device should fully consider the safety of personnel and equipment during the test process, should comply with the relevant requirements of GB/T37666, and have reliable measures to prevent personal injury accidents such as electric shock, mechanical injury, or high-pressure oil injection in case of failure.

3) Test proportional/servo valve. The response frequency of the test proportional/servo valve should be more than 3 times the highest test frequency of the hydraulic cylinder under test. The rated flow of the test proportional/servo valve should meet the maximum movement speed of the hydraulic cylinder under test.

4) Hydraulic source. The hydraulic source of the test device should meet the pressure requirements for testing, ensure stable oil supply pressure for the proportional/servo valve, and meet the instantaneous flow requirements for dynamic testing; it should have temperature adjustment, control, and display functions; it should meet the cleanliness level requirements for hydraulic oil, see 2.(3).

5) Pipeline and pressure measurement point location.
① In the test device, the pipeline between the test proportional/servo valve and the hydraulic cylinder under test should be as short as possible, and hard pipes should be used as much as possible; the pipe diameter should be as small as possible under the premise of meeting the maximum instantaneous flow.

② The pressure measurement points should comply with the provisions of 7.2 in GB/T28782.2-2012.

6) Instruments.
① The automatic recording analyzer should be able to measure the amplitude ratio and phase shift between sinusoidal input signals.

② The signal generator with adjustable amplitude and frequency should be able to output sinusoidal signals, and can perform sweep frequency between 0.1 Hz and the highest frequency required by the test; it should also be able to output forward step and reverse step signals.

③ The test device should have the function of real-time sampling of parameters such as speed, displacement, and output force of the hydraulic cylinder under test, and the sampling speed should meet the needs of test control and data analysis.

For single-rod cylinders, it is better to take the starting pressure of the rodless chamber as the standard, and it is advisable to conduct the inspection after 20 trial operations.
(4) Regarding the test of dynamic friction force under load, since the load condition will affect the test results, this test may have great problems.

5.4.2 DB44/T11692013 "Servo Hydraulic Cylinder
Part 2: Test Method"
In DB44/T11692013 (already obsolete, for reference only)
Servo hydraulic cylinders are defined as: hydraulic cylinders with requirements for static and dynamic indicators. Through cooperation with built-in or external sensors, servo valves or proportional valves, controllers, etc., it can form a hydraulic control system with high control accuracy and fast response speed. Static indicators include trial operation, pressure resistance, internal leakage, external leakage, minimum starting pressure, load friction force, deflection, leakage under low pressure, stroke detection, load efficiency, high temperature test, durability, etc. Dynamic indicators include step response, frequency response, etc.

5.6.1 High Temperature Test
Although GJB150.3A-2009 "Environmental Test Methods for Military Equipment - Part 3: High Temperature Test" stipulates that this standard is applicable to high temperature testing of military equipment, it has reference value for high temperature testing of hydraulic cylinders in other fields.
1. Purpose and Application
(1) Purpose
The purpose of this test is to obtain relevant data to evaluate the impact of high temperature conditions on the safety, integrity, and performance of equipment.
(2) Application
This test is applicable to evaluating equipment used in high temperature environments.
(3) Limitations
This test is only applicable to evaluating thermal effects with shorter evaluation times (months rather than years) and uniform heat distribution throughout the test piece, and is generally not suitable for:
a) Evaluating the effect of performance degradation over time during long-term stable exposure to high temperature conditions (storage or operation) (because this may include some superimposed effects). Such high temperature degradation effects should be evaluated through natural environment.
b) Evaluating thermal effects caused by solar radiation, as solar radiation will produce significant temperature gradients in equipment. The direct effect of solar radiation should be evaluated using procedure I of GJB150.7A-2009.
c) Evaluating photochemical effects (photochemical effects should be evaluated using procedure II of GJB150.7A-2009).
d) Evaluating aerodynamic heating effects.
2. Tailoring Guide
(1) Selection of Test Method
1) Overview. Analyze the requirements of relevant technical documents, apply the results obtained from implementing GJB4239-2000 "General Requirements for Equipment Environmental Engineering" during the equipment (product) ordering process, determine the equipment life (week) 267 Hydraulic Cylinder Manual

PHASE OCCURRING DURING PERIOD OF HIGH TEMPERATURES. DETERMINE WHETHER TO PERFORM THIS TEST ACCORDING TO THE FOLLOWING ENVIRONMENTAL EFFECTS. WHEN IT IS DETERMINED THAT THIS TEST NEEDS TO BE PERFORMED, AND THIS TEST USES THE SAME SPECIMEN AS OTHER ENVIRONMENTAL TESTS, IT IS ALSO NECESSARY TO DETERMINE THE ORDER OF THIS TEST AND OTHER TESTS.

(2) ENVIRONMENTAL EFFECTS. HIGH TEMPERATURES WILL CHANGE THE PHYSICAL PROPERTIES OR DIMENSIONS OF THE MATERIALS USED IN THE EQUIPMENT, WHICH WILL TEMPORARILY OR PERMANENTLY REDUCE THE PERFORMANCE OF THE EQUIPMENT. THE FOLLOWING ARE TYPICAL PROBLEMS THAT MAY OCCUR UNDER HIGH TEMPERATURE CONDITIONS RELATED TO THE EQUIPMENT UNDER TEST:

a) DIFFERENT MATERIALS EXPAND INCONSISTENTLY, CAUSING PARTS TO BITE OR STICK.

b) THE VISCOSITY OF LUBRICANTS DECREASES AND LUBRICANTS FLOW OUT, REDUCING THE LUBRICATION CAPACITY OF CONNECTIONS.

c) THE DIMENSIONS OF MATERIALS CHANGE UNIFORMLY OR DIRECTIONALLY.

d) INCLUDING MATERIALS, LINING, GASKETS, BEARINGS AND SHAFTS, DEFORMATION, BINDING AND FAILURE OCCUR, CAUSING MECHANICAL FAILURE OR INTEGRITY DAMAGE.

e) LINING PERMANENTLY DEFORMS.

f) HOUSINGS AND SEALING STRIPS ARE DAMAGED.

g) THE RESISTANCE VALUE OF FIXED RESISTORS CHANGES.

h) THE STABILITY OF ELECTRONIC CIRCUITS CHANGES DUE TO DIFFERENT TEMPERATURE GRADIENTS AND INCONSISTENT EXPANSION OF DIFFERENT MATERIALS.

i) TRANSFORMERS AND ELECTROMECHANICAL COMPONENTS OVERHEAT.

j) THE PICKUP/RELEASE RANGE OF RELAYS AND MAGNETICALLY OR THERMALLY OPERATED DEVICES CHANGES.

k) SERVICE LIFE IS SHORTENED.

l) SOLID PILLS OR CHARGE SEPARATE.

m) HIGH PRESSURE IS GENERATED INSIDE SEALED CASINGS (SHELLS, EXPLOSIVES, ETC.).

n) EXPLOSIVES OR PROPELLANTS BURN FASTER.

o) CAST EXPLOSIVES EXPAND IN THEIR CASINGS.

p) EXPLOSIVES MELT AND SEEP OUT.

q) ORGANIC MATERIALS FADE, DECOMPOSE OR CRACK.

r) COMPOSITE MATERIALS OUTGAS.

ANOTHER EXPRESSION FOR PARTS BINDING OR BEARINGS AND SHAFTS BINDING MAY BE "BINDING OF SHAFT", PLEASE REFER TO STANDARDS SUCH AS JB/T11772-2014 AND JB/T13101-2017.

(3) SELECTING THE TEST SEQUENCE.

① GENERAL REQUIREMENTS. SEE 3.6 IN GJB150.1A-2009 "TEST METHODS FOR ENVIRONMENTAL ENGINEERING LABORATORY TESTING PART 1: GENERAL REQUIREMENTS".

② SPECIAL REQUIREMENTS. THERE ARE AT LEAST TWO PRINCIPLES THAT CAN BE FOLLOWED IN DETERMINING THE TEST SEQUENCE:

a) LIFE SAVING. FIRST APPLY THE ENVIRONMENTAL STRESS THAT CAUSES THE LEAST DAMAGE TO THE SPECIMEN, SO THAT THE SPECIMEN CAN PERFORM MORE TEST ITEMS. FOR THIS PURPOSE, THIS TEST SHOULD BE PERFORMED EARLY IN THE TEST SEQUENCE.

b) THE APPLIED ENVIRONMENT SHOULD BE ABLE TO MAXIMIZE THE DISPLAY OF SUPERIMPOSED EFFECTS. FOR THIS PURPOSE, THIS TEST SHOULD BE PERFORMED AFTER MECHANICAL ENVIRONMENT TESTS SUCH AS VIBRATION AND SHOCK.

NOTE: THIS TEST WILL ALSO HAVE A SIGNIFICANT IMPACT ON THE RESULTS OF LOW PRESSURE TESTS OF SEALED PRODUCTS [SEE 2.(1)2)d)～f)].

(2) SELECTING THE TEST PROCEDURE.

1) OVERVIEW. THIS TEST INCLUDES TWO TEST PROCEDURES: PROCEDURE I - STORAGE AND PROCEDURE II - OPERATION. THE TEST PROCEDURE TO BE USED SHOULD BE DETERMINED BEFORE THE TEST.

2) FACTORS TO CONSIDER WHEN SELECTING THE TEST PROCEDURE. WHEN SELECTING THE TEST PROCEDURE, THE FOLLOWING SHOULD BE CONSIDERED:

a) THE PURPOSE OF THE EQUIPMENT.

b) NATURAL EXPOSURE ENVIRONMENT.

c) TEST DATA CONSISTENT WITH THE ACTUAL USE OF THE EQUIPMENT.

d) THE ORDER OF PROCEDURES. IF BOTH OF THE ABOVE PROCEDURES ARE SELECTED, PROCEDURE I IS PERFORMED FIRST, FOLLOWED BY PROCEDURE II.

e) OTHER MAJOR HEAT SOURCES THAT AFFECT THE EQUIPMENT, SUCH AS ELECTRIC MOTORS, ENGINES, POWER SUPPLIES OR EXHAUST GASES.

3) DIFFERENCES BETWEEN PROCEDURES.

① OVERVIEW. THE DIFFERENCE BETWEEN THE TWO PROCEDURES IS THE TIME OF PERFORMANCE TESTING, WHICH IS PERFORMED AFTER HIGH TEMPERATURE EXPOSURE IN PROCEDURE I AND DURING HIGH TEMPERATURE EXPOSURE IN PROCEDURE II. PROCEDURE I IS APPLICABLE TO EVALUATE THE EFFECT OF HIGH TEMPERATURE STORAGE ON EQUIPMENT PERFORMANCE, AND PROCEDURE II IS APPLICABLE TO EVALUATE THE EFFECT OF HIGH TEMPERATURE ON EQUIPMENT DURING OPERATION.

② PROCEDURE I - STORAGE. PROCEDURE I IS USED TO EXAMINE THE EFFECT OF HIGH TEMPERATURE DURING STORAGE ON THE SAFETY, INTEGRITY AND PERFORMANCE OF THE EQUIPMENT. IN THIS PROCEDURE, THE SPECIMEN IS FIRST EXPOSED TO HIGH TEMPERATURES (AND LOW HUMIDITY IF APPLICABLE) THAT MAY BE ENCOUNTERED DURING EQUIPMENT STORAGE, AND THEN PERFORMANCE IS TESTED UNDER STANDARD ATMOSPHERIC CONDITIONS.

③ PROCEDURE II - OPERATION. PROCEDURE II IS USED TO EXAMINE THE EFFECT OF HIGH TEMPERATURE ON PERFORMANCE WHEN THE EQUIPMENT IS OPERATING. THERE ARE TWO IMPLEMENTATION METHODS:

a) EXPOSE THE SPECIMEN TO THE CONDITIONS OF THE TEST CHAMBER TEMPERATURE CYCLE, SO THAT THE SPECIMEN WORKS CONTINUOUSLY, OR WORKS DURING THE MAXIMUM TEMPERATURE RESPONSE (WHEN THE SPECIMEN REACHES THE HIGHEST TEMPERATURE).

b) EXPOSE THE SPECIMEN TO A CONSTANT TEMPERATURE, SO THAT THE SPECIMEN WORKS WHEN ITS TEMPERATURE REACHES STABILITY.

③ Special conditions. High temperature tests usually only consider the average temperature of the air surrounding the equipment. When the following conditions exist, these conditions should be included or simulated in the high temperature test setup as much as possible:
a) Enhanced solar radiation. When equipment is located below glass or transparent material panels, or in enclosed, unventilated compartments below thin metal skins, direct solar irradiation may temporarily raise local air temperatures. Due to increased risk of damage, caution should be exercised when applying extreme temperature values. In this case, tests should be based on field measurement data (in this case, solar radiation tests can be conducted separately or both tests can be performed).
b) Artificial heat sources. Artificial heating devices (motors, engines, power supplies, high-density electronic packaging, etc.) can significantly increase the local air temperature around equipment through radiation, convection, or impact of exhaust airflow.
4) Test duration.
① Overview. Determine the exposure duration that equipment must undergo under the specified various exposure conditions. Exposure can be constant or cyclic. In cyclic cases, the number of occurrences of exposure must also be determined.
② Constant temperature exposure. After the test specimen is exposed to a high temperature environment until temperature stabilization is achieved, maintain the test temperature for at least 2 hours.
③ Cyclic exposure. The test duration for cyclic exposure should be determined based on the required number of cycles to meet design requirements and the following guidelines. Both Procedure I and Procedure II expose the test specimen to cyclic temperatures, so the number of cycles is very critical. Unless otherwise specified, each cycle period is 24 hours.
a) Procedure I - Storage. Storage tests should be conducted for at least 7 cycles, corresponding to the number of hours during the most severe month of a normal year in the most severe region when extreme temperatures occur at a rate of 1%. In each cycle, the highest temperature occurs for approximately 1 hour. If storage time for critical materials or high-temperature sensitive materials needs to be extended, the number of cycles should be increased to ensure design requirements are met.
b) Procedure II - Operation. Operational exposure tests should be conducted for at least 3 cycles. This is usually sufficient for the test specimen to reach its highest response temperature. When temperature response is difficult to reproduce, it is recommended to use up to 7 cycles.
5) Technical state of the test specimen. The technical state of the test specimen should be determined based on the expected actual state of the equipment during storage and operation, and should at least consider the following technical states:
a) Enclosed in a transport/storage container or transfer box.

c) Normal operating state.
d) State after modification for special purposes.
e) Technical state of stacked or pallet-stacked configuration.

When the test specimen must operate, prepare the test operation procedure according to the following requirements:
1) General requirements are given in GJB150.1A-2009, 3.9.2.
2) Special requirements are as follows:
a) Include the operating state with maximum power (generating the most heat).
b) When voltage changes affect the thermal consumption or temperature response of the test specimen (such as power generation and fan speed), include the required range of input voltage condition variations.
c) Introduce cooling media (such as forced cooling air or coolant) that are typically used during operation. When using cooling media, consider the temperature and flow rate at the inlet of the cooling media to reflect typical and worst-case temperature and flow conditions.
d) For constant temperature tests, when the temperature of internal critical operating parts is relatively constant, it is considered that the temperature has stabilized (in reality, due to the periodic nature of the test specimen's operation or the operating characteristics of the test specimen, the operating temperature cannot be constant).
e) For cyclic temperature tests, the temperature of the test specimen is related to the cyclic temperature and the characteristics of the test specimen, so the temperature cannot be stabilized. In this case, the temperature response of the test specimen is also cyclic, i.e., the peak response temperature is within 2°C compared to the peak response temperature of the previous cycle.

4. Test Requirements
(1) Test Equipment
1) The test chamber should be equipped with auxiliary instruments that can maintain and monitor high-temperature air conditions around the test piece (and humidity when applicable).
2) Except when the platform environment has proven it reasonable to use other speeds and to prevent heat transfer in the test piece that would not occur in practice, the wind speed near the test piece should not exceed 1.7 m/s.
3) The temperature measurements in the test chamber should be continuously recorded, and if necessary, the temperature measurements of the test piece should also be continuously recorded.
(2) Test Control
1) Temperature. Except as otherwise specified in the technical documentation, if any action other than the operation of the test piece (such as opening the chamber door) causes a significant change (greater than 2°C) in the test temperature or the chamber temperature, the test piece should be allowed to stabilize again to the specified temperature before continuing the test. If performance checks cannot be completed within 15 minutes, the test piece should be restored to the specified conditions before continuing the inspection.
2) Temperature Change Rate. Except as otherwise specified, the temperature change rate should not exceed 3°C/min to avoid temperature shock.
(3) Test Interruption
1) General Requirements. See GJB150.1A-2009 Section 3.12.
2) Special Requirements.
① Insufficient Test Interruption.
a) Cyclic Test. If a high-temperature cyclic test is interrupted unexpectedly during the test such that the test conditions drop to standard atmospheric conditions and exceed the tolerance, the test should be resumed from the point where the last successful cycle was completed.
b) Constant Test. If a constant test is interrupted unexpectedly during the test such that the test conditions drop to standard atmospheric conditions and exceed the tolerance, the test piece should be stabilized again at the specified test temperature, and the test should continue from the point where the test conditions deviated. The time when the temperature exceeds the tolerance during the interruption is not included in the total test time. The duration of the test segments before and after the interruption should be recorded.
② Excessive Test Interruption (such as chamber malfunction).
a) Physical Inspection and Performance Check. If the interruption of a cyclic or constant test exposes the test piece to an environment more severe than specified in the product standard, a comprehensive physical inspection and performance check should be conducted after the interruption (if possible), and then a decision should be made whether to continue the test based on the inspection and check results.
b) Safety, Performance, and Material Issues. When safety, performance, and material issues are found after an excessive test, the best course of action is to terminate this test and repeat it with new test pieces. If this is not done and the test piece fails during the remaining tests, the test results will be considered invalid due to the excessive test conditions. If no safety, performance, or material issues are found, the following measures should be taken:
● For constant temperature tests, the previous conditions should be restored, and the test should continue from the point where the test tolerance was exceeded, with the time during the test interruption included in the total test time.
● For cyclic temperature tests, the test should be resumed from the point where the last successful cycle was completed, and the incomplete cycle during the excessive test interruption is not included in the total number of cycles.
(4) Installation and Debugging of Test Pieces
1) General Requirements. See GJB150.1A-2009 Section 3.9.
2) Special Requirements. The installation and debugging of test pieces should include all additional heat sources or appropriate simulated heat sources (see 2.(3)3)③).
5. Test Process
(1) Test Preparation
1) Pre-test Preparation. Before the test begins, determine the test procedure, technical status of the test piece, number of cycles, test duration, and the values of the storage/operating environmental parameters of the test piece based on relevant documents.
2) Initial Inspection. All test pieces need to be inspected under standard atmospheric conditions before the test to obtain baseline data. The inspection is conducted in the following steps:
a) Visually inspect the test piece, paying special attention to stress areas (such as corners of castings), and record the inspection results.
b) Install temperature sensors on, in, or around the test piece according to the technical documentation. For Program II, to ensure the measurement of the maximum temperature response of the test piece, the temperature sensors should be installed on the functional components.
c) Place the test piece in the test chamber under standard atmospheric conditions.
d) Perform performance checks according to the technical documentation and record the results. If the test piece operates normally, proceed with Program I or Program II based on the specific situation.
(2) Test Program
1) Program I - Storage.
① Cyclic Storage. The steps for cyclic storage testing are as follows:
a) Place the test piece in the storage technical state.
b) Adjust the environment in the test chamber to the test conditions for the start of the test, and stabilize the temperature of the test piece under these conditions.
c) Expose the test piece to the temperature (and humidity if applicable) conditions of the storage environment for a duration of at least 7 cycles (or a total of 168 hours if using a 24-hour cycle) or the number of cycles specified in the technical documentation. If required by the technical documentation, record the temperature response of the test piece.
d) After the end of the cyclic temperature exposure, adjust the air temperature in the test chamber to standard atmospheric conditions and maintain it under standard atmospheric conditions until the temperature of the test piece stabilizes.
e) Visually inspect and perform performance checks on the test piece, record the results, and compare them with the pre-test data.
② Constant Temperature Storage. The steps for constant temperature storage testing are as follows:
778:
a) Put the test piece into storage technical state.
b) Adjust the environment in the test chamber to the specified test conditions, and keep the test piece at stable temperature under these conditions.
c) After the test piece reaches stable temperature, continue to maintain the test temperature for at least 2 hours to ensure that the temperature of internal components/parts that cannot be measured truly reaches stability. If the temperature of internal components/parts cannot be measured, additional thermal soaking time should be determined based on thermal analysis to ensure the temperature of the entire test piece reaches stability.
d) After the end of constant temperature exposure, adjust the air temperature in the test chamber to standard atmospheric conditions, and maintain these standard atmospheric conditions until the test piece temperature stabilizes.
e) Perform visual inspection and functional performance testing on the test piece, record the results, and compare them with pre-test data.
2) Procedure II - Operation.
① Constant temperature operation. The test steps for constant temperature operation are as follows:
a) Install the test piece according to the operational technical state.
b) Adjust the air temperature in the test chamber to reach the required constant temperature (and humidity if applicable).
c) After the test piece temperature reaches stability, continue to maintain the conditions in the test chamber for at least 2 hours. If the temperature of internal components/parts cannot be measured, additional thermal soaking time should be determined based on thermal analysis to ensure the temperature of the entire test piece reaches stability.
d) Inspect the test piece visually as much as possible, record the inspection results, and compare them with pre-test data.
e) Operate the test piece and allow it to reach stable temperature again. Perform performance testing on the test piece according to the technical document requirements, record the test results, and compare them with pre-test data.
f) Stop the operation of the test piece, adjust the air temperature in the test chamber to standard atmospheric conditions, and maintain these conditions until the test piece temperature stabilizes.
g) Perform comprehensive visual inspection and functional performance testing on the test piece according to the technical document requirements, record the inspection and test results, and compare them with pre-test data.
② Cyclic operation. The test steps for cyclic operation are as follows:
a) Install the test piece according to the operational technical state.
b) Adjust the air temperature (and humidity if applicable) in the test chamber to reach the initial conditions of the operational cycle specified in the technical document, and maintain these conditions until the test piece temperature stabilizes.
c) Expose the test piece for at least 3 cycles or the number of cycles required to ensure the highest response temperature of the test piece is reached. During the cyclic exposure period, perform comprehensive visual inspection of the test piece as much as possible, and record the inspection results.
d) Operate the test piece during the highest temperature response period of the exposure cycle (due to the thermal lag effect of the test piece, the highest temperature response period may not coincide with the highest temperature period of the temperature cycle). Repeat this step until all functional performance testing of the test piece is completed according to the technical document. Record the test results.
e) Stop the operation of the test piece, adjust the air temperature in the test chamber to standard atmospheric conditions, and maintain these conditions until the test piece temperature stabilizes.
f) Perform comprehensive visual inspection and functional performance testing on the test piece according to the technical document requirements, record the inspection and test results, and compare them with pre-test data.

In addition to the guidelines provided in 3.1.7 of GJB150.1A-2009, the following information is also helpful for evaluating test results. Any data that does not meet the product specification requirements can be used for analysis in this test. Consider the following relevant information at the same time:
a) Results of non-destructive inspection after storage testing under extreme temperatures (if applicable).
b) Degradation or changes in operational performance under extreme high temperatures.
c) The necessity of special tooling or specific operating procedures during high temperature exposure.

5.6.2 Low Temperature Test
Although GJB150.4A-2009 "Military Equipment Laboratory Environmental Test Methods Part 4: Low Temperature Test" stipulates that this standard is applicable to low temperature testing of military equipment, it has reference value for low temperature testing of hydraulic cylinders used in other fields.
1. Purpose and Application
(1) Purpose
The purpose of this test is to evaluate the impact of low temperature conditions on the safety, integrity, and performance of equipment during storage, operation, and disassembly.
(2) Application
This test is applicable to evaluating equipment used in low temperature environments.
(3) Limitations
This test is not applicable to equipment installed and operated on non-pressurized aircraft, which is usually tested according to the provisions of GJB150.24A-2009.
2. Tailoring Guide
(1) Selection of Test Method
1) Overview. Analyze the requirements of the relevant technical document, apply the results obtained from implementing GJB4239-2001 "General Requirements for Equipment Environmental Engineering" during the equipment (product) ordering process, determine the stages in the equipment life cycle when low temperature environments occur, and determine whether this test is necessary based on the following environmental effects. When it is determined that this test is necessary and the same test piece is used for this test and other environmental tests, also determine the sequence of this test and other tests.
779:
2) Environmental Effects. Low temperatures have an adverse effect on almost all substrate materials. For equipment exposed to low-temperature environments, since low temperatures will alter the physical properties of the constituent materials, they may cause temporary or permanent damage to their operational performance. Therefore, as long as the equipment is exposed to temperatures below standard atmospheric conditions, consideration should be given to conducting low-temperature testing. Considering the following typical low-temperature environmental effects helps determine whether this test is applicable to the equipment under test:

a) Hardening and embrittlement of materials.
b) Differential shrinkage of different materials in response to temperature transients, and different expansion rates of different components, causing components to seize.
c) Reduced lubrication and fluidity of lubricants due to increased viscosity.
d) Performance changes in electronic components (resistors, capacitors).
e) Performance changes in transformers and electromechanical components.
f) Increased rigidity of vibration isolators.
g) Cracking of solid explosive charges or columns (such as ammonium nitrate).
h) Rupture and crazing, brittle fracture, changes in impact strength, and strength reduction.
i) Static fatigue in constrained glass.
j) Condensation and freezing of water.
k) Reduced flexibility, hearing, and vision of personnel wearing protective clothing.
l) Changes in burning rate.

3) Selection of test sequence.

① General requirements. See GJB150.1A-2009 "Military Equipment Laboratory Environmental Test Methods Part 1: General Requirements" 3.6.

② Special requirements. The selection of test sequence should at least follow the following two principles:

a) Life saving. First apply environmental stresses that cause the least damage to the test item, so that the test item can undergo more test items. To this end, this test should be conducted early in the test sequence.

b) The applied environment should maximize the display of superposition effects. To this end, this test should be conducted after mechanical environment tests such as vibration and shock.

Although not explicitly specified, this test can be combined with vibration and shock tests to evaluate the effect of mechanical events (i.e., transportation, loading/unloading, impact) on materials at low temperatures. At the same time, this test will also significantly alter the sealing performance of the product during the low-pressure test in GJB150.2A-2009.

(2) Selection of test procedures

1) Overview. This test includes three test procedures: Procedure I - Storage, Procedure II - Operation, and Procedure III - Assembly/Disassembly Operations. Determine the applicable test procedure, combination of test procedures, or the order of implementation of each procedure based on the demand for test data. In most cases, all three procedures should be used.

2) Factors to consider when selecting test procedures. When selecting test procedures, the following should be considered:

a) Purpose of the equipment. According to the requirements of relevant documents, determine the functions that the equipment should achieve under low-temperature environments and any other restrictive conditions (such as storage).

b) Natural exposure environment.

c) The following test data that matches the actual use of the equipment:
   ● Expected temperature in the deployment area.
   ● Expected duration in the deployment area.
   ● Technical status of the equipment.

d) Sequence of procedures. When determining the sequence of the three low-temperature tests, the following should be considered:
   ● Procedure II can be performed after Procedure I/Procedure III. If the equipment needs to be stored at low temperatures before use, Procedure I should be performed before Procedure II; if assembly/disassembly operation testing is required, Procedure III can be performed before the operational test; if the equipment is not intended to be stored at low temperatures or disassembled/ reassembled before use, proceed directly to Procedure II.
   ● If necessary, assembly/disassembly operation testing can be performed after storage testing/operational testing.

3) Differences between procedures. Although all procedures involve low temperatures, they differ fundamentally in the timing of performance testing and performance aspects.
   a) Procedure I is used to check the safety of the equipment during storage and after storage under low-temperature conditions, as well as the impact on the equipment's performance after storage.
   b) Procedure II is used to check the operational status of the equipment under low-temperature environments. The "operation" in this section refers to the startup and operation of the equipment with minimal personnel contact.
   c) Procedure III is used to detect whether it is easy for operators to assemble and disassemble the equipment while wearing heavy cold-weather clothing.

(3) Determination of test conditions
1) Overview. After selecting this test and the corresponding procedure, the test conditions and test techniques for that procedure should also be selected according to the provisions of relevant documents and the information provided for that procedure. The determination of test conditions should consider the contents of 2.(3)2) to 2.(3)4).
2) Climatic conditions. It is best to select specific test temperatures according to relevant documents. If there is no such information, the test temperatures should be determined based on the area where the equipment will be used and other factors. Although low-temperature environments usually vary cyclically, in many cases it is acceptable to conduct tests using constant low temperatures. Only in cases where exposure to changing low-temperature environments is considered important in design evaluation should low-temperature cyclic testing be selected. The low-temperature conditions for low-temperature cyclic testing should be determined according to relevant documents. 3) Duration of exposure. The duration of low temperature exposure affects the safety, integrity and performance of equipment, and can be selected based on the material, structural characteristics and usage of the equipment itself:

a) Non-hazardous or non-safety-related (non-life support) equipment. Most of this type of equipment (in a non-operating state) (except for those with organic plastics) will not exhibit performance degradation after reaching temperature stability at low temperatures. If there is no other suitable time, the storage time can be 4 hours after the test piece reaches temperature stability.

b) Equipment containing explosives, ammunition, organic plastics and other products. The performance of such products in this type of equipment may continue to deteriorate after temperature stabilization, so they need to be subjected to long-term low temperature testing. After the test piece reaches temperature stability, at least 72 hours of storage testing should be performed, as this is the typical low temperature exposure duration for such products.

c) Equipment containing products such as limit glass. Glass, ceramics and glass products that need to be installed or restricted to a specific position, or equipment (such as optical systems, laser systems and electronic systems) that need to be installed or restricted to a specific position, often cause damage to the equipment due to static fatigue of such products. Therefore, a longer low temperature test time may be required to induce this phenomenon. If there is no other reference data, an exposure time of 24 hours is recommended.

4) Technical status of the test piece. The technical status of the test piece is an important factor in determining the degree of temperature impact. Therefore, the test should be conducted using the technical status that the equipment is expected to have during storage or use. At least the following technical statuses should be considered:

a) Installed in a transport/storage container or transport box.

b) Protected or unprotected state.

c) Normal use status.

d) Status after modification for specific use.

(3) Limitations

This test cannot reproduce all humidity effects related to natural environments, such as long-term effects; nor can it reproduce humidity effects related to low humidity environments. This test does not reproduce complex temperature and humidity environments, but rather provides a general stress (usage) environment to expose potential problems that may occur in equipment. Therefore, this test does not include natural or induced temperature and humidity cycles. This test does not evaluate the interior of airtight sealed components (such as hydraulic cylinders), nor does it consider the following situations:

a) Condensation inside airborne and ground equipment caused by changes in pressure and temperature.

b) Condensation caused by blackbody radiation (such as night sky effect).

c) Combined effects of biological and chemical pollutants with moisture or condensation.

d) Accumulation of liquid water inside equipment or packaging and retention for a considerable period of time.

② Accelerated chemical reactions.

③ Chemical or electrochemical destruction of organic or inorganic surface coatings.

④ Corrosion layers produced by the interaction of surface moisture and foreign adhesions.

b) Changes in material properties, such as:

① Material expansion due to absorption effects.
