4. Disassembly Methods for Typical Connecting Parts

Typical connecting parts mainly include threaded connecting parts, keyed connections, static connections, pin connections, interference fit connections, non-disassemblable connections, and flexible connections. Methods for disassembling typical connecting parts are given in Appendix of GB/T 32810-2016, with specific details referable to Table 6-2.

Table 6-2 Disassembly Methods for Typical Connecting Parts

Connection Type Disassembly Method

Threaded Connection
Broken Stud Bolt
When the broken stud bolt protrudes above the machine body surface, a hole can be drilled in the bolt, and a multi-sided hardened steel rod can be driven in and then unscrewed; when the broken stud bolt is below the machine body surface, a hole can be drilled in the broken end, a reverse-threaded bolt can be screwed in, and then unscrewed; when the broken stud bolt is thick, it can also be chiseled out along the circumference of the bolt.

Slipping Hex Socket Head Bolt
When the hex socket head bolt becomes rounded and slips, a hex nut with a hole diameter slightly smaller than the outer diameter of the bolt head can be welded onto the hex socket head bolt, and then unscrewed with a wrench.

Rusty Bolt
Soak with kerosene for disassembly, or tighten the bolt further and then loosen it, repeating this process to gradually unscrew it.

Group of Threaded Connections
Disassemble in the order of first the surrounding then the middle, alternating along diagonal directions, while avoiding stress concentration on the final bolts that could damage parts.

Interference Fit Threaded Connection
The part with internal threads can be heated to increase its diameter before unscrewing.

Keyed Connection
Flat Key Connection
If the key is damaged, use a flat chisel to chisel it out. When the key fits too tightly in the slot, a hole can be drilled and threaded in the key, and then a screw can be used to push it out.

Taper Key Connection
Pay attention to the disassembly direction, and use a punch to punch it out from the thinner end of the key. If the taper key has a hook head, use a hook to pull it out.

Static Connection
Use a puller for disassembly, or use local heating or cooling for disassembly.

Pin Connection
Use a punch with a diameter slightly smaller than the pin to punch it out. When the pin is bent, use a drill bit with a diameter slightly smaller than the pin to drill out the pin. Cylindrical locating pins can be pulled out with needle-nose pliers.

Interference Fit Connection
First check for locating pins, screws, and other additional locating or fastening devices, then disassemble from loose to tight according to the tightness of the part fit, using tools or equipment such as cones, rods, pullers, and hydraulic presses in sequence. When the interference is too large, the containing part can be heated or the contained part can be cooled before rapidly pressing it out.

Non-disassemblable Connection
Welded or riveted parts can be destroyed and disassembled by sawing, chiseling, or gas cutting.

Flexible Connection
Flexible hose connections should be disassembled according to the method for threaded connections, while wire connections can be cut with shearing tools. If there is no corrosion between the flexible sleeve and the shaft head, it is advisable to disassemble it as a threaded connection; if corrosion has occurred, hydraulic shears can be used to cut the flexible shaft.

6.4.3 Technical Specifications for Cleaning Re-manufactured Hydraulic Cylinders

Cleaning of re-manufactured hydraulic cylinders and their parts (i.e., re-manufactured blanks) can be classified in different ways, such as according to the re-manufacturing process, which can be divided into pre-disassembly cleaning, post-disassembly cleaning, re-manufacturing processing cleaning, pre-assembly cleaning, pre-coating cleaning, and post-testing cleaning; according to the cleaning object, which can be divided into part cleaning, component cleaning, and assembly cleaning; according to the type of surface contaminants, which can be divided into oil cleaning, carbon deposit cleaning, scale cleaning, coating cleaning, impurity cleaning, rust cleaning, and other contaminant cleaning; according to the cleaning technical principle, which can be divided into physical cleaning, chemical cleaning, and electrochemical cleaning; according to the cleaning technical means, which can be divided into thermal cleaning, ultrasonic cleaning, vibration grinding cleaning, shot blasting cleaning, sandblasting cleaning, dry ice cleaning, high-pressure water jet cleaning, laser cleaning, ultraviolet cleaning, and solution cleaning.

1. General Requirements

1) Based on the characteristics of the cleaning object and its surface contaminants, combined with the requirements of subsequent re-manufacturing processing technology, formulate a reasonable cleaning plan and process guidelines to ensure the economy, environmental protection, and safety of cleaning, and avoid damage to the cleaning object, operators, and external environment.

2) The cleaning of re-manufactured blanks should not affect subsequent re-manufacturing evaluation testing, processing, assembly, and coating, as well as the quality and performance of the re-manufactured hydraulic cylinder and its parts.

2. General Requirements

(1) Cleanliness Requirements

1) For pre-disassembly cleaning, the accumulated dust, oil, sand, and other contaminants on the exterior of the re-manufactured hydraulic cylinder should be basically removed to facilitate subsequent disassembly and avoid bringing contaminants into the factory process interior.

2) For cleaning before re-manufacturing processing, it should meet the subsequent re-manufacturing requirements.
832:
Manufacturing Process Requirements.
3) For cleaning before assembly, it should meet the requirements of subsequent assembly processes.
4) For cleaning before surface coating, it should meet the requirements of surface cleanliness as specified in GB/T8923.1, GB/T8923.2, etc.
(2) Requirements for the Surface State and Structural Organization of Remanufactured Blanks
1) The surface corrosion state and surface roughness of remanufactured blanks should be reasonably controlled according to the type of remanufactured blanks, cleaning methods, and remanufacturing processes. For remanufactured blanks using remanufacturing processes such as thermal spraying, the surface roughness requirements can be relaxed on the condition that subsequent processing requirements are met.
2) The cleaning process should avoid causing changes in the structural organization of the remanufactured blank surface, stress deformation, and surface damage to prevent affecting subsequent remanufacturing processes and assembly.
3) During the cleaning process, necessary protective measures should be taken to prevent damage, destruction, and corrosion to non-cleaning surfaces, and to avoid hard particles and corrosive media entering the internal cavity of the remanufactured blank or mating surfaces that do not require cleaning.
4) After cleaning, measures should be taken to prevent contamination, corrosion, and other damage to cylinder parts during storage or transportation.
(3) Site, Labor Safety, and Environmental Protection Requirements
1) The cleaning site should be equipped with necessary facilities such as ventilation, noise reduction, dust removal, and anti-seepage according to different cleaning process requirements.
2) Necessary labor protection should be provided for cleaning operators to prevent injuries.
3) Environmentally friendly cleaning processes, equipment, materials, and methods should be given priority.
4) Various harmful solid, liquid, and gaseous waste generated from cleaning should be classified and collected, and disposed of according to relevant laws, regulations, and standards of China.

6.4.4 Surface Repair Technology Specifications for Remanufactured Cylinder Parts
The surface repair technology of remanufactured cylinder parts refers to a series of surface engineering technologies involved in the process of repairing the surface of remanufactured cylinder parts (remanufactured blanks) to restore their geometric parameters and performance to those of the original new products, including additive manufacturing technology.
The surface repair technology of remanufactured cylinder parts can be classified in different ways. For example, according to the bonding principle between the repair layer and the blank substrate, it can be divided into metallurgical bonding repair technology, mechanical bonding repair technology, semi-metallurgical / semi-mechanical bonding repair technology, chemical bonding repair technology and physical bonding repair technology; according to the degree of damage to the remanufactured blank, it can be divided into surface damage repair technology and volume damage repair technology; according to the repair technology means, it can be divided into welding repair technology, surface deposition repair technology, surface coating repair technology and adhesive repair technology, etc.
1. Design and Selection Principles
(1) Adaptability Principle
1) The repair layer should have good matching with the remanufactured blank material in physical, chemical and mechanical properties, and the influence of the repair process on the shape, size, performance, etc. of the remanufactured blank should meet the relevant drawings and technical requirements.
2) Based on the original service environment, stress state, working medium and failure mode of the remanufactured blank, the mechanical properties, physicochemical properties, environmental characteristics and organizational structure that the repair layer should have should be comprehensively considered, and appropriate surface repair technology and materials should be selected.
(2) Economic Principle
On the premise of meeting the quality and performance requirements of remanufactured cylinder parts, comprehensive consideration should be given to technical input cost, process flow complexity and remanufacturing economy and other indicators, priority should be given to low-cost and low-pollution repair materials and technologies, automated repair processes should be given priority, and the process flow should be simplified as much as possible.
(3) Environmental Protection Principle
When selecting surface repair technology, consideration should be given to reducing resource consumption, energy consumption and environmental pollution; in repair process design and material selection, conditions should be created for realizing multiple remanufacturing, recycling or extending the service life of cylinder parts.
2. Requirements
(1) Basic Requirements
1) For surface repair of remanufactured cylinder parts, environmentally friendly processes, equipment, materials and methods should be given priority.
2) The remanufactured cylinder parts after repair should not be lower than the original new products in 2 2 8 Hydraulic Cylinder Manual
834:
Dimensional accuracy, technical parameters, quality characteristics and safety performance requirements.
(2) Requirements before repair
1) Surface remanufacturing repair design and demonstration should be carried out according to the service conditions, failure modes and functional requirements of the hydraulic cylinder and its parts, comprehensively considering technical, environmental and economic feasibility, to determine the repair technology plan and process flow, and formulate repair operation guidance documents, determine the type, composition, structure and related physical and chemical properties and mechanical property indexes of the surface repair layer.
2) According to the requirements of surface repair technology on the surface state of materials, the remanufacturing blank should be cleaned, inspected and subjected to corresponding pretreatment and surface protection. Cleaning should comply with the provisions of GB/T3280, and inspection should comply with the provisions of GB/T3120.
(3) Requirements during repair process
1) The remanufactured cylinder parts and their surface repair layer should be inspected after repair, and the content, method, plan and results of inspection should comply with the provisions of relevant technical documents.
2) The remanufactured cylinder parts and their surface repair layer should be subjected to dimensional inspection and accuracy inspection to ensure that the overall and local dimensions and accuracy of the repair parts meet the requirements of process guidance documents.
3) Necessary hardness, bonding strength, residual stress or defect inspection should be carried out according to the quality requirements of the repair layer, giving priority to the use of non-destructive testing technology and conducting inspection according to relevant standards.
4) Necessary factory test should be carried out according to the test requirements of the hydraulic cylinder, such as sealing test, etc.
5) Measures should be taken to prevent the remanufactured cylinder parts from being contaminated, corroded, damaged or deformed during storage or transportation.

In a solution containing metal ions, using the base metal of the remanufactured blank as the cathode, through electrolysis, the cations of the metal to be plated in the plating solution are reduced to metal atoms on the cathode surface and deposited on the base metal surface to form a plating layer, including electroplating technology and brush plating technology.
The repair layer and the substrate are chemically bonded, with a small surface roughness value and no thermal effect on the substrate.
Electroplating technology is suitable for repairing remanufactured blanks with complex structure and shape, while brush plating technology is suitable for repairing remanufactured blanks with regular structure and shape. For remanufactured blanks with a repair layer thickness requirement usually less than 100μm, it is mostly used for surface repair.
6 Vapor Deposition Technology
Under vacuum or atmospheric conditions, using physical methods or relying on vapor phase action and chemical reactions, a thin film repair layer is deposited on the surface of the remanufactured blank. According to the principle, it can be divided into physical vapor deposition technology and chemical vapor deposition technology.
The film and the substrate are chemically or metallurgically bonded, with extremely small surface roughness values and no thermal effect on the substrate.
It is suitable for remanufacturing surface damage repair of precision mating parts and functional devices, with the repair layer usually ranging from tens of nanometers to several micrometers, and can only be used for repairing minor surface damage.
7 Surface Bonding Technology
Mix high molecular polymers with special fillers (such as graphite, molybdenum disulfide, metal powders, ceramic powders and fibers, etc.) into composite adhesives, and apply them to the damaged surface of the remanufactured blank to achieve sealing, leak plugging, electrical conductivity, defect repair, and size restoration.
The bonded repair layer and the substrate are physically bonded, with adjustable repair layer thickness and no thermal effect on the substrate.
It is suitable for repairing cracks, scratches, dimensional out-of-tolerance and casting defects, as well as remanufacturing surface repair of metal components that are more sensitive to temperature.

According to the composition of the corrosive medium, select the corresponding repair technology and material, and consider the following factors: 1) Priority is given to repair layers with single-phase structure; 2) Under the condition of the presence of an electrolyte, the repair layer should have a lower electrode potential than the substrate to effectively play the role of sacrificial anode protection; 3) If the repair layer has pores, necessary sealing treatment should be carried out.

Before repair, non-destructive testing should be carried out on the surface and internal cracks, stress concentration, etc. of the remanufactured blank, and the remaining service life should be evaluated, and on this basis, a suitable surface repair technology should be selected.

According to the service conditions and failure mode of the mechanical product, select a suitable additive remanufacturing technology and material for repair, and at the same time, carry out strength, stiffness and structural safety detection and verification on the remanufactured mechanical product.

Nanocomposite brush plating technology is not only a new technology in surface engineering, but also a key technology for remanufacturing parts, as well as a new method for manufacturing metal-ceramic materials. Nanocomposite brush plating technology is a combination of nanotechnology and traditional technology, which not only retains all the functions of traditional technologies such as electroplating, brush plating, and chemical plating, but also expands their application range, achieving broader, better, and stronger application effects:

(1) Improve the wear resistance of part surfaces
Using brush plating solution with added nano-ceramic particles for nanocomposite brush plating, due to the dispersed distribution of nano-ceramic particles in the matrix metal of the plating layer, a metal-ceramic brush plating layer is formed. The countless nano-ceramic hard points in the matrix metal of the brush plating layer significantly improve the wear resistance of the brush plating layer. This type of brush plating layer can replace processes such as hard chromium plating, carburizing, nitriding, and phase transformation hardening for parts.

(2) Reduce the friction coefficient of part surfaces
Using brush plating solution with added nano-solid particles (such as molybdenum disulfide, graphite, etc.) with friction-reducing effects for nanocomposite brush plating can obtain a nanocomposite friction-reducing layer. This brush plating layer contains countless dispersed solid lubrication points, which can effectively reduce the friction coefficient of friction pairs, playing a role in solid friction reduction, thereby reducing wear on part surfaces and extending the service life of parts.

(3) Improve the high-temperature wear resistance of part surfaces
Using brush plating solution with added nano-ceramic particles for nanocomposite brush plating, the ceramic phase in the formed metal-ceramic plating layer has excellent high-temperature resistance. When the brush plating layer works at higher temperatures, the ceramic phase can maintain excellent high-temperature stability, providing overall support for the brush plating layer and effectively improving the high-temperature wear resistance of the brush plating layer.

(4) Improve the fatigue resistance of part surfaces
The plating layers and coating layers obtained by many surface engineering technologies can quickly restore the dimensional accuracy and geometric accuracy of damaged parts, improving the surface hardness, wear resistance, and corrosion resistance of parts, but they are difficult to withstand alternating loads and have low fatigue resistance. Nanocomposite brush plating layers have higher fatigue resistance because countless nano-solid particles are deposited at defect sites in the nanocomposite brush plating, equivalent to placing countless "limiting piles" on many dislocation lines. These "limiting piles" can effectively prevent lattice slip. Dislocations are an internal stress source in crystals, and the existence of "limiting piles" also changes the stress state of the crystal. Therefore, the fatigue resistance of nanocomposite brush plating layers is significantly higher than that of ordinary brush plating layers.

(5) Improve the performance of non-ferrous metal surfaces
Many parts or part surfaces are manufactured using non-ferrous metals, mainly to utilize the electrical conductivity, thermal conductivity, friction reduction, and corrosion resistance of non-ferrous metals. However, due to their low hardness and poor strength, non-ferrous metals often have short service life and are prone to damage. Preparing nanocomposite brush plating layers can not only maintain the inherent excellent properties of non-ferrous metals but also improve their wear resistance, friction reduction, corrosion resistance, and heat resistance. For example, treating various lead bronze and tin bronze bearing bushes (hydraulic cylinder guide sleeves) with nanocomposite brush plating can effectively improve their performance.

(6) Realize part remanufacturing and enhance their performance
The remanufacturing of hydraulic cylinders is based on used cylinder parts as blanks, with the first step being to restore the dimensional accuracy and geometric accuracy of damaged cylinder parts. Therefore, traditional electroplating and brush plating methods can be used first to quickly restore worn dimensions, and then nanocomposite brush plating technology can be used to brush plate a nanocomposite plating layer on the size plating layer as the working layer to improve the surface performance of parts, making their performance superior to prototype new products.

Using brush plating or brush plating + brush plating nanocomposite plating to repair scratches, grooves, and dents on cylinder parts (such as cylinder barrels and piston rods) is a fast and effective process method.

Since brush plating technology is already a traditional or ordinary technology, and there is abundant relevant literature and information, it will not be introduced here.

When selecting important process parameters for nanocomposite brush plating, attention should be paid to:

1) Brush plating voltage. Since the nanocomposite brush plating solution contains a large amount of nanoparticles, to ensure good deposition of these particles in the brush plating layer, the brush plating voltage is generally slightly higher than that of the substrate metal plating solution. Typically, when the workpiece is small, the workpiece temperature is low, or the relative movement speed between the plating pen and the workpiece is slow, the brush plating voltage should be lower. During the nanocomposite brush plating process, the initial plating voltage should be slightly higher, and after a period of time (e.g., 10-20 s), it should be reduced to the normal brush plating voltage.

2) Brush plating temperature. Throughout the entire nanocomposite brush plating process, the ideal plating temperature for the workpiece is room temperature. This helps maintain the physicochemical properties of the plating solution stable, ensuring that the brush plating effect (deposition rate, uniform plating ability, current efficiency, etc.) remains in the best state, which is beneficial for nanoparticle deposition. The resulting nanocomposite plating layer has low internal stress and high bonding strength.

According to reference literature, during the entire nanocomposite brush plating process, the brush plating temperature should not be lower than 15°C and should not exceed 50°C.

3) During the nanocomposite brush plating process, the relative movement speed between the workpiece and the plating pen is generally 6-10 m/min. If the relative movement speed is too fast, it is not conducive to nanoparticle deposition and can easily cause excessive stress in the nanocomposite plating layer. If the speed is too slow, the local heat generation is high, which can easily cause the surface of the nanocomposite plating layer to turn black, and can also lead to loose structure and rough surface.

1. Micro Pulse Resistance Welding Repair Technology
Micro pulse resistance welding repair technology is represented by "GM-3450 series mold repair machine and its process". This technology is also developed according to the needs of mechanical parts maintenance practice.

The repair process of GM-3450 series mold repair machine is to melt the repair material onto the parent material through the action of electric pulse. Three types of repair materials can be used: powder materials, wire materials and sheet materials. Place the repair material close to the parent material to be repaired, connect the negative pole of the repair machine power supply to the parent material, and connect the positive pole of the repair machine power supply to the welding electrode. Hold the welding electrode and press it against the parent material through the repair material to form a contact resistance R between the repair material and the parent material. At this time, if the pulse current I passes through the positive pole→welding electrode→repair material→contact resistance R→parent material→negative pole, then the Joule heat generated on R is proportional to I2RΔt (where Δt is the duration of the electric pulse). This heat can cause the temperature of a micro area at the interface between the repair material and the parent material to rise rapidly until metal melting occurs. The melting zone is between the repair material and the parent material, and there is a very short metallurgical reaction, after which the electric pulse disappears, and due to rapid heat conduction, a micro-zone welding point is obtained. A large number of such welding points constitute the construction process of GM-3450 series mold repair machine.
Since the time without electric pulse is long enough, this cooling process is very sufficient. From a macro perspective, during the welding process, the overall temperature rise of the workpiece (parent material) in the repair area is very small. Therefore, micro pulse resistance welding is a "cold welding" technology.
According to the material, structure, status, failure mode, etc. of the workpiece to be repaired, selecting appropriate repair materials and process parameters can achieve no damage to the parent material, firm bonding between the repair material and the parent material, and surface metal repair with modification effect.

The general repair process for laser-like high-energy pulse precision cold repair welding is as follows:

1) Select the pulse current size and pulse time according to the wire diameter.
2) Hold the welding gun, with the tungsten electrode at a 70° angle to the workpiece, and place the wire at a 15° angle to the workpiece.
3) Step on the foot pedal (or hand control) switch to produce a weld point, and operate sequentially to produce continuous weld lines.
4) After reaching the required repair dimensions, perform surface finishing.

Laser-like high-energy pulse precision cold repair welding has the following performance characteristics:

1) It has high repair welding accuracy. Since this technology can precisely control the output current and time, adjusting within a certain range, and running stably, even using ф0.2 mm wire can achieve perfect repair welding, reaching the accuracy of laser repair welding.
2) It has small repair welding impact. 3) It has a small heat-affected zone. Since this technology can precisely control the output current and time, the input energy can be precisely controlled, ensuring that the input energy is only sufficient for the fusion between the workpiece and the filler material, with small heat input to the base metal, small heat-affected zone, no degradation of base metal performance, and no macroscopic thermal deformation.
4) It has high joint strength. This technology can achieve metallurgical bonding between the base metal and the filler material, with high joint strength after welding, suitable for various machining methods, and will not have problems such as weak bonding or falling off.
5) It has a wide repair range. Except for materials with very low melting points such as zinc and tin, and cemented carbide, other various metal workpiece materials can be repaired using this technology.

Surface Coating Repair Technology (referred to as surface coating technology) is a surface engineering technology that involves mixing high molecular polymers with special fillers (such as graphite, molybdenum disulfide, metal powders, ceramic powders, and fibers) to form composite adhesives, which are then applied to the damaged surfaces of remanufactured blanks to achieve specific purposes (such as sealing, leak plugging, wear resistance, corrosion resistance, insulation, conductivity, heat preservation, radiation protection, defect repair, dimensional restoration, and their combinations).

Surface coating technology has a simple process, adjustable coating thickness, and does not produce a heat-affected zone or deformation in the substrate. It is suitable not only for repairing cracks, scratches, dimensional tolerances, and casting defects, as well as surface repair of temperature-sensitive metal components in remanufacturing, but also for repairing failed components with explosion hazards (such as underground equipment and oil and gas equipment). This technology is safe and reliable, requires no special equipment, can be performed on-site, has a short remanufacturing cycle, saves labor hours, and effectively improves productivity. It is a fast and economical remanufacturing technology with very broad application prospects.

The surface coating process includes the following steps:

1) Initial cleaning. Initial cleaning mainly involves removing oil and rust from the surface to be restored, in order to measure, formulate the coating repair process, and perform pre-processing. Initial cleaning of parts can be done by rough washing in gasoline, kerosene, or diesel, followed by final cleaning with acetone.

2) Pre-processing. To ensure that the repair layer has a certain thickness, the parts must be mechanically processed before applying the adhesive. The pre-processing depth for the surfaces to be repaired is generally 0.5 to 3 mm. To prevent edge damage to the coating, a margin of 1 to 2 mm should be left on both sides when processing the coating surface. To enhance the bonding strength between the coating and the substrate, the surface to be coated should be processed into a "zigzag" shape. A rough surface with zigzags can increase the coating area and improve the coating strength.

3) Final cleaning and activation treatment. Final cleaning can be done using acetone; if conditions permit, sandblasting can be used on the coating surface for coarse activation treatment to thoroughly remove the surface oxide layer; flame treatment or chemical treatment can also be used to improve the surface activity of the coating.

4) Mixing the adhesive. The coating material is usually composed of two components. To achieve the best results, it must be mixed in the correct proportions. After the coating material is thoroughly mixed, it should be used immediately.

5) Applying the coating. Coating construction methods include scraping, coating stamping, mold forming, etc.

6) Curing. The curing speed of the coating is related to the ambient temperature, with higher temperatures leading to faster curing. Generally, room temperature curing takes 24 hours, and the coating reaches its maximum performance after 7 days; if cured at 80°C, it takes 2 to 3 hours.

7) Trimming, cleaning, or post-processing. For coatings that do not require subsequent processing, excess coating material on the edges of parts can be trimmed using saw (knife) blades or files. If there are pores larger than 1 mm on the coating surface, they should be cleaned with acetone first, then repaired with adhesive, and polished after curing.

For coatings that require subsequent processing, turning or grinding methods can be used for processing to restore dimensions and precision.

Over the past few decades, with the continuous emergence of new coating adhesives, surface coating technology has developed significantly and is widely used in equipment maintenance and remanufacturing, such as restoring worn parts and dimensional tolerances. After parts are worn, wear-resistant repair adhesive can be directly applied to the worn surface, and then mechanical processing or grinding can be used to restore the part dimensions to the design dimensions. Compared with methods such as build-up welding, thermal spraying, electroplating, and brush plating, this method has the advantages of being able to repair temperature-sensitive metal components and having adjustable coating thickness. The two major series of cold-bonded wear-resistant coatings developed by Germany, SKC (SKC) and DIAMANT (DIAMANT), were used earlier on heavy gantry milling machine worktable guide rails, beam guide rails, hydraulic cylinder pistons, and other components, with very good results. The HNT epoxy wear-resistant coating material developed by Guangzhou Machine Tool Research Institute is one of the earliest products developed domestically, used for machine tool guide rails or other friction surfaces (repair); the AR-4 and AR-5 developed by Xiangfan City Adhesive Technology Research Institute, and the TG series super metal repair agents developed by Armored Engineering Academy are widely used in the fields of wear and corrosion repair and pre-protection treatment of mechanical components, achieving very good results.

In addition, solid lubricant films can be used to solve the lubrication problems of friction pairs in rockets, spacecraft, and other machinery; surface coating layers can be used to restore and pre-protect chemical pipelines, ship hulls and propellers; repair scratches on hydraulic cylinder bodies and machine tool guide rails, restore worn and oversized parts to design dimensions; and solve sealing and corrosion resistance issues.

However, due to the limitations of adhesive performance, its application is currently subject to the following restrictions:

1) The surface coating layer has a limited lifespan when working under conditions of moisture, heat, alternating cold and heat, impact, and other complex environments.

2) The high-temperature resistance of organic adhesive-based surface coating layers is not high, generally not exceeding 350°C. Inorganic adhesives can withstand high temperatures of 1000°C, and ceramic adhesives can withstand temperatures above 2000°C, but they are more brittle.

3) The surface coating has high tensile and shear strength but low peel strength.

4) The use of organic adhesives, especially solvent-based adhesives, involves safety issues such as flammability and toxicity.

With the development of materials science, the performance of adhesives is also being greatly improved. Improving the bonding strength and rapid curing performance of coatings, developing new environmentally friendly, high-temperature resistant, long-life, high-strength, and functional nano-adhesives are the main development directions of adhesive technology.

1. Introduction to Thermal Spraying Repair Technology
(1) Basic Concept and Characteristics of Thermal Spraying
Thermal spraying repair technology (abbreviated as thermal spraying technology) refers to heating powder or wire materials to a molten or semi-molten state using a heat source (flame, arc, plasma arc), atomizing and spraying them onto the surface of the remanufacturing blank under the action of high-pressure airflow, forming a lamellar structure and accumulating into a coating, which is a remanufacturing surface repair technology.
Thermal spraying is an important means of product remanufacturing. It can not only restore the dimensions of product parts but also improve the surface performance of parts, and has been widely used in the remanufacturing and maintenance of equipment parts, producing significant comprehensive benefits.
Thermal spraying has the following characteristics:

1) The selection range of thermal spraying materials is extensive, including almost all metals, alloys, ceramics, plastics, and organic polymer materials.
2) The functions of the repair layer are diverse, including wear resistance, corrosion resistance, high temperature resistance, oxidation resistance, heat insulation, conductivity, insulation, sealing, friction reduction, lubrication, and radiation protection.
3) It is suitable for various substrate materials, such as metals, ceramics, glass, and other inorganic materials, as well as plastics, wood, paper, and other organic materials.
4) The thermal influence on the substrate is small, and the thickness of the repair layer is easily controlled, but the surface roughness value is large.
5) The repair layer and substrate are mechanically bonded or semi-metallurgical/semi-mechanical bonded, with low bonding strength, and the tensile bonding strength is only 30-40 MPa.
6) The thermal spray coating usually has a layered structure, with pores, incompletely melted particles, oxide films, and residual stress.
Reference [110] points out that when using the spraying method to repair internal holes, due to the cooling shrinkage of the internal hole substrate after repair, cracks, peeling, or even falling off of the repair layer often occur. Therefore, this method is not suitable for repairing internal hole parts such as hydraulic cylinders.
(2) Basic Principles and Classification of Thermal Spraying
Taking powder spraying as an example, during the thermal spraying process, the spraying material roughly goes through the following processes: heating → acceleration → melting → re-acceleration → impact on the substrate → cooling and solidification → formation of the coating. The overall process can be approximately divided into three stages:
1) The spraying material is heated, accelerated, and melted.
2) The melted material is atomized by the hot gas flow, further accelerated to form a particle flow; the melted particles interact with the surrounding medium.
3) The particles collide, deform, solidify, and accumulate on the substrate surface.
The spraying material is related to many factors such as the heating temperature, speed, material type, powder particle size, energy type, spray gun structure, and powder feeding method.
According to the type of heat source (or principle) used, thermal spraying can be classified as follows:
1) Using combustion flame as the heat source, including flame spraying, explosion spraying, supersonic flame spraying, plastic spraying, etc.
2) Using electric arc as the heat source, including arc spraying, high-speed arc spraying, etc.
3) Using plasma as the heat source, including atmospheric plasma spraying, supersonic plasma spraying, low-pressure plasma spraying (vacuum plasma spraying), water-stabilized plasma spraying, etc.
4) Using other heat sources, including wire explosion spraying, laser spraying, cold spraying, etc.
Thermal spraying materials are classified by shape, including powder, wire, strip, rod; by composition, including metal, ceramic, organic, composite materials; by function, including wear-resistant, heat-resistant, oxidation-resistant, corrosion-resistant, etc.
(3) Thermal Spraying Process and Characteristics
The thermal spraying process is as follows: substrate surface pretreatment, including surface purification, pre-processing, roughening, etc.; applying various spraying methods for spraying; coating post-treatment, including pore sealing treatment, mechanical processing, heat treatment, etc.

2. Plasma Spraying Repair Technology
(1) Plasma Spraying Equipment
Plasma spraying equipment mainly includes the following parts:
1) Plasma spray gun. It is actually a non-transfer arc plasma generator and is the core device of plasma spraying equipment. It concentrates water, electricity, gas, powder, etc. of the entire system, and the most critical components are the nozzle and cathode. Among them, the nozzle is made of high thermal conductivity pure copper, and the cathode mostly uses cerium tungsten electrode (tungsten oxide mass fraction is 2%-3%).
846:
2) Power supply. It is used to supply direct current to the spray gun, which is usually a full-wave silicon rectifier device. Commonly available are three specifications with rated power of 40 kW, 50 kW and 80 kW.

3) Powder feeder. It is a device used to store spray coating powder and feed the powder to the spray gun according to the process requirements. Its main technical requirements are high powder feeding accuracy, convenient powder feeding adjustment, and wide adaptability to powder particle size.

4) Heat exchanger. It is mainly used to enable the spray gun to obtain effective cooling, so as to achieve the purpose of prolonging the service life of the spray gun, usually adopting water cooling system.

5) Gas supply system. It includes the supply system of working gas and powder feeding gas.

6) Control equipment. It is used to regulate and control water, electricity, gas and powder, and can adjust and control the action program and process parameters of the spraying process.

(2) Plasma spraying process parameters

In the plasma spraying process, there are many factors affecting the quality of the coating, but the main process parameters are:

1) Plasma gas. Common gases include nitrogen and argon, and the purity of the gas is required to be no less than 99.9%. The selection of gas is mainly based on its availability and economy. Nitrogen is cheap, has high plasma flame enthalpy, fast heat transfer, and is conducive to powder heating and melting, but it cannot be used for powders or substrates that are prone to nitriding reactions; argon has a lower ionization potential, stable plasma arc and easy ignition, and a shorter arc flame, which is suitable for spraying small parts or thin parts. Argon also has a good protective effect, but argon has low thermal enthalpy and high price.

The size of gas flow directly affects the thermal enthalpy and flow rate of the plasma flame flow, thereby affecting the spraying efficiency, coating porosity and bonding force. If the gas flow rate is too large, the gas will take away useful heat from the plasma jet and accelerate the speed of the sprayed particles, reducing the "retention" time of the sprayed particles in the plasma flame, resulting in the sprayed particles not reaching the semi-melting or plastic state necessary for deformation, resulting in poor tensile bonding strength, density and hardness of the coating, and a significant decrease in deposition rate; on the contrary, if the gas flow rate is too small, it will cause the arc voltage value to be inappropriate and greatly reduce the speed of the sprayed particles. In extreme cases, it may cause the sprayed particles to overheat, causing the sprayed particles to be excessively melted or vaporized, causing the molten powder particles to accumulate at the nozzle or powder spray port, and then deposit in the coating in larger spherical particles, forming large holes.

2) Plasma arc power. If the plasma arc power is too high, more gas will be converted into plasma, and under the condition of high power and low working gas flow rate, almost all working gas will be transformed into active plasma flow, and the plasma flame temperature is also very high, which may cause some sprayed particles to vaporize and cause the coating composition to change, and the vapor of the sprayed particles melted between the substrate and the coating or inside the coating will condense, resulting in poor bonding. In addition, it may also cause the nozzle and electrode to be burned. If the plasma arc power is too low, the obtained is partial plasma gas and a plasma flame with lower temperature, which will cause insufficient heating of the sprayed particles, and the tensile bonding strength, hardness and deposition efficiency of the coating will be low.

3) Powder feeding. The powder feeding speed must be adapted to the input power. If the powder feeding speed is too fast, raw powder (unmelted) will appear, resulting in a decrease in spraying efficiency; if the powder feeding speed is too slow, the sprayed particles will be severely oxidized, and the substrate will be overheated. The powder feeding position will also affect the coating structure and spraying efficiency. Generally speaking, the powder must be fed to the flame core to obtain the best heating effect and the highest spraying speed.

4) Spraying distance and spraying angle. The coating material and coating characteristics are very sensitive to the spraying distance. The distance between the spray gun and the workpiece will affect the speed and temperature of the sprayed particles when they impact the substrate. If the spraying distance is too large, the speed and temperature of the sprayed particles will decrease, and the tensile bonding strength and spraying efficiency of the coating will decrease significantly, and the porosity will increase; if the spraying distance is too small, the substrate temperature will be too high, and the substrate and coating will be oxidized, affecting the bonding of the coating. However, under the condition that the substrate temperature rise is allowed, it is better to have a slightly smaller spraying distance.

The spraying angle refers to the angle between the flame flow axis and the surface of the sprayed part. When this angle is less than 45°, due to the influence of the "shadow benefit", the coating structure will deteriorate and form holes, resulting in a loose coating.

5) Relative movement speed of spray gun and workpiece. The movement speed of the spray gun should ensure that the coating is flat and prevent the appearance of ridges. In other words, there should be sufficient overlap between the widths of each stroke. Under the premise of meeting the above requirements, a higher spray gun movement speed is generally used in the spraying operation, which can prevent local overheating and surface oxidation.

6) Substrate temperature control. The ideal process is to preheat the workpiece to the temperature to be reached during the spraying process before spraying, and then use air cooling to keep it at the original temperature during the spraying process.

3. Plasma spraying and welding repair technology

(1) Plasma spraying and welding equipment

Plasma spraying and welding or plasma arc surfacing is a new surfacing process, which has the advantages of shallow melting depth, high surfacing rate, and low dilution rate. According to the filling material used during surfacing, plasma arc surfacing machines can be hot wire plasma arc surfacing machines, cold wire plasma arc surfacing machines, powder plasma arc surfacing machines, and melting pole plasma arc surfacing machines. Among them, the powder plasma arc surfacing machine is the most commonly used one.

The powder plasma arc surfacing machine uses the high temperature generated by the plasma arc to melt specific wear-resistant, corrosion-resistant or high-temperature alloy powder, and is a surfacing equipment that melts it onto the surface of the workpiece. By adjusting the plasma arc parameters, the thickness, width, and hardness of the surfacing layer can be conveniently adjusted within a certain range, and a surfacing layer with excellent performance can be obtained. Therefore, this equipment is widely used in the surfacing of bearings, bearing necks, valve plates, valve seats, worm gear blades and other parts, as well as the repair of wear after oil drill rods, bearings, shafts, and rolling mill rolls. Of course, this equipment can also be used for the repair of hydraulic cylinders and metal cylinder parts.

The powder plasma arc surfacing machine is roughly the same as the general plasma welding machine.

( 2 ) Plasma spraying welding or plasma arc overlaying process
According to the introduction in reference [1 1 6] , powder plasma arc overlaying is a method of overlaying by automatically sending alloy powder into the plasma arc area , also known as spraying welding. Powder plasma arc overlaying uses argon as the ionization gas . By adjusting various welding parameters and controlling the heat transferred to the workpiece , a high-quality coating with shallow melting depth , low dilution rate , and flat and smooth forming can be obtained.
In powder plasma arc overlaying , two DC arc welding machines with steep drop external characteristics are generally used as the power source . The negative poles of the two welding machines are connected in parallel to a high-frequency oscillator , and then connected to the cerium tungsten electrode of the spray gun through a cable . Among them , the positive pole of one welding machine is connected to the spray nozzle of the spray gun to generate a non-transfer arc ; the positive pole of the other welding machine is connected to the workpiece to generate a transfer arc . Argon is used as the ionization gas , which enters the spray gun through an electromagnetic valve and a rotor flowmeter . After the power is turned on , a non-transfer arc is ignited by a high-frequency spark , and then a conductive channel between the electrode and the workpiece is formed by the jet of the non-transfer arc , thereby igniting the transfer arc . Before or simultaneously with the establishment of the transfer arc , the powder feeder sends powder to the spray gun , blows it into the arc , and sprays it onto the workpiece . Once the transfer arc is established , an alloy molten pool is formed on the workpiece , so that the alloy powder "melts" on the workpiece . As the spray gun or workpiece moves , the liquid alloy gradually solidifies , eventually forming an alloy overlay layer.
The characteristics of powder plasma arc overlaying are low dilution rate , generally controlled at 5 % ～ 1 5 % , which is beneficial to fully guarantee the performance of the alloy material . For example , if 5 mm overlay is required by stick electrode arc overlaying , only 2 mm overlay is needed by plasma arc overlaying . The plasma arc has high temperature and concentrated energy , stable process , strong directionality , and is less disturbed by external factors . The alloy powder is fully melted and has little spatter . The slag and gas in the molten pool are easily excluded , so that the obtained overlay layer has excellent quality , is flat and smooth , and has a wide and precisely controllable size range . The width of one overlay can be controlled at 1 ～ 1 5 0 mm , and the thickness can be 0 . 2 5 ～ 8 mm , which is difficult to achieve by other overlaying methods . In addition , powder plasma arc overlaying has high productivity , is easy to mechanize and automate , and can reduce labor intensity .

1. Laser Cladding Repair Technology
Laser cladding is a laser processing technology that uses a high-energy density laser beam to heat and melt cladding material, forming a molten pool on the substrate surface. After cooling and solidification, a metallurgical bonding layer is formed on the substrate surface, which is the laser cladding repair technology. This technology can restore the shape and dimensions of damaged parts and enable the metallurgical bonding layer formed on the substrate surface to have properties such as wear resistance, corrosion resistance, heat resistance, and oxidation resistance. Furthermore, it can prepare high-performance alloy surfaces on low-performance, inexpensive steel materials. It is a surface modification technology and waste parts repair and re-manufacturing technology with high economic efficiency.

According to different methods of supplying cladding material to the workpiece surface, it can be divided into powder feeding laser cladding, wire feeding laser cladding, and pre-placed laser cladding. According to different working modes of the laser beam, it can be divided into pulsed laser cladding and continuous laser cladding. Pulsed laser cladding generally uses YAG (solid-state laser medium is Nd:YAG) pulsed laser, while continuous laser cladding mostly uses continuous wave CO2 laser. The laser cladding process includes two aspects: optimizing and controlling laser heating process parameters; determining the cladding material and its supply method to the workpiece surface. For the CO2 laser cladding process widely used in industry, the main process parameters that need to be optimized and controlled include laser output power, spot size, and scanning speed.

The laser repair process design specified in GB/T 29796-2013 includes two contents: laser cladding material selection and laser and process parameter selection.

Laser cladding material refers to the material added during the laser cladding process. It can be powder, wire, tape, or foil, among which powder material is the most widely used. At present, the powder materials for laser cladding are generally borrowed from thermal spray powders and self-designed and developed powder materials, mainly including self-fluxing alloy powders, metal-ceramic composite (mixed) powders, and metal powders independently designed and developed by various application units.

Based on the principles of similar thermal expansion coefficients, similar melting points, and wettability between the cladding material and substrate, the laser cladding process also needs to be optimized. The quality control of the laser cladding layer mainly focuses on reducing component contamination, cracks, and pores in the laser cladding layer, as well as preventing oxidation and burn-through.

The evaluation of the laser cladding process and the quality inspection of repaired parts should follow the standards specified in GB/T 29796-2013.

2. Laser Forming and Cladding Repair Technology
According to the literature [86], laser cladding usually uses pre-placed coating or powder feeding methods to add cladding metal. Utilizing the characteristics of laser beam focusing with extremely high energy, only a slight melting of the substrate surface occurs in an instant, while the metal powder with the same or similar material to the substrate is completely melted. After the laser leaves, rapid solidification occurs, obtaining a dense (melted) cladding layer surface that is metallurgically bonded with the substrate, restoring the geometric dimensions of the part surface, and also strengthening the surface coating. The basic principle and technical essence of laser forming and cladding remanufacturing (repair) technology are the same as those of laser cladding rapid forming remanufacturing technology.

Laser forming and cladding repair technology solves the problems of material selection limitations, process heat stress, thermal deformation, coarse material grains, and difficult to guarantee the bonding strength between the substrate material that cannot be solved by repair processes such as vibration welding, argon arc welding, spraying, and plating. This technology has the following characteristics:
1) The laser cladding layer is metallurgically bonded with the substrate, and the bonding strength is not lower than 90% of the original substrate material.
2) Only the surface of the substrate material slightly melts during laser processing, with a micro-melting layer of 0.05～0.1 mm, and the heat-affected zone of the substrate is extremely small, generally 0.1～0.2 mm.
3) The temperature rise of the substrate does not exceed 80°C during laser processing, and there is no thermal deformation after laser processing.
4) The controllability of laser cladding technology is good and it is easy to achieve automation.
5) There is no coarse casting structure in the cladding layer and the substrate, and the structure of the cladding layer and the interface layer is dense, with fine crystals, and no defects such as pores, inclusions, and cracks.
6) The laser cladding layer is a gradient functional material composed of a bottom layer, a middle layer, and a surface layer, each with its own characteristics. The bottom layer has good wettability with the substrate and high bonding strength; the middle layer has high strength and hardness, and good crack resistance; the surface layer has properties such as erosion resistance, wear resistance, and corrosion resistance. This makes the repaired or remanufactured parts perform better and safer when used in equipment.

According to relevant information, laser forming and cladding is also known as laser profile following cladding, which needs to solve two problems:
1) How to imitate the prototype to repair the damaged part of the part, that is, profile following cladding repair or profile following cladding repair.
2) How to ensure that the repair layer is metallurgically bonded with the substrate and has a small heat-affected zone, and at the same time, the repair layer can grow outward in a single pass.

To this end, relevant proprietary technologies can be referred to (for a fee) to solve the above problems.

In the application of laser forming and cladding repair technology, the different irradiation characteristics of CO2 laser and Nd-YAG laser should also be considered, and they can be used alternately during the repair process to adapt to the processing of cladding layers in different areas.

6.6 Mechanical Processing Technology for Surface Repair Layers of Cylinder Parts
6.6.1 Basic Requirements for Mechanical Processing of Surface Repair Layers of Cylinder Parts
The mechanical processing of the surface repair layer of cylinder parts refers to the mechanical processing of the remanufacturing coating and cladding layer on the surface of cylinder parts. There are some basic requirements for the mechanical processing of the surface repair layer of cylinder parts.
1. Requirements before processing
1) First, the processing area, range, and process plan should be determined.
2) The absence of defects that affect performance should also be determined.
3) The residual repair layer outside the processing area should be removed to prevent affecting subsequent processing.
2. Requirements during processing
1) Processing needs to consider geometric tolerances to determine its positioning and process.
2) Different processes should be selected according to the characteristics of different cylinder parts.
3) The positioning datum should be checked and trimmed to ensure that the dimensional tolerance and geometric tolerance can meet the drawing and technical requirements. Processing should be carried out according to the process regulations.
4) When mechanically processing the remanufacturing repair layer, suitable cutting tools, cutting parameters, or special processing methods should be used. The cutting tools should have sufficient strength, rigidity, toughness, and wear resistance.
5) During processing, a smaller cutting feed rate, depth of cut, and lower speed should be used, and the cooling of the cutting tool and repair layer should be strengthened to prevent the repair layer from falling off, cracking, burning, etc.
6) For remanufacturing coating, grinding is recommended; for remanufacturing cladding layer, turning, milling, or grinding can be used.
7) The mechanical processing of cylinder parts should be inspected and accepted according to the process, and only after the previous process is qualified can it be transferred to the next process.
8) During the handling, processing, and storage of cylinder parts, damage such as bumps, scratches, corrosion, and deformation should be prevented.
3. Requirements after processing
1) After processing, the surface performance, dimensional accuracy, geometric accuracy, and surface roughness of the cylinder parts should meet the requirements of the drawing and technical requirements.
2) Except for special requirements, the sharp corners of the processed cylinder parts should be dulled.
6.6.2 Turning Processing of Surface Repair Layers of Cylinder Parts
Turning is one of the most commonly used mechanical processing methods for surface repair layers of cylinder parts. However, due to some characteristics of the surface repair layer of the parts, this turning processing often has the following problems:
(1) Large impact and vibration during processing
Due to the uneven surface of the thermal spray coating and metal surfacing layer, as well as the uneven hardness inside and the presence of hard points (carbides, borides, etc.), the impact and vibration during processing are large.
852:
and gaps, etc., these will cause the cutting force to fluctuate during turning, resulting in large impacts and vibrations during the machining process. Therefore, the process system composed of the lathe, fixture, workpiece, and tool is required to have good rigidity, and higher requirements are also put forward for the strength of the tool.
(2) The tool is prone to chipping and abnormal wear
Due to the hard outer skin, sand holes, pores, etc. of the metal surfacing layer, the hard points inside the thermal spray coating, coupled with the vibration and impact during cutting, it is easy to cause chipping and abnormal wear of the cutting edge, resulting in loss of cutting ability.
(3) Short tool life
Since the metal surfacing layer and thermal spray coating generally have high hardness and wear resistance, especially the high-hardness metal surfacing layer and thermal spray coating, therefore, during machining, large cutting force and cutting heat are generated, which accelerates the wear of the cutting edge and causes it to become dull quickly. This brings great difficulties to cutting processing, and even makes it difficult to carry out cutting processing. Due to the short tool life, the improvement of cutting dosage is limited, and the productivity is reduced.
(4) The thermal spray coating is prone to peeling
The bonding strength between the thermal spray coating and the substrate is not high. The coating obtained by the spray process has a mechanical or semi-mechanical bonding with the substrate, and the tensile bonding strength is generally 30-50 MPa. In addition, the coating is generally thin, so during cutting processing, when the cutting force exceeds a certain limit, the coating is prone to peeling. This is something that should be prevented during cutting processing.
6.6.2.1 Turning of Surfacing Layer
Using the surfacing method to obtain the dimensional restoration layer of the wear surface of parts is a commonly used remanufacturing method. Although the metallurgical properties of the surfacing restoration layer mainly depend on the material of the surfacing electrode, due to the large and uneven thickness of the restoration layer caused by the surfacing method, surface hardening and changes in the organization within the layer, etc., the machinability of the surfacing layer will become poor, and it needs to be fully considered and noted during cutting processing.
1. Turning of low-alloy steel surfacing layer
Due to the different carbon content of the surfacing electrode, the hardness of the obtained surfacing layer is also different, which can be divided into medium-hardness surfacing layer and high-hardness surfacing layer from the perspective of hardness. The medium-hardness surfacing layer is the most widely used in the remanufacturing of mechanical parts. The medium-hardness surfacing layer is formed under normal cooling speed during surfacing, and the organization of the surfacing layer is pearlite plus a small amount of ferrite; when the cooling speed is faster, martensite will appear. In order to avoid the appearance of martensite and facilitate cutting processing, attention should be paid to reducing the cooling speed, such as adopting heat preservation and cooling.
The hardness of the medium-hardness surfacing layer is 200-350 HBW (such as surfacing layer with electrode 107, the hardness is about 250 HBW; with electrode 127, the hardness of the surfacing layer is about 350 HBW). The alloy elements such as Cr and Mn in the surfacing metal will dissolve in ferrite, playing a role in solid solution strengthening, and can also make the carbide alloy, so that the surfacing layer has a certain hardness and wear resistance, as well as good impact resistance.
The surfacing layer has a certain hardness and wear resistance, and when it is cut, the vibration and impact generated are large. In order to ensure that the tool is not damaged during processing and that the tool has a certain life, according to the commonly used tool materials and cutting performance and characteristics at present, tools such as carbide YG8, YT5, and YW1 can be selected for rough machining. These tool materials have good toughness and high bending strength, and are not prone to chipping during processing. For finishing, in addition to requiring the tool to have good wear resistance, it is also required to withstand the impact and vibration of hard points, pores, and sand holes left over from rough machining. At this time, tools such as carbide YT15 with higher hardness and better wear resistance can be selected.
2. Turning of stainless steel surfacing layer
The stainless steel surfacing layer is mostly obtained by surfacing with austenitic electrodes, and the metallographic organization is austenite. The austenitic organization has large plasticity and is prone to work hardening. In addition, the thermal conductivity is also very low (about 1/3 of that of 45 steel), so the austenitic stainless steel surfacing layer is also difficult to process.
For the stainless steel surfacing layer, YT-class carbide tools are not suitable for processing the stainless steel surfacing layer, because the titanium element in YT-class carbide steel is prone to cold welding with the titanium element in the workpiece material, which aggravates tool wear. Therefore, YG-class, YH-class, or YW-class carbide tools are generally used, and high-performance high-speed steel tools can also be used.
Tool geometric parameters: the front angle is -5° to 0°; the back angle is 4° to 6°; the edge inclination angle is -5° to 0°; the main deflection angle should be appropriately reduced, and the tool tip arc radius should be increased.
The cutting dosage is selected as ap=1.5-2mm, f=0.3-0.4mm/r, vc=14-18m/min.
6.6.2.2 Turning of Thermal Spray Coating
The biggest feature of thermal spray coating is its high hardness and high wear resistance, and its hardness can reach 50-70 HRC. Such thermal spray coatings can be called high-hardness thermal spray coatings, which are difficult to process. When cutting these coatings, there are special requirements for the selection of tool materials, tool geometric parameters, and cutting dosage.
1. Selection of tool materials
The general requirements for thermal spray coating on tool materials are high hardness, high wear resistance, sufficient bending strength and toughness. General carbide grades cannot be used for processing high-hardness thermal spray coatings. At present, the following three tool materials are better for processing thermal spray coatings:
1) Ultrafine-grained carbide with added tantalum carbide and niobium carbide.
The main functions of tantalum carbide (TaC) and niobium carbide (NbC) in carbide are as follows: they improve the hardness of carbide at normal and high temperatures, because their melting point is as high as 3500-3880°C, thereby improving the wear resistance of carbide; they prevent the growth of WC grains during the sintering process, thereby playing a role in refining grains, improving the bending strength, impact toughness and wear resistance of YT-class carbide; they improve the bonding temperature of carbide and steel, because their bonding temperature is higher than that of WC and TiC, reducing the diffusion of alloy components into steel, thereby reducing tool bonding wear and extending tool life. In ultrafine-grained carbide, due to the high dispersion of WC and cobalt, 148 Chapter 6 Remanufacturing of Hydraulic Cylinder

Increasing the bonding area improves bonding strength, thereby increasing hardness by 1.5 to 2 HRA, and significantly improving bending strength. Therefore, ultra-fine grain cemented carbide with added tantalum carbide and niobium carbide exhibits better performance in terms of hardness, wear resistance, bending strength, and toughness, and can be used for low-speed cutting without chipping, adapting to the cutting processing of high-hardness thermal spray coatings.

2) Ceramic tool materials. Ceramics used as tool materials include pure Al2O3 ceramics, Al2O3-TiC mixed ceramics, and Si3N4-based ceramics. The domestic grades are SG5 (94 HRA, bending strength greater than 0.7 GPa) and AG2 (93.5 to 95 HRA, bending strength greater than 0.8 GPa). Using them for cutting thermal spray coatings yields good results, but their bending strength still needs further improvement. For example, using an SG5 blade to cut a nickel-based 102 spray coating (55 to 60 HRC), with cutting parameters ap=0.1 mm, f=0.3 mm/r, v=29 m/min, to machine an outer diameter of 50 mm and a length of 650 mm, the tool travels a cutting distance of 150 mm, and the wear VB behind the tool is 0.15 mm, with a surface roughness value of 10 to 2.5 μm.

3) Cubic boron nitride. Cubic boron nitride (CBN) is obtained by transforming hexagonal boron nitride under high temperature and high pressure with the addition of a catalyst. It is divided into polycrystalline cubic boron nitride and cubic boron nitride composite blades. The advantages of cubic boron nitride are obvious: it has very high hardness and wear resistance, with a microhardness of 8000 to 9000 HV, second only to diamond; it has very high thermal stability (heat resistance can reach 1400 to 1500 ℃), much higher than diamond (heat resistance 700 to 800 ℃); it has great chemical inertness, and does not easily react chemically with iron group metals at 1200 to 1300 ℃. The overall bending strength is currently still at a relatively low level, with some blades reaching above 0.5 GPa. Cubic boron nitride tools can be used for cutting difficult-to-machine materials such as cemented carbide, quenched steel, chilled cast iron, and high-temperature alloys, with processing effects comparable to grinding. Currently, for high-hardness thermal spray coatings, it is the tool material with the highest cutting efficiency, and the cutting speed can be 4 to 5 times higher than that of YCO9 cemented carbide blades.

3. Selection of cutting parameters for thermal spray coatings

The cutting parameters for thermal spray coatings are also limited by tool life. Therefore, when prioritizing cutting parameters, the selection order is as follows: first, use the maximum depth of cut ap as much as possible, then select the allowable feed rate according to the machining conditions and requirements, and finally, select the maximum cutting speed under the conditions of allowable tool life or machine power.

6.6.3 Grinding of Repair Layers on Cylinder Parts

Grinding is mainly used for precision machining of outer circles, inner circles, planes, and various formed surfaces (gears, threads, splines, etc.). It can be used to machine difficult-to-machine thermal spray coatings, but its productivity is lower compared to grinding other difficult-to-machine metal materials. Generally, grinding accuracy can reach IT6~IT5 grade, and surface roughness can reach 0.08~0.20μm.

1. Characteristics of Grinding Thermal Spray Coatings

Higher accuracy and smaller surface roughness values can be obtained through grinding, so it is usually used for precision machining of thermal spray coatings. For high-hardness spray coatings, grinding is relatively difficult, mainly due to the following two reasons:

1) Grinding wheels tend to become dull rapidly and lose their grinding ability. The main reasons for the rapid dulling of grinding wheels are the dulling and breaking of the abrasive grains, and the "loading" of the grinding wheel. This is particularly prominent when grinding inner holes, as the diameter of the grinding wheel for inner holes is restricted by the hole size, unlike when grinding outer circles where larger diameter grinding wheels can be used. Therefore, the number of times the abrasive grains are engaged in grinding increases relatively within the same time period, leading to intensified wear and shortened wheel life.

2) Large radial cutting forces can cause vibration during the machining process, as well as make it easy for grinding heat to burn the surface and cause cracks in the machined surface, all of which affect the quality of the machined surface and the improvement of grinding parameters. Therefore, for grinding high-hardness thermal spray coatings, artificial diamond grinding wheels and cubic boron nitride grinding wheels are mostly used.

At present, domestic comparative test data for grinding nickel-based thermal spray coating outer circles using artificial diamond grinding wheels, green silicon carbide grinding wheels, and white corundum grinding wheels show that the performance of artificial diamond grinding wheels is far superior to that of green silicon carbide grinding wheels and white corundum grinding wheels.
