6.6.4 Special Processing Techniques for Surface Repair Layers of Cylinder Parts

1. Electrolytic Grinding

Electrolytic grinding utilizes the electrochemical effect of electrolyte on the metal being processed (electrolytic action) and the mechanical grinding action of the conductive grinding wheel on the processing surface to remove the surface layer of metal. Electrolytic grinding of thermal spray coatings features high productivity, good processing quality, good economy, strong adaptability, and wide processing range, making it a new processing technology for difficult-to-process thermal spray coatings.

The electrolyte is an extremely important factor affecting productivity and processing quality in the electrolytic grinding process. During actual production, the optimal electrolyte for electrolytic grinding should be selected based on the technical requirements of different products and different materials. Tests show that for electrolytic grinding of difficult-to-process thermal spray coatings, electrolytes with sodium dihydrogen phosphate as the main component have better grinding performance.

The machine tools for electrolytic grinding can be either specialized electrolytic grinding machines or ordinary grinding machines and lathes that have been modified. The DC power supply for electrolytic grinding requires adjustable voltage (5-20V) and relatively stiff external characteristics. The maximum working current can be selected from 10-1000A depending on the processing area and required productivity. The circulating pump for supplying electrolyte generally uses a small centrifugal pump, equipped with devices for filtering and settling impurities in the electrolyte. Electrolyte is typically sprayed using pipes and flat nozzles, with the nozzle attached to the pipe and spraying electrolyte toward the working area. The internal grinding head consists of a high-speed grinding wheel shaft and a three-phase AC motor. The process parameters for electrolytic grinding can be formulated based on the following factors:

1) Process parameters of the grinding wheel. The grinding wheel can use conductive grinding wheels with diamond-bronze binder or graphite and silver-impregnated conductive grinding wheels. The peripheral speed of the grinding wheel vs=15-20m/s, axial feed speed vfa=0.5-1m/min (internal and external grinding), vfa=10-15m/min (surface grinding), workpiece peripheral speed vw=10-20m/s, radial feed speed vfr=0.05-0.15m/min (double stroke).

2) Voltage and current specifications. During rough machining, voltage is 8-12V, current density is 20-30A/cm²; during finish machining, voltage is 6-8V, current density is 10-15A/cm².

If blackening of the grinding surface is observed when applying the above process parameters, the voltage should be reduced or the radial feed speed decreased while increasing the axial feed speed.

2. Ultrasonic Vibration Turning

Ultrasonic vibration turning is a processing method that uses a cutting tool to produce high-frequency vibration along the cutting speed direction for turning. The fundamental difference between ultrasonic vibration turning and ordinary turning is that in ultrasonic vibration turning, the cutting edge and the metal being cut form separated cutting, meaning the tool completes one cutting and separation cycle in an extremely short time during each vibration. In ordinary turning, the cutting edge and the metal being cut undergo continuous cutting without separation. Therefore, the mechanism of ultrasonic vibration turning is different from that of ordinary turning.

The main features of ultrasonic vibration turning are that both cutting force and cutting heat are much lower than in ordinary turning. The cutting force is approximately 1/3 to 1/20 of that in ordinary turning, and the cutting heat is approximately 1/5 to 1/10 of that in ordinary turning. This is the fundamental reason why ultrasonic vibration turning can achieve high processing accuracy and good surface quality.

Tests show that for ultrasonic vibration turning of difficult-to-process thermal spray coatings, the cutting edge and tip of the tool must have high strength and wear resistance. The selection of tool material and tool geometric parameters should meet the following requirements:

1) Tool material. Tool materials such as YC09 and YW2 have good cutting performance when machining difficult-to-process Ni60 thermal spray coatings. For Al₂O₃ ceramic spray coatings, cubic boron nitride blades must be used. The tool life for both reaches a good practical level and is longer than in ordinary turning.

2) Tool geometric parameters. To ensure high strength of the cutting edge, the rake angle is generally selected as γo=0°; to reduce friction, the clearance angle is generally selected as αo=8°-12°; to enhance tip strength, both the principal cutting edge angle κr and auxiliary cutting edge angle κ'r can take small values, and the tip arc radius rε can take a large value to enhance tip strength, generally selected as rε=2-3mm.

Ultrasonic vibration turning of thermal spray coatings has been well applied in engineering practice. After engine piston pins of certain construction machinery became worn and were scrapped in large quantities, they were remanufactured by thermal spraying (spray coating material was Ni60 with hardness of 60HRC). Mechanical processing was difficult after coating. The dimensional tolerance for the outer diameter of the piston pin was 0.011mm, and the surface roughness value was 0.32-0.04μm. Ordinary turning could not meet these requirements. Using ultrasonic vibration turning with the following process parameters: vibration frequency 20kHz, amplitude a=15μm, workpiece speed vw=4.8m/min, feed rate f=0.08mm/rev, depth of cut ap=0.1mm. After processing, the outer circle of the piston pin was measured with a dimensional error of 0.009mm and surface roughness value of 0.16μm, meeting assembly and usage requirements.

3. Magnetic Abrasive Polishing

Magnetic abrasive polishing involves placing magnetic abrasive materials in a magnetic field, where the abrasive particles arrange themselves along magnetic force lines to form a magnetic brush. The workpiece is placed between the N-S magnetic poles, maintaining a certain gap between the workpiece and the poles. When the workpiece rotates relative to the magnetic poles, the magnetic abrasive particles polish the workpiece surface. If an ultrasonic vibration device is placed axially on the workpiece, each point on the workpiece will vibrate longitudinally at 18000-25000Hz, producing an excellent ultrasonic-magnetic composite polishing effect. Let magnetic abrasive particle A be a particle close to the workpiece surface. Under the influence of the magnetic field, point A will generate a force fx pressing against the workpiece along the magnetic force line direction. Due to workpiece rotation, a tangential cutting reaction force fy is applied to point A by the workpiece surface. Also, because the magnetic field of the magnetic pole is non-uniform, point A also experiences a magnetic force Fm in the tangential direction due to the gradient change in magnetic field strength. This force is opposite to the fy direction and can prevent the magnetic field force on abrasive particle A (the resultant of fx and Fm) from being greater than the cutting reaction force fy. At this time, magnetic abrasive particle A is in a normal cutting state. When the magnetic field force on particle A is less than the cutting reaction force fy, particle A will slide or roll. The magnitude of the magnetic force is proportional to the square of the magnetic field strength, and the magnetic field strength increases with increasing DC power supply voltage. Inspection is divided into component inspection and assembly inspection; according to inspection items, it can be classified into mechanical processing inspection, surface repair layer inspection, assembly inspection, performance inspection, coating inspection, and packaging inspection.

1. General Provisions
1) Products of the same type and same model produced using the same remanufacturing process belong to the same inspection batch. The sampling quantity for the same inspection batch of remanufactured products should be at least 10% higher than that for sampling of original new products. For products with single batch quantity less than 10 pieces, inspection should be conducted at a ratio of not less than 50%. Other requirements should follow the provisions of GB/T28282.1.
2) Before inspection, clear inspection procedures should be formulated. Appropriate selection should be made for measuring equipment, testing equipment, instruments, gauges, and special tools required for inspection to meet inspection requirements.
3) During inspection, clear requirements should be proposed for the controlled inspection environment, especially for precision measurements sensitive to environmental factors.
4) The inspection process should be protected as required to prevent injuries that may be caused by high-pressure and/or high-temperature hydraulic oil splashing or spraying during inspection.
5) Waste generated during the inspection process should be treated in an environmentally harmless manner.

2. Component Inspection
(1) Mechanical Processing Inspection
1) During the processing of remanufactured components, force-bearing parts and important working surfaces should not have defects such as sand holes, scratches, bruises, and rust spots that reduce component strength, lifespan, or affect appearance.
2) The heat treatment of the processed surface of components should not have oxide scale. The mating surfaces after processing should not require annealing treatment.
3) Workpieces with residual magnetism caused by processing or inspection should be demagnetized. Burrs on the surface of components (including keyways) should be removed, and sharp edges and corners should be chamfered.
4) After mechanical processing of the surface repair layer, geometric dimensions, geometric tolerances, and surface quality should be inspected, and they should meet the requirements of drawings and technical specifications.

(2) Repair Layer Inspection
1) Coating Layer
① Use a tensile strength tester to inspect the tensile bond strength and hardness of the coating layer.
② The coating surface should have no cracks, peeling, or flaking, and the surface roughness should meet design requirements.
2) Brush Plating Layer
① The brush plating layer can be inspected using a hardness tester.
② After mechanical processing, the plating layer should have no defects such as peeling or flaking that affect usage.
3) Welding Layer
① Through fatigue, wear resistance, and other tests, as well as metallographic analysis, determine whether the welding layer meets mechanical performance requirements.
② Through tensile tests, pressure tests (strength inspection), and non-destructive testing, determine whether the tensile bond strength and air tightness meet the repair process requirements.
③ The surface of the welding layer should be uniform, without peeling or delamination. The dimensions and standard quality should meet the repair process requirements.
4) Other Repair Layers. For components with special inspection requirements, they can be executed according to the requirements agreed upon by both parties.

3. Assembly Inspection
1) Before assembling the hydraulic cylinder assembly, each component should be cleaned or washed, and there should be no burrs, flash, oxide scale, rust, chips, sand particles, dust, or oil stains, and they should meet the corresponding cleanliness requirements. Except for special requirements, sharp edges and corners of components should be chamfered before assembly.
2) For components assembled using repair methods, the main mating dimensions after repair should meet the requirements of drawings and technical specifications.

4. Performance Inspection
According to the quality characteristics and safety performance of remanufactured products, they should not be lower than the relevant provisions of original new products. The inspection methods for hydraulic cylinder assemblies should follow the relevant sections of Chapter 5.

Hydraulic cylinders should undergo type inspection in any of the following situations:
1) For new remanufactured products or old products transferred to a new manufacturer.
2) Once every three years after formal production.
3) After being out of production for more than two years and resuming production.
4) When there is a significant difference between the factory inspection results and the previous type inspection.

5. Coating Inspection
1) Before coating, there should be no burrs, oxide scale, sand adhesion, oil stains, or other contaminants.
2) Special parts should be protected.

6. Packaging Inspection
1) The factory documents for remanufactured hydraulic cylinders should include the following contents:
   a) Certificate of remanufactured hydraulic cylinder.
   b) User manual for use and maintenance.
   c) Quality assurance card.
2) Necessary measures for dust prevention, corrosion prevention, and other physical damage prevention should be adopted.
3) The packaging of remanufactured hydraulic cylinders should be marked with remanufactured product identification. Other requirements should follow the provisions of GB/T28618.

6.8.1 Remanufacturing Repair Examples of Hydraulic Cylinder Body (Barrel)

The remanufacturing of hydraulic cylinder body (barrel) should adopt corresponding remanufacturing technologies according to the detection results, as listed in some specific methods in reference [121]:

(2) Honing Process

The cylinder barrel is an important part of the hydraulic cylinder. Most cylinder barrels are scrapped due to internal particles causing scratches on the inner wall of the barrel, leading to excessive internal leakage, failure to meet the required working pressure and cylinder output force. Therefore, using honing technology to repair scratches on the inner wall of the barrel has become the main method. The honing process of the honing machine can be divided into three steps: rough honing, fine honing, and polishing.

During rough honing, at the initial stage, since there are scratches or peeling on the inner wall of the barrel and the oil stone on the honing head also has edges and burrs, the stroke speed and spindle load should be smaller, and after running smoothly, they should be gradually increased. Observe the change of the pressure gauge reading, and manually correct the taper of the barrel as needed; during fine honing, the spindle speed should be increased by about 10%, and the spindle load should also be increased accordingly, and the short stroke switch should be turned off; during polishing, the spindle speed and spindle load should remain the same as during fine honing. At this time, first turn off the spindle rotation, use the manual button to reduce the honing head, and add a special polishing emery cloth pad under the oil stone to continue honing. This is to improve the surface quality of the inner wall of the barrel. Observe whether the scratches, peeling, and other damage on the inner wall of the barrel have been completely honed to meet the requirements, then clean the cylinder body to remove the residual honing oil inside; after cleaning, apply a layer of protective oil to protect the inner wall of the barrel.

2. Experiment and Application of Cold Welding Technology in Hydraulic Support Bottom Cylinder Repair and Remanufacturing
According to the introduction in reference [123], cold welding technology is a new cold arc welding process that has emerged in recent years, which is a major improvement on the traditional melting pole gas shielded welding process. This technology uses advanced electronic technology to control the welding current waveform and voltage, and cooperates with the short-circuit transition of the molten droplet, thereby realizing the control of welding heat input. It can not only greatly reduce welding heat input, reduce the dilution rate of the cladding layer, but also improve the quality of the cladding layer.
Cold welding technology has the following main characteristics:
1) Low welding heat input. During cold welding, its heat input is only 1/3 of that of traditional melting pole gas shielded welding, or even lower. Therefore, the heat affected zone is small and the workpiece deformation is small.
2) Low dilution rate of the cladding layer. The dilution rate of the cladding layer after cold welding is less than 2%, which is comparable to laser cladding, and a cladding layer with higher quality and performance can be obtained.
3) Wide range of applicable welding materials and base materials. Cold welding equipment can basically be used for all carbon steel, stainless steel, Al, Cu, Ni and other types of flux-cored, solid wire and base materials on the market.
4) Less spatter. During cold welding, there is very little spatter, which can basically achieve spatter-free welding.

6.8.2 Repair Examples of Hydraulic Cylinder Piston Rod Remanufacturing

Hydraulic cylinder piston rod remanufacturing should use corresponding remanufacturing technologies according to inspection results, as some specific methods listed in reference [121]:

1) For piston rod surface plating layer peeling, local (minor) rust, bumps, and scratches, use a special stripping process to strip the hard chrome plating layer, repair local damage, and then re-chrome plate.
2) For cases where the piston rod diameter must be reduced, such as large-area rust, adjust the piston rod diameter by a certain amount, customize corresponding seals and end caps; simultaneously perform heat treatment strengthening on the piston rod to improve its mechanical strength and reduce remanufacturing costs.
3) For piston rods with severe surface bumps and scratches, use a cold welder for local welding to repair defects; plasma laser quenching can also be used to change the dimensions of the piston rod body, then overall reprocessing. Plasma laser quenching can also improve the mechanical properties of components and extend service life.

For piston rods with severe surface damage or those requiring improved quality characteristics, advanced remanufacturing technologies such as plasma spraying and laser cladding should be used.

1. Application of Laser Cladding Remanufacturing Technology for Columns and Jacks of Hydraulic Supports in Coal Mines

The laser cladding remanufacturing technology for columns and jacks of hydraulic supports in coal mines is a remanufacturing technology that uses laser cladding of stainless steel powder to restore the quality characteristics of columns and jacks that have failed due to internal leakage, peeling of the chrome plating layer, severe scratches, etc., to a level equal to or better than that of new products.

According to references [1, 2, 4], the service life of columns repaired by electroplating and remanufactured by laser cladding under the same working conditions in the same coal mine is as follows: the service life of columns repaired by electroplating is 1 to 1.5 years; after 4.5 years of use, columns remanufactured by laser cladding do not show problems such as rusting and decreased sealing performance. According to the results of simulated tests, the actual service life of columns remanufactured by laser cladding should be 6 times that of columns repaired by electroplating.

According to the provisions of DB37/T1932-2011, columns and jacks should undergo thorough cleaning, degreasing, etc., and defect evaluation to determine whether they are suitable for remanufacturing. If any of the following conditions occur, they should be judged as unsuitable for remanufacturing:

a) The axial scratch depth on the sealing mating surface of the middle cylinder body and small column is greater than 2 mm.

b) The radial scratch depth on the sealing mating surface of the middle cylinder body and small column is greater than 2 mm.

c) There are cracks in the cylinder body, and the threads, annular grooves, or other connecting parts at the end of the cylinder body are incomplete.

d) The linearity error of the inner hole of the cylinder body is greater than 0.05%; the roundness and cylindricity errors are greater than 0.2% of the nominal size.

e) The linearity error of the live column is greater than 0.1%.

For part evaluation, please refer to standards such as DB37/T26882-2015.

DB37/T1932-2011 also stipulates the requirements for main parts before cladding and the requirements for laser-clad stainless steel remanufactured columns.

Requirements for main parts before cladding:

a) The welds of the outer cylinder body, middle cylinder body, and piston rod should be subjected to ultrasonic testing according to the requirements of GB/T6402 and GB/T5777.

b) Check the damage, dimensions, and linearity of the outer cylinder body and middle cylinder body. If necessary, use laser cladding or electroplating technology to repair the inner hole to meet the technical requirements.

Requirements for laser-clad stainless steel remanufactured columns:

a) The thickness of the laser cladding layer should not be less than 0.5 mm.

b) After laser cladding, the surface hardness should not be lower than 40 HRC. After rolling treatment, it should not be lower than 42 HRC.

c) The cladding layer should be uniform and firm, without peeling, falling off, or blistering. There should be no burning, cracks, or dense pitting and other appearance defects.

(1) Application of Laser Cladding Technology in Hydraulic Supports of Coal Mines

1) Necessity of Laser Cladding for Hydraulic Support Columns. According to reference [1, 2, 5], the Shanxi Fenxi Mining Group uses electroplating technology for the overhaul of hydraulic supports and the repair of various jacks. According to environmental protection requirements, the number of hard chrome plating manufacturers is decreasing year by year, while the price of hard chrome plating is increasing, becoming a bottleneck in the repair of hydraulic support columns and jacks. Moreover, the quality of hard chrome plating is difficult to meet the requirements of coal mine users, especially in mines with corrosive gases or liquids, where H2S corrosion has the greatest impact on hard chrome plating layers.

The service life of laser cladding layers is more than 5 times that of hard chrome plating layers. At present, most high-end hydraulic support remanufacturing in China adopts laser cladding. After laser cladding, the next overhaul of the column is particularly simple. Because when the column with hard chrome plating has a rust spot or scratch, during overhaul, the hard chrome plating layer must go through the complex process of complete stripping, repair, and re-hard chrome plating, which is time-consuming, laborious, and cumbersome, and pollutes the environment. For columns that have undergone laser cladding, during the next support overhaul, under the premise of ensuring sealing, most columns do not need to be disassembled and processed. Individual damaged areas only need micro-processing (repairing the damaged points by argon arc welding, then polishing and polishing with oilstone), which is inexpensive, time-saving, labor-saving, and environmentally friendly.

2) Comparison of Electroplating Layer and Laser Cladding Layer Performance of Columns. Electroplating is a surface treatment technology that uses an electrolytic process to deposit chromium on the substrate surface to form a chromium plating layer. The bonding between the plating layer and the substrate is chemical bonding, with weak bonding force, which is prone to blistering, cracking, and falling off. The electroplating process of columns and jacks generally adopts composite plating layer technology of copper-tin alloy plus hard chromium. The thickness of the electroplating layer is generally 0.05 to 0.06 mm. The chrome plating layer has high brittleness. When it is locally subjected to compression or impact, the plating layer is prone to cracks, and moisture in humid air will seep through the gaps to the substrate surface to form rust spots. With the passage of time, the spots continue to expand and increase, and connect into large areas. In severe cases, it will cause the support to fail.

Taking the laser cladding of high mining height column middle cylinder as an example, laser cladding technology uses a high-power laser beam to gather extremely high energy to instantly melt the surface of the workpiece to be processed. At the same time, the alloy powder pre-placed on the surface of the part is completely melted to obtain a dense cladding layer with metallurgical bonding with the substrate. After finishing, the single-sided thickness of the cladding layer is maintained at 0.50 to 0.60 mm, which is 8 to 10 times that of the electroplating layer, and it has a firm metallurgical bond with the substrate. Due to the concentrated and dense characteristics of the laser beam energy, most of the light energy is used for melting the powder, only slightly melting the substrate surface, and the heat-affected zone of the substrate is extremely small, generally 0.1 to 0.2 mm, effectively ensuring that the performance and shape of the base material do not change.

There are two types of mechanical processing technology after cladding: one is rough turning → fine turning → polishing; the other is rough turning → grinding → polishing. After fine turning, the surface roughness value after polishing by a special polishing machine can reach Ra0.4 μm or below.

3) Economic Analysis. According to research and calculation, the cost of using laser cladding technology is 3189.5 yuan/m2, and the cost of using electroplating technology is 1450 yuan/m2.

(2) Application of stainless steel cladding remanufacturing technology in repairing hydraulic cylinder piston rods

According to the introduction in reference [126], investigations have shown that due to the long-term use of comprehensive support in harsh underground natural environments, under high load conditions, the hydraulic cylinder piston rod extends about 2/3 out of the hydraulic cylinder during operation, making it prone to corrosion and bending. This results in poor dust seal performance, creating a vicious cycle that brings dust and impurities into the hydraulic cylinder along with the extension and retraction of the piston rod. At the same time, due to most being used beyond their service life, pits appear on the rod surface. When the hydraulic cylinder piston rod extends, the seal ring at the pit position will cause seal failure, and the hydraulic cylinder cannot maintain pressure. For the above situations, methods such as re-copper plating or spraying wear-resistant plastic powder on the rod surface can be used. However, if the clearance exceeds the tolerance too much, copper plating cannot solve this problem, while spraying processes are often affected by various factors, causing the sprayed layer to easily fall off, and the hardness and impact resistance of the plastic powder are also poor. Through research, using stainless steel cladding technology for piston rod remanufacturing repair can increase surface hardness, reduce surface roughness values, and improve wear resistance and corrosion resistance, thereby improving the overall service life of the hydraulic cylinder. Therefore, using stainless steel cladding technology for remanufacturing repair of comprehensive support hydraulic cylinder piston rods can achieve good economic benefits.

Hydraulic cylinder piston rod stainless steel powder cladding repair is a technology that uses high-energy laser beam scanning to melt the stainless steel powder in the scanned area to achieve surface hardening. Its basic principle is to use a laser with a certain energy density (10^3-10^5 W/cm^2) to irradiate the hydraulic cylinder piston rod, rapidly heating the worn surface layer area to above the phase transition point; below the melting point, the temperature at this time causes the stainless steel powder coated on the workpiece surface to reach the melting point and start melting, while the workpiece substrate remains in a cold state, with a large temperature gradient between the heating area and the substrate; when the laser beam stops irradiating, due to the effect of heat conduction, the heating area will rapidly cool (10^6-10^8 °C/s) and undergo stainless steel powder solution cooling, melting the stainless steel powder onto the metal hydraulic cylinder piston rod surface, achieving repair of the workpiece surface layer.

Using stainless steel cladding remanufacturing technology to repair hydraulic cylinder piston rods has the following characteristics:

1) The laser beam provides rapid heating and self-cooling, without the need for insulation and cooling liquid cooling, making it a non-polluting green heat treatment process that can easily achieve cladding repair of the hydraulic cylinder piston rod surface.

2) Due to the fast laser heating speed, small heat-affected zone, and surface scanning heating, i.e., instantaneous local heating, the deformation of the repaired hydraulic cylinder piston rod is very small.

3) Due to the very small laser scattering angle and good directionality, it can accurately perform local melting repair on the hydraulic cylinder piston rod surface through a light guide system.

4) The cladding layer thickness of laser surface cladding is generally 0.7-1.5 mm. This repair technology can repair hydraulic cylinder piston rods with surface scratch and wear depths exceeding 1.5 mm.

In summary, using stainless steel powder cladding technology to repair various mining comprehensive support hydraulic cylinder piston rods is both economically and technically feasible. Multiple batches of experiments have been completed in Xinxin Mining Group with good results.

2. Application of high-frequency welding and brush plating remanufacturing technology in repairing the piston rod of the slewing hydraulic cylinder on ship-mounted pile driving machines

According to the introduction in reference [60], high-frequency welding multi-metal defect repair is a technology that uses a high-frequency welding multi-metal defect repair machine (referred to as the multi-metal defect repair machine, which is a patented product of Beijing Aoyukexin Group) to repair defects on the surface of various metal component surfaces (such as pores and sand holes in castings, peeling and wear marks generated during the use of different metal components). The working principle of the multi-metal defect repair machine is that when the equipment is working, it can charge the capacitor in a cycle of 10^-3-10^-1s, and in an ultra-short time of 10^-6-10^-5s, high-frequency discharge can be performed. Using various metal filler materials as electrodes of the repair machine, when they contact the defect part of the metal substrate to be repaired, the high-frequency discharge voltage will break down the gas to form plasma, thereby generating electric sparks with temperatures above 6000°C, instantly melting the electrode (metal filler material) and the contact part (position) with the metal material of the substrate to be repaired, and then transitioning to the surface layer of the part to be repaired. Since an alloying effect is generated between the filler material and the substrate, it diffuses and infiltrates into the interior of the part to be repaired, forming a diffusion layer, obtaining a high-strength metallurgical bond.

Since during the welding process, the time between each discharge and the next discharge is extremely short, the repair machine has enough relative stopping time, so the heat will quickly diffuse to the outside through the substrate, and the repaired part of the substrate will not accumulate heat. Although the temperature rise of the substrate is almost maintained at room temperature, due to the instantaneous melting, the temperature of the electrode filler material can reach about 1000°C.

When using high-frequency discharge for repair processing, although the input heat is low, the bonding strength of the molten zone is very high. This is because the high temperature instantly generated by the electrode filler material melts the filler material metal, and it quickly transitions to the contact part with the substrate metal, forming a strong diffusion layer similar to the filler material "taking root" deep into the surface layer of the repaired part, and some may even form metallurgical bonding, thus showing very high bonding performance.

After research, it was decided to use a repair scheme combining high-frequency fusion welding and brush plating. The specific repair steps are as follows.

(1) Disassembly and decomposition of the hydraulic cylinder

1) Overall disassembly of the hydraulic cylinder. This ship-mounted pile driver's variable amplitude hydraulic cylinder has a maximum outer diameter of 1.27 m, a total length of 11.66 m, and a net weight of about 28 t. Among these, the piston rod, piston, and piston rod hinge head weigh 12 t, the upper end cover weighs 1.0 t, the bottom end cover weighs 3.0 t, and the cylinder barrel weighs 12 t. Before disassembling the hydraulic cylinder, the piston rod must be retracted to the limit position, the hoses removed, and the joints sealed. Use lifting equipment to lift the hydraulic cylinder, remove the hinge pin, then load the hydraulic cylinder onto a truck, transport it, and bring it into the factory.

2) Decomposition of the hydraulic cylinder. Remove the vent screw, take out the steel ball, connect a prepared pipe joint to the vent hole, connect the pipe, and inject compressed air into the lower cylinder (pressure is 0.6-0.8 MPa). Discharge the hydraulic oil in the upper cylinder into a clean oil drum (20 empty oil drums should be prepared). Place a prepared support trolley (or use sleepers) under the piston rod, and use compressed air to push out the piston and piston rod assembly (stroke is 8.25 m), trying to move the piston to the limit position to drain as much hydraulic oil as possible from the hydraulic cylinder; at the same time, during this process, ensure the concentricity of the cylinder barrel with the piston and piston rod.

a) Remove the upper end cover. Use a trolley to support the bottom of the upper end cover, clean the screws on the upper end cover and its surroundings, and use a special wrench to remove the screws. Weld two top rod nuts symmetrically on the end cover, and use threaded top rods to push out the upper end cover.

b) Remove the bottom end cover. Clean the screws on the bottom end cover and its surroundings, and use a special wrench to remove the screws.

c) Pull out the piston and piston rod. When the piston is about to be pulled out, the trolley should move closer to the piston.

Because this time a repair process combining high-frequency fusion welding and brush plating was adopted, the piston and piston rod do not need to be further decomposed, which reduces the amount of disassembly work and difficulty.

(2) Inspection of the hydraulic cylinder

1) Clean the cylinder barrel (inner wall), piston, and piston rod, etc. with light diesel, using tools such as silk cloth.

2) Check and measure the dimensions and tolerances of each mating surface, as well as the straightness, roundness, and cylindricity of the cylinder barrel, piston rod, etc.

3) Check whether there is eccentric wear on the guide sleeve of the upper end cover.

After inspection, the results are as follows:

a) The piston rod is severely worn and rusted. The original chrome plating layer on the surface is worn and rusted for a length of 4.6 m, with a depth of 1.0 mm.

b) The wear on the inner wall of the cylinder barrel has expanded from the original three scratch grooves to a wear surface with a width of 300-500 mm, a length of 5.1 m, and a depth of 1.0 mm.

c) The guide sleeve of the upper end cover is severely worn, and the V-shaped seal ring is severely deformed.

(3) Repair of the piston rod

1) Repair requirements. Achieve the purposes of wear resistance and corrosion resistance, with a hardness above 55 HRC and a surface roughness value not higher than Ra0.2μm.

2) Process flow. Use a repair process combining high-frequency fusion welding and brush plating. The process flow is: trimming and grinding the base surface → cleaning and washing → high-frequency fusion welding → trimming and grinding the high-frequency fusion welding surface → brush plating → restoring the dimensions of the worn and corroded surfaces → mechanical polishing of the repaired surfaces.

3) Repair process.

① Cleaning and determining the repair reference. Hang the piston rod to be repaired onto a walking trolley (the distance between trolleys should not be less than 5 m). Since it has not been decomposed from the piston, pay attention to protecting the seals on the piston. Use a cleaning agent to clean the oil stains on the surface of the piston rod, then use an external diameter vernier caliper to measure the dimensions of the reference surface (measure the unworn surface of the lower end of the piston rod near the piston), and use this surface dimension as the reference for repair.

② Grinding of the surface to be repaired. Use a grinding machine to grind off the remaining chrome plating layer on the worn and corroded surface. For the worn surface, where the wear is more severe, first use a grinding machine for rough grinding, then use a grinding machine for grinding. The grinding belt should be adjusted according to the grinding situation, and should be used in the order from coarse to fine grinding belts. For areas with deep corrosion, first use an angle grinder for grinding, then use a high-frequency fusion welding repair machine to weld the corroded areas flat, and then use a special grinding tool to grind (polish) the welded areas flat.

③ Use brush plating technology to brush plate the surface to be repaired. Use reverse pulse brush plating to brush plate the surface to be repaired. The process is as follows: electrolytic cleaning → activation with activating solution No. 1 → activation with activating solution No. 2 → activation with activating solution No. 3 → activation with activating solution No. 4 → activation with activating solution No. 5 → activation with activating solution No. 6 → activation with chrome surface activating solution → special nickel → nickel-chromium alloy. For areas with more corrosion or pitting, activation with copper activating solution can be used.

During the brush plating process, the quality of the brush plating layer is determined by the controlled temperature and current, as well as the technical level of the operator. Especially for the brush plating of transition surfaces, whether two materials can be well contacted, and the dimensional control of the transition surfaces, etc. are difficult points. During the brush plating process, using the stress-relief interlayer process can ensure that the brush plating layer has no cracks, no pitting, etc.

④ Mechanical polishing and inspection. The thickness of the brush plating layer should leave a certain amount of allowance for polishing and machining. After brush plating, mechanical polishing should be performed. 7.1.2 Cleanliness Indicators Required for Hydraulic Systems and Their Components

7.1.3 Flushing and Filtering of Pipelines and Working Medium in Hydraulic System
The initial cleanliness level of hydraulic system will affect the performance and service life of hydraulic system. If the solid particle pollutants generated during the assembly and manufacturing process of hydraulic system are not removed, the solid particle pollutants will circulate in the hydraulic system and damage the components of hydraulic system. In order to reduce the probability of such damage, the hydraulic oil and the inner surface of hydraulic system need to be filtered and flushed to reach the specified cleanliness level.
Flushing the pipelines of hydraulic system is a method to remove the solid particle pollutants inside the hydraulic system, but it is not the only method. The flushing and filtering of pipelines and working medium in hydraulic system should be carried out according to the following methods.
1. Preparation
1) From the perspective of pipeline flushing of hydraulic system, the following inspections should be done on hydraulic system and components:
① Whether the most pollution sensitive components in hydraulic system, such as proportional valves and servo valves, have been removed and replaced by flushing plates or other valves.
② Whether there are blind ends that cannot be flushed in the design of hydraulic system.
③ Whether there are parallel connected pipelines in the design of hydraulic system, and it is impossible to make each pipeline have sufficient flow.
④ Whether there are flow limiting components or internal filters in the hydraulic system.
⑤ Whether there are components that are vulnerable to damage by high flow rate or solid particle pollutants in the hydraulic system.
⑥ Whether all pipelines in the hydraulic system can be connected to each other for flushing.
The problem of pipeline flushing in hydraulic system should be fully considered at the design stage, otherwise, changing the hydraulic circuit or removing some components for flushing will cause trouble or adverse consequences to pipeline flushing. However, bypassing or isolating some components is a conventional practice during pipeline flushing.
2) In order to enable the pipeline flushing of hydraulic system to reach the specified cleanliness level, the following influencing factors also need to be considered:
① The components, pipes and oil tank in the hydraulic system must be cleaned and comply with the cleanliness index specified in the relevant standards.
② The initial cleanliness of the hydraulic oil in the oil tank or newly injected should comply with the requirements of hydraulic pump.
③ If the hydraulic system is designed with an independent cooling and filtering system, it is necessary to make it run for a sufficient long time first.
④ It is necessary to design a proper flushing program.
⑤ It is necessary to establish a turbulent state in the pipeline.
⑥ Select a filter with a suitable filtering ratio to ensure that the specified cleanliness level can be reached within the allowed time period;
⑦ Both parties should confirm the relevant standards (or methods) for extracting oil samples and the standards based on which the oil sample inspection is carried out before pipeline flushing.
877:
Inspection report on oil sample issued by qualified inspection unit is one of the necessary technical documents provided by Party B to Party A, so it is also necessary for both parties to determine the inspection unit before pipeline flushing.

2. Pipeline Flushing
1) Establish special files for the pipelines to be flushed and record their achieved cleanliness levels.
2) The flushing method should be adapted to the actual conditions. However, in order to obtain satisfactory flushing results, the following main criteria should be met before flushing:
   a) The initial cleanliness of the hydraulic oil in the oil tank should meet the requirements of the hydraulic pump and be comparable to the cleanliness level specified in the hydraulic system.
   b) Do not introduce air into the hydraulic system. If necessary, the hydraulic oil can be filled to overflow state (design upper limit), or necessary air separation measures can be taken, such as heating and degassing.
   c) If a flushing filter is installed on the hydraulic system, it should be installed on the return pipeline and close to the return port.
   d) A coarse filter can also be installed at the suction port of the hydraulic pump.
   e) The installed flow and temperature measuring devices should be as close as possible to the return port.
The filtering characteristics of the flushing filter should be selected according to the cleanliness level required by the hydraulic system, for example, the allowable cleanliness level (ACL) of the hydraulic system. ACL represents an acceptable contamination level, and ACL should be coordinated with the contamination level that the most sensitive hydraulic component (such as proportional valve, servo valve) can accept and the allowable service life of the filter. If ACL is not specified, the classification specified in ISO4406 can be used as a guide for selecting filter accuracy, as shown in Table 7-14.

3) The hydraulic oil with a Reynolds number (Re) greater than 4000 should be used to flush the pipeline. Re and the required flow rate (qv) can be calculated by formula (7-1) or formula (7-2).
   Re = 21220qv / (vd) (7-1)
   or

   where qv is the flow rate, in L/min; v is the kinematic viscosity, in mm²/s; d is the inner diameter of the pipeline, in mm.

   It may be difficult to obtain Re greater than 4000. Re increases with the increase of hydraulic oil flow rate or the decrease of viscosity. Reducing the viscosity of hydraulic oil is the preferred method to obtain turbulence.

   When the Reynolds number Re ≤ 3000, the cleaning process of the system is permeation washing; when the Reynolds number Re ≥ 3000, the cleaning process of the system is flushing.

4) It is preferable to use the working medium of the hydraulic system for flushing or use hydraulic oil with the same viscosity grade as the working medium for flushing.

5) The filter should be equipped with a clogging monitoring device (such as a pressure differential indicator) and the filter element should be replaced in time according to the clogging of the filter element.

6) The minimum flushing time required for hydraulic system pipelines mainly depends on the capacity and complexity of the hydraulic system. Even if the oil sample indicates that the specified cleanliness level has been achieved after flushing for a short time, flushing should continue for a sufficiently long time.

7) The recommended minimum flushing time (t) can be estimated by formula (7-3).

7.1.4 Detection and Maintenance of Hydraulic System Working Medium
Detection and maintenance of the working medium of the hydraulic system are to ensure that the cleanliness level of the hydraulic oil required by the hydraulic system and components (hydraulic cylinder) is not inferior to the specified value and to extend the service life of the working medium.
Contaminants in hydraulic systems and components, especially solid particle contaminants, are the most common and harmful type of contaminants in hydraulic systems. They may be contaminants originally present (or remaining) in the hydraulic system and components (including piping), or contaminants that invade from the outside or are generated internally.
Contaminants that invade from the outside may be generated and invade the system as follows:
1) Inappropriate cleaning, installation, or maintenance allows solid particles, fibers, seal fragments, and other contaminants to invade the system.
2) Dust in the air invades the system through a tank with poor sealing or an air filter with low precision.
3) The hydraulic oil is contaminated during storage and transportation, or unqualified hydraulic oil is added to the system without fine filtration.
4) Dust is sucked in from the air when adding hydraulic oil in an open manner.
It should be emphasized that inappropriate cleaning of hydraulic components and piping during the manufacturing process of hydraulic systems may be a major source of contaminant invasion into the system. Inappropriate cleaning means that on the one hand, contaminants such as chips and sand particles that should be removed by cleaning are not removed from the hydraulic components and piping; on the other hand, new contaminants such as fabric fibers and dust are allowed to invade the hydraulic components and piping during cleaning.
Internal self-generated contaminants may be generated as follows:
1) Metal particles generated by normal mechanical wear of friction pairs of pumps, cylinders, and valves, or rubber particles generated by seal wear.
2) Debris from hoses or filter elements falling off.
3) Degradation products of the oil.
The types of these contaminant substances are generally as follows:
1) Particulate contaminants: rust, metal shavings, weld slag, sand, dust, etc.
2) Fiber contaminants: fibers, cotton yarn, seal tape pieces, paint coating layers, etc.
3) Chemical contaminants: hydraulic oil degradation caused by oxidation of the hydraulic oil or residual cleaning solvents and their products such as gels and sludge.
4) Water or air: water is brought in from the oil tank or the piston rod of the hydraulic cylinder, water leaks into the heat exchanger, air is mixed into the hydraulic oil, etc.
There is also a type of contaminant - energy contaminants. In a broad sense, static electricity, magnetic fields, thermal energy, and radiation in hydraulic systems are contaminants in the form of energy.

3. Hydraulic Oil Moisture Content Detection Method
JB/T 12920-2016 "Hydraulic Transmission - Hydraulic Oil Moisture Content Detection Method" stipulates the method of detecting hydraulic oil moisture content by Karl Fischer titration, which is suitable for detecting moisture content in hydraulic oil. Detection of moisture content in other system working media can also be carried out according to this standard.
(1) Working Condition Requirements for Karl Fischer Titrator
When detecting moisture content in hydraulic oil, the following working condition requirements should be met:
1) Ambient temperature: 3~30°C.
2) Relative humidity: ≤70%.
3) No vibration and electromagnetic interference that affects instrument use.
4) No corrosive gases in the room, with good ventilation facilities. The work area should avoid direct sunlight and be separated from the air conditioning system's air supply in the test room.

Karl Fischer titration instrument is a special testing instrument for water content in hydraulic oil, with a measuring range ≥10μg/g (H2O).

(2) Determination of test results

1) Repeatability. According to the operating requirements of JB/T12920-2016 standard, the same operator performs 3 tests on the same instrument for the same sample to be tested, and calculates the percentage difference (the difference between the maximum value and the minimum value, divided by the arithmetic mean of the 3 test results, taking the absolute value of the percentage). Take the arithmetic mean of the three test results as the value of the water content report of the sample to be tested.

4. Monitoring of particulate contamination in hydraulic oil

GB/T37162.1-2018 "Monitoring of particulate contamination of hydraulic fluid - Part 1: General rules" specifies methods and techniques for monitoring particulate contamination of hydraulic systems, and describes the advantages and disadvantages of various methods to correctly select monitoring methods under given conditions. The methods described in this standard are applicable to monitoring: cleanliness of hydraulic systems; flushing process; auxiliary equipment and test benches.

This standard is also applicable to monitoring other liquids (such as lubricants, fuels, processing liquids).

Instruments used to monitor particulate contamination cannot be used or called particle counters, even if they use the same physical principles as particle counters. For health and safety requirements, see GB/T37162.1-2018.

(1) General rules

The selection of monitoring instruments or methods depends on, but is not limited to:

1) Use of the instrument, i.e. working method.

2) Purpose of analysis.

3) Parameters to be tested.

4) Nature of the liquid.

(2) Selection of monitoring methods

First, comprehensively consider the various working parameters described in Appendix A and Appendix B of GB/T37162.1-2018, then select the monitoring method according to the monitoring requirements, and then select the monitoring instrument.

Appendix A of GB/T37162.1-2018 A.1 explains various working and analysis methods, A.2 gives the various factors that should be comprehensively considered when selecting monitoring methods, and also provides a selection table. When particles pass through the parallel beam, the light is scattered and diffracted at different angles according to the particle size. Mesh Blockage Method
(1) Outline
The mesh blockage method is a detection method that measures the change in the characteristics of a mesh when a liquid sample passes through a mesh with uniform and known openings (or micropores).
When the liquid sample passes through the mesh, particles larger than the pore size of the micropores are filtered out, and the mesh gradually becomes blocked, resulting in an increase in the pressure difference across the mesh (constant flow principle) or a decrease in the flow rate through the mesh (constant pressure difference principle).
By analyzing the number of micropore blockages (blockage condition) and the volume of liquid flowing through the mesh, or by using calibration methods, the concentration of particles in the liquid sample larger than the mesh pore size can be estimated, and then the detection results can be converted to contamination level codes (GB/T 14039-2002).
Since the pressure drop across the mesh is proportional to viscosity, for constant flow detection instruments, the influence of viscosity changes must be corrected during the analysis, and the degree of correction depends on the instrument used. Changes in the density of the liquid sample during the analysis have little effect on the detection results.
See ISO 21018-3.
(2) Main Features
1) It can be used for various analysis methods:
   - Online analysis of high and low pressure pipelines
   - Analysis of oil tanks and container suction
   - Offline analysis of sample bottles
2) It can detect various liquids (such as mineral oil, synthetic liquids, emulsions, solvents, fuels, cleaning liquids, and water-based liquids)
3) As long as the state of the liquid does not change during the analysis, liquids with optical interfaces can be detected (such as water in oil, gas in liquid, and incompatible liquids)
4) A wide range of contamination levels can be detected using a single instrument
5) Depending on the type of instrument, the analysis time is usually 3 to 6 minutes.
(3) Limitations
1) The particle size range is limited (currently available instruments usually have only one or two meshes)
2) Constant pressure difference instruments cannot detect liquid samples with low particle contamination levels (such as contamination levels better than /13/11)
3) Constant flow instruments take a long time (about 8 minutes) to detect liquid samples with low particle contamination levels (such as contamination levels better than /10/8)
4) Individual particle sizes cannot be measured because this method is only limited to monitoring the general level of particle contamination in the system
According to Table A.7 in GB/T 37162.1-2018, the measured size is 6 to 14 μm.
Weight Analysis Method
(1) Outline
The weight analysis method is a detection method that separates and collects particles in a liquid sample on a pre-weighed filter membrane (pore size ≤1.0μm) by vacuum filtration, and then reweighs the filter membrane after removing oil and drying to calculate the mass of particles.
See GB/T 27613-2011 "Hydraulic Transmission - Liquid Contamination - Determination of Particle Contamination Level by Weighing Method"
(2) Main Features
1) It can measure a large amount of contaminants
2) Contaminants on the filter membrane can be analyzed by other methods
(3) Limitations
1) The error is very large when detecting liquid samples with low contamination levels
2) Unless the volume of the analysis liquid is increased, it is not suitable for systems that are too clean (contamination level better than 17/15/12, see GB/T 14039-2002)
3) The analysis time for liquid samples is usually 35 minutes
4) Particle size distribution cannot be measured
5) Auxiliary equipment (such as ovens and balances) is required
Magnetic Detection Method
(1) Outline
The magnetic detection method is a detection method that measures the change in the radiated magnetic field when a test liquid containing magnetic and paramagnetic particles passes through the sensing area. This type of instrument has various configurations:
1) Some instruments can place the sample (liquid containing particles, filter membrane containing particles, or substrate containing magnetic separation particles) into the detector to measure the content of magnetic particles. Through calibration, this content can be given as a dimensionless index or in the form of mass fraction. Such instruments have a wide range of particle sizes that can be measured and can detect submicron particles (<0.5μm).

Automatic Particle Counting Method
(1) Overview
In this type of instrument, the liquid sample to be detected passes through a narrow channel illuminated by light (such as a low-power laser) of the sensor. When a single particle passes through the light beam, the amount of light received by the detector (usually located on the opposite side of the liquid flow) is reduced, and the amount of reduction is proportional to the projected surface area of the particle. Thus, when a particle passes through the light beam, it will generate a voltage pulse, which is then detected and recorded by the instrument. The correspondence between the particle size of the instrument/sensor and the pulse voltage can be obtained through calibration according to GB/T18854-2015 "Hydraulic Transmission - Calibration of Liquid Automatic Particle Counters" or GB/T21540-2008 "Hydraulic Transmission - On-line Automatic Particle Counting System Calibration and Verification Methods". - Fixed installation in the main line of the system for analysis
- Suction analysis from tanks and containers

2) Wide particle size measurement range, up to 1.0~3000μm (depending on the design, the dynamic range of such instruments is usually 50~100)

3) Heavily contaminated liquids need to be diluted before detection, otherwise incorrect results will be produced
4) When there are a large number of small particles smaller than the minimum set size of the instrument in the liquid sample, it will affect the accuracy of the count
5) High environmental requirements for off-line analysis
6) Large particles (>200μm) can block the sensor
7) Detection results are easily affected by the state of the liquid (such as gels and opacity)

Optical Microscope Counting Method
(1) Overview
Particles in the liquid sample are separated and collected on a filter membrane through vacuum filtration. The pore size of the filter membrane depends on the state of the liquid sample and the minimum particle size to be counted, but is typically 1.2 μm. For ease of manual counting, the filter membrane usually has 3.1 mm grids printed on it, but when using image analysis, there is no need to use a filter membrane with grids.
After the filter membrane is dried, it can be directly placed under an optical microscope for analysis using incident light, or it can be treated to become transparent and analyzed using transmitted light. Using a calibrated eyepiece reticle (manual counting) or by analyzing the number of pixels occupied by the particles (image analysis), the particle size is measured by the longest chord of the particles. Both methods are calibrated using traceable micrometers.
When performing manual counting, statistical techniques can be used to reduce measurement time. First, the size and count of individual particles in a selected number of grids are measured to obtain the values for any given size, and then these values are corrected to obtain the results for the entire volume of the liquid sample that passed through the filter membrane. When using image analysis for automatic counting, the entire surface of the filter membrane can be measured and analyzed. When measuring different particle sizes, different microscope magnifications need to be used.
Image analysis can also use a camera to convert the particles collected on the filter membrane or the particles in the liquid flow directly into images, and then use a computer or electronic device for image analysis.
See GB/T 20082-2006 "Hydraulic Transmission - Liquid Contamination - Method for Determining Particle Contamination Degree Using Optical Microscope"
(2) Main Features
1) Considered a standard method, most international and national standards that specify counting methods involve this method
2) Wide range of particle sizes that can be measured (≥2 μm)
3) Particles are visible, allowing timely detection of potential counting problems
4) Low equipment cost for manual counting
5) Information about particle types can be obtained when needed
6) If the liquid is filterable, the test results are independent of the state of the liquid
7) Image analysis can be used for automatic detection, reducing human error and improving measurement accuracy
8) Image analysis can be performed both offline and online
(3) Limitations of Manual Counting Method
1) High skill level required
2) Counting 6 particle sizes takes 30 minutes
3) High environmental requirements
4) Only used for offline analysis
5) Particles are easily obscured by sludge or gel
(4) Limitations of Image Analysis Method
1) When particles overlap or are not in focus, manual processing is required, resulting in increased testing time
2) To make the results more representative, retesting and verification at other magnifications are required
Scanning Electron Microscope Method
(1) Overview
A small piece of the filter membrane containing particles (usually 1 cm²) is fixed on an aluminum base, a conductive layer (gold, silver, or carbon) is sputtered on it, and then it is placed in the vacuum chamber of a scanning electron microscope for electron bombardment. The electron beam irradiates the sample (similar to the role of photons in an optical microscope), and the image is displayed on a monitor. Finally, the image is electronically processed and the corresponding results are output in a manner similar to image analysis (see the optical microscope counting method above).
When the electron beam is focused on the surface of the sample, it causes ionization of the atoms, producing characteristic X-rays of the material. By analyzing the spectrum of the characteristic X-rays, the elemental composition and content of the particles can be obtained.
See ISO 16232-7 and ISO 16232-8
(2) Main Features
1) High resolution (detection lower limit for particles is 0.01 μm)
2) When using image analysis, both particle size and quantity can be provided simultaneously
3) Elemental composition of particles can be provided
4) High-definition images that are almost unaffected by depth of field can be provided
5) Software can be used to create particle maps based on type and size
(3) Limitations
1) Only used for laboratory analysis
2) High cost and long time consumption (analysis time is usually 1-3 hours)
3) Requires skilled operators
4) Limited depth of electron penetration into the material (about 5 μm)

Film Erosion Method
(1) Summary
Install the monitoring instrument on a branch line of the hydraulic system (online analysis), using a nozzle to direct the fluid flow at a relatively high velocity (25 m/s) to spray onto one of two metal strips in the sensor. The second metal strip in the sensor is positioned directly opposite the first, with both strips vacuum-coated with a thin conductive film that, when electrically connected, forms a bridge network. Particles colliding with the active sensor will erode part of the conductive film, changing the metal strip's resistance. The amount of resistance change is proportional to the particle's concentration, hardness, and erosive characteristics. The instrument records the resistance change over time and frequency, expressing it as erosion rate. This method can detect individual particles of larger sizes.
(2) Main Features
1) Can provide particle hardness and erosion characteristics
2) Used for online/main line analysis
(3) Limitations
1) Cannot detect particle size, quantity, or contamination level
2) Not commonly used in the fluid power industry
3) Detection results are related to fluid viscosity
4) Detection results vary with particle hardness

7. Thermal Pollution's Effect on Hydraulic Oil
Understanding excessive heat in hydraulic working media as a form of energy pollution is itself a scientific advancement, because "contaminants" as defined in GB/T 17446-2012 do not include energy-based pollutants. Although this energy pollutant is determined under given conditions, when conditions change, it may no longer be considered a pollutant.
Based on practical experience, when a hydraulic system experiences systemic failures such as multiple component and pipeline external leaks, accelerated wear of multiple components, or jamming/clogging of various components, it may have been operating for an extended period at high temperatures or for a shorter period at even higher temperatures. In such cases, the most obvious manifestation should be the deterioration of the hydraulic oil in the original system.

The greatest danger of high hydraulic oil temperature is the final decomposition of the hydraulic oil itself, accompanied by the loss of viscosity and lubricity of the hydraulic oil. Decomposition will lead to the formation of varnish (oxide ions) substances, acidic substances, and sediment substances in the hydraulic oil. Varnish and sediment substances will cause valve sticking and eventually cause blockage, and also cause throttle orifice blockage; acidic substances will corrode metal surfaces and accelerate the wear of pumps, cylinders, and valves.

In most cases, high temperature will cause severe loss of viscosity and lubricity of hydraulic oil. Thin hydraulic oil may cause greater impact and vibration, increase the possibility of component damage, and even cause loosening of assemblies and connections with the base. If lubricity is lost and the lubricating oil film disappears, metal-to-metal direct contact will occur, leaving scratch marks on the surface.

Temperature is the main accelerator of hydraulic oil oxidation. For every 10°C increase in temperature, the oxidation reaction will double. When the temperature is below 60°C, the oxidation rate will be very low; when the temperature is above 60°C, the service life of mineral-based oil will be halved for every 10°C increase in temperature, and the service life loss rate will be as high as 97% at 100°C.

Based on these facts, a lower working temperature of the hydraulic system is beneficial to minimize oxidation reaction and hydraulic oil degradation. However, the oil temperature in the oil tank is not the actual oil temperature, and the temperature at the pump outlet can represent the actual temperature. In this way, the area where local oxidation is very severe will be hotter.

The thermal stability of oil refers to its ability to resist decomposition caused by temperature. If its use is not damaged within a specific range, then the upper limit of the hydraulic oil's extreme temperature is determined.

Some literature introduces that most failures of hydraulic systems, especially electro-hydraulic servo valve-servo hydraulic cylinder control systems, are caused by hydraulic oil contamination, especially solid particle contaminants. When the system exhibits intermittent characteristics or other unreasonable characteristics, and unexplained failures occur, it should be suspected that it is caused by solid particle contaminants in the hydraulic oil.

7.2 Selection and Use of Hydraulic Cylinders

7.2.1 Selection of Hydraulic Cylinders

1. Guidelines for Selecting Hydraulic Cylinders

Guidelines for selecting hydraulic cylinders are given in Reference [54].

Improper selection of hydraulic cylinders will not only cause economic losses to users, but may also lead to accidents. When selecting, the working conditions of the hydraulic cylinder should be carefully analyzed, appropriate structural and installation types should be selected, and reasonable parameters should be determined.

The selection of hydraulic cylinders should mainly consider the following points:

1) Structure type of hydraulic cylinder
2) Cylinder forward stroke output force or cylinder return stroke output force
3) Nominal (maximum rated or rated) pressure and working pressure range
4) Cylinder diameter and piston rod diameter
5) Maximum stroke of the cylinder and working stroke range of the cylinder
6) Reciprocating speed
7) Installation type
8) Environmental conditions (such as ambient temperature, environmental pollutants, etc.)
9) Usage conditions
10) Working medium
11) Sealing device
12) Other devices (such as buffering devices, exhaust (discharge) devices, etc.)

When selecting hydraulic cylinders, priority should be given to using standard hydraulic cylinders from related series, which has many advantages: first, it can greatly shorten the design and manufacturing cycle; second, it is convenient for spare parts, and has greater interchangeability and versatility. In addition, standard hydraulic cylinders have been carefully analyzed and calculated during design, have undergone bench tests and field tests, and professional manufacturers have dedicated equipment, jigs, and relatively complete testing equipment, and the quality is guaranteed.

2. Selection of Hydraulic Cylinder

2.1 Selection of Hydraulic Cylinder Structure Type

The selection of hydraulic cylinder structure type should consider the following factors:

1) Working conditions of the hydraulic cylinder
2) Installation conditions of the hydraulic cylinder
3) Space limitations of the installation site
4) Maintenance and repair convenience
5) Cost and price factors

According to the above factors, the following hydraulic cylinder structure types can be selected:

1) Piston type hydraulic cylinder: suitable for high-pressure, high-speed, and high-precision applications
2) Plunger type hydraulic cylinder: suitable for low-pressure, low-speed, and low-precision applications
3) Telescopic type hydraulic cylinder: suitable for applications with large stroke requirements
4) Double-acting type hydraulic cylinder: suitable for applications requiring bidirectional force output
5) Single-acting type hydraulic cylinder: suitable for applications requiring unidirectional force output
6) Cushion type hydraulic cylinder: suitable for applications requiring cushioning effect
7) Self-aligning type hydraulic cylinder: suitable for applications with installation angle deviation
8) Special structure type hydraulic cylinder: suitable for special applications with special requirements

When selecting the hydraulic cylinder structure type, the following points should be noted:

1) The selected structure type should meet the working requirements of the hydraulic cylinder
2) The selected structure type should be able to adapt to the installation conditions of the hydraulic cylinder
3) The selected structure type should be able to meet the space limitations of the installation site
4) The selected structure type should be convenient for maintenance and repair
5) The selected structure type should have reasonable cost and price

In summary, the selection of hydraulic cylinder structure type should be based on the specific working conditions and requirements, comprehensively consider various factors, and select the most suitable structure type.

Selection of Main Parameters for Hydraulic Cylinders

When selecting hydraulic cylinders, according to the requirements of the motion mechanism, not only must the hydraulic cylinder have sufficient acting (output) force, speed, and stroke, but also sufficient strength and rigidity.

However, in some special cases, to use standard hydraulic cylinders or to utilize existing hydraulic cylinders, such as the rated pressure of hydraulic cylinders, it is permissible to slightly exceed their rated working range. For example, if the rated working pressure of a hydraulic cylinder is 6.3 MPa, to increase its acting (output) force to push mechanical motion exceeding the rated load, it is allowed to increase its working pressure to 6.5 MPa or slightly higher. This is because when designing hydraulic cylinder parts, there is a certain safety margin. However, the following issues should be noted:

① The rated values of hydraulic cylinders should not be exceeded too much, otherwise the safety factor will be excessively reduced, making accidents prone to occur.

② The working conditions of hydraulic cylinders should be relatively stable, and the hydraulic system should not have unexpected impact pressure.

③ The strength of certain parts of the hydraulic cylinder should be recalculated. In particular, the strength of the cylinder barrel, the connection strength of the cylinder head, and the longitudinal bending strength of the piston rod should be checked.

Note: It is not recommended to select hydraulic cylinders beyond the nominal pressure, maximum rated pressure, or rated pressure of hydraulic cylinders, especially for hydraulic cylinders that have been used for a period of time.

Selection of Installation Type for Hydraulic Cylinders

Selection of Reasonable Installation Type

There are many types of hydraulic cylinder installations, each with different characteristics. When selecting the installation type for a hydraulic cylinder, it is necessary to ensure that the machinery and hydraulic cylinder can move freely, make the hydraulic cylinder work stably, and place the installation part in a favorable stress state. In order to obtain greater freedom of movement, the hydraulic cylinders of construction machinery and agricultural machinery mostly use swing axis types, such as ear ring hinge shafts or ball heads, such as telescopic cylinders, luffing cylinders, dump cylinders, boom cylinders, and lifting cylinders; However, the hydraulic cylinders for the worktable of metal cutting machine tools all use fixed axis type hydraulic cylinders, such as bracket and flange installation types.

Ensure Sufficient Installation Strength

Installation components must have sufficient strength. For example, if the bracket of a bracket type hydraulic cylinder is very thin and lacks rigidity, even if the installation is correct, the cylinder barrel will warp upward under pressure, causing the piston to not move normally, and even accidents such as bending and breaking of the piston rod may occur.

Note: The installation components here should be considered as accessories of the cylinder; The bracket should be a bracket; However, there is no bracket type hydraulic cylinder, and the following is the same.

Try to Improve Stability

When selecting the installation type of hydraulic cylinders, try to use a type with better stability, such as the stability of the head hinge axis of a hinge axis type hydraulic cylinder is the best, and the stability of the tail hinge axis is the worst.

Note: "Hinge axis" should be "hinge pin".

Determine a Favorable Installation Direction

The same installation type, with different installation directions, will experience different forces. For example, the flange type hydraulic cylinder has four types: external flange at the head, internal flange at the head, external flange at the tail, and internal flange at the tail. Moreover, due to the different directions of the thrust and pull forces of the hydraulic cylinder, it constitutes eight working states of the flange. Among these eight working states, only two states are the best. For hydraulic cylinders that work in the direction of piston rod retraction, using an external flange at the head is most advantageous. When the working direction is to push out the piston rod, using an external flange at the tail is most advantageous. This is because only in these two cases will the flange not produce bending moments, while the other six working states will produce bending effects. In bracket type hydraulic cylinders, the overturning moment received by the radial bracket is the smallest, the tangential bracket is larger, and the axial bracket is the largest, all of which should be considered.
