Influence of Speed on Selection of Hydraulic Cylinder
Low Speed Movement
When the hydraulic cylinder moves at low speed, special attention should be paid to the crawling problem. There are many reasons for the crawling of hydraulic cylinders, but they can be summarized into the following three aspects:
① The friction force between the relative moving parts of the mechanism pushed by the hydraulic cylinder is too large, the friction resistance changes, and there are contaminants on the mutual friction surfaces, such as the guide rails of the machine tool table being adjusted too tightly, poor lubrication conditions, etc.
② The internal causes of the hydraulic system. Such as poor flow stability of the speed control valve, compressibility of the oil, water hammer effect (water hammer phenomenon) in the system, air entrainment, unclean oil, pulsation of hydraulic pressure, unreasonable circuit design, no back pressure in the return oil, etc.
③ Internal causes of the hydraulic cylinder. Such as excessive friction force of the seal, unreasonable clearance between sliding surfaces, low machining accuracy and surface finish (large surface roughness value), air entrainment in the hydraulic cylinder, poor rigidity of the piston rod, etc.
Therefore, when solving the crawling problem of the hydraulic cylinder at low speed, in addition to solving the external problems of the hydraulic cylinder, the internal problems of the hydraulic cylinder should also be solved, that is, corresponding technical measures should be taken in the structure. The main points to note are as follows:
① Select sealing parts with small sliding resistance, such as sliding seal, clearance seal, piston ring seal, plastic seal parts, etc.
② The piston rod should be subjected to stability verification.
③ Make the clearance between sliding surfaces as large as possible within the allowable range, so that even if there are assembly errors, it will not cause large unilateral friction between sliding surfaces and affect the sliding of the hydraulic cylinder.
④ The surface roughness value Ra of the sliding surface should be controlled between 0.05～0.2μm.
⑤ The guide sleeve should be made of materials that can be immersed in oil, such as gray cast iron, aluminum bronze, tin bronze, etc.
⑥ Adopt a reasonable exhaust device to remove the residual air in the hydraulic cylinder.
Note: The term "low speed" is not based on any standard; "sliding seal" is not clear what it refers to (sliding seal, plastic seal, etc. are not included in the sealing parts of piston and piston rod in Table 2 0 - 6 - 2 1 of reference [5 4]); the surface roughness value Ra of the sliding surface should be controlled between 0.05～0.2μm does not comply with the relevant standards and is impossible in practice.
High Speed Movement
The main problems of the high-speed hydraulic cylinder are the wear resistance of the sealing parts and the buffering problem.
① The maximum working speed of general rubber sealing parts is 60 m/min. But from the perspective of service life, the working speed is best not to exceed 20 m/min. Because when the sealing parts are rubbed at high speed, frictional heat will be generated, which is easy to cause burning, sticking, damage the sealing performance, and shorten the service life. In addition, high-speed hydraulic cylinders should use sealing parts that are not easy to twist, or take appropriate anti-twisting measures.
② When necessary, high-speed moving hydraulic cylinders should be equipped with buffering devices. To determine whether to use a buffering device, not only should the high speed of the hydraulic cylinder movement and the total mass and inertia force of the moving parts be considered, but also the working requirements of the hydraulic cylinder. Generally, when the speed of the hydraulic cylinder is in the range of 10～25 m/min, it is necessary to consider using a buffering device. If it is less than 10 m/min, it is not necessary to use a buffering structure. However, when the speed is greater than 25 m/min, only taking buffering measures on the hydraulic cylinder is often not enough, and buffering measures should also be considered in the return circuit.
Note: High-speed reciprocating hydraulic cylinders also have a problem, that is, the external leakage will be very large, and even cause the piston rod seal to fail.
Influence of Stroke on Selection of Hydraulic Cylinder
When using a long-stroke hydraulic cylinder, the following two issues should be noted:
① Floating measures for the cylinder barrel. The cylinder barrel of a long-stroke hydraulic cylinder is very long, and the oil temperature in the hydraulic system is prone to rise during work, which may cause the expansion and elongation of the cylinder body. If both ends of the cylinder barrel are fixed, the cylinder body cannot elongate, and internal stress or deformation will inevitably occur, affecting the normal operation of the hydraulic cylinder. Using one end fixed and the other end floating can avoid thermal stress in the cylinder barrel.
② Supporting measures for the piston rod. The piston rod (or plunger) of a long-stroke hydraulic cylinder is very long, and it is prone to sag when fully extended, causing unilateral wear on the guide sleeve, sealing parts, and piston rod. Therefore, it should be considered to use a support bracket to support the piston rod or plunger as much as possible.
Note: Long-stroke hydraulic cylinders may also have the problem of radial expansion of the cylinder barrel. Therefore, some hydraulic cylinders (such as those with a stroke exceeding 1 m) require the hydraulic cylinder to be stopped at half the stroke for internal leakage testing.

The Effect of Temperature on Hydraulic Cylinder Selection
Generally, hydraulic cylinders are suitable for operation within the temperature range of -10 to 80°C, with a maximum limit not exceeding -20 to 105°C. Since most hydraulic cylinders use nitrile rubber as sealing elements, their operating temperature cannot naturally exceed the working temperature range of nitrile rubber. Therefore, the working temperature of hydraulic cylinders is limited by the performance of the sealing elements.
Additionally, the working of hydraulic cylinders at different temperatures should also have different considerations for the selection of component materials and determination of dimensions.
① When working at high temperatures, sealing elements should use fluororubber, which can work for a long time at high temperatures of 200 to 250°C, and its durability is also significantly superior to that of nitrile rubber.
In addition to solving the heat resistance of sealing elements, heat insulation and cooling measures can also be taken on the hydraulic cylinder. For example, the cylinder barrel and piston rod can be covered with heat insulation materials such as asbestos to reduce the influence of the heat source on the hydraulic cylinder.
The piston rod can be made hollow to allow the introduction of circulating cooling air or cooling water. The cooling of the guide sleeve is to introduce cooling air or cooling water from the cylinder barrel to take away the heat of the guide sleeve sealing element and piston rod.
For hydraulic cylinders working at high temperatures, due to the different coefficients of linear expansion of various materials, the dimensions of sliding surfaces should be properly adjusted. For example, the coefficient of linear expansion of steel is 10.6×10⁻⁶/°C, while that of oil-resistant rubber is 10 to 20 times that of steel. Undoubtedly, the expansion of sealing elements will increase the friction between sliding surfaces, so it is necessary to properly adjust the dimensions of sealing elements. To reduce the thermal influence of high temperature on the dust ring, in addition to using an asbestos heat insulation device, an aluminum bronze plate can also be added to the outside of the dust ring.
If the hydraulic cylinder works at a temperature higher than the recrystallization temperature of the materials used, the changes of hydraulic cylinder components should also be considered, especially the creep and strength changes of fasteners.
② When working at low temperatures, such as hydraulic cylinders working below -20°C, it is best to also use fluororubber or nitrile rubber with a plasticizer of 0259 mixed grease to make sealing elements and dust rings. Since the piston rod is prone to ice formation when working below 0°C, to protect the dust ring from damage, an aluminum bronze alloy scraper is often added outside the dust ring.
Special attention should be paid to the low-temperature brittle fracture of the metal materials of hydraulic cylinders when they work at -40°C or below. The tensile strength and fatigue limit of steel increase with decreasing temperature (except for carbon steel with a carbon mass fraction of 0.6%, whose fatigue limit drops sharply at -40°C). However, the impact performance starts to decrease significantly at -40°C, resulting in poor toughness of the steel. When subjected to strong external impact, it is prone to fracture and damage. Therefore, for hydraulic cylinders working at -40°C or below, high-carbon steel, ordinary structural steel and other materials with low impact values should be avoided as much as possible, and nickel-based stainless steel, chromium-molybdenum steel and other alloy steels with high impact performance should be used.
If the hydraulic cylinder has welded parts, the strength and reliability of the weld seam under low-temperature conditions should also be carefully checked.
Note: Many contents in the above text are inaccurate, so be sure to pay attention when referring to them, such as the working temperature range of general hydraulic cylinders, the working temperature range of sealing elements and sealing materials, etc., which do not conform to the current relevant standards.
Effect of Working Environment on Hydraulic Cylinder Selection
Overview
Many hydraulic cylinders often work under harsh conditions. For example, excavators often work in wind and rain and constantly collide with dust, sand and stones; hydraulic cylinders working on the sea or seashore are easily eroded by seawater or humid air; hydraulic cylinders in chemical machinery often come into contact with acid and alkali solutions, etc. Therefore, corresponding measures should also be taken according to the working environment of hydraulic cylinders.
Dust Prevention Measures
In occasions with a lot of dust, such as foundry workshops and ore crushing sites, special attention should be paid to the dust prevention of hydraulic cylinders. The entry of dust into the hydraulic cylinder will not only cause faults but also increase the wear of the sliding surfaces of the hydraulic cylinder. At the same time, powdery metal will be precipitated, and this powdery metal will further accelerate the wear of the hydraulic cylinder, forming a vicious cycle.
In addition, the dust mixed into the hydraulic cylinder can also easily be carried into other hydraulic devices by the circulating hydraulic oil, causing faults or aggravating wear. Therefore, dust prevention is very important.
The external dust prevention measures for hydraulic cylinders mainly involve adding dust rings or dust covers. When selecting dust telescopic sleeves, attention should be paid to their durability during high-frequency actions, as well as whether the air holes of the telescopic sleeves can timely introduce sufficient air during high-speed movement. However, the installation of telescopic sleeves will bring some difficulties to the assembly and adjustment of hydraulic cylinders.
Note: After checking, the so-called "dust cover", "dust telescopic sleeve", "telescopic sleeve", etc. in reference [54] lightweight rod-type hydraulic cylinder and other references are called "protective cover".

Work Environment Impact on Hydraulic Cylinder Selection
Rust Prevention Measures
In humid air environments, particularly in marine, underwater, or coastal operations, hydraulic cylinders are very susceptible to corrosion and rust. Therefore, rust prevention measures are crucial.
One effective rust prevention method is chrome plating. After metal is chrome plated, its chemical stability resists corrosion from humid air and other gases, as well as from alkalis, nitric acid, organic acids, etc. Additionally, chrome plating increases hardness and reduces the friction coefficient, greatly enhancing wear resistance. However, it cannot resist corrosion from hydrochloric acid, hot sulfuric acid, etc.
For general rust prevention or merely for wear resistance, a chrome plating layer of only 0.02-0.03 mm is sufficient. For hydraulic cylinders operating in wind, rain, or humid air, the chrome plating layer should be above 0.05 mm, or nickel plating may be used. For hydraulic cylinders operating in seawater, it is best to use materials like stainless steel.
Additionally, bolts, nuts, and other components of the hydraulic cylinder should also consider using stainless steel or chromium-molybdenum steel.
Surface Hardening of Piston Rod
Some hydraulic cylinders operate under very harsh external conditions. For example, the piston rod of an excavator's hydraulic cylinder frequently collides with sand and gravel, while the piston rod or plunger of a press's hydraulic cylinder must directly press workpieces. Therefore, the surface hardness of the piston rod must be increased. The main method is high-frequency induction hardening, with a depth of 1-3 mm and a hardness of 40-50 HRC.
Impact of Force Conditions on Hydraulic Cylinder Selection
Overview
The force conditions on hydraulic cylinders are relatively complex. During alternating loads and frequent direction changes, hydraulic cylinders experience significant vibration; during heavy-load high-speed motion, they bear substantial inertial forces; under certain conditions, hydraulic cylinders must also bear lateral loads. Therefore, when designing and selecting hydraulic cylinders, appropriate measures should be taken according to the force conditions.
Vibration
There are many causes of vibration in hydraulic cylinders. In addition to reasons from pumps, valves, and the system, certain reasons from the cylinder itself can also cause vibration, such as improper part processing and assembly, excessive sealing resistance, direction change impact, etc.
Vibration can easily cause the connecting screws of hydraulic cylinders to loosen, which can lead to cylinder head separation, causing O-ring extrusion and damage, resulting in oil leakage.
There are many methods to prevent screws and nuts from loosening, such as using fine thread, installing spring washers, lock washers, lock nuts, pins, set screws, etc.
Additionally, tightening screws with stress greater than 50-60% above the yield strength can also prevent loosening.
For hydraulic cylinders with significant vibration, attention should not only be paid to whether the connecting threads and screws of the cylinder head are prone to loosening, but also to the loosening problem of the threads connecting the piston and piston rod.
Note: Based on the author's experience, the method of "tightening screws with stress greater than 50-60% above the yield strength to prevent loosening" has not been seen applied to hydraulic cylinders.
Inertial Force
When a hydraulic cylinder has a large load and high speed, it will be subjected to great inertial force, causing oil pressure to rise sharply, cylinder expansion, and the fastening parts to suddenly bear increased stress, which may even lead to cracking. Therefore, buffer structures need to be adopted.
Lateral Load
When a hydraulic cylinder bears a large lateral load, it is easy to squeeze out the oil film on one side of the sliding surface of the hydraulic cylinder, causing excessive wear, burning, or even seizure. When selecting materials for hydraulic cylinder sliding parts, the following measures should be considered:
1. Bronze surfacing on the outside of the piston or installation of a wear-resistant ring
2. High-frequency induction hardening of the piston rod, with guide sleeves made of bronze, cast iron, or nitrided steel
Attention should be paid to the impact of seals and working oil on hydraulic cylinder selection
When the friction force of seals is large, crawling and vibration are likely to occur. To reduce sliding resistance, seals with low friction are often used, such as sliding seals.
Additionally, the high-temperature resistance, low-temperature resistance, hardness, and elasticity of seals have a significant impact on the operation of hydraulic cylinders. Seals with poor high-temperature resistance are prone to sticking and adhesion when working at high temperatures; after the hardness of seals decreases, the phenomenon of being squeezed into gaps becomes more severe, further accelerating their damage and destroying the sealing effect; seals with poor low-temperature resistance are prone to permanent deformation in compression when working below -10°C, also affecting the sealing effect; seals with low hardness and poor elasticity are easily squeezed into the sealing gap and destroyed. Polyurethane seals are easily decomposed in aqueous solutions and should be given special attention.
The selection of working oil should consider the pump, valve, hydraulic cylinder, and the entire hydraulic system, as well as analyze the working conditions and temperature of the hydraulic device to select appropriate working oil.
When working under high temperature, high pressure, and low speed conditions, working oil with higher viscosity should generally be selected. When working under low temperature, low pressure, and high speed conditions, working oil with lower viscosity should be selected. Non-flammable oil should be used under hot and high-temperature conditions. However, it should be noted that when using water-based non-flammable oil, polyurethane rubber seals cannot be used; when using phosphate ester-based non-flammable oil, nitrile rubber seals cannot be used, otherwise hydrolysis and erosion will occur. High viscosity index oil should be used in precision machinery.

2. Selection Method for Multi-stage Hydraulic Cylinders
The UDZ type multi-stage hydraulic cylinder belongs to a single-acting telescopic sleeve hydraulic cylinder, with advantages such as small size and large stroke. The UDZ type multi-stage hydraulic cylinder has three installation types: cylinder bottom universal joint bearing ear ring, cylinder body hinge shaft, and flange. The cylinder head first stage is equipped with a universal joint bearing ear ring. The UDZ type multi-stage hydraulic cylinder has seven types of plunger diameters, which can be combined into six types of secondary cylinders, five types of tertiary cylinders, four types of quaternary cylinders, and three types of five-stage cylinders. Under the premise of allowing stability, the hydraulic cylinder manufacturer can provide UDZ type multi-stage hydraulic cylinders with strokes exceeding 20m.
Since the UDZ type multi-stage hydraulic cylinder is composed of cylinders with various plunger diameters, each stage of the cylinder has different speeds when the system flow rate is constant. During the lifting load process, under normal circumstances, the plunger with the largest diameter extends first and at a slower speed; when the stroke of the large plunger ends, the next stage large diameter plunger extends again, and its speed will become faster; the plunger with the smallest diameter extends last, but its extension speed is the fastest. When retracting under external force, the plunger with the smallest diameter retracts first, at the fastest speed; then it retracts in sequence; the plunger with the largest diameter retracts last, and the retraction speed is also the slowest. For the speed requirements of the UDZ type multi-stage hydraulic cylinder, generally the time required for the full stroke is specified, or the operating speed of a certain stage.
Taking the UDZ type multi-stage hydraulic cylinder as an example, the selection method for multi-stage cylinders is given below:
1) Working pressure. The rated pressure of the UDZ type multi-stage hydraulic cylinder is 16MPa (factory test pressure is 24MPa). The user system should be adjusted within the range of 16MPa. For short-stroke UDZ type multi-stage hydraulic cylinders with a stroke of less than or equal to 500mm per stage, the rated pressure can reach 21MPa, but it must be marked on the order model.
2) Determine the cylinder diameter of the UDZ type multi-stage hydraulic cylinder. If a constant thrust output is required for the full stroke, the thrust generated by the first stage (the stage with the smallest diameter) plunger under the provided medium pressure must be greater than the required constant thrust. For example, if the required constant thrust is 30kN and the system pressure is 12MPa, then the selected first stage plunger diameter is 56.4mm, and at this time, a cylinder with a diameter of approximately ф60mm for the first stage should be selected from the specifications. If the system pressure is 16MPa, then the ф60mm first stage cylinder can be directly selected according to Table 7-21. If the required thrust is a variable, then the variable force-stroke curve and the UDZ type multi-stage hydraulic cylinder stroke thrust curve should be made to determine the optimal cylinder diameter selection. Since the UDZ type multi-stage hydraulic cylinder is a single-acting cylinder, it must rely on gravity load or other external forces to drive the return stroke. The minimum starting pressure of the UDZ type multi-stage hydraulic cylinder is less than or equal to 0.3MPa, from which the minimum return force of each plunger cylinder can be calculated.

7.2.2 Working Conditions for Hydraulic Cylinders
The working conditions for hydraulic cylinders generally refer to a set of characteristic values such as environmental conditions, nominal pressure or rated pressure, speed, and working medium determined by the purpose of the hydraulic cylinder. Generally, the rated working conditions are given during hydraulic cylinder design.
The environmental conditions during the use of hydraulic cylinders should include environmental temperature and its variation range, inclination or swaying conditions, vibration, air humidity (including icing), salt spray, environmental pollution, radiation (including thermal radiation), etc.; rated pressure includes minimum rated pressure (i.e., starting pressure) and maximum rated pressure (i.e., pressure resistance pressure), speed includes minimum (stable) speed and maximum speed, and working medium includes the type, cleanliness, and temperature of the working medium.

The rated operating conditions are conditions that must be given or determined when designing a hydraulic cylinder, and the hydraulic cylinder can only guarantee sufficient service life if it is designed according to these conditions.

The extreme operating conditions are a special condition. Under these conditions, the hydraulic cylinder can only operate for a given time; otherwise, irreparable damage will be caused to the hydraulic cylinder, such as over-running during pressure resistance or high-temperature testing.

1. Temperature Range

Rated Operating Conditions:
Generally, the ambient temperature for the operation of a hydraulic cylinder should be -20 to 50°C.

Extreme Operating Conditions:
According to standards, when the ambient temperature is 65°C ± 5°C and the working medium temperature is 70°C ± 2°C, the hydraulic cylinder should be able to continuously reciprocate at the specified speed for 1 hour.

When the ambient temperature is -25°C ± 2°C and the working medium temperature is -15°C, the hydraulic cylinder should be able to continuously reciprocate at the specified speed for 5 minutes.

Therefore, the extreme ambient temperature range is temporarily set at: -25 to 65°C.

2. Maximum Rated Pressure

Because the maximum rated pressure is the pressure resistance pressure, the pressure resistance pressure is theoretically determined by the structural strength of the hydraulic cylinder, mainly by the structural strength of the generalized cylinder body. Therefore, if the structure of the hydraulic cylinder is already determined, then the pressure resistance pressure of the hydraulic cylinder can also be determined.

Although the maximum rated pressure can be determined by analogy, reverse design, etc., according to the above method in hydraulic cylinder design, it is usually determined to be 1.5 times the nominal pressure, i.e., the pressure resistance pressure.

JB/T 10205—2010 "Hydraulic Cylinder" Standard applies to single and double-acting hydraulic cylinders with a nominal pressure below 31.5 MPa, using hydraulic oil or other mineral oils with comparable performance as the working medium.

According to GB/T 23346—2003 "Fluid Transmission and Components Nominal Pressure Series", where 31.5 MPa is below 25 MPa, the standard stipulates that the maximum rated pressure (pressure resistance pressure) is 1.5×25 MPa=37.5 MPa for single and double-acting hydraulic cylinders using hydraulic oil or other mineral oils with comparable performance as the working medium.

It is recommended to determine the pressure resistance test pressure of the hydraulic cylinder through negotiation between the manufacturer and the user: when the nominal pressure is greater than or equal to 20 MPa, the pressure resistance test pressure should be 1.25 times the nominal pressure.

If this is the case, then JB/T 10205—2010 "Hydraulic Cylinder" Standard stipulates that the maximum rated pressure (pressure resistance pressure) is 1.25×25 MPa=31.25 MPa for single and double-acting hydraulic cylinders using hydraulic oil or other mineral oils with comparable performance as the working medium.

It is also important to emphasize a few points:

1) The maximum rated pressure or pressure resistance test pressure should be combined with the corresponding temperature to form a combined condition.

2) The maximum rated pressure or pressure resistance test pressure should be a static pressure and can be verified.

3) The maximum rated pressure is the pressure immediately below the burst pressure.

3. Speed Range

In hydraulic cylinder testing, the starting pressure corresponding to the lowest (minimum) speed is generally not the lowest speed, because at this time the hydraulic cylinder is only starting, rather than having a stable speed.

The lowest speed of hydraulic cylinders specified in current standards, including seal standards, is generally not lower than 4.0 mm/s, usually the lowest speed is 8.0 mm/s; the lowest stable speed of marine digital hydraulic cylinders should not be greater than 20 pulse equivalents per second.

The highest speed of a hydraulic cylinder is closely related to the design of seals and sealing systems. Nitrile rubber seals generally limit the speed to below 500 mm/s, usually the highest speed is below 300 mm/s; the highest speed of marine digital hydraulic cylinders can reach 2000 pulse equivalents per second.

Hydraulic cylinders with speeds higher than 200 mm/s must be equipped with a cushioning device.

4. Working Medium

JB/T 10205—2010 "Hydraulic Cylinder" Standard stipulates that single and double-acting hydraulic cylinders use hydraulic oil or other mineral oils with comparable performance as the working medium. The working medium must be compatible with the materials, mainly the sealing materials.

Except for special requirements, during other hydraulic cylinder tests, the kinematic viscosity of the hydraulic oil at 40°C on the test bench should be 29 to 74 mm2/s, and it is best to coordinate with the user.

GB/T 7935—2005 "Hydraulic Components General Technical Conditions" stipulates that the kinematic viscosity of the test hydraulic oil at 40°C should be 42 to 74 mm2/s (special requirements are subject to separate regulations).

JB/T 6134—2006 "Hydraulic Cylinders for Metallurgical Equipment (PN≤25 MPa)" stipulates that the test oil viscosity grade should be VG32 or VG46.

JB/T 9834—2014 "Agricultural Double-Acting Hydraulic Cylinder Technical Conditions" stipulates that the test oil should use N100D tractor transmission and hydraulic dual-purpose oil or mineral oil with comparable viscosity, and its kinematic viscosity at 40°C should be 90 to 110 mm2/s.

JB/T 13141—2017 "Tractor Steering Hydraulic Cylinder" stipulates that the viscosity of the test oil: the kinematic viscosity of the oil at 40°C should be 90 to 110 mm2/s, or the kinematic viscosity at 65°C should be 25 to 35 mm2/s.

JB/T 3818—2014 "Hydraulic Press Technical Conditions" stipulates that the oil temperature in the oil tank (or the oil temperature at the inlet of the hydraulic pump) should not exceed 60°C, and the oil temperature should not be lower than 15°C.

7.3.1 Evaluation and Control of Hydraulic Oil Contamination

The hydraulic oil used in hydraulic systems should be compatible with all system components, accessories, synthetic rubber, and filter elements.

1. Evaluation of Hydraulic Oil Contamination

In hydraulic systems and components, contaminants exist to a greater or lesser extent.
895:
The quantitative index for evaluating this degree of pollution is the pollution degree or cleanliness, with the antonym of pollution degree being cleanliness.

Solid particle contaminants present in hydraulic oil may cause serious consequences, thus requiring their measurement.

GB/T 1403-2002 "Hydraulic Transmission - Fluid - Solid Particle Contamination Level Codes" stipulates the codes used to determine the level of solid particle contaminants in the fluid of hydraulic systems.

GB/Z 20423-2006 "Hydraulic System Assembly - Cleanliness Inspection" stipulates the procedures for determining and inspecting the cleanliness level that must be achieved before the hydraulic system is shipped after assembly.

GB/T 2763-2011 "Hydraulic Transmission - Liquid Contamination - Determination of Particle Contamination Degree by Weighing Method" stipulates two weighing methods for determining the particle contamination degree of the working medium of hydraulic systems, namely the double membrane and single membrane methods. This standard is applicable for detecting particle contamination degrees greater than 0.2 mg/L of the working medium of hydraulic systems.

JB/T 9954-1999 "Press Machinery - Hydraulic System Cleanliness" stipulates the representation method, limits, and measurement method for the cleanliness of hydraulic systems in press machinery. GB/T1403-2002 is normatively referenced by JB/T10205-2010 "Hydraulic Cylinder".

2. Control of Hydraulic Fluid Contamination Degree

Hydraulic systems include various hydraulic components, accessories, pipelines (oil blocks), oil tanks, and working media. As a type of hydraulic component, hydraulic cylinders may contain contaminants that can cause a decrease in the performance and reliability of the hydraulic system. Controlling the contamination degree (cleanliness) of hydraulic cylinders during the manufacturing and installation process can achieve and control the expected cleanliness level of the hydraulic fluid. However, the cleanliness of the hydraulic fluid should be controlled first.

(1) Control of Hydraulic Fluid Cleanliness

The requirements for hydraulic fluid cleanliness in hydraulic systems can be determined based on the sensitivity of the main hydraulic components to contamination and the system's control precision requirements, or according to the requirements specified in the manuals of the main hydraulic components to determine the acceptable cleanliness of the hydraulic fluid.

The cleanliness of newly purchased hydraulic fluid can be 1-2 levels lower than the system requirements. The oil can be filtered during installation to meet the system's cleanliness requirements.

During the normal use of the hydraulic system, filter elements should be replaced regularly or in a timely manner according to the pressure difference alarm signal of the filter to ensure the filtering accuracy and meet the specified cleanliness requirements of the hydraulic fluid.

Additionally, preventing water contamination is an important aspect of controlling the cleanliness of hydraulic fluid. After water mixes with hydraulic fluid, it can reduce the lubricating properties of the hydraulic fluid, causing corrosion of hydraulic components and emulsification of the oil. Under low-temperature working conditions, water droplets in the oil can condense into ice particles, blocking the gaps or small holes of control components and causing system malfunctions. When necessary, the water content in new oil should be tested according to the method given in JB/T 12920-2016 "Hydraulic Transmission - Hydraulic Oil - Water Content Test Method".

(2) Control of Hydraulic Cylinder Cleanliness

Since the cleanliness (contamination degree) of hydraulic cylinders can be evaluated based on the mass of residual contaminants inside the hydraulic cylinder (see JB/T 7858-2006 "Hydraulic Component Cleanliness Evaluation Method and Hydraulic Component Cleanliness Index") or by using the method of counting solid particles in a unit volume of oil to determine the contamination level (see GB/T1403-2002 "Hydraulic Transmission - Fluid - Solid Particle Contamination Level Codes"), controlling the cleanliness of hydraulic cylinders means ensuring that their cleanliness (contamination degree) complies with the relevant standard requirements.

In JB/T11588-2013 "Large Hydraulic Cylinders", the cleanliness test of hydraulic cylinders uses one chamber to pressurize and another to discharge oil, using an oil contamination detector to inspect the discharged oil.

In CB/T 3812-2013 "Ship Hatch Cover Hydraulic Cylinders", the cleanliness of hydraulic cylinders is determined by cleaning the internal cavity of the hydraulic cylinder, then slowly pouring the cleaning liquid onto a filter membrane (with an accuracy of 0.8μm) placed on the funnel outlet for filtration. After filtration, the membrane is dried and weighed. The difference in mass between the membrane before and after filtration is the mass of contaminants in the internal cavity of the hydraulic cylinder.

The control method for hydraulic cylinder cleanliness should generally follow these regulations:

1) The cleanliness of hydraulic cylinders is controlled and maintained through appropriate procedures (processes), so a set of procedures needs to be established.

2) Since each process and procedure requires human operation and execution, employees should be educated on the basics of contamination control.

3) Control the pollution of the workshop environment and eliminate dirty environments.

4) Control the cleanliness of cylinder parts through the cleaning process, but seals generally should not be cleaned.

5) After testing, the hydraulic fluid in each cavity of the hydraulic cylinder should be drained and each oil port should be promptly sealed.

6) Avoid paint contamination inside the hydraulic cylinder and protect the surface of the piston rod from paint contamination.

7) Packaging, storage, and transportation should ensure that the hydraulic cylinder is protected from contamination.

For further control of contamination in hydraulic cylinders, refer to GB/Z19848-2005 "Guide for Achieving and Controlling Cleanliness of Hydraulic Components from Manufacturing to Installation".

(3) Control of Hydraulic System Cleanliness

There may be a large amount of contaminants in hydraulic systems, which may be residual substances from various parts that make up the hydraulic system, such as chips, sand, filings, dust, welding spatter, welding slag, rubber, sealant, water, water-containing impurities, chlorine, acid, and descaling agents. During the use of hydraulic systems, some contaminants may also be generated or increased, such as water, acid, worn metal (mechanical impurities), (n-pentane) insoluble matter, etc.

The control method for hydraulic system cleanliness should generally follow these regulations:

1) Manufacturers should inform buyers through effective information about the harmful effects of contaminants entering the internal components.

2) Provide components that comply with GB/T 17489-1998 "Hydraulic Particle Contamination"
896: Analysis of staining - take out liquid samples from the working system pipeline" to extract representative oil samples to check the cleanliness level of the hydraulic oil. 3) The cleanliness level of the hydraulic oil must be the same as or higher than that of hydraulic cylinder and other components. 4) The hydraulic system should be equipped with appropriate filtering devices to quickly remove contaminants generated during use. 5) Use the oil tank specified in G B / T3 7 6 6—2 0 1 5 "Hydraulic Transmission - General Rules and Safety Requirements for Systems and Their Components" to ensure that the hydraulic oil is within the specified temperature range, especially not exceeding the high temperature. 6) Generally speaking, the buyer is not allowed to disassemble hydraulic components and hydraulic systems, even as part of the quality assurance program and based on the sampling of a certain percentage. 7) Establish oil change indicators, check in time, and change oil in time. 7.3.2 Failure Modes and Risk Assessment of Hydraulic Cylinders The failure of hydraulic cylinders is the loss of the ability to execute requirements. The technical activity and management activity of judging the failure mode, finding the cause and mechanism of the failure, and putting forward countermeasures to prevent the failure from occurring again is called failure analysis. 4. General failure modes of hydraulic cylinders
In addition to the above-mentioned failure modes of the hydraulic cylinder barrel and piston rod, the main failure modes of general hydraulic cylinders are:
1) Deformation or fracture of the installation or connection structure of the hydraulic cylinder.
2) Deformation or fracture of the accessory structure of the hydraulic cylinder.
3) Bending or instability.
4) Damage such as indentation, bumping, scratching, and corrosion of cylinder parts.
5) External leakage or seepage other than at the piston rod seal.
6) Large internal leakage and large external leakage at the piston rod seal.
7) Large internal leakage or external leakage under specified high or low temperature and low pressure.
8) External contaminants (including air) entering the inside of the hydraulic cylinder.
9) High starting pressure.
10) Abnormal phenomena such as vibration, abnormal noise, crawling, deviation, or jamming occur when the piston and piston rod move.
11) Abnormal wear of cylinder parts made of metal, rubber, plastic, etc., and severe contamination of the working medium.
12) Loose connection and separation of mating surfaces between cylinder parts.
13) Change in maximum cylinder stroke or inaccurate positioning of the stroke.
14) The exhaust device cannot discharge or completely remove air from the various cavities inside the hydraulic cylinder.
15) Cavitation of the cylinder parts that form the cavity of the hydraulic cylinder.
16) Excessive impact between the piston or piston head and other cylinder parts.
17) Damage to the port.
5. Risk assessment
Risk is a combination of the probability of injury occurrence and the severity of the injury. However, in all cases, hydraulic cylinders should be designed, selected, applied, installed, and adjusted in such a way that when a failure occurs, personnel safety should be considered first, and damage to the hydraulic system and the environment should be prevented.
When designing hydraulic cylinders, all possible failures (including failures of the control part) should be considered.
Risk assessment is the entire process including risk analysis and risk evaluation. It is a series of logical steps to analyze and evaluate risks related to machinery using systematic methods. The purpose is to eliminate hazards or reduce risks. For example, through risk assessment, hydraulic cylinders with fire hazards should consider using flame-retardant hydraulic fluids.
Risk evaluation is based on risk analysis and is the basis and premise for making a final judgment on whether risk reduction is necessary.
Risk analysis includes:
1) Determination of mechanical limitations.
2) Hazard identification.
3) Risk assessment.
Information on risk evaluation includes:
1) Description of the machinery.
2) Relevant regulations, standards, and other applicable documents.
3) Relevant usage experience.
4) Relevant human engineering principles.
Among them, the user's hydraulic cylinder usage (technical) specification, the expected service life description (description) of the hydraulic cylinder, failure modes, relevant standards, etc., are very important for the design and manufacturing of hydraulic cylinders.
In addition, the pressure that a single hydraulic cylinder can normally withstand has a certain relationship with its rated fatigue pressure and rated static pressure. This relationship can be estimated and can serve as the basis for evaluating the expected service life of the hydraulic cylinder in standalone applications. This evaluation must be made by the user, and the user must also make judgments about factors such as impact, heat, and misuse during use.
It is stipulated in JB/T8779-2014: "The buyer should establish a system for regular maintenance, replacement of high-pressure components, and scrapping of the press to ensure the safe operation of the press."
6. Fatigue pressure test method for hydraulic cylinders
Since the fatigue failure mode is closely related to the safety function and service life of the hydraulic cylinder, it is very important for both the manufacturer and the customer of the hydraulic cylinder to master the reliability data of the hydraulic cylinder.
GB/T19934.1-xxxx/ISO10771-1:2015 "Hydraulic Transmission - Fatigue Pressure Test of Metal Pressure Vessels - Part 1: Test Method" stipulates the method for conducting fatigue tests on the metal pressure vessels of hydraulic components under continuous stable and periodically changing internal pressure loads.
This test method is only applicable to hydraulic components whose pressure vessels are made of metal, work at temperatures where creep and low-temperature embrittlement do not occur, are subjected only to stresses caused by (internal) pressure, and do not experience strength reduction due to corrosion or other chemical effects. The pressure vessel may include gaskets, seals, and other non-metallic parts, but these parts are not considered part of the pressure vessel of the hydraulic component being tested during the test.
This test method is not applicable to pipeline components (such as pipe fittings, hoses, rigid pipes, etc.) specified in ISO4413. For fatigue test methods for pipeline components, see ISO6803 and ISO6605.
The test pressure is determined by the user, and the evaluation method is given in ISO/TR10771-2.

7.3.3 Online State Monitoring and Fault Diagnosis of Hydraulic Systems and Hydraulic Cylinders
The online monitoring of hydraulic cylinders mainly uses instruments or devices installed on machines or hydraulic cylinders, and on hydraulic systems to monitor the pressure, temperature, input and output flow rate, contamination degree (cleanliness) of the working medium, piston rod movement speed, position, etc. in each chamber of the hydraulic cylinder.
The hydraulic cylinders on general hydraulic presses mainly monitor pressure, temperature, and the extreme positions of piston rod movement.
1. Pressure Monitoring
Pressure monitoring of hydraulic cylinders online often uses general pressure gauges, electric contact pressure gauges, digital pressure gauges, and other instruments. Among them, digital pressure gauges must be used together with pressure sensors or pressure modules and other pressure-sensitive elements.
General pressure gauges can only monitor visually. Permanent installed pressure gauges should use pressure limiters (pressure gauge dampers) or pressure gauge switches for protection, and the pressure gauge switches must be able to completely cut off when closed. The upper limit of the pressure gauge range should be at least about 1.75 times the nominal pressure of the hydraulic cylinder (hydraulic system).
Electric contact pressure gauges and digital pressure gauges can further control other components through the detected pressure, limiting or regulating the pressure of the entire hydraulic cylinder (hydraulic system).
The measurement point of the pressure gauge (or pressure sensor) used to detect the pressure of the hydraulic cylinder should be located at 2-4 times the inner diameter of the connecting pipeline away from the oil port of the hydraulic cylinder.
2. Temperature Monitoring
The online temperature monitoring device of hydraulic cylinders should generally be installed in the oil tank. In order to control the temperature range of the working medium, cooling or heating devices (collectively referred to as heat exchangers) are generally designed on hydraulic systems.
The simplest temperature monitoring device is a liquid level and liquid temperature gauge installed on the oil tank, which can only be used for visual monitoring.
Hydraulic thermometers or controllers can be used for both oil tank temperature monitoring and heat exchanger control.
When conducting factory inspection of hydraulic cylinders, the measurement point used to detect the temperature of hydraulic cylinders is generally required to be located at 4-8 times the inner diameter of the connecting pipeline away from the oil port of the hydraulic cylinder.
3. Monitoring of Contamination Degree of Working Medium
Except for large, precise, and expensive hydraulic equipment, online monitoring devices (such as online particle counters) for the contamination degree of working medium are not installed on general hydraulic systems or hydraulic equipment.
In order to monitor the contamination degree of the working medium in the chambers of hydraulic cylinders more accurately, oil sampling ports should be set according to the requirements of relevant standards.
The most difficult thing in practice is whether it is possible to persist in regular monitoring and timely handle problems when they are detected.
In JB/T11588-2013 "Large Hydraulic Cylinders", it is stipulated to use an oil contamination detector to detect the oil discharged from hydraulic cylinders.
4. Monitoring of Extreme Positions of Piston Rod Movement
For general hydraulic cylinders that do not use hydraulic cylinders as the actual limiters, monitoring the position of the piston or piston rod is mainly to prevent the piston from directly contacting (colliding) with the cylinder bottom or cylinder head (guide sleeve), that is, limiting the extreme positions of the piston and piston rod stroke. The methods often used are travel switches and proximity switches or setting soft limits in numerical control systems.
For hydraulic cylinders with requirements for stroke positioning and repeated positioning accuracy, displacement sensors (such as magnetostrictive displacement sensors) are generally set inside or outside the hydraulic cylinder, or displacement sensors (such as rod-type, slider-type displacement sensors) are installed or connected on the piston rod (or its connecting parts, such as sliders) of the hydraulic cylinder. Among them, the most used on hydraulic presses is the grating linear displacement sensor, that is, the grating ruler.
5. Fault Diagnosis of Hydraulic Cylinders
Because after the hydraulic cylinder fails, one or several functional items of the hydraulic cylinder have faults, so according to the failure mode of the hydraulic cylinder, the faults of the hydraulic cylinder are diagnosed.
The faults of hydraulic cylinders are not only manifested in the inability to complete the specified functions under the specified conditions and within the specified time, but may also be manifested in the specified conditions and within the specified time, with one or several performance indicators exceeding the standard, or damage to hydraulic cylinder components (including jamming or seizure).
The faults listed in this section do not include those caused by hydraulic control systems or hydraulic cylinder drive systems.

7.3.4 On-site maintenance and servicing of hydraulic cylinders
1. Maintenance regulations for hydraulic cylinders
(1) Preparation
1) Hydraulic cylinders should be maintained by technically trained personnel when undergoing regular maintenance or malfunction.
2) There should be a maintenance plan, fault investigation, availability of drawings, spare parts, disassembly and assembly tools, and scheduled work period.
3) Prepare maintenance site, handle external oil leakage, ensure clean and pollution-free operation.
4) Before disassembling hydraulic cylinder, be sure to support and secure connected parts (such as sliders), and use lifting tools for hoisting.
5) When necessary, pre-evaluate the restoration of performance (including accuracy), safety, and reliability of maintained hydraulic cylinder.
6) Hydraulic cylinder must be maintained after shutdown, including disconnecting main power (power source).
7) After removing fittings at port, take immediate blocking measures to avoid and reduce environmental pollution.
6 9 8 Hydraulic Cylinder Manual
908:
8) Generally, the disassembly of hydraulic cylinders should be completed by the manufacturer. When the manufacturer agrees with the user to allow the user to disassemble it themselves, the manufacturer should generally provide an operation guidance document.

Warning: Before disassembling the connectors and piping at the hydraulic cylinder ports, the connection between the hydraulic cylinder and the driven component (such as the slide block) must be disconnected, and the pressure in each chamber of the hydraulic cylinder must be relieved to zero. Otherwise, disassembling the hydraulic cylinder may result in danger.

(2) Disassembly

1) Disassemble the hydraulic cylinder according to the drawing and process (operation guidance document), and avoid rough disassembly, such as directly hammering cylinder parts.

2) Before disassembly and inspection, if there is no online monitoring device for the contamination degree of the working medium installed, the working medium in the cavity of the hydraulic cylinder should be sampled first, and then the surface of the hydraulic cylinder should be cleaned. The offline analysis of the working medium should be carried out synchronously with the maintenance of the hydraulic cylinder.

3) After cleaning, the installation and connection parts of the hydraulic cylinder should be inspected first, and records should be made.

4) The seals on the piston seal (system) and piston rod seal (system) must be inspected and recorded before disassembly. During disassembly, their integrity should be maintained as much as possible, and other parts should not be damaged. The disassembled seals (including retaining rings, support rings, etc.) must be scrapped, but should be kept for a certain period of time as required for reference.

5) In addition to checking the external dimensions of the hydraulic cylinder, the inner diameter of the cylinder, the diameter of the piston rod, the outer diameter of the piston, the matching hole of the guide sleeve (cylinder head), the shaft (mainly the inner hole of the guide sleeve), and the surface quality and dimensions of the grooves of each seal, the focus should be on checking and analyzing the parts involved in the failure.

6) Finding the cause of the failure, i.e., failure analysis, is a science and should be completed jointly by engineering technicians with professional knowledge. According to the "Failure Analysis Report" made by engineering technicians, specific measures should be taken for each component of the hydraulic cylinder, including reuse, repair, replacement, redesign and remanufacturing, scrapping, or returning the whole machine (scrapping).

7) During regular maintenance, there should also be a "Failure Analysis Report". For hydraulic cylinders and their parts whose functions are degraded or have serious damage or hidden dangers, and whose continued use will result in the loss of reliability and safety, specific explanations should be made for the parts or the whole machine.

8) Hydraulic cylinders that have been disassembled without making a "Failure Analysis Report" are not allowed to be reassembled.

(3) Maintenance

1) Parts that need maintenance should be transported out of the disassembly and assembly workshop.

2) Welded hydraulic cylinders that have not been disassembled are not allowed.

3) Maintenance should not damage the datum of the original hydraulic cylinder and its parts, especially the center holes at both ends of the piston rod.

4) The maintained hydraulic cylinder should comply with relevant standards as much as possible, such as the inner diameter of the cylinder, the diameter of the piston rod, the thread of the piston rod, the oil port, and the groove of the seal.

5) Specific problems should be analyzed specifically, and safe, reliable, fast, and cost-effective maintenance methods should be adopted for repair. Generally speaking, except for replacing all seals including retaining rings, support rings, etc., the repairability of hydraulic cylinders and their parts is poor.

6) Cylinder parts that are deformed or broken due to strength and stiffness problems are generally not allowed to be repaired and reused, i.e., they have "no repairability".

(4) Assembly

1) The assembly of hydraulic cylinders should be carried out according to the assembly process of hydraulic cylinders.

2) All parts used for the assembly of hydraulic cylinders must be qualified parts, including outsourced parts and purchased parts. If worn-out parts that exceed the tolerance are used for assembly, they must be approved.

3) All original seals must be replaced, including retaining rings, support rings, etc.

4) The cleanliness requirements of hydraulic cylinders must be guaranteed.

(5) Testing

1) The maintained hydraulic cylinder should be inspected and qualified on the test bench before being used for installation on the host machine.

2) There are dangers in inspecting the hydraulic cylinder using the hydraulic system of the host machine. The possible dangers include:

① Unexpected misoperation or misaction.
② Hydraulic oil spraying and splashing.
③ Overpressure and bursting.
④ Squeezing of other parts, etc.

3) At least a sealing performance test should be passed before the hydraulic cylinder can be connected to the driven component (such as the slide block).

4) The hydraulic cylinder should be run several times under no-load and low-speed conditions until the air in the cylinder is exhausted before being connected to the driven component.

5) The leakage inside the hydraulic cylinder can be checked by measuring the settlement.

2. Maintenance of Hydraulic Cylinders

The maintenance of hydraulic cylinders is of great significance for ensuring the safety and reliability of hydraulic cylinders and extending their service life. The maintenance of hydraulic cylinders should focus on the hydraulic system and even the whole machine, and the most important content of daily maintenance is to ensure the cleanliness of the working medium and to work at the specified temperature. Specifically, it should include the following contents:

1) Clean and replace the filter element of the filter in time.

2) Ensure that there is sufficient heat exchange medium in the heat exchanger.

3) Regularly monitor and inspect the quality of the oil, and change the oil according to the oil change cycle and in time.

4) Inspect or spot-check the oil tank temperature as required, and ensure that the hydraulic machine works within the specified temperature range.

5) Regularly inspect the installation and connection of the hydraulic cylinder.

6) Replace the protective cover of the piston rod in time after it is damaged.

7) Repair according to the specified time, and replace all seals (including retaining rings, support rings) etc.

8) Generally, hydraulic cylinders that have experienced severe vibration, tilting, and swaying should be disassembled and inspected every 7978 years, as described in Chapter 7 "Use and Maintenance of Hydraulic Cylinders".

After that, a trial run should be conducted before starting work.
9) Hydraulic cylinders that have malfunctioned should be repaired promptly and must not be operated while faulty.
10) For long-term idle hydraulic cylinders, the pressure in each chamber should be released, but the hydraulic oil should not be drained.
11) Protect the outer surface of the hydraulic cylinder from corrosion, and it can be repainted.
12) Protect the nameplate and warning signs.
13) When lifting the entire machine, do not use the lifting holes or hooks of the hydraulic cylinders that are components.
14) Hydraulic cylinders that have reached their expected service life should generally be scrapped. If the user continues to use them, special protection is required.

The hydraulic cylinder is a major component of a hydraulic press. Once a malfunction occurs, the hydraulic press may be forced to shut down. The hydraulic cylinder is also a relatively precise hydraulic component that requires skilled personnel to carefully maintain and service it. The maintenance and servicing of hydraulic cylinders should be included in the technical documents of the hydraulic press and be implemented in practice.

The marking of cylindrical pipe threads is composed of thread characteristic code, size code, and tolerance grade code.

The thread characteristic code is represented by the letter "G".

The thread size code is the fraction or integer specified in the first column of Table 1-77.

Thread tolerance grade code: For external threads, mark with grades A and B; for internal threads, do not mark the tolerance grade code.

Marking example: The marking for a right-handed cylindrical internal thread with size code 2 is G2.

The marking for an A-grade right-handed cylindrical external thread with size code 3 is G3A.

The marking for a B-grade right-handed cylindrical external thread with size code 4 is G4B.

When the thread is left-handed, add the notation "LH" after the tolerance grade code of the external thread or the size code of the internal thread.

Marking example: The marking for a left-handed cylindrical internal thread with size code 2 is G2LH.

The marking for an A-grade left-handed cylindrical external thread with size code 3 is G3A-LH.

2.10.3 General Technical Requirements for Hydraulic Cylinders on the Quality of Sealing Products
1. Appearance Quality
Under natural conditions, when observed with a 2x magnifying glass under appropriate lighting, the surface of the sealing product should not have defects, cracks, damage, bubbles, impurities, or other surface defects exceeding the allowable limits.
The working surface of the rubber seal should be flat and smooth, without pores, impurities, cracks, bubbles, scratches, or axial flow marks.
The working surface of the fabric-reinforced rubber seal should not have broken wires, exposed fabric, delamination, bubbles, impurities, or unevenness. For fabric-reinforced rubber seals with a parting line on the working surface, the height, width, and depth of trimming should not exceed 0.2 mm. Slight unevenness of the fabric layer at the corners is allowed.
The appearance quality of O-ring rubber seals for hydraulic and pneumatic use should comply with the relevant provisions of GB/T3452.2-2007.

3. Hardness
Whether using a Shore hardness tester or a portable international rubber hardness tester to measure rubber hardness, a certain indentation depth is formed on the rubber surface by a comprehensive effect, which is used to represent the hardness measurement result. International rubber hardness is a measure of rubber hardness, and its value is derived from the indentation depth of a indenter on a sample under specified conditions.
Although correction values for converting Shore hardness to international rubber hardness have been established for certain rubbers and compounds, it is now not recommended to directly convert Shore hardness (Shore A, Shore D, Shore AO, Shore AM) values to international rubber hardness (IRHD) values.
The hardness of vulcanized rubber and thermoplastic rubber can be determined by the methods specified in GB/T 531.1-2008《Test Methods for Indentation Hardness of Vulcanized Rubber or Thermoplastic Rubber - Part 1: Shore Hardness Tester Method (Shore Hardness)》 or GB/T 531.2-2009《Test Methods for Indentation Hardness of Vulcanized Rubber or Thermoplastic Rubber - Part 2: Portable International Rubber Hardness Tester Method》 and GB/T 6031-1998《Determination of Hardness of Vulcanized Rubber or Thermoplastic Rubber (10-100 IRHD)》.
The micro-hardness tester specified for O-ring hardness determination in GB/T 5720-2008 should comply with the relevant provisions in GB/T 6031.
The micro-hardness test method specified in GB/T 6031 is essentially a scaled-down version of the conventional test method, suitable for rubber hardness in the range of 35-85 IRHD, and can also be used for rubber with hardness in the range of 30-95 IRHD and sample thickness less than 4 mm.
MT/T 985 cites the GB/T 531 standard in its normative references. The hardness of polyurethane sealing rings specified in MT/T 985 is:
1）At 23°C, the hardness value of single-piece sealing rings should be 90 +5/-4 Shore A.
2）At 23°C, the hardness value of the outer ring of composite sealing rings should be greater than 90 Shore A.
3）At 23°C, the hardness value of the inner ring of composite sealing rings should be greater than 70 Shore A.
4. Tensile Strength
Tensile strength is the maximum tensile stress during the stretching of a sample until fracture. Dumbbell-shaped samples should be used to determine tensile strength.
The tensile strength of vulcanized rubber and thermoplastic rubber can be determined by the method specified in GB/T 528-2009《Determination of Tensile Stress-Strain Properties of Vulcanized Rubber or Thermoplastic Rubber》. The principle is: on a tensile testing machine with moving clamps or pulleys moving at constant speed, dumbbell-shaped samples are stretched, and the maximum force value during the continuous stretching of the sample is recorded as required.
GB/T 5720-2008《Test Methods for O-Rubber Sealing Rings》 cites GB/T 528-1998 (replaced by GB/T 528-2009) and HG/T 2369-1992《Technical Conditions for Rubber and Plastic Tensile Testing Machines》 (already obsolete) in its normative references.
MT/T 985 cites the GB/T 528 standard in its normative references. The tensile strength of polyurethane sealing rings specified in MT/T 985 is:
1）At 23°C, the tensile strength of single-piece sealing rings and the outer ring of composite sealing ring products should be greater than 35 MPa.
2）At 23°C, the tensile strength of the inner ring of composite sealing rings should be greater than 16 MPa.
5. Elongation at Break
Elongation at break is the percentage elongation at break of a sample. Ring-shaped samples can obtain approximately the same elongation at break values as dumbbell-shaped samples under the following conditions:
1）The elongation of ring-shaped samples is calculated as a percentage of the initial inner circumference.
2）If the "calendering effect" is obvious, the dumbbell-shaped sample is cut perpendicular to the calendering direction along the length.
The elongation at break of vulcanized rubber and thermoplastic rubber can be determined by the method specified in 281 Hydraulic Cylinder Manual.

6. Compression Set

When rubber is under compression, physical and chemical changes will inevitably occur. After the compressive force is removed, these changes prevent the rubber from returning to its original state, resulting in permanent deformation. The magnitude of compression set depends on the temperature and time under compression, as well as the temperature and time during height recovery. At high temperatures, chemical changes are the main reason for compression set in rubber. Compression set is measured after removing the compressive force applied to the specimen and allowing it to recover to a standard height. When testing at low temperatures, changes caused by hardening and crystallization in the glassy state are the main factors; these effects disappear when the temperature rises. Therefore, the test height must be measured at the test temperature.

The test principles given in GB/T 7759 are divided into room temperature/high temperature test principles and low temperature test principles:

(1) Room temperature and high temperature test principles

At standard laboratory temperature, the specimen of known height is compressed to the specified height according to the compression requirements, maintained under standard laboratory temperature or high temperature for a certain time, then the compression is removed at a certain temperature, and the specimen is allowed to recover freely for a specified time before measuring its height.

(2) Low temperature test principles

At standard laboratory temperature, the specimen of known height is compressed to the specified height according to the compression requirements, maintained for a certain time at the specified low temperature test temperature, then the compression is removed at the same low temperature, and the specimen is allowed to recover freely before measuring its height; measurements can be taken at regular intervals (obtaining a logarithmic curve of specimen height versus time to evaluate the compression set characteristics of the specimen), or measurement can be taken after a specified time.

1) Normal temperature compression set. Testing is conducted at normal temperature, with test temperature of (23±2)°C or (27±2)°C.

In the normative references of GB/T 5720-2008 "Test Methods for O-ring Rubber Seals", GB/T 7759-1996 is cited.

In the normative references of MT/T 985, GB/T 7759-1996 is cited. The normal temperature compression set for polyurethane seals specified in MT/T 985 is:

① The compression set for single-piece seals should be less than 25%.

② The compression set for the outer ring of composite seals should be less than 30%.

2) High temperature compression set. Testing is conducted at high temperature, with test temperature options of (40±1)°C, (55±1)°C, (70±1)°C, (85±1)°C, (100±1)°C, (125±2)°C, (150±2)°C, (175±2)°C, (200±2)°C, (225±2)°C, or (250±2)°C.

7. Fluid Resistance Properties

The action of liquids on vulcanized rubber or thermoplastic rubber typically results in the following:

1) Liquid is absorbed by the rubber.

2) Soluble components are extracted from the rubber.

3) Chemical reactions occur with the rubber.

Generally, the amount of absorption (1) is greater than the amount extracted (2), causing the rubber volume to increase. This phenomenon is called "swelling". Absorption of liquid causes significant changes in the physical and chemical properties of rubber such as tensile strength, elongation at break, and hardness. Additionally, plasticizers and antioxidant-type soluble substances in rubber are easily extracted by volatile liquids, and the physical and chemical properties of the dried rubber also change significantly. Therefore, it is important to test the properties of rubber after soaking or further drying.

GB/T 1690-2010 "Test Methods for Fluid Resistance of Vulcanized Rubber and Thermoplastic Rubber" specifies testing the changes in properties of rubber before and after soaking in test fluids to evaluate the effects of liquids on rubber.

In the normative references of GB/T 5720-2008 "Test Methods for O-ring Rubber Seals", GB/T 1690-1992 (replaced by GB/T 1690-2010) is cited, and GB/T 5720 provides calculation methods for percentage mass change and percentage volume change.

In the normative references of MT/T 985, GB/T 1690-1992 is cited. The fluid resistance properties for polyurethane seals specified in MT/T 985 are:

① The mass change rate should be less than 15%.

② The volume change rate should be less than 25%.

8. Heat Aging Performance

The heat aging and heat resistance test of vulcanized rubber or thermoplastic rubber under atmospheric pressure is a test in which samples are aged in high-temperature air under atmospheric pressure, and their performance is measured and compared with that of unaged samples. The physical properties often measured include tensile strength, elongation at a specified stress, elongation at break, and hardness.

GB/T5720-2008 "Test Methods for O-Ring Rubber Seals" normatively references GB/T3512-2001 "Heat Aging and Heat Resistance Test for Vulcanized Rubber or Thermoplastic Rubber".

MT/T985 normatively references GB/T3512-2001 standard.

MT/T985 stipulates that after aging, the performance of polyurethane single-piece sealing rings and the outer rings of composite sealing rings shall meet:

1) Hardness change decrease shall be less than 8%.
2) Tensile strength change decrease shall be less than 10%.
3) Elongation at break change decrease shall be less than 12%.

MT/T985 stipulates that after aging, the performance of the inner rings of polyurethane composite sealing rings shall meet:

1) Hardness change decrease shall be less than 8%.
2) Tensile strength change decrease shall be less than 10%.
3) Elongation at break change decrease shall be less than 30%.

9. Low-Temperature Performance

GB/T7758-2002 "Determination of Low-Temperature Performance of Vulcanized Rubber - Temperature Retraction Method (TR Test)" stipulates the method for determining the temperature retraction performance of stretched vulcanized rubber. The principle is: stretch the sample at room temperature, then cool it to a sufficiently low temperature at which no retraction occurs when the stretching force is removed. Remove the stretching force and raise the temperature at a uniform rate. Measure the temperature at which the specified retraction occurs.

GB/T5720-2008 "Test Methods for O-Ring Rubber Seals" normatively references GB/T7758-2002 standard.

MT/T985 normatively references GB/T7759-1996 "Determination of Compression Set of Vulcanized Rubber and Thermoplastic Rubber at Room Temperature, High Temperature, and Low Temperature". Please refer to Section 6 of this paper for the principle.

MT/T985 stipulates that after low-temperature treatment, the performance of the inner and outer rings of polyurethane single-piece sealing rings and composite sealing rings shall meet:

1) Hardness change decrease shall be less than 8%.
2) Tensile strength change decrease shall be less than 10%.
3) Elongation at break change decrease shall be less than 12%.

However, the measurement of the above three performance parameters lacks standard basis.

10. Reliability

The reliability of sealing rings refers to the ability to ensure their sealing performance under specified conditions for a specified time. Reliability is determined by various factors such as design, manufacturing, use, and maintenance, and is therefore a comprehensive performance index.

The term reliability is sometimes used in a general sense to indicate availability (effectiveness) and durability. The reliability of sealing rings specified in JB/T10205-2010 mainly includes pressure resistance performance (including low-pressure resistance performance) and durability performance. Please refer to JB/T10205-2010 "Hydraulic Cylinders" for details.

MT/T985 stipulates that polyurethane sealing rings shall meet the requirement of 21,000 test cycles for reliable sealing. However, durability tests conducted without "specified conditions" generally do not have repeatability and comparability. Therefore, it is still appropriate to follow the relevant provisions in JB/T10205-2010 regarding the reliability of sealing rings.

11. Operating Temperature Range

According to the provisions of JB/T10205-2010 "Hydraulic Cylinders" standard, generally, the operating temperature of hydraulic cylinders should be within the range of -20 to 50°C, and the working medium temperature should be within the range of -20 to 80°C. At the same time, it is also stipulated that when the product has high-temperature requirements, under rated pressure, 90°C working oil should be input into the tested hydraulic cylinder, and reciprocating operation for 1 hour should meet the high-temperature requirements of the hydraulic cylinder agreed upon by both parties.

HG/T2810-2008 "Materials for Reciprocating Rubber Seals" standard stipulates that reciprocating rubber seal materials are divided into two categories: A and B. Category A is nitrile rubber material, divided into three hardness grades and five types of rubber, with an operating temperature range of -30 to 100°C; Category B is castable polyurethane rubber material, divided into four hardness grades and four types of rubber, with an operating temperature range of -40 to 80°C.

MT/T985 stipulates that polyurethane sealing rings should be able to adapt to temperatures in the range of -20 to 60°C.

12. Sealing Pressure Range

Sealing pressure refers to the pressure of the sealing medium that the sealing ring bears during operation. Generally speaking, the sealing pressure of a sealing ring is closely related to factors such as the sealing material and structure type of the sealing ring, the sealing medium and temperature, groove type and dimensions and tolerances, unilateral radial clearance, surface quality and relative movement speed of the mating parts. Therefore, the sealing pressure or sealing pressure range must be specified under certain conditions.

2.1.10.4 Test Methods for Performance of Hydraulic Reciprocating Seal Elements

The test conditions and methods for performance of hydraulic reciprocating seal elements specified in GB/T32217-2015 are applicable for evaluating the performance of hydraulic reciprocating seal elements using hydraulic oil as the transmission medium.

To obtain comparative data on reciprocating seal performance and provide a basis for seal design and selection, the following factors affecting seal performance must be strictly controlled in testing hydraulic reciprocating seal elements:

(1) Installation
1) Seal system design including support rings, seal elements, and dust wipers
2) Installation tolerances including seal groove, piston rod, support ring, and extrusion gap
3) Piston rod material and hardness
4) Piston rod surface roughness - values outside Ra0.08-0.15μm or greater than Rt1.5μm will seriously affect seal performance. The optimal surface roughness varies with different seal materials
5) Groove surface roughness - should be less than Ra0.8μm to avoid static leakage and seal wear during pressure cycling
6) Support ring material including effects on piston rod texture and boundary layer

(2) Operation
1) Fluid medium including viscosity, lubricity, compatibility with seal material and additives, and contamination level
2) Pressure including pressure cycling
3) Speed especially speed cycling
4) Speed/pressure cycling such as start-stop conditions
5) Stroke length especially short strokes (2 times or less than the seal contact width) that prevent oil film formation
6) Temperature including effects on viscosity and seal material properties
7) External environment

When using standard test results to predict actual seal performance, all these factors and their potential effects on seal performance must be considered.

Author's note:
1. Without control of factors affecting installation and operation of reciprocating seals, devices, or systems, test results for reciprocating seals will be unpredictable and cannot be used for performance comparison.
