GB/T 3227-2015 "Hydraulic Transmission - Sealing Device - Test Method for Evaluating the Performance of Hydraulic Reciprocating Motion Seals" was issued on December 10, 2015, and implemented on January 1, 2017. The author has interpreted and discussed it many times, and has also used this standard to evaluate the performance test bench of a domestic seal company. Now some issues that need attention in the application process of this standard are explained:
1) Hydraulic reciprocating motion seals or sealing devices undoubtedly include hydraulic cylinder piston dynamic sealing devices and hydraulic cylinder piston rod dynamic sealing devices. This can be proved from the normative references of the standard, because it cites GB/T 1524.2-2017 "Hydraulic Cylinder Piston and Piston Rod Dynamic Sealing Device Dimensional Series Part 2: Support Ring Dimensional Series and Tolerances". In GB/T 3227-2015, only the schematic diagram of the hydraulic cylinder piston rod dynamic sealing test device is given (see Figure 1), but the schematic diagram of the hydraulic cylinder piston dynamic sealing test device is not given, that is, the test device for evaluating the hydraulic cylinder piston dynamic sealing device (or seal) is missing, that is, this standard lacks the content that should be included in evaluating the piston seal of hydraulic reciprocating motion. It is recommended that all parties speed up research and provide test devices and test methods for hydraulic cylinder piston dynamic sealing devices (or seals).
2) The test medium temperature specified in GB/T 3227-2015 has only one temperature, which is inconsistent with some hydraulic cylinder standards. This will lead to the test results obtained according to this standard cannot be used as a reference when the hydraulic cylinder actually applies this type of seal, and it loses the engineering significance that the test should have, or can be expressed as: the test cannot "provide a basis for the design and selection of seals". It is recommended that, like other test parameters, the test temperature should also provide "series standard values", among which at least one test temperature value should be adapted to the current hydraulic cylinder standard.
3) The starting friction force test specified in GB/T 3227-2015 is also different from the hydraulic cylinder starting pressure characteristic test specified in general standards. For example, JB/T 10205-2010 stipulates: "The pressure in the rodless chamber (double rod hydraulic cylinder, either chamber can be used) is gradually increased until the hydraulic cylinder starts, and the recorded starting pressure is the minimum starting pressure." The seal is subjected to gradually increasing pressure, rather than "maintaining the test pressure p1" to measure the starting friction force. The "starting pressure characteristic" test specified in JB/T 10205-2010 is basically the same as the working conditions of the actual application of the hydraulic cylinder, while the "steps for measuring the starting friction force" driven by external force specified in GB/T 3227-2015 does not match the actual working conditions of the hydraulic cylinder, and the consistency of the test results of the two cannot be evaluated, and the test may not be able to "provide a basis for the design and selection of seals".
4) It can be determined from Figure 5 given in GB/T 3227-2015 that the so-called dust ring 1 (see Figure 6) does not have the structural characteristics of "a device used on a reciprocating rod to prevent contaminants from intruding", because it does not have a sealing lip to prevent contaminants from intruding, and its structural shape is consistent with the Y-shape or U-shape specified in the current standards. In this regard, hydraulic cylinders should generally have dust protection devices, and piston rod sealing systems or devices without dust seals have no practical application value; at the same time, test devices without dust protection devices are also very dangerous in tests. In addition, this standard does not specify the cleanliness of the test environment. It is recommended to use a double-lip dust ring (such as a C-type dust ring), which can play the role of dust prevention and auxiliary sealing.
5) Judging from the test steps specified in GB/T 3227-2015, some issues affect the specific operation of the test:
① In "The test device reciprocates at a linear velocity v and stable medium pressure p1 for 1 h", v and p1 are not specified, so it is not easy to operate and it is easy to cause disputes.
② According to the test steps specified in GB/T 3227-2015, the test is mainly divided into three stages: reciprocating motion for 1 h and maintaining test pressure p1 and test temperature for 16 h, and measuring starting friction force is the first stage; completing 200,000 uninterrupted cycles (at a linear velocity of 0.05 m/s, completing 91 Hydraulic Cylinder Manual

6 million cycles) is the second segment; completing a total of 300,000 uninterrupted cycles (at a linear speed of 0.05 m/s, completing 100,000 cycles) is the third segment. There is a problem here: in addition to the linear speed of 0.05 m/s, the standard values for the speed series also include two other speeds of 0.15 m/s and 0.5 m/s, so how to choose the speed in the latter two stages of the test is an issue.

③ In the above three stages of tests, the friction force (under constant pressure) was recorded or measured respectively, but how to deal with these three friction force values is not clearly specified in Appendix B (normative appendix) of GB/T32217-2015.

④ Similarly, in the latter two stages of tests, "starting friction force" measurements were also performed, so how to deal with these two starting friction force values is also an issue.

6) There are also some statements, algorithms, or practices in this standard that are worth discussing:

① In the introduction of this standard, "key variables" are proposed, and it is required that "tests on sealing elements should strictly control these key variables," but no subsequent text specifies what the key variables are.

② In "At the beginning of each test, the inherent friction force F1 of the sliding bearing ring and dust seal ring should be measured," the "sliding bearing ring" and "inherent friction force F1" are unknown as to which standard they come from, and it is also unclear how to measure the inherent friction force F1.

③ Due to the issue of "inherent friction force F1," the calculation formula (2-56) for the average friction force of the tested sealing element also has problems. Of course, the calculation result (average friction force of the tested sealing element) is also worth discussing.

④ In "Fs -- the average value of the friction force during the forward stroke and return stroke of a single tested sealing element," the "forward stroke" and "return stroke" are unknown as to which standard they come from, and their specific meanings are also unclear.

⑤ In the "steps for measuring starting friction force," the "drive circuit pressure" is unclear because there is no drive circuit in the test device schematic diagram (original figure 1), only a "linear driver."

⑥ Since this standard includes both "starting friction force" and "kinetic friction force," the original formula (1) should be for calculating the average kinetic friction force of the tested component, rather than "calculating the average friction force of the tested component." There are also situations elsewhere where "kinetic friction force" and "friction force" are mixed.

2.10.5 Hydraulic cylinder sealing elements and their grooves

1 O-ring rubber sealing elements and their grooves

(1) Characteristics and functions of O-rings

As shown in Figure 2-17, O-ring rubber sealing elements (abbreviated as O-rings) are rubber rings with a ring shape and a circular cross-section (or cross-sectional shape of O-ring), which are the most widely used and produced sealing elements. They can be used for both static and dynamic sealing, and are also the basic components of many combined sealing devices. The O-rings currently in use are basically molded from synthetic rubber. Ordinary O-rings for hydraulic systems are divided into two categories, I and II, based on their working temperature range, and each category is further divided into four levels based on hardness. Category I has a working temperature range of -40 to 100°C, while category II has a working temperature range of -25 to 125°C; the applicable working medium is petroleum-based hydraulic oil and lubricating oil. O-rings for other working conditions and working media different from those mentioned above need to be selected from other suitable rubber materials. If ordinary O-ring molds are still used for pressing, it may result in incorrect inner diameter dimensions and cross-sectional diameter dimensions of the O-ring; in this case, it is necessary to redesign the sealing groove or open a new molding mold to achieve the O-ring corresponding to the standard groove. Since the design and manufacturing of O-ring molding molds are relatively simple, O-rings are chosen for sealing in many special occasions. Therefore, there are many situations where O-ring grooves need to be designed.

For the design and manufacturing of O-rings, readers can further refer to Reference [102] and its references.

O-rings have the following advantages compared to other sealing rings:

1) The sealing groove is simple and has small dimensions.

2) It can achieve bidirectional sealing and can be used for both dynamic and static sealing.

3) It has good static sealing performance.

4) It has small dynamic friction resistance and can also be used in situations with alternating pressure.

5) Both O-rings and their grooves have current standards, making them easy to select and use.

6) They are easy to manufacture and inexpensive.

The design of the sealing groove mainly includes determining the shape (structural type), dimensions and tolerances, surface roughness, etc. of the sealing groove. It should be emphasized that the design of chamfers or fillets, geometric tolerances, etc. at various parts of the groove is particularly important; determining the fitting clearance for reciprocating motion sealing is also very important. Generally speaking, the higher the working pressure, the smaller the clearance should be; the higher the hardness of the sealing material, the larger the clearance can be.

(3) Design method of O-ring groove

Based on relevant standards and the author's technical design experience, the O-ring groove can be designed by the following method:

1) Determine whether to use piston seal or piston rod seal.

2) Determine the highest rated pressure or working pressure range of the seal.

3) Select the appropriate O-ring material and size based on the working conditions and pressure range.

4) Calculate the required groove dimensions based on the selected O-ring material and size, as well as the desired compression rate.

5) Design the groove shape and dimensions to ensure proper sealing and prevent extrusion of the O-ring.

6) Verify the design by checking the calculated groove dimensions against the extreme values given in Tables 2-72 and 2-73.

7) If necessary, adjust the design based on the verification results.

8) Finalize the design and provide detailed drawings for manufacturing.

(4) Selection of O-rings

The selection of O-rings should first consider the material of the O-ring according to the specified working conditions, taking into account the nature of the hydraulic transmission medium, working temperature range, sealing properties, sealing type, nominal pressure range, etc., and especially the reciprocating motion speed. If the selected O-ring is not used in petroleum-based hydraulic working media, or the working temperature is not within the range of -40～125℃, it may not be easily available on the market. For example, seals on hydraulic support (cylinder) and cylinders using phosphate ester flame-retardant hydraulic fluid in mines using emulsion require customization or purchase from the manufacturer.

When selecting the cross-sectional size of the O-ring, a larger cross-section O-ring should be preferred. Larger cross-section O-rings are less prone to twisting and extrusion. (3) Maximum Working Pressure of Seals

According to GB/T1020.5-2010 "Hydraulic Cylinders", the pressure resistance test stipulates: the tested hydraulic cylinder piston shall be stopped at both ends of the formed stroke (single-acting hydraulic cylinder at the stroke limit position), and hydraulic fluid with 1.5 times the nominal pressure shall be applied to the working chamber respectively. (4) High Temperature and High Pressure Seals

Based on the relevant standards for hydraulic cylinder seals, existing seal materials, structural types, and working conditions, static seals (such as O-rings) and reciprocating motion seals with a maximum working temperature higher than 90°C and a maximum working pressure greater than 31.5 MPa are defined as high temperature and (ultra) high pressure seals.

It is difficult to predict the high temperature and high pressure sealing performance of seals, mainly because it is not only related to the sealing material and structural type, but also to the working conditions, such as the extrusion gap of the seal (including the maximum extrusion gap with eccentricity), which is difficult to determine accurately during design. Therefore, the sealing design of any hydraulic cylinder must be tested under actual working conditions (actual machine sealing performance test).

Here, readers are reminded that in GB/T32217-2015 "Hydraulic Transmission - Sealing Devices - Test Methods for Evaluating the Performance of Hydraulic Reciprocating Motion Seals", the test medium temperature is specified as 60-65°C, and the (maximum) test pressure as 31.5 MPa.

2.10.9 Comparison and Analysis of Sealing Technical Requirements for Hydraulic Cylinders and Selection of Seals for Servo Hydraulic Cylinders

1. Comparison and Analysis of Sealing Technical Requirements for Servo Hydraulic Cylinders

DB44/T11169.1-2013 "Servo Hydraulic Cylinders Part 1: Technical Conditions" (has been abolished, for reference only) stipulates the technical requirements for single and double acting servo hydraulic cylinders. The technical requirements related to servo hydraulic cylinder seals mainly include: minimum starting pressure, internal leakage, load efficiency, external leakage, durability, pressure resistance, load-carrying dynamic friction force, and leakage under low pressure. Judging only from the technical requirements stipulated in this standard, the technical requirements for seals account for most of the content.

Except for the load-carrying friction force, the other sealing technical requirements are also specified in other hydraulic cylinder standards.

DB44/T11169.1 stipulates the load-carrying friction force index, and DB44/T11169.2-2013 "Servo Hydraulic Cylinders Part 2: Test Methods" stipulates the test method for load-carrying friction force.

(1) Comparison and Analysis of Minimum Starting Pressure

Comparing the minimum starting pressure specified in each standard, the minimum starting pressure index for double acting servo hydraulic cylinders given in DB44/T11169.1-2013 is almost 1/10 or lower than the index given in other hydraulic cylinder standards, see Table 2-158.

The static and dynamic friction forces of gap seal are the smallest for piston seal. 1) The minimum starting pressure index specified in DB44/T11169.1-2013 is too low.

2) The specified values (indices) of minimum starting pressure for combined seal and gap seal are the same, which is not very reasonable.

Considering the current situation of designing and manufacturing hydraulic cylinders controlled by electro-hydraulic servo valves in China, as well as the development level of hydraulic cylinder sealing technology, it is more appropriate to refer to hydraulic cylinders with starting pressure not exceeding 0.3 MPa for electro-hydraulic servo valve controlled hydraulic cylinders as low friction hydraulic cylinders.

Comparing the internal leakage specified in each standard, the internal leakage index for single and double acting servo hydraulic cylinders given in DB44/T11169.1 is exactly the same as the index given in other hydraulic cylinder standards, see Tables 2-159 and 2-160.

2.13.3 Technical Requirements for Pressure Sensors Used in Hydraulic Cylinders
Pressure sensors are sensors that can sense pressure and convert it into usable output signals. Technical requirements for pressure sensors are specified in JB/T 6170-2006.
Pressure sensors belong to physical quantity sensors. Pressure sensors, differential pressure sensors, and absolute pressure sensors are occasionally used in hydraulic cylinders.
1. Basic Parameters
(1) Measuring Range
The measuring range of the sensor should comply with the provisions of product technical conditions (detailed specifications). Unless otherwise specified, the measuring range of the sensor is recommended to be selected from the following numbers:
1×10n, 1.6×10n, 2×10n, 2.5×10n, 3×10n, 4×10n, 5×10n, 6×10n, 8×10n.
Where n is an integer, n=0, ±1, ±2, ±3....
The unit of measuring range is Pa, kPa, MPa, GPa.
(2) Type of Pressure Felt by the Sensor
1) Gauge Pressure Sensor (pg).
2) Absolute Pressure Sensor (pa).
3) Differential Pressure Sensor (pd).
(3) Type of Medium Being Measured
The type of medium in contact with the pressure chamber, such as gas, liquid, corrosive medium, non-corrosive medium, etc.
(4) Material in Contact with the Measured Medium
List the name and grade of the material in contact with the measured medium.
(5) Installation Effect
If the maximum installation force or torque affects the performance of the sensor, specific provisions should be made.
(6) Direction
The direction is determined based on the axial direction of the sensor pressure interface (i.e., the direction in which the measured medium enters the sensor), with the direction consistent with it being the Y-axis, and the rest being X and Z axes, with an outline drawing attached for explanation.
(7) Enclosure Sealing
When the sensor's enclosure needs to be sealed, the sealing material and sealing method should be specified, and the electrical connector should have the same requirements. When the sensor's enclosure has protection requirements, the protection level should be given, with the protection level specified according to GB/T 4208.
(8) Electrical Connection Method
The electrical connector model, electrical connection principle diagram, and necessary explanations should be provided.
(9) Excitation
The excitation of the sensor should comply with the provisions of product technical conditions (detailed specifications).
(10) Operating Temperature Range
The operating temperature range of the sensor should comply with the provisions of product technical conditions (detailed specifications), and it is recommended to select from the following five levels.
1) Commercial Grade: 0~70℃.
2) Industrial Grade: -25~85℃.
3) Automotive Grade: -30~100℃.
4) Military Grade: -55~125℃.
5) Special Grade: -60~350℃.
(11) Storage Temperature Range
The lower limit temperature of the storage temperature range is usually 10℃ lower than the lower limit value of the operating temperature, and the upper limit temperature is usually 15~20℃ higher than the upper limit value of the operating temperature.
2. Technical Requirements
(1) Product Technical Conditions (Detailed Specifications)
The sensor should comply with the provisions of this technical requirement and relevant product technical conditions (detailed specifications). When the requirements of this technical requirement and product technical conditions (detailed specifications) are inconsistent, the product technical conditions (detailed specifications) shall prevail.
(2) Appearance
The appearance of the sensor should be free from obvious defects, scratches, rust, and damage; the threaded parts should be free from burrs; the markings should be clear, complete, and accurate.

2. Processing Accuracy Analysis
During the product technical design phase, process designers should analyze and evaluate the processability of the product structure. Under the premise of meeting the functional and performance requirements of the product, the processing accuracy should be limited to the economical processing accuracy as much as possible to achieve the best economic benefits.
Processing accuracy refers to the degree of conformity between the actual geometric parameters (dimensions, shapes, and positions) of the part after processing and the ideal geometric parameters. However, in general cases, processing accuracy can be predicted and judged based on accumulated practical experience and summarized process trials. Therefore, process design and process review are indispensable processes in product technical design.
When necessary, process verification can be conducted to further check the rationality of the process design. The WC67Y-100T hydraulic cylinder has undergone process verification.
Processing accuracy analysis is the analysis of the feasibility and economic feasibility of achieving the designed accuracy under existing conditions, including analysis of processing errors, process capability, and economical processing accuracy.
The following is the processing accuracy analysis of the main cylinder components of the WC67Y-100T hydraulic cylinder. In the following text, except for surface roughness, all length dimensions are in millimeters.
(1) Processing Accuracy Analysis of the Cylinder Body
The processing accuracy of the cylinder body mainly involves the cylinder bore, piston rod seal groove, and threaded connection. The following mainly analyzes the processing accuracy of the cylinder bore and piston rod seal groove of the cylinder body (right side) of the WC67Y-100T hydraulic cylinder shown in Figure 3-5.
1) Processing Accuracy Analysis of the Cylinder Bore. Using single-action chuck clamping and aligning the cylinder body, turning the inner bore and other parts of the cylinder, and finishing rolling the inner bore, based on the current process level and practical experience, it is completely possible to achieve the dimensions and tolerances, geometric accuracy, and surface roughness shown in Figure 3-5.
The main problem in the processing of the cylinder bore now is that rough machining and finish machining are performed simultaneously (in one clamping) for processing. Even if the surface roughness value can reach Ra1.6μm or below before finishing rolling, the geometric accuracy may be out of tolerance. The main issue is the out-of-tolerance of cylindricity, i.e., the out-of-tolerance of parallelism.
The ordinary lathe used must ensure its geometric accuracy and working accuracy; otherwise, the inner bore of the cylinder will definitely be out of tolerance during processing.
Under the premise of ensuring the accuracy of the ordinary lathe, the following issues should be noted for finish turning:
① Before finish turning, the workpiece must be cooled to room temperature or the specified temperature.
② The finish turning allowance should not be left too small; it should be at least enough for two finish turning cuts.
③ Measurement should be taken before finish turning. When finish turning the first cut for a certain length, measurement should be taken again.
④ When finish turning the first cut, it is generally not advisable to directly turn to the relief groove.
⑤ When finish turning the last cut, it must be completed in one processing.
⑥ When turning steel parts, the turning tool should be able to break chips (with chip-breaking grooves) and remove chips in a timely manner.
According to the characteristics of the rolling process and practical experience, it is recommended to use clean emulsified or synthetic cutting fluid for cooling, lubrication, rust prevention, and cleaning when rolling the inner bore of the steel cylinder.

2. Technical Requirements
(1) General Requirements
1) The drawings and technical documents of hydraulic press should comply with the requirements of JB/T12769—2015 standard, and can only be put into production after approval according to the prescribed procedures.
2) The shape and layout of hydraulic press products should consider the requirements of process aesthetics and ergonomics, and the components and devices should be reasonably arranged and of moderate height, facilitating the operator to observe the processing area.
3) Hydraulic press should be convenient for use, maintenance, assembly, disassembly, and transportation.
4) Hydraulic press should be able to work normally under the following environmental conditions:
  ① Ambient temperature: 5 ~ 40°C.
  ② Relative humidity: When the highest temperature is 40°C, the relative humidity should not exceed 50%, and when the temperature is lower, higher relative humidity is allowed.
  ③ Altitude: Hydraulic press should be able to work normally at an altitude below 1000 m.
(2) Performance, Structure, and Function
1) Hydraulic press should have sufficient rigidity. Under the maximum load condition, hydraulic press should be able to work normally.
2) The speed of the slide should comply with the provisions of Table 4-70 and the requirements of technical documents, realizing the functions of fast descent, pressing, and return.
3) Hydraulic press should have pressure holding function, and the pressure holding time should be adjustable.
4) Hydraulic press has the functions of stamping, stretching, blanking, shaping, and forming.
5) The CNC system of hydraulic press can control the pressure of the slide, the force of the hydraulic cushion, the stroke of the slide, the stroke of the hydraulic cushion, etc., and can realize synchronous or separate control.

1) The hydraulic system of the hydraulic press shall comply with the provisions of GB/T3766. All hydraulic components in the hydraulic system shall comply with the provisions of GB/T7935.

(7) Appearance quality
1) The surface of the hydraulic press shall not have defects such as unevenness, roughness, etc. that are not specified in the drawing.
2) The edges of the mating surfaces of the parts shall be neat and uniform, with a misalignment not greater than 1 mm. No obvious gaps shall exist at the mating surfaces of doors, covers, etc.
3) Exposed hydraulic, pneumatic, electrical pipes, etc. shall be arranged neatly, installed firmly, and shall not contact relatively moving parts.
4) The paint of the hydraulic press shall comply with the provisions of 5.7 in JB/T50000.12-2007.
3. Test methods
(1) Performance test
1) Test conditions.
① Empty running test and load running test shall be conducted respectively with the installation height of the movable beam and the worktable corresponding to the actual use of the mold.
② The load running test shall be conducted in the automatic cycle working state, with a continuous running time not less than 2 h under the rated nominal pressing force.
③ Before the vacuum brick test, the mold shall be installed.
2) Empty running test.
① Oil pump start-stop test. The test shall be conducted in no-load state, with the start and stop of the oil pump not less than 3 times, to check the reliability of the action.
② Hydraulic system working pressure adjustment test. The system working pressure shall be adjusted in stages from low pressure to high pressure, and finally adjusted to the rated pressure value to check the smoothness and reliability of the pressure adjustment.
③ Manual operation test. Under the manual working specification, the actions of the movable beam, mixing-type feeding mechanism, brick clamping mechanism, etc. shall be tested to check the accuracy of the action and the smoothness of the movement.
④ Stroke and speed adjustment test. The strokes and speeds of the upper movable beam, lower movable beam, and mixing-type feeding mechanism shall be adjusted respectively from small to large within the specified range to check the accuracy and reliability of the adjustment.
⑤ Automatic empty cycle test. During the automatic empty cycle test, the movement mode of the movable beam shall generally follow Figure 1, Figure 2, Figure 3, or Figure 4 in JC/T2034-2010 (the action of the upper movable beam is rapid descent, deceleration braking descent, rapid ascent), without applying pressing force, and the mixing-type feeding mechanism, brick clamping mechanism, etc. shall operate synchronously to check the coordination and stability of the hydraulic press under no-load operation.
⑥ Empty cycle times. During the above-mentioned automatic cycle test, the stopwatch shall be used for measurement, and the strokes of the upper movable beam and the mixing-type feeding mechanism shall comply with the provisions of Table 4-93.

4.4.2 Hydraulic Mud Gun
Mud gun (iron mouth plugging machine) is a special equipment for plugging iron mouths. It is classified into electric mud gun and hydraulic mud gun according to the driving mode of working mechanism. In YB/T017-2017 "Technical Conditions for Hydraulic Mud Gun", the terms and definitions, models, types and parameters, technical requirements, test methods, inspection rules, signs, packaging, transportation and storage of hydraulic mud gun are specified, which are applicable to 400-5800 m3 blast furnaces for iron smelting and COREX reduction method iron smelting furnaces with equivalent capacity, using hydraulic oil or other mineral substances with performance equivalent to hydraulic oil as hydraulic power medium, and using refractory mud to plug the iron mouth of iron smelting furnace. Other similar mud guns can also be used as reference.
1. Models, Basic Types and Parameters
(1) Product Models, Specifications and Their Meanings
Product models, specifications and their meanings are shown in YB/T017-2017.
(2) Types of Hydraulic Mud Gun
1) Type YPE Hydraulic Mud Gun. Type YPE hydraulic mud gun adopts side inclined circular base, closed or semi-closed box-shaped rotating arm, uses slewing bearing, has built-in slewing mechanism, two-end ear ring type or cylinder bottom ear shaft rod end ear ring type slewing hydraulic cylinder, cylinder body pushes copper ring mud plug type mud punching mechanism, has short body and moderate weight. When the mud gun is arranged on the same side as the iron mouth opening machine, the YPE type hydraulic mud gun operates below the iron mouth opening machine, as shown in Figure 1a in YB/T017-2017.
2) Type YPF Hydraulic Mud Gun. Type YPF hydraulic mud gun adopts positive inclined square base, rectangular section beam type rotating arm, external slewing mechanism, middle ear shaft rod end thread type slewing hydraulic cylinder, cylinder body pushes copper ring mud plug type mud punching mechanism, has moderate body height and weight. When the mud gun is arranged on the same side as the iron mouth opening machine, the YPF type hydraulic mud gun operates above the iron mouth opening machine, as shown in Figure 1b in YB/T017-2017.
3) Type YPK Hydraulic Mud Gun. Type YPK hydraulic mud gun adopts side inclined square base, rectangular section beam type rotating arm, external slewing mechanism, middle ear shaft rod end thread type slewing hydraulic cylinder, cylinder body pushes integral mud plug type mud punching mechanism, has the characteristics of compact structure and light weight. When the mud gun is arranged on the same side as the iron mouth opening machine, the YPK type hydraulic mud gun operates above the iron mouth opening machine, as shown in Figure 1c in YB/T0172017.

(2) Test Procedure
1) Cyclic pressure test. The number of test cycles should be in the range of 105-107.
2) General Requirements
① Use non-destructive testing methods to verify the consistency of the tested hydraulic cylinder with the manufacturing specification.
② If necessary, metal balls or other similar equivalent loose fillers can be placed inside the tested hydraulic cylinder to reduce the volume of pressurized oil, but ensure that the placed objects do not prevent pressure from reaching all test areas and do not affect the fatigue life of the hydraulic cylinder (such as shot peening strengthening).
③ When the hydraulic cylinder has multiple chambers with different pressure-bearing capacities due to design, the isolating part between the chambers should be tested for mechanical fatigue as part of the pressure-bearing shell.
(3) Failure Criteria
The following situations are considered as failures:
1) Any external leakage caused by fatigue.
2) Any internal leakage caused by fatigue.
3) Material rupture (such as cracks, etc.).

3) Application of Test Pressure. The front and rear ends of the hydraulic cylinder should preferably have two sets of oil ports, one connected to the pressure source and the other connected to the pressure measuring device.
